bugs.title: Message logged during system boot: Failed to start reboot.target:
bugs.symptoms: System messages report that BIG-IP system will reboot after the firmware update but the system does not actually reboot. Note: If you try to reboot while the update is in progress, the reboot fails and logs a message indicating that the system is going down for reboot. It does not reboot, however. Messages displayed: -- Failed to start reboot.target: Transaction contains conflicting jobs 'stop' and 'start' for systemd-reboot.service. Probably contradicting requirement dependencies configured. -- See system logs and 'systemctl status reboot.target' for details. -- Broadcast message from root@localhost on ttyS0 (Tue 2021-01-28 10:18:33 PST): The system is going down for reboot NOW!
bugs.conditions: -- Firmware is being updated. -- You initiate a system reboot.
bugs.impact: The system prevents rebooting while the firmware upgrade is in progress, but the system reports an erroneous message indicating that a reboot will occur.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to reboot during a firmware update. The message is erroneous and you can safely ignore it.

bugs.title: The CLI does not include firmware version information for sirr or ssd.
bugs.symptoms: The show components components information does not include the firmware version information for the sirr or ssd.
bugs.conditions: Running the show components command.
bugs.impact: The show components command does not report the firmware version information for the sirr or ssd data fields.

bugs.title: Root and Admin users need to have their passwords changed from default simultaneously
bugs.symptoms: When the root or admin password is changed for the first time, the other account password is changed if it is still set to the default.
bugs.conditions: Initial password change
bugs.impact: The initial password change will change both the root and admin passwords.
bugs.behavior: When the root or admin password is changed for the first time, the other account password is changed if it is still set to the default.

bugs.title: Interface 'in-discards' counter not reset
bugs.symptoms: If you issue a reset counters command, the in-discards counter is not reset to 0.
bugs.conditions: Issue 'reset counters interfaces <interface>' or 'reset counters all' commands.
bugs.impact: Counter is not reset to 0.

bugs.title: USB device presence causes errors in the blade log
bugs.symptoms: When a USB device is present in the blade, the velos.log file contains a large number of errors from platform-hal related to the USB device and attempts to detect it.
bugs.conditions: USB device is present in the blade.
bugs.impact: Numerous unnecessary messages appear in the log.
bugs.workaround: These messages are benign, and you can safely ignore them.

bugs.title: Wrong chassis serial number chs599996s populates to VELOS tenants
bugs.symptoms: Under some corner cases, system controllers may have a blank serial number in the /etc/PLATFORM file. If partition software is started during this period, any tenants deployed on that partition will report an incorrect chassis serial number chs599996s.
bugs.conditions: - Restarting the system controllers - Removing and adding the blades from the tenant
bugs.impact: VELOS tenants may report the wrong serial number, visible in "tmsh show sys hardware" or "tmsh list cm device". If a VELOS tenant spans multiple blades, and the different blades pick up different serial numbers from F5OS, the tenant may fail to properly cluster; multiple tenant blades will function as cluster primary, competing over the cluster management IP.
bugs.workaround: The correct chassis serial number can be seen in the license file, which can be viewed from a tenant by running "tmsh show sys license". If a tenant is currently bifurcated (multiple blades functioning as cluster primary), the immediate mitigation is to set the tenant to "provisioned" and then back to "deployed". If a tenant is reporting the incorrect chassis serial number (chs599996s), then the following should restore the correct serial number: 1. Determine which controller has a blank serial number for the partition, by looking at "grep CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO /var/log/sw-util.log | tail -1" run on each controller, e.g.: [root@controller-2 ~]# for i in controller-{1,2}; do echo -n "$i: "; ssh $i grep CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO /var/log/sw-util.log | tail -1; done controller-1: ++ CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO=chs700144s controller-2: ++ CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO= [root@controller-2 ~]# In this example, controller-2 is affected. 2. Reboot the affected controller. After it reboots, check whether it has a blank serial number. Repeat this step until it boots, and reports a non-blank serial number. 3. From the partition, set the tenant to "provisioned" and then back to "deployed". 4. After the tenant reboots, confirm the serial numbers is now correct (not chs599996s) in the output of "tmsh show sys hardware"

bugs.title: qkview Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, qkview does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Occurs while running qkview.
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions, qkview does not follow current best practices.

bugs.title: Status led may be left off after LCD test.
bugs.symptoms: Status LED may be left in the off state after an LCD test.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs after the LCD test is executed.
bugs.impact: Status LED may not reflect actual state of the system after an LCD test.
bugs.workaround: Power-cycling the chassis resolves the Status LED state.

bugs.title: Switch-related events with Notice severity found in confd event log during blade reboot.
bugs.symptoms: Several switch-related events sometimes occur when a blade is rebooted. These events are generated if the switch port to which the blade is connected reports an FEC Uncorrected Error, and posts error messages similar to the following: -- NOTICE 'Switch Port in fault state'. The errors usually clear soon after the blade boots up.
bugs.conditions: This occurs upon system startup.
bugs.impact: The system generates a few unwanted events. If the blade boots successfully and networking is functioning normally, you can safely ignore the 'Switch Port in fault state' events.

bugs.title: Qkview collection running on peer does not cancel when main qkview is canceled.
bugs.symptoms: Qkview collection is distributed, and there is a main process for collecting qkview information from peer devices. The main qkview process (running on the active system controller) or the partition manager, spawns processes to collect from its peers. Peers are not aware of whether the main qkview operation has been canceled.
bugs.conditions: A qkview is canceled, and then immediately restarted.
bugs.impact: Partial qkview collection. When a qkview is canceled on the main collection system, the peers are not aware of this, and continue to collect. The peer qkviews may not be collected if the peers are still processing the last qkview request.
bugs.workaround: Wait 5 minutes after canceling, and then run qkview again.

bugs.title: The tenant deployment fails if the tenant name exceeds 49 characters.
bugs.symptoms: If an admin configures a tenant with a name that is longer than 49 characters, tenant deployment fails.
bugs.conditions: Partition created and enabled on VELOS hardware for admin to login and create a tenant configuration.
bugs.impact: A configured tenant fails to schedule on the VELOS cluster. If the tenant name has more than 49 characters, the server rejects the deployment request.
bugs.workaround: Delete the existing tenant and create a new tenant deployment using a name with 49 or fewer characters. Note: The system might not prevent you from using more characters, but the recommendation is 49 or fewer.

bugs.title: 'limited' user and role are visible
bugs.symptoms: 'limited' user and role are for internal use but the role is not hidden.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the list of available users and roles.
bugs.impact: The 'limited' user is visible when it should not be.
bugs.fix: The 'limited' user and role is now hidden.

bugs.title: The 'show image' report can have staggered output.
bugs.symptoms: The 'show image' report can conflate subtable output into a single, long set of columns. In some instances, the report begins to stagger row output. Although the information presented is accurate, the format is suboptimal.
bugs.conditions: Very wide screen widths cause table conflation to take place for the 'show image' report.
bugs.impact: Some rows (right-hand side of report) wrap around to the next line, making the report more difficult to interpret.
bugs.workaround: Adjust the screen width before running 'show image', as in: syscon-1-active# screen-width 60 syscon-1-active# show image
bugs.fix: System images report no longer produces conflated output with staggered rows.

bugs.title: Creating a partition using the CLI, 'commit check' fails
bugs.symptoms: When creating a partition using the CLI, and trying to validate the changes with 'commit check', a validation error occurs: partitions 'partition part1 uuid' is not configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a partition using the CLI. -- Attempt to validate the changes using 'commit check'.
bugs.impact: The 'commit check' operation rejects this config change. This error is misleading, indicating that you need to specify a uuid value. Note: Not only is uuid irrelevant, it is not possible for you to specify it.

bugs.title: Qkview generation mishandles filename with space in it.
bugs.symptoms: If the qkview filename contains a space, the system uses only first word for the qkview filename.
bugs.conditions: Using filenames with spaces in them while generating a qkview.
bugs.impact: Only the first word is used in the generated qkview filename.
bugs.workaround: Do not use space in qkview filenames.

bugs.title: System date/time do not display in the GUI, cannot be set.
bugs.symptoms: The system does not display the current date/time and timezone in the GUI, which can make it difficult to review alerts or logs without knowing/remembering how the system is configured. The system does not provide a mechanism to update the system clock directly, without NTP.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to view or set system time and date via the GUI.
bugs.impact: You cannot view or set system time and date through the GUI.

bugs.title: The ed25519 certificate and key are not accepted.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI stops working without any warning or error if an ed25519 crt/key is imported.
bugs.conditions: Import an ed25519 crt/key.
bugs.impact: GUI stops working. In the system controller log you see errors: -- controller-1 /usr/bin/authd[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000026 msg="OpenSSL PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey failed read key" file="server.key". -- controller-1 /usr/bin/authd[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000022 msg="OpenSSL X509_PUBKEY_get failed to get key.".
bugs.workaround: Do not use ed25519 crts/keys.

bugs.title: Import and sync of platform software on both controllers takes up to 15 minutes.
bugs.symptoms: When importing platform software on a controller, it can take up to 15 minutes to fully import and synchronize between both controllers.
bugs.conditions: Transferring an ISO image to a VELOS controller for import.
bugs.impact: Import takes a long time, and the import may appear to be stuck or failed when it is not.
bugs.fix: Platform software import and synchronization times have been significantly reduced.

bugs.title: Fields on file import and export popups are reset after a failed file import attempt.
bugs.symptoms: All previously filled in fields are reset and cleared on the file import/export popup upon a failed transfer attempt.
bugs.conditions: A file import or export operation fails.
bugs.impact: You must fully reenter the information in all of the fields in order to resubmit the file transfer request.
bugs.workaround: Reenter the data into the fields and reattempt the file transfer.

bugs.title: Certificate import interface does not provide correct actionable error.
bugs.symptoms: Confd CLI gives an irrelevant error message when an expired cert is set to a TLS certificate element. Aborted: 'system aaa tls config certificate': Key public_key does not match Certificate public_key.
bugs.conditions: # system aaa tls config key <key> # system aaa tls config certificate <expired cert content>
bugs.impact: A misleading error message is printed.
bugs.fix: CLI is fixed to give correct error message in all the following cases: 'Public Key does not match certificate' 'Not valid Certificate/Key Contents' 'Certificate is expired.' 'Certificate is not yet valid.' 'Not an OpenSSL Key' 'Bad public key from private key'

bugs.title: tcpdump Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, tcpdump does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Under certain conditions, tcpdump does not follow current best practices.
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions, tcpdump does not follow current best practices.

bugs.title: Nodes are displayed in the tenant instance IDs table even after removing them from the tenant
bugs.symptoms: When running the following command in confd: show running-config tenants tenant dag-tenant config nodes One of the fields displayed is tenant-instance-ids. The ID is displayed even after deleting the tenant instance.
bugs.conditions: Add a tenant and then delete it.
bugs.impact: The tenant instance ID is still displayed. This is cosmetic and there is no functional impact.
bugs.fix: The active tenant list is now displayed properly.

bugs.title: Two different partitions can be assigned the same management IP address
bugs.symptoms: It is possible to assign the same management IP address to multiple partitions.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when creating new partitions using the CLI. You can duplicate the management IP address without getting an error.
bugs.impact: Creating a duplicate management IP address can cause management traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the affected partitions with unique IP addresses.

bugs.title: Transient system error for AOM/LOP fault due to not receiving health reports from all installed fantrays or PSU controllers.
bugs.symptoms: The system may report a transient error for a fault in the AOM/LOP due to not receiving health reports from all installed VFC (fantray) or VPC (PSU controller) cards, and then the error condition is resolved only a couple of seconds later. For example, the error condition occurring: 65543 controller-1 aom-fault ASSERT ERROR "Fault detected in the AOM" "2020-12-30 01:16:32.522027731 UTC" 65543 controller-1 aom-fault EVENT Network Access "Asserted: LOP is not receiving health reports from all installed VPC cards" "2020-12-30 01:16:32.522051183 UTC" The resolution of the error two seconds later: 65543 controller-1 aom-fault CLEAR ERROR "Fault detected in the AOM" "2020-12-30 01:16:34.184866455 UTC" 65543 controller-1 aom-fault EVENT Network Access "Deasserted: LOP is not receiving health reports from all installed VPC cards" "2020-12-30 01:16:34.184891732 UTC" These transient error reports do not indicate an AOM/LOP fault and can be ignored.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions cause the transient error report for an AOM/LOP fault caused by not receiving health reports from all installed fantrays and PSU controllers. It may occur at any time.
bugs.impact: The transient error report for an AOM/LOP fault caused by not receiving health reports from all installed fantrays and PSU controllers can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: The transient error report for an AOM/LOP fault caused by not receiving health reports from all installed VFC(fantray) and VPC(PSU controller)cards can be ignored.
bugs.fix: Fixed in CC-LOP firmware v1.00.1085.00.1 and later available with F5OS-C 1.2.0.

bugs.title: Qkview truncates lines of top command at 80 characters.
bugs.symptoms: The top command defaults to 80 characters, if run outside of a console, as it is in qkview. When top is executed in this fashion, the -w parameter must be used, in order to specify output width.
bugs.conditions: Run qkview.
bugs.impact: Output of top command is truncated at 80 characters. Some contents of the top command may be missing in qkview files.
bugs.workaround: Run top separately from qkview.
bugs.fix: Previously, qkviews were not always complete. This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Partition status displayed by system controller may not be accurate
bugs.symptoms: The system controller may display a partition status of "running" rather than "running-active" or "running-standby".
bugs.conditions: If the system controller component responsible for reporting the partition state restarts, or misses a state-transition message, the state will not be updated until the next state-transition.
bugs.impact: Incomplete and possibly misleading status information is reported to the user.
bugs.fix: The state-reporting mechanism has been updated to account for missed messages or restarts, so that displayed status will be accurate.

bugs.title: Slow system controller operations for CLI image commands.
bugs.symptoms: A number of system controller operations related to images suffer from an approximately 5-second delay. This includes CLI commands such as 'show image partition' and 'show image controller', but there is also a delay when using tab-completion to view suggested completions for such commands. The delay appears to be mostly constant, independent of the number of partitions in the system. The delay is always present for these commands.
bugs.conditions: Using CLI commands related to images.
bugs.impact: In addition to the 5-second delays experienced directly on the CLI, there is likely similar impact to related GUI functionality, such as the partition management page. These delays do not appear to negatively impact any functionality.
bugs.fix: Previously, there was a delay when using CLI commands such as 'show image partition' and 'show image controller', or when using tab completion with these commands. This has been fixed and there is no longer a delay.

bugs.title: CLI commands for DNS and NTP could be simplified
bugs.symptoms: The CLI commands to configure DNS and NTP require specifying addresses twice. For example, specifying a DNS server: config system dns servers server 10.10.10.10 config address 10.10.10.10 commit
bugs.conditions: Configuring a DNS or NTP server using the CLI commands.
bugs.impact: There is no operational impact; however, it is preferable to enter the IP address only once.
bugs.workaround: None. You have to specify the IP address twice.

bugs.title: Unable to read key from storage.
bugs.symptoms: The checksum changed from size 256 to 512. Systems that created the encryption keys using 256 would fail when upgrading.
bugs.conditions: System must have been configured with old software that wrote 256-bit hashes and upgraded to a newer version that expected 512-bit hashes.
bugs.impact: The upgrade does not accept the key since the hash does not match.
bugs.workaround: Going into the vcc-confd container and requesting the key twice would change the key and store a new 512 hash. From the System Controller: # docker exec -it vcc-confd bash # getConfdMasterKey.sh --storage eeprom # exit
bugs.fix: With the fix, either 256 or 512 hash keys are accepted so upgrading from an older system does not fail as before.

bugs.title: PSU data missing in the show components component.
bugs.symptoms: After a system controller failover, the PSU information may not be populated in the command: show component component.
bugs.conditions: Active system controller fails over to the standby.
bugs.impact: PSU data is not listed. There is no operational impact to the system.
bugs.workaround: A total system reboot is the only option for listing the PSU data in the 'show components component' output.
bugs.fix: PSU data is now present in show components component results.

bugs.title: Partition config-backup silently overwrites a previous config backup.
bugs.symptoms: The partition 'system database config-backup' command overwrites an existing backup file.
bugs.conditions: Running the partition 'system database config-backup' command.
bugs.impact: If a config backup exists, the operation silently overwrites it.
bugs.workaround: Specify a unique filename for each backup operation: system database config-backup name unique-filename

bugs.title: Viewing the content of restricted directories
bugs.symptoms: The file list/show command provides unrestricted access to all the directories.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the content of directories.
bugs.impact: User can view all the directories.
bugs.fix: Fixed the File list/show commands to restrict access to whitelisted directories.

bugs.title: Interface config TPID leaf is exposed but it is not supported.
bugs.symptoms: Interface config tpid leaf is exposed but it is not supported.
bugs.conditions: -- In CLI config mode, the system presents tpid as a possible config option. -- In CLI show mode, tpid is shown as oper data.
bugs.impact: Interface config tpid leaf is exposed but it is not supported.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the tpid from interface/config or interface/state.

bugs.title: The URL field on file import does not validate a HTTPS protocol.
bugs.symptoms: A URL that does not specify HTTPS as the protocol is accepted as valid input, but results in a failed file transfer.
bugs.conditions: -- Importing a file to the device. -- Enter a URL that does not specify HTTPS as the protocol.
bugs.impact: The URL field accepts the input, but the file transfer fails. Lack of protocol validation on the URL input does not prevent you from entering a URL that can result in a failed file import.
bugs.workaround: All file import URLs must use HTTPS protocol.
bugs.fix: URL field on file import now validates HTTPS protocol.

bugs.title: Importing a file can result in errors when parameters are correct.
bugs.symptoms: Importing a file using File Utilities, or using the Software Management import utilities for System Controller and Chassis Partition software images can result in an error, even when the URL and other parameters are correct.
bugs.conditions: -- Importing a file. -- The first attempt has an invalid URL. -- Subsequent import attempts contain similarities in the URL paths used on the first attempt.
bugs.impact: The import fails and the error is ambiguous.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the screen and initiate a new file import attempt, making sure the URL and all other parameters entered are correct and valid.
bugs.fix: Importing a file no longer reports errors when parameters are correct.

bugs.title: File extension validation on URL input fields for F5OS File Utilities and Software Management are not case insensitive.
bugs.symptoms: The input validation on the URL field when you import a file, checks that the URL ends in .iso or .img, but it does not accept mixed case or uppercase entries, for example, .ISO / .IMG / .iMg / .Iso, etc.
bugs.conditions: -- Importing a file, either with File Utilities or the Software Management import utilities for System Controller and Chassis Partition software images. -- The URL has a file extension that is not lowercase.
bugs.impact: The URL field reports a validation warning.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the file extension appended on the end of the URL is all lowercase.
bugs.fix: File extension validation on URL input fields for F5OS File Utilities and Software Management features is now case insensitive.

bugs.title: Tenant operational state has incorrect data when it has no nodes.
bugs.symptoms: When the admin removes nodes from tenant configuration and upgrades the system controller software, the tenant status comes up with an error state.
bugs.conditions: Admin removes nodes from the tenant configuration using either of the following commands: no tenants tenant <name> config nodes tenants tenant <name> config nodes [ ]
bugs.impact: This has no effect on system functionality. The system is simply reporting an incorrect state of the tenant.
bugs.workaround: To process any traffic through the tenant, you must have a minimum of one node in the tenant config, for example: show running-config tenants tenant <name> config nodes tenants tenant example1 config nodes [ 1 ] !

bugs.title: Primary-Key-Migration set response message references incorrect command.
bugs.symptoms: After setting the primary key, the system reports the following message: -- Response Info: Key migration is initiated. Use 'show system primary-key state status' to get status. This is the wrong command.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when running the following command: system aaa primary key set
bugs.impact: The prompt for the set command is misleading.
bugs.workaround: Use the command: show system aaa primary-key state status

bugs.title: Admin cannot edit the tenant config in Deployed state from GUI if the tenants are created via CLI
bugs.symptoms: Tenant validations are not working when a tenant is created using the CLI and subsequently edited in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Admin creates the tenant via CLI and subsequently edits the following tenant config when the running-state is set to Deployed: -- Scale-up/Scale-down the tenant. -- Add/Remove VLAN.
bugs.impact: Admin cannot scale up/scale down the cluster using the GUI if the tenant is initially deployed via CLI.
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI to scale-up/scale-down and add/remove the VLAN to the tenant.

bugs.title: 'TPM Randomization failed' message displays in the log.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIOS on a blade is freshly updated and the blade is booted, there may be a 'TPM Randomization failed' message observed in the log output. This message occurs only once (if at all) and is then followed by a successful boot of the system. This is caused by the TPM randomization step of the boot not being completed. The next boot of the system, initiated by the BIOS when this condition is encountered, allows the TPM randomization to complete. For security purposes, the system does not boot to the OS until TPM randomization has successfully completed.
bugs.conditions: This particular instance of this message may occur after a fresh BIOS update to the system. If the initial boot after a BIOS install is interrupted, the subsequent boot may display this message in the log. The BIOS then causes the blade to reboot, allowing the TPM randomization step to complete.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to the functionality of the system. The message is for informational purposes only in this situation. If the TPM randomization step of the BIOS execution is not able to complete successfully, the BIOS causes the blade to reboot until the TPM randomization is successful. Note: If the system continually fails to boot due to this issue, you may have a hardware issue that requires F5 response to correct.
bugs.workaround: Allow the blade to continue to boot. Once the BIOS has caused the blade to reboot, the condition clears itself and the message no longer appears as part of the boot process.

bugs.title: VELOS system controller/chassis partition should support a system hostname
bugs.symptoms: System hostname is missing in operational data (state data). For example: Even after configuring the system hostname, it is not visible when you run the "show system state hostname" command. syscon-2-active# show system state hostname % No entries found.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure hostname in config mode using this command: system config hostname <name> 2. Display the configured hostname using this command: show system state hostname
bugs.impact: Hostname is not visible in state info.
bugs.workaround: Check for the configured hostname from the system controller login prompt or by checking the running configuration using the "show running-config system config hostname" command.
bugs.fix: Hostname now displays when you use the "show system state hostname" command.
bugs.behavior: The "show system state hostname" command now provides a valid response and displays the currently-set hostname.

bugs.title: Tenant Management MAC address is not correctly displayed in tmsh or iControl interfaces
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS partition CLI correctly displays the tenant management MAC address that matches what the tenant reports via 'ifconfig mgmt'. However, 'tmsh show sys mac-address' shows a different value. vCMP guests also exhibit this behavior.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on F5OS tenants and vCMP guests.
bugs.impact: No functional impact known; just reports incorrect data.
bugs.workaround: If the tenant MAC address is required, use 'ifconfig mgmt' inside the tenant, or use the value in the partition CLI.

bugs.title: System controller does not have remote method to power on after being remotely powered off.
bugs.symptoms: If the system controller is powered off from the Linux bash shell using 'shutdown -P' or an equivalent command, there is no method available in Always On Always-On Management (AOM) menu, or any other method, to remotely power back on the system controller. Once the system controller is powered off, it can be powered on only by either reseating the system controller or performing a full chassis power cycle.
bugs.conditions: The system controller is powered off using a bash command.
bugs.impact: You are unable to remotely power on a system controller after it has been powered off.
bugs.workaround: Reseat the controller or power cycle the chassis.

bugs.title: Image import is not re-attempted if controller reboots while importing
bugs.symptoms: If a system controller reboots in the middle of importing platform software, the import does not automatically restart on the next boot. Additionally, it is not possible to overwrite it via a new file transfer to try again.
bugs.conditions: -- Valid F5OS software has begun importing on a system controller, but the import is not complete yet. -- A reboot is issued by either the admin user or the software.
bugs.impact: The software is not imported.
bugs.workaround: Follow this procedure: 1. Download the software again, but using a different destination file name. 2. Try the import operation again.

bugs.title: Partition shows "failed" state when enabled for brief period
bugs.symptoms: After enabling a partition, the "show partitions" command will show a status of "failed" while the partition instance is in the process of starting up, but has not yet started. Once the startup completes, the status will transition to "running", "running-active", or "running-standby".
bugs.conditions: Partition is starting after being enabled.
bugs.impact: The user may think the partition software has encountered a failure condition.
bugs.workaround: Wait for 20 to 30 seconds for the status to be reported correctly.
bugs.fix: The partition status reporting logic now uses additional state information to correctly distinguish between "starting" and "failed".

bugs.title: Lost traffic on previously active system controller.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic is lost on the previously active system controller, so half of the traffic is lost.
bugs.conditions: If active system controller does not function, here are some examples: -- The system controller is physically non-functional (no electrical activity, etc.). -- System software results in system controller failures for a long time.
bugs.impact: Traffic is lost on the previously active system controller, so half of the traffic is lost.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the newly active system controller.
bugs.fix: The system does not lose traffic when the active system controller fails and does not come back.

bugs.title: The LACPD process crashes and writes a core file following physical interface deletion.
bugs.symptoms: The lacpd process crashes and writes a core file following deletion of the physical interface if the interface is a working member of an LACP trunk. Physical interface deletes are commonly caused by either removing an associated blade from the partition or changing the port bifurcation configuration (e.g., from 1x100G to 4x25G).
bugs.conditions: Delete a physical interface that is a working member of an LACP trunk.
bugs.impact: Lacpd crashes and writes a core file; traffic disrupted while lacpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Delete the aggregate-id for any physical interface before the interface is deleted.
bugs.fix: The system now checks whether the working member is deleted and does not core.

bugs.title: IPv6 addresses defined in RADIUS servers fail
bugs.symptoms: Setting up a IPv6 RADIUS server fails.
bugs.conditions: -- RADIUS server being defined -- An IPv6 address is used
bugs.impact: Radius servers configured with IPv6 cannot be used.
bugs.workaround: Use only IPv4 addresses.
bugs.fix: The fixed version now allows both ipv4 or ipv6 addresses. Note that the radius server might need to have a separate entry for each type of address.
bugs.behavior: ipv6 addresses are now supported which wasn't the case before.

bugs.title: Changing chassis-id in system network config causes the OpenShift cluster not to install correctly.
bugs.symptoms: If the chassis-id is changed from the default of 1 in the 'system network' configuration on the system controller, the OpenShift cluster does not reinstall correctly once the change takes effect.
bugs.conditions: Chassis-id is changed from default of 1 to any other value.
bugs.impact: OpenShift cluster does not re-install correctly, which means tenants cannot be launched on the system.

bugs.title: Bi-directional optics part is not recognized and interface remains in the down state.
bugs.symptoms: Interface remains in down state even with optics and fiber inserted, and the optics type is not identified
bugs.conditions: Bi-Directional optics is present in the system
bugs.impact: Interface will not be operational
bugs.fix: Bi-Directional optics type should be recognized and interface should be operational

bugs.title: Management session may be unresponsive after rebooting the standby System Controller.
bugs.symptoms: When the standby system controller is rebooted, the management session may freeze for 10-15 seconds.
bugs.conditions: The standby system controller is rebooted
bugs.impact: The management session is frozen briefly, then resumes normal operation.

bugs.title: Partition high availability (HA) framework core on shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Corefile named "underdog-1.core.gz" is found.
bugs.conditions: If the partition "system database config-backup" or "system database config-restore" commands are used the high availability (HA) framework daemon (process named "underdog") may produce a corefile the next time it is shut down.
bugs.impact: A corefile is produced.
bugs.fix: The config-backup/config-restore commands no longer corrupt memory and produce a corefile.

bugs.title: Backplane connectivity failures upon blade boot
bugs.symptoms: After powering on or rebooting one or more blades in a partition, blades can fail to establish data plane connectivity between each other across the backplane, resulting in complete loss of traffic in between blades. This can exhibit itself with symptoms such as an inability for multi-blade tenants to cluster, or traffic received by one blade being unable to route that traffic to another blade, among other possibilities. The problem can be identified more specifically by inspection of the tmstat 'vqf_cfg' table in the partition_fpga container. On each blade perform the following: docker exec -it partition_fpga tmctl -d blade -w 120 vqf_cfg If the 'active_blades' column does not have the same value for all assigned and enabled blades within a partition, and are otherwise expected to be running with good states, then this issue has likely been encountered.
bugs.conditions: A blade is booted for the first time, or rebooted.
bugs.impact: Loss of data plane traffic in between blades within a partition.
bugs.workaround: Attempt to reboot the blade until the condition clears.

bugs.title: System controller config backup and restore causes the system not to function properly.
bugs.symptoms: After restoring a config backup, the system controller software assigns auto-generated IDs for the partitions. These auto-generated IDs are not mapped to blades and OpenShift cluster namespaces. This behavior causes the system to not work properly.
bugs.conditions: Reset the system to factory default settings using the system controller CLI, and then restore the backup.
bugs.impact: System goes into an Inoperative state for tenant deployments.
bugs.workaround: The steps outlined below walk you through the entire process of taking a backup of the system, and then restoring the system to the factory default settings. The steps also include sample commands. Note: You must have console access to the system to complete this task. Running the reset-to-default command removes the management network. Backup ======= 1.) Backup tenant configs by logging into the tenant. Save the config, and then copy the config file backup to a safe, external location: tmsh save sys ucs /var/tmp/config.ucs 2.) Backup partition configs by logging into each partition. Backup the database, and then copy the database backup to a safe, external location: part2-1(config)# system database config-backup name <partition-backup-filename> result = Database backup successful. part2-1(config)# scp admin@@partitionIP:configs/<partition-backup-filename> <external-device-ip> 3.) Backup the controller config by logging into the system controller using a floating IP address, and then copy the backup config file to a safe, external location: syscon-2-active(config)# system database config-backup name <controller-backup-filename> response Succeeded. syscon-2-active(config)# scp root@floatingIP:/var/confd/configs/<controller-backup-filename> <external-machine-ip> Important: Once you execute the reset-to-default command, the system controller deletes the associated filesystems and backup files. So make sure to backup the system controller, tenant, and partition configs before continuing. 4.) Delete partition configs: part2-1(config)# system database reset-to-default proceed yes result Database reset-to-default successful. part2-1(config)# System message at 2021-03-11 00:02:21... Commit performed by admin via tcp using cli. 5.) Put all slots in the none-partition: syscon-2-active(config)# slots slot 1 partition none syscon-2-active(config)# slots slot 2 partition none syscon-2-active(config-slot-2)# commit Commit complete. 6.) Remove the partitions from the system controller: syscon-2-active(config)# no partitions partition part2 syscon-2-active(config)# no partitions partition part3 syscon-2-active(config)# commit Commit complete. 7.) Using a console connection, reset the controller config to factory defaults from the system controller CLI: syscon-2-active(config)# system database config reset-default-config true syscon-2-active(config)# commit Commit complete. 8.) Reboot the controllers. Once controllers are fully rebooted, proceed to the restore task. Restore ======= 1.) Set up the system controller mgmt network using the wizard/CLI. 2.) Import the backup from the external device to the system controller: ssh root@floatingip mkdir -p /var/confd/configs/ scp <external-machine>:<backup> /var/confd/configs/ 3.) Restore the controller config: syscon-1-active(config)# system database config-restore name <controller-backup> response Succeeded. 4.) Reboot the blades. 5.) To restore the partition config (including VLANs/tenants/interfaces/etc.), import the partition config to the active partition that is running on the controller (running 'show partitions' from the system controller CLI displays which controller is running the active partition): part2-2(config)# system database config-restore name <partition-backup> result Database restore successful. part2-2(config)# System message at 2021-03-11 01:10:34... Commit performed by admin via tcp using cli. 6.) Restore the tenant config once the tenant mgmt-ip is reachable. To do so, copy the config after the partition restores (where config.ucs is your .UCS filename): tmsh load sys ucs /var/tmp/config.ucs
bugs.fix: Config backup and restore to factory default settings now works properly.

bugs.title: No platform trunk information passed to tenant
bugs.symptoms: Trunk information is not being published to BIG-IP tenants for use in high availability (HA) group definitions.
bugs.conditions: When defining high availability (HA) groups.
bugs.impact: No trunk or trunk member information is reported. This reduces the usefulness of information used to compare the relative health of high availability (HA) peers and potentially initiating a tenant failover, depending on that output.
bugs.fix: Trunk information is now synchronized between the VELOS system and tenants, enhancing the tenant high availability (HA) health check.
bugs.behavior: Trunk information is now synchronized between the VELOS system and tenants, which increases the usefulness of information used to compare the relative health of high availability (HA) peers and potentially initiating a tenant failover, depending on that output.

bugs.title: Partition manager qkview data collection inadequate
bugs.symptoms: The partition manager container does not capture sufficient status information for problem diagnosis.
bugs.conditions: Capturing a qkview to diagnose system problems.
bugs.impact: It is difficult to determine the conditions that may have caused failures.
bugs.fix: Qkview now contains the complete partition running-config, and additional internal and operational state.

bugs.title: If the initial partition database startup is interrupted, it can leave an empty database
bugs.symptoms: After the partition initially starts up, the partition cannot be used because there are no users or roles defined.
bugs.conditions: A problem occurs when the partition is starting up for the first time. This could happen if the partition were disabled shortly after being enabled, or if a controller failover occurs at the wrong time. The problem will not occur after the database has initialized correctly.
bugs.impact: The partition cannot be used, since it is not possible to log in and set a configuration.
bugs.workaround: After a partition is created, if it is not possible to log in, the chassis administrator can remove all slots from the partition and delete it. After the transaction commits, re-create the partition with the desired slots.
bugs.fix: The database software correctly detects and recovers from this condition.

bugs.title: Crypto/Compression Acceleration not enabled by default when creating a tenant
bugs.symptoms: Prior to version 1.1.2, high-performance crypto processing and compression had to be explicitly enabled using the Crypto/Compression Acceleration setting on the Add Tenant Deployments screen.
bugs.conditions: When creating a new tenant deployment on a chassis partition.
bugs.impact: Performance can be impacted when Crypto/Compression Acceleration is disabled.
bugs.workaround: Manually enable Crypto/Compression Acceleration for the tenant instances that require it.
bugs.fix: Beginning with F5OS version 1.1.2, Crypto/Compression Acceleration is enabled by default when deploying a new tenant. Note that you may need to explicitly enable the setting on tenants deployed on a previous F5OS version.

bugs.title: The "show system mgmt-ip" command displays "Application Timeout" on the active system controller
bugs.symptoms: On a system where the standby system controller is rebooting, running the 'show system mgmt-ip' command from the CLI might display an "Application Iimeout" error.
bugs.conditions: -- Standby system controller is rebooting. -- Run the 'show system mgmt-ip' command from the CLI.
bugs.impact: This problem is limited to the system controller management IP address only.
bugs.workaround: The command fails the very first time the command runs while the standby controller is rebooting. After it fails the first time, the command displays output in subsequent retries.
bugs.fix: The 'show system mgmt-ip' command now works while the standby system controller is rebooting.

bugs.title: Controller sshd service dies under rare circumstances.
bugs.symptoms: Under rare circumstances, the 'sshd' service on controllers will die and not automatically restart in response to rapid modification of host ssh keys.
bugs.conditions: Running a pre-1.2.0 version of the system controller OS.
bugs.impact: Under rare circumstances, 'sshd' dies and does not automatically restart, restricting ssh access to controllers.
bugs.workaround: 1. Connect to the system controller serial console. 2. In bash, execute the command 'systemctl restart sshd'. OR 1. Reboot the affected system controller.
bugs.fix: Fix intermittent issue that would cause 'sshd' on system controllers to die and not restart under certain circumstances.

bugs.title: Under rare conditions, blades may fail to start partition platform containers
bugs.symptoms: After encountering a rare import bug, subsequent upgrades of partition software may result in a state where blades in a partition fail to start partition platform services after a system controller failover event.
bugs.conditions: 1. A rare issue leads to the conditions of ID 984977 occurring during an import of some version of the partition ISO or services. 2. That version of partition services is configured for use by an active partition. 3. The system controllers fail over and switch active/standby roles. 4. Blades in partition are rebooted. 5. Blades fail to pull and start partition services, or pull and start the wrong version of services.
bugs.impact: Partition performance is degraded or disrupted.
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove all software configuration for the affected partition and disable the partition. 2. Re-enable the partition and re-configure the software versions you wish to use. or 1. In bash on the affected blade(s), run 'cp /var/export/chassis/partition/<partition ID>/blade/* /var/docker/config/' 2. Reboot the affected blade(s). Both workarounds will only persist until the next time the system controllers fail over, at which point they would need to be performed again. A more persistent workaround will require more involved, case-by-case modification of import structure by a support engineer.
bugs.fix: Blades no longer fail to start partition platform services under certain rare conditions

bugs.title: Orchestration-manager cores on standby system controller during cluster bringup
bugs.symptoms: A core file from orchestration-manager might be created on the standby system controller during cluster bringup.
bugs.conditions: This might occur intermittently during cluster bringup.
bugs.impact: A core file is generated, but orchestration-manager will restart and will not cause any issues with system function.
bugs.workaround: None ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Networks Technical Support web site: http://www.f5.com/support/ The AskF5 web site: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/home The F5 DevCentral web site: http://devcentral.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Tue Sep 21 12:09:24 2021 PDT Copyright F5 Networks (2021) - All Rights Reserved Contact Support

bugs.title: System controller 'show partitions' output can be inaccurate.
bugs.symptoms: The output of the 'show partitions' command should display the current operational status (disabled, running, starting, stopping, failed, etc.) for each partition instance. In some cases, the displayed status is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: When the chassis has multiple partitions, and there are gaps in the partition IDs, the internal state tracking can fail to record and report the partition state, typically showing that a partition is 'failed', when it is actually operating normally.
bugs.impact: The user will be misled about the system state.
bugs.fix: The operational state monitoring has been fixed.

bugs.title: Partition set-version command should warn user about reboot/traffic disruption when used on CLI
bugs.symptoms: The "set-version" command causes the partition control-plane software to be restarted, and reboots blades and tenant instances. This will disrupt dataplane traffic. The user should be warned, and acknowledge the intent to interrupt network traffic processing.
bugs.conditions: The chassis administrator changes the partition software version with the partition set-version command.
bugs.impact: Chassis administrator may inadvertently cause network traffic interruption.
bugs.fix: The "set-version" command now issues a warning and requires confirmation from the user before beginning the software installation. The prompt may be optionally bypassed by adding the "process yes" argument to the command.

bugs.title: VQF hot signal asserted warnings
bugs.symptoms: A PEL log entry occurs indicating an FPGA HOT signal asserted: Warning | AOM | 5 | Na | VQF hot thermal event
bugs.conditions: This issue happens at system startup.
bugs.impact: If the issue occurs during system startup, it is an erroneous error message and can be safely ignored.
bugs.workaround: Fixed an erroneous FPGA HOT signal that occurs during system startup.
bugs.fix: Fixed an erroneous FPGA HOT signal that occurs during system startup.

bugs.title: iHealth indicates multiple unhealthy and critical states for empty PSU bays
bugs.symptoms: The component health for empty PSU bays in the VELOS chassis is shown as unhealthy along with an iHealth critical severity.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on a VELOS chassis that has one or more PSUs not populated.
bugs.impact: The chassis health of empty PSU bays are shown has unhealthy in iHealth.
bugs.fix: Modified diag-agent service so that it does not mark an unhealthy state for PSUs that are not present in the chassis.

bugs.title: L2 Table corruption results in a traffic loss.
bugs.symptoms: The Layer 2 (L2) table on a blade can become corrupted under certain conditions. When this happens, traffic to the affected destination (either a tenant or a external interface) do not flow properly.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system with more than one blade installed. -- A packet for a tenant associated with one blade arrives on a different blade that is encountering the L2 table corruption.
bugs.impact: Traffic loss to a tenant or the front-panel interfaces. This may include partial or full packet loss to the tenant.
bugs.fix: FPGA Manager now detects the corruption so incorrect entries are not written to the L2 table. This prevents traffic loss from occurring.

bugs.title: Using curl to access 'scp:' URIs on the partition management IP does not work
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to upload a tenant image via "curl filename scp:IMAGES" would fail, even though "scp filename admin@mgmt-ip:IMAGES" works.
bugs.conditions: Accessing ssh/scp via curl rather that the scp application.
bugs.impact: Cannot use curl to copy files.
bugs.workaround: Use scp directly rather than curl.
bugs.fix: The ssh/scp server has been fixed to correctly interpret the file/directory names supplied by the 'curl' command.

bugs.title: SwitchD may fail to start due to insufficient memory.
bugs.symptoms: The system controller is unable to communicate with one or more of the running blades. The 'show cluster' command indicates a blade(s) is NotReady even though the blade is fully booted. The other system controller may show similar mis-reporting of blades, but on different blades. An assert in the switchd vendor SDK code is triggered if a 16MB allocation cannot be satisfied during switchd startup. SwitchD will not provide required switch configuration when this occurs resulting in a management port and chassis internal network outage.
bugs.conditions: The problem can manifest any time SwitchD starts/restarts. It is most likely to manifest during installation or live update of the system controller software.
bugs.impact: The problem persists until the system controller on which the condition occurs is rebooted.

bugs.title: Config backup files cannot be deleted.
bugs.symptoms: The config backup files that reside in /mnt/var/confd/configs on the System Controller and on /var/f5/partition/configs on the Partition, can not be deleted. When you attempt to delete these files using "file delete ..", the CLI throws an error.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to delete config backup files using "file delete ..." CLI.
bugs.impact: The backup files will take the disk volume and the system may work in an unexpected way.
bugs.fix: Backend support is added to allow deletion of the config backup files.

bugs.title: 1.2.1 platform software cannot be imported on Controller OS versions below 1.2.0
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to import 1.2.1 platform software (Controller or Partition OS, services, or ISOs) on Controller OS versions lower than 1.2.0.
bugs.conditions: 1. Running a version of Controller OS <1.2.0 2. Try to import 1.2.1 platform software.
bugs.impact: You are unable to import platform software version 1.2.1 if the Controller OS version is lower than version 1.2.0.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to import platform software version 1.2.1 while running version 1.1.4 of the Controller OS (but still not prior 1.1.X releases).

bugs.title: Erratic VLAN assignment during tenant start-up.
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting a tenant, the tenant might receive some erratic VLAN assignment requests, but the VLANs are not associated with this tenant. This spurious VLAN assignment may impact traffic.
bugs.conditions: 1. A tenant is created without an assigned VLAN 2. Reboot the blade that tenant is assigned to The second step is not required every time, but it is triggered due to the first step.
bugs.impact: Application traffic through the chassis could be impacted.
bugs.workaround: There are 2 workarounds: 1. Assign VLAN(s) to the tenant which does not have assigned VLANs and reboot all the blades of this tenant 2. Assign VLAN(s) to the tenant which does not have assigned VLAN and run 'docker restart of API_SERVICE_GW container' on all blades
bugs.fix: When a tenant is not configured with any VLANs, the tenant will no longer receive incorrect VLANs when a blade is rebooted.

bugs.title: Tenant virtual disk is deleted when the tenant running-state is set to "configured."
bugs.symptoms: A VELOS tenant's virtual-disk is deleted when the tenant running-state is set back to "configured" after having been "deployed." This behavior differs from vCMP. It is recommended that you set the tenant running-state to "provisioned" in order to stop the running tenant.
bugs.conditions: Tenant running-state changed from "deployed" to "configured."
bugs.impact: Virtual disk is deleted, resulting in loss of tenant configuration.
bugs.workaround: Fixed. No workaround needed.
bugs.fix: The system no longer deletes the virtual disk when the state is changed from deployed to configured.

bugs.title: Timestamps not consistent across chassis.
bugs.symptoms: Blade logs use the PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) or PST (Pacific Standard Time) timezone. Other logs use the timezone local to the device (i.e., on a properly configured BIG-IP), and some controller logs record in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time).
bugs.conditions: You can see the differences when viewing the chassis logs across.
bugs.impact: Timezones are not consistent across chassis. This can impact troubleshooting.

bugs.title: Blade out of memory condition when using a large number of VLANs.
bugs.symptoms: If a tenant or tenants are assigned a large number of vlans, an out of memory condition can be triggered on the blade after several days.
bugs.conditions: A large number of vlans is assigned to a single tenant.
bugs.impact: Tenants may die and new tenants may fail to launch on the affected blade.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of vlans assigned to a single tenant.

bugs.title: Timeout/failure on blade/controller pxeboot.
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to pxeboot blades or system controllers, it fails with a timeout.
bugs.conditions: This happens in the following scenarios: -- The steps to configure pxeboot have not been performed. -- The services provided by the image-server container have stopped working properly.
bugs.impact: Pxeboot fails.
bugs.workaround: To configure for pxeboot, be sure that a partition iso file has been imported, a partition has been configured and enabled, and the slots to boot are assigned to that partition. If those steps are performed properly, then it is possible the image-server services are no longer properly functioning. In that case, you can recover using either of the following workarounds: -- Restart the vcc-image-server container. -- Reboot the system controller.

bugs.title: In rare cases, the blade software can disconnect from the system controller and never recover.
bugs.symptoms: In very rare scenarios, blade software components may be unable to communicate with the database on the system controller. LACP and STP daemons hang at startup, and it could cause other issues in a partition.
bugs.conditions: The issue can occur when both system controllers are rebooted at once.
bugs.impact: The LACP, LLDP, and STP daemons may be indefinitely unusable. It is suspected there could be other impacts depending on which blade software component is affected, though no other issue has been observed.
bugs.workaround: 1. Reboot the affected blade. 2. Disable then re-enable the affected partition.
bugs.fix: The affected blade software component can now detect the connection issue and will re-establish the connection to the system controller's database.

bugs.title: System allows creation of duplicate VLAN names
bugs.symptoms: The /vlans/vlan/config/name value is a free format string and allows duplicate names to be created.
bugs.conditions: Creating a VLAN using a name that already exists (encountered at the /vlans/vlan/config/name endpoint).
bugs.impact: Duplicate VLANs are created without error. Which VLAN the system uses is not predictable.
bugs.workaround: Ensure VLAN names are unique.
bugs.fix: VLAN names now have the following constraints: - May start with an alphabetic character (Aa-Zz). - Cannot exceed 56 characters in length. - May contain alpha-numeric characters, periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_). - Must be unique among VLANs. !Important! Before upgrading: -- Ensure that all VLAN names meet these constraints. -- Update any scripts that create VLANs whose names violate these constraints.
bugs.behavior: VLAN names now have the following constraints: - May start with an alphabetic character (Aa-Zz). - Cannot exceed 56 characters in length. - May contain alpha-numeric characters, periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_). - Must be unique among VLANs. Important upgrade information: Before upgrading: -- Ensure that all VLAN names meet these constraints. -- Update any scripts that create VLANs whose names violate these constraints. -- Configurations from previous versions containing /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will fail to load after upgrade. -- Configuration scripts with /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will fail after upgrade.

bugs.title: VLAN name validation changes
bugs.symptoms: Previously, the /vlans/vlan/config/name was a free-format string. Now, the name has the following constraints: -- May start with just a letter -- Cannot exceed 56 characters in length -- May contain alpha characters, numbers from 0 through 9, period (.), hyphen (-), and underscore (_) -- Must be unique among VLAN names
bugs.conditions: When you configure /vlans/vlan/config/name leaf, which is an optional leaf.
bugs.impact: Previous configuration with /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will not load. Previous configuration scripts with /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will fail.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading (ideally) or after upgrading and before saving the configuration or exercising scripts, adjust all /vlans/vlan/config/names so they meet the validation requirements.
bugs.fix: Additional validations were added to VLAN names. You must adjust existing configuration's /vlans/vlan/config/name strings and scripts to meet the new validation rules.
bugs.behavior: Previously, the /vlans/vlan/config/name was a free-format string. Now, the name has the following constraints: -- May start with just a letter -- Cannot exceed 56 characters in length -- May contain alpha characters, numbers from 0 through 9, period (.), hyphen (-), and underscore (_) -- Must be unique among VLAN names

bugs.title: System allows creation of VLAN names that are too long
bugs.symptoms: The /vlans/vlan/config/name value is a free format string. Creating long VLAN names can violate common naming rules.
bugs.conditions: Creating VLANs whose names are longer than 56 characters (encountered at the /vlans/vlan/config/name endpoint).
bugs.impact: The F5OS software does not prevent you from creating VLAN names that are too long, however, the BIG-IP system cannot use them. Note: When this issue is fixed, VLAN names in configurations and scripts will no longer behave as expected. Before upgrading, make sure to follow the instructions in Behavior Change to ensure your upgrade succeeds.
bugs.workaround: Create shorter VLAN names.
bugs.fix: VLAN names now have the following constraints: - May start with an alphabetic character (Aa-Zz). - Cannot exceed 56 characters in length. - May contain alpha-numeric characters, periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_). - Must be unique among VLANs. !Important! Before upgrading: -- Ensure that all VLAN names meet these constraints. -- Update any scripts that create VLANs whose names violate these constraints.
bugs.behavior: VLAN names now have the following constraints: - May start with an alphabetic character (Aa-Zz). - Cannot exceed 56 characters in length. - May contain alpha-numeric characters, periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_). - Must be unique among VLANs. Important upgrade information: Before upgrading: -- Ensure that all VLAN names meet these constraints. -- Update any scripts that create VLANs whose names violate these constraints. -- Configurations from previous versions containing /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will fail to load after upgrade. -- Configuration scripts with /vlans/vlan/config/name strings that do not meet the new validation rules will fail after upgrade.

bugs.title: Live Up/Downgrade to non-patch version on Controller image with patch version produces instability.
bugs.symptoms: Under certain Controller installation/upgrade conditions, a live upgrade of Controller Platform Services produces transient instability in running container versions after rebooting the affected Controller. This instability is fixed automatically within several minutes of controller reboot, but can have negative side effects.
bugs.conditions: 1. A Controller was imaged using a 'patch version' ISO (Ex. 1.1.1, 1.1.2). 2. The Controller Platform Services are live up/downgraded to a 'non-patch' version of controller services (Ex. 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0). 3. The Controller is subsequently rebooted, either automatically or by the user.
bugs.impact: The Controller will temporarily run the wrong version of platform containers after rebooting (it will run the container versions defined in the 'patch' version of services plus the container versions defined in the 'non-patch' version). If the patch version of services includes changes to the ConfD container, this can result in ConfD database corruption/instability.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue with Controller live upgrade instability affecting systems that were initially imaged with particular versions of Controller SW.

bugs.title: On system controller failover, tenant mgmt IP's may be unreachable for several minutes.
bugs.symptoms: During a system controller failover, tenant management IP's may be unreachable for several minutes. Once the ARP entry for the tenants IP times out in the upstream router, it will be re-populated with the correct MAC after the failover and begin working again.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during a system controller failover due to the ARP entries not being updated for the tenants.
bugs.impact: The tenant management IP may be unreachable for several minutes after a system controller failover. Once the upstream ARP entry has timed out, the tenant management IP will be reachable again.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, and once the upstream ARP entry has timed out, the tenant management IP will be reachable again.
bugs.fix: The tenant orchestration layer will now cause Gratuitous ARPs to be sent for the tenant management IPs when a system controller failover happens. The restores tenant management IP connectivity quickly after a system controller failover.

bugs.title: New blank blades inserted into system can wind up in a reboot loop and possibly be damaged
bugs.symptoms: Blades fresh from manufacturing do not contain an OS image. If not made part of a chassis partition with an os image defined, when inserted, they will wind up in a continuous reboot loop. There is potential that this might cause damage to blade components if allowed to continue for an extensive period of time. As systems shipped from factory include all slots in the default chassis partition and that partition is set up with a partition image already configured, this condition should only be possible when blades are added in the field, and the site has added chassis partition definitions that do not have OS images set.
bugs.conditions: Freshly-manufactured blade installed in a system slot that is not part of a chassis partition with a defined ISO image.
bugs.impact: Potential drive media damage if the reboot loop is allowed to continue for an extended period of time.
bugs.workaround: Options to mitigate: 1. Install an os image on the new blade. 2. Power down the blade using AOM until ready to load an image. The simplest method to install an os image is to be sure the installation slot is part of a chassis partition definition that includes a set os image. By default the blade will PXE boot that image.

bugs.title: Management port issues with instance names containing lacpd, lldpd, stpd, or tmstat-rsync
bugs.symptoms: The management port stops working when instance names contain any of the following: lacpd, lldpd, stpd, or tmstat-rsync.
bugs.conditions: Instances whose names include any of the following: - lacpd - lldpd - stpd - tmstat-rsync
bugs.impact: Management port no longer works.
bugs.workaround: Avoid naming instances using any of the following: - lacpd - lldpd - stpd - tmstat-rsync
bugs.fix: You can now successfully name instances using strings containing the following: - lacpd - lldpd - stpd - tmstat-rsync

bugs.title: Restoring config saved with different portgroup mode than what is running leaves interfaces without a hardware MAC address.
bugs.symptoms: Restoring configuration file saved with different portgroup mode(s) than the running configuration leaves interfaces without a hardware MAC address.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when the user does a restore of a backup file which has portgroup mode configuration different than what is currently running on the box.
bugs.impact: The lack of hw-mac-address per interface impacts the overall functionality of L2 protocols (e.g. LACP members cannot become operationally UP because LACP BPDUs exchange require port hw-mac-address).
bugs.workaround: On a chassis after backup/restore with different portgroup modes, follow the steps to address the issue: - change the portgroup modes of the impacted blades to default MODE_100GB - commit and allow blade(s) to reboot - verify the blade ports are now matching the 100GB mode - restore the portgroup mode of the impacted blades to desired mode (matching what is in the backup file) - commit and allow blade(s) to reboot - verify the ports are published to match the desired mode and the state contains hw-mac-address (issue command: show interfaces interface ethernet state hw-mac-address) - reapply the configuration that references the interfaces (e.g. add back interface members into the LACP LAG)
bugs.fix: Restoring configuration files now works when the restored configuration has different portgroup modes.

bugs.title: Restoring from a chassis partition backup restores out-of-date tables
bugs.symptoms: When running "system database config-restore" on the chassis partition CLI, the fdb and vlan-listeners tables are erroneously restored. These tables can contain stale data that interferes with datapath configuration.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when running "system database config-restore" on the partition CLI.
bugs.impact: The datapath to tenants may not work until the tenants are re-deployed.
bugs.workaround: Delete the fdb and vlan-listeners tables immediately after restoring the configuration. Follow this procedure: 1. system database reset-to-default proceed yes 2. system database config-restore name <backup_filename> 3. no fdb ; no vlan-listeners ; commit
bugs.fix: Deleting the "fdb" and "vlan-listeners" tables is no longer necessary after running system database config-restore" on the chassis partition CLI.

bugs.title: Unable to delete the tenant images.
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to delete the tenant images using the CLI.
bugs.conditions: When an image is downloaded using "file import ..." CLI and then trying to delete the same image using "images remove .. " CLI, the removal fails and throws an error.
bugs.impact: The partition disk volume fills up and may cause the system to behave in an unexpected way.
bugs.fix: Images are given correct permission so that the delete is possible.

bugs.title: After a system controller reboot, the tenant operational status is set to a failed state in confd even though tenant stays running.
bugs.symptoms: After the active system controller reboots, the state of the tenant in the 'show tenants' confd output displays a failed state even though the tenant remained in the running state.
bugs.conditions: -- The active system controller has been recently rebooted. -- The Openshift API server has not yet come online.
bugs.impact: You will see an incorrect tenant state of failed when the actual tenant state is running.
bugs.workaround: The tenant status will be updated correctly once the openshift API server is back online. This could take up to 5 minutes.
bugs.fix: During the system controller reboot when the Openshift API server is offline, the state of the tenant is no longer updated to a failed state since the tenant is still in a running state.

bugs.title: Tcpdump captures to a file include FILEINFO with incorrect information.
bugs.symptoms: When tcpdump captures are done to a file, the pcap file includes FILEINFO which has version, platform and other such information but the information is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: Tcpdump capture to a file (-w optin) is performed
bugs.impact: Correct information about version and platform cannot be obtained from captured file
bugs.fix: FILEINFO will have correct version, platform and other information

bugs.title: L2 Listener entries are not created for tenants sharing the same VLAN
bugs.symptoms: After creating two tenants that share a VLAN, the L2 Listener entries for these tenants were not created. This results in all tenant traffic matching the RBCAST-LISTENER vlan-listener where it is handled by the Software Rebroadcaster.
bugs.conditions: STEPS TO REPRODUCE: - Here used the default partition - Create a vlan default-2(config)# vlans vlan range 1155 config name lab-vlan - Assign vlan to an interface default-2(config)# interfaces interface 1/1.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans 1155 - Create two tenants that share vlan 1155. default-2(config)# tenants tenant foo-tenant config image BIGIP-14.1.4.3-0.0.8.ALL-VELOS.qcow2.zip.bundle cryptos enabled nodes 1 mgmt-ip 10.10.10.1 prefix-length 24 gateway 10.10.10.254 running-state deployed vlans 1155 default-2(config-tenant-foo-tenant)# default-2(config)# tenants tenant bar-tenant config image BIGIP-14.1.4.3-0.0.8.ALL-VELOS.qcow2.zip.bundle cryptos enabled nodes 1 mgmt-ip 10.10.10.2 prefix-length 24 gateway 10.10.10.254 running-state deployed vlans 1155 default-2(config-tenant-bar-tenant)# commit - Run "show fdb" to see if L2 listener entries were created for the tenants.
bugs.impact: This issue results in all tenant traffic matching the RBCAST-LISTENER vlan-listener where it is handled by the Software Rebroadcaster.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where L2 Listener entries were not created after creating two tenants that share a VLAN.

bugs.title: iHealth related show commands fail when run individually or as part of "show system."
bugs.symptoms: Either when " show system" runs, or when individually run as in "show system diagnostics ihealth state username", these commands fail with ""error-tag": "malformed-message". /var/confd/log/devel.log will show error messages as follows: devel-c get_elem error {external_timeout, ""}
bugs.conditions: show system" command is run , or when individually ihealth show commands are run as in "show system diagnostics ihealth state username
bugs.impact: Show commands will fail
bugs.fix: " show system" command and ihealth show commands such as "show system diagnostics ihealth state username" will succeed

bugs.title: Observing genError when SNMPWalk performed after removing blade from the partition.
bugs.symptoms: After removing blade from partition, snmpwalk fails
bugs.conditions: 1. Remove blade from partition 2. After removing blade, perform snmpwalk for same partition
bugs.impact: An error occurs while running snmpwalk on the partition.
bugs.fix: Updated attribute's range in snmp platform-stats mib.

bugs.title: The partition storage is limited.
bugs.symptoms: Tcpdump or qkview dump fails due to lack of volume free space.
bugs.conditions: When tcpdump log is too big or qkview is captured multiple times, it can run out of partition volume space.
bugs.impact: Partition will will unstable.
bugs.workaround: -- Limit tcpdump logging. -- Don't capture qkview multiple times before removing old ones.
bugs.fix: Increase partition volume size.

bugs.title: Partition high availability (HA) framework can fail to report 'failed' state if the node crashes immediately when becoming 'active'
bugs.symptoms: The system controller "show partitions partition" status output shows both controller 1 and controller 2 as "running-active". The partition "show system redundancy" also reports incorrect active/active status.
bugs.conditions: Normally, the partition instance runs on both system controllers in an Active/Standby configuration. If the Active yields or fails, the Standby will become Active. If the partition instance crashes immediately after reporting Active status, it does not update the status reported to the system controller software, so will appear to be active. The other partition instance will detect the crash, and reclaim the active role if possible. The observed instance of this problem occurred when the partition volume ran out of space due to an large number of qkviews and tcpdumps.
bugs.impact: The system controller and partition CLI/GUI will display both partition instances as "active", even though only one of them is.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the crash, limit the number of partition qkviews stored on the partition. Once taken, the qkview should be promptly copied to another system and deleted before taking another.
bugs.fix: The partition high availability (HA) framework no correctly updates status to when a database crash is detected, and now shows a "failed" when the database is inoperable.

bugs.title: Media type of optics with part number OPT-0047 reports as unknown.
bugs.symptoms: Optics media types is displayed as unknown
bugs.conditions: Optics with part number OPT-0047 is present in the system
bugs.impact: Media type will not be known
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Media type should be reported as 100G PAM4 BiDi

bugs.title: Adding a VLAN to a LAG that is already configured on a tenant may not configure the VLAN correctly.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic egressing the VELOS system does not reach the external destination.
bugs.conditions: A VLAN is configured on a tenant and the VLAN is added to a LAG which does not have members from all blades in the partition.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Remove VLANs from the tenant, then add them to the lag, then re-add them to the tenant.
bugs.fix: When a VLAN is added to a LAG, program the host VLAN table for blades that do not contain LAG members.

bugs.title: Tcpdump capture file can fill the /var/F5/partition.
bugs.symptoms: Tcpdump capture files are located at /var/F5/partition. As captures grow in size, these may use up all the space on /var/F5/partition, starving other components that want to use this storage.
bugs.conditions: Tcpdump has to be started with a capture to file ( "-w") option
bugs.impact: /var/F5/partition may run out of space, and other components that need space might error
bugs.fix: This fix does the following: - If started with the "-w" option, the pcap file size is limited to: available space in /var/F5/partition - 2GB - If there is less than 2GB, tcpdump will throw an error ("ERROR: Only ... 1K blocks available in /var/F5/partition. Need atleast ... 1K blocks of free space.") and not start the tcpdump session - If there is less than 100MB, tcpdump will print a "WARNING__Capture_file_size_will_be_limited_to_97216_1K_blocks)" - If the space is less than 1 MB, tcpdump will fail. Explicit -C option can be used to override

bugs.title: Both system controllers may report as active.
bugs.symptoms: Vcc-ConfD may hang, causing a watchdog timer to expire. This causes both controllers to appear as 'active.'
bugs.conditions: It is unknown which conditions trigger this.
bugs.impact: When it occurs, the system is degraded. System upgrades will fail, other management operations may fail, and traffic could be disrupted.
bugs.fix: Vcc-ConfD should no longer hang and let the watchdog timer expire.

bugs.title: Link aggregation names with spaces
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Next exhibits erroneous behavior for a LAG when it is created with a name that contains spaces.
bugs.conditions: The LAG name contains spaces.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP Next cannot successfully handle a LAG with spaces in the name. The LAG is not recognized.
bugs.workaround: Refrain from using names with spaces. &start; This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Networks Technical Support web site: http://www.f5.com/support/ The AskF5 web site: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/home The F5 DevCentral web site: http://devcentral.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Thu May 5 16:29:51 2022 PDT Copyright F5 Networks (2022) - All Rights Reserved Contact Support

bugs.symptoms: A confusing and misleading status and error message is displayed within the 'show tenants' command when the partition services are not fully functional: "Resource allocation failed - Verify node is synchronized with the partition" "Tenant deployment will be processed when the blade synchronized with partition"
bugs.conditions: This is encountered with the CLI command 'show tenants' when the partition services are not fully operational on the blade.
