bugs.title: Colon character is not allowed in the password.
bugs.symptoms: Password change fails when the password has colon character
bugs.conditions: Colon character in the password
bugs.impact: Password change fails.
bugs.fix: Handle colon in the password properly

bugs.title: The upgrade fails when there are many partitions.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails with an error syscon-2-active(config)# system image check-version iso-version 1.2.0-8089 Error: Compatibility verification failed.
bugs.conditions: 8 or so partitions
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails
bugs.workaround: $ echo 256 > /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances
bugs.fix: Increase inotify tunable.

bugs.title: ConfD Encryption key gets rewritten intermittently
bugs.symptoms: The key should always return the same value and hash, unless it is changed via key-migration. The reading of memory (EEPROM) will sometimes return "resource temporarily unavailable," which is treated as an error instead of simply doing a retry.
bugs.conditions: The EEPROM might be busy because of use by other components.
bugs.impact: The encryption key changes, thus invalidating all currently-encrypted items, thus requiring re-entry of these.
bugs.workaround: Re-enter all encrypted items and hope that the "resource temporarily unavailable" does not occur.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where the system no longer considers "resource temporarily unavailable" as an error unless it happens ten times in a row. The system does a retry and if that works, the system avoids setting a new key.

bugs.title: Confusing message displays when running "file delete"
bugs.symptoms: When running the "file delete" command, a confusing error message displays: syscon-1-active# file delete file-name log/host/ansible.log Only /mnt/var/confd/configs/ /var/shared/ configs/ diags/shared/ paths are allowed for Delete file operation on system controller CLI.
bugs.conditions: When attempting a file delete operation from a directory that does not have delete permission.
bugs.impact: The error message lists the actual paths along with the virtual paths on which delete is supported.
bugs.fix: When performing a file delete operation, only virtual paths are now listed.

bugs.title: Chassis partition 'show interfaces' command can be slow
bugs.symptoms: A 'show interfaces' command or the corresponding RESTCONF API request that includes 'show interfaces interface state counters' or 'show interfaces interface ethernet state counters' might take a long time to execute.
bugs.conditions: When a blade was present in the chassis partition, but is either physically removed or powered off, but the slot is not removed from the partition configuration. When running 'show interfaces interface state counters' command for an aggregate (trunk), a delay will also be observed.
bugs.impact: The webUI screen refresh is slow (2 to 8 seconds per missing blade), or the CLI 'show' command takes a long time to return.
bugs.workaround: Use the system controller webUI or CLI to remove the non-existent blade from the chassis partition.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing the "show interfaces" command to be slow when a blade is removed.

bugs.title: webUI is affected due to /api/data/f5-cluster:cluster/nodes/node taking more than 25 seconds to complete
bugs.symptoms: The 'show cluster nodes node' command takes more than 25 seconds to complete.
bugs.conditions: This happens on a chassis that is not fully populated.
bugs.impact: The get api /api/data/f5-cluster:cluster/ takes more time, resulting in slow page load times in the webUI.
bugs.fix: Modified diag-agent partition to check that the blade is in a ready status before contacting it for disk-usage information. This reduces the timeout.

bugs.title: When a large number of VLANs are configured, a blade might run out of memory
bugs.symptoms: When a large number of VLANs are configured, the system might run out of memory. The api_svc_gateway service's memory usage might grow without bounds.
bugs.conditions: A large number of VLANs are configured.
bugs.impact: System might become slow and go down.
bugs.fix: Fixed unbounded memory usage by api_svc_gateway.

bugs.title: QKView reports status of "partial file recorded" when out of disk space
bugs.symptoms: When QKView attempts to create a QKView file and there is insufficient disk space, the status recorded is "partial file recorded". The actual cause is low disk space, and no QKView is collected in this case. The recorded status should indicate so.
bugs.conditions: Run the QKView collection with less than 1 GB of available disk.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic.
bugs.fix: The status now indicates: Out-of-disk. Unable to create QKView file.

bugs.title: When using IPv6 on floating management address and DHCP, it is possible to get different IP addresses on failover
bugs.symptoms: When running IPv6 and using DHCP to assign the floating management address, a chassis failover event might cause the IP address to be changed.
bugs.conditions: Running IPv6, using DHCP for floating management address and failing over a system controller. IPv4 and static IPv6 addresses are unaffected.
bugs.impact: Services will not be available on the floating management address as expected, and the interface will map to an unexpected IPv6 address.

bugs.title: Key-migrationd service might crash if server elements are incomplete
bugs.symptoms: The key-migrationd service crashes after defining some server-group information for Radius/LDAP servers.
bugs.conditions: This might occur after not fully defining system > aaa > server-groups >server-group item, and then attempting to read the item.
bugs.impact: Core file is created and key-migration malfunctions.
bugs.workaround: Remove the partially-defined server group or fully define all server-group items.
bugs.fix: The key-migration now works without crashing.

bugs.title: Missing controller images in show image controller CLI operation
bugs.symptoms: After a software upgrade, the images displayed when running the "show image controller" command shows only active system controller images. The standby controller images are missing in "show image controller" CLI command. This is very occasional and won't happen always.
bugs.conditions: Using CLI/RESTCONF command operations for show image controller
bugs.impact: User won't see the standby controller images when running the "show image controller" command.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the standby controller from the CLI using the "system reboot controllers controller standby" command. This resolves the issue and brings the controller images back into the CLI display.

bugs.title: Source address for TACACS+ server group configuration does not work
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to set the source-address for a TACACS+ server group configuration might fail or does not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to configure source-address for TACACS+ server group.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, as the source-address isn't used.
bugs.workaround: The source-address is not used by the TACACS+ client. Do not configure source-address.

bugs.title: Some of the PCie AER severity and types are incorrect in the diagnostic monitoring
bugs.symptoms: Some AER (Advanced Error Reporting) error type and severity events are displayed incorrectly in the diagnostics monitoring.
bugs.conditions: If an AER error occurs, the decoding of the error type and severity as reported in the diagnostic might be incorrect.
bugs.impact: AER errors in diagnostic monitoring could be interpreted incorrectly as a 'Fatal' error.
bugs.workaround: As there is not a complete mitigation for this, the AER errors are correctly logged in the system logs and can be confirmed by timestamp and device to obtain the correct information
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with incorrect diagnostics reporting.

bugs.title: Vcc-lacpd on a system controller can crash and leave a core file while restarting
bugs.symptoms: Vcc-lacpd on a system controller crashes, leaving behind a core file and a system log indicating a crash occurred. After the crash, the daemon recovers within a few seconds.
bugs.conditions: The crash only occurs during a restart of vcc-lacpd. Most commonly, a restart will occur during a system controller software update, using the "go-standby" command, or from a fatal error.
bugs.impact: The internal mgmt network to all blades may go down for a few seconds. Traffic running on tenants will be unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Limit failover scenarios on the system controllers, such as use of the system controller "go-standby" command or system controller software updates.
bugs.fix: Vcc-lacpd no longer leaves a core file under these conditions.

bugs.title: Switch daemon crashes occasionally on shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Shutting down the system sometimes causes the switch daemon to crash.
bugs.conditions: This occurs rarely during system shutdown.
bugs.impact: A core file is saved to /var/shared/core/container/.
bugs.fix: This has been fixed in F5OS-C 1.2.2 and F5OS-C 1.3.

bugs.title: Chassis partition merged stats only reflect one blade when tmstat-rsync service moves to another blade
bugs.symptoms: A few show stats commands such as 'show qos state' that report stats for all blades in a chassis partition might report only the stats from a single blade when the tmstat-rsync service moves from one blade to another blade.
bugs.conditions: The tmstat-rsync service has moved to a blade other than the initial blade it was running on, and a show command that combines stats from all the blades in a chassis partition is run.
bugs.impact: A few show stats commands will only report data from a single blade.
bugs.workaround: Restart the tmstat-rsync service so it runs back on the initial blade.

bugs.title: Last-change value does not display date of password change.
bugs.symptoms: Last-change value is shown as days since 1970-01-01, which will reflect something like: 18970, it should be in date format, like: 2021-12-09,while running confd cmd: "show system aaa authentication users user".
bugs.conditions: When running confd cmd: "show system aaa authentication users user"
bugs.impact: Last-change value for users is displayed in unreadable format (number of days since Jan 1, 1970). CLI command to check users information: "show system aaa authentication users"
bugs.workaround: None ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Technical Support website: http://www.f5.com/support/ The MyF5 website: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/ The F5 DevCentral website: http://community.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Wed Aug 26 05:10:48 2026 UTC ©2026 F5, Inc. bugs.title: Chassis partition config restore operation might cause the system to stop processing FDB files
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, a chassis partition "config-restore" operation might cause a race condition that locks up a platform component. This causes forwarding database (FDB) files to no longer be processed and can affect traffic processing.
bugs.conditions: Running a "config-restore" operation on the chassis partition CLI. This issue is more likely to occur when the number of tenants increases.
bugs.impact: FDB files will no longer be processed. Traffic processing can be impacted due to missing FDBs.
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart the network manager on both system controllers: - "docker restart partition<partition_number>_network_manager" 2. Redeploy all tenants.

bugs.title: The system image displays data for only one VELOS controller
bugs.symptoms: The 'show system image' command displays image details for only one VELOS controller, even though there is more than one.
bugs.conditions: Running the 'show system image' command after uploading VELOS software.
bugs.impact: No image information is displayed for a VELOS controller on the user interface.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the VELOS controllers (specifically vcc-partition-software-manager container).
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Permissions of some QKView control files do not follow standards
bugs.symptoms: Permissions of some QKView control files do not follow standards.
bugs.conditions: Viewing permissions of QKView files.
bugs.impact: Some do not follow standards.
bugs.fix: Permissions of all QKView control files now follow the standards.

bugs.title: Tcpdump capture might not include broadcast and multicast egress (generated by the system and being sent out) when "--dls true" option is used
bugs.symptoms: When DLS feature is enabled using the "--dls true" option, broadcast and multicast packets generated by the host CPUs of the system and egressing out of the VELOS system will not be part of the capture. The default mode when no "--dls" option is specified is "--dls false", which functions correctly.
bugs.conditions: The 'DLS' feature of tcpdump is enabled by explicitly invoking packet capture with the non-default mode "--dls true".
bugs.impact: Capture will not be complete and will not contain the egressing broadcast and multicast packets.
bugs.workaround: Use the default mode (no "--dls" option specified) or explicitly turn off dls mode ("--dls false").

bugs.title: QOS and Software install status screens missing online help
bugs.symptoms: The QOS and Software Install webUI screens should have online help, but they do not.
bugs.conditions: This is specific to the QOS and Software Install screens in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Online help is missing for these screens.
bugs.fix: Help screens are available starting in F5OS-C 1.2.1.

bugs.title: System controller upgrade from F5OS-C 1.2.0-10357 to 1.2.1-10301 intermittently fails&start;
bugs.symptoms: The upgrade proceeds to the point where both system controllers boot to the new image, but neither system controller becomes active.
bugs.conditions: When this issue is observed, the output of the "show full-configuration system redundancy config mode" command is something other than the default (auto).
bugs.impact: Neither system controller becomes active, and the ability to configure the system controllers is compromised.
bugs.workaround: Restarting both Vcc-ConfD containers (or a reboot of both system controllers) should clear the problem.
bugs.fix: Intermittent loss of active system controller when upgrading from F5OS-C 1.2.0-10357 to 1.2.1-10301 is now fixed in F5OS-C 1.2.1.

bugs.title: ETCD-HA Instance might not initialize correctly after PXE booting the system controller
bugs.symptoms: The ETCD-HA instance might not initialize correctly after PXE booting a system controller and re-installing that system controller into the OpenShift cluster. When the instance initializes incorrectly and one of the system controllers is down, the OpenShift API does not operate correctly.
bugs.conditions: PXE boot of a system controller in a running OpenShift cluster.
bugs.impact: When the instance initializes incorrectly and one of the system controllers is down, the OpenShift API does not operate correctly.
bugs.fix: The orchestration-manager now correctly re-initializes the ETCD-HA instance when a system controller is PXE booted and then added to the OpenShift cluster.

bugs.title: Configuring spanning tree protocol (STP) while disabled might display incorrect state
bugs.symptoms: While STP is disabled, configuring a field such as MSTP max-hop causes the the enabled-protocol to display an incorrect value.
bugs.conditions: Delete the enabled-protocol configuration field. Delete another STP configuration field such as MSTP max-hop
bugs.impact: The STP enabled-protocol display is incorrect.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate, do not configure STP while it is not enabled.
bugs.fix: Configuring STP while it is disabled will no longer lead to an incorrect display.

bugs.title: Unable to remove platform services versions that appear unused
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, a version of controller or partition services might appear "not in use" in CLI/webUI tables, but removal of that version is still blocked because other parts of the service package are still in use by other system components.
bugs.conditions: 1. Attempt to remove an (apparently CLI) version of controller or partition services via ConfD or webUI. 2. Other components on the system still silently depend on that version of services, even though CLI/webUI output does not reflect this.
bugs.impact: Unable to remove versions of software that appear unused, and the cause is unclear.
bugs.fix: Removal of platform services that appear "unused" is no longer blocked by hidden higher-level component dependencies.

bugs.title: Allow configurable partition hostname
bugs.symptoms: The partition name is set by the chassis administrator at creation time and cannot be changed. Every chassis starts with a partition named "default", so it can be difficult to determine what partition the user is connected to.
bugs.conditions: Users who have multiple partitions on multiple chassis, and need to easily tell them apart.
bugs.impact: User confusion, possible unintended configuration changes when connected to the wrong partition.
bugs.workaround: Create all partitions with unique names, and remove/do not use the "default" partition.
bugs.fix: The partition now has a configurable hostname under /system/config/hostname. This hostname accepts either a simple label or a fully qualified domain name, following DNS name rules. The first label is used in the partition prompt in preference to the partition name. The partition hostname can be set by the chassis administrator, or by partition administrator if not configured at the chassis level.
bugs.behavior: Partition hostname can now be configured, and is used in the partition CLI prompt if present.

bugs.title: Inconsistencies in disk threshold limits.&start;
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistencies are being observed while configuring disk threshold limits. default-2# show cluster disk-usage-threshold state cluster disk-usage-threshold state warning-limit 85 cluster disk-usage-threshold state error-limit 90 cluster disk-usage-threshold state critical-limit 97 cluster disk-usage-threshold state growth-rate-limit 10 cluster disk-usage-threshold state interval 60 No checks are implemented to raise an exception if you attempt to set a critical limit to a value less than error/warning limit.
bugs.conditions: The problem is seen only while upgrading to F5OS-C 1.3.0 and when you configure the disk threshold limits against the constraints.
bugs.impact: Upgrade can fail if the constraints introduced in F5OS-C version 1.3.0 are violated.
bugs.workaround: Configure the critical limit > error and warning limit error limit > warning limit or set to default values before upgrading to F5OS-C 1.3.0. From the chassis partition CLI: ------------------------- default-2(config)# cluster disk-usage-threshold config critical-limit 90 default-2(config)# cluster disk-usage-threshold config error-limit 85 default-2(config)# cluster disk-usage-threshold config warning-limit 80 default-2(config)# commit Commit complete.

bugs.title: KubeVirt pods are not reinstalled after recovering cluster using internal debug setting&start;
bugs.symptoms: While reinstalling the OpenShift cluster by configuring an internal debug flag, the KubeVirt pods were not reinstalled. Without these pods, the tenant will not operate.
bugs.conditions: When a cluster reinstall was initiated by configuring the internal debug flag, an internal variable was not being reset which prevented the KubeVirt pods to be installed.
bugs.impact: The tenant will not operate.
bugs.workaround: In a bash console shell, run this command: systemctl restart orchestration_manager_container.service
bugs.fix: Fix is in release F5OS-C v1.2.2.

bugs.title: On initial installation, blades fail to PXE boot after chassis startup
bugs.symptoms: On initial installation, blades fail to PXE boot after the chassis powers on. Other symptoms: 1. When trying to deploy a tenant on a single blade or when multiple blades are bundled for the same chassis partition in the Chassis Partition webUI (TENANT MANAGEMENT > Tenant Deployments), the "Running Version" remains "Unavailable" indefinitely. 2. Blades are not available for login or other activity from the CLI.
bugs.conditions: Multiple factory-fresh blades are powered up.
bugs.impact: Blades fail to PXE boot. This means they failed to load an initial image and cannot join a cluster.
bugs.workaround: On both system controllers, reboot the system controller or restart the image server container. Type this command to restart the image server on each system controller: docker restart vcc-image-server

bugs.title: Removal of old chassis partition images might cause tenant issues after blade reboot&start;
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading the system to F5OS-C version 1.1.4, when you remove old chassis partition images from the system, tenants might not start up correctly after a reboot of the blade hosting the chassis partition.
bugs.conditions: This might occur if the tenant was started after the system was upgraded to an interim release (such as F5OS-C 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3), after originally running F5OS-C version 1.1.0.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start correctly, will not pass traffic, or be accessible on their management interfaces.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Upgrade the system controller to F5OS-C1.1.4. 2. Wait for the system controller upgrade to complete. 3. Upgrade the chassis partition(s) to F5OS-C 1.1.4. 4. Wait for chassis partition upgrade(s) to complete. 5. Configure all tenants to return to the "Provisioned" state. 6. Wait for all tenants to stop. 7. Configure all tenants back to the "Deployed" state. 8. Remove the old chassis partition and system controller software versions.

bugs.title: dagd core
bugs.symptoms: Dagd crashes and leaves a core file.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions, especially from a user point of view, are not yet known.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while dagd restarts.
bugs.fix: Made dagd more robust against system conditions.

bugs.title: Under certain circumstances, platform services are not marked as "in use" when they should be.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to a minor release, you are unable to delete the older release from the image list.
bugs.conditions: -- A "patch" version of platform services (one with a non-zero third version element, such as 1.1.4, 1.2.1, 1.2.2) is enabled for active use with either a partition or controller. -- You attempt to delete the base version, e.g 1.2.0.
bugs.impact: You are unable to delete the base version from the images list because the base version is still in use, but it is incorrectly marked as not in use.

bugs.title: Output from the image removal command is confusing and reveals extraneous details
bugs.symptoms: When running commands such as "image <controller|partition> remove iso <version>", the error output contains the following message, among other details: "Error: unexpected response back from API: 1"
bugs.conditions: The output occurs after you run a command to remove system controller or chassis partition images that are in use. A typical example is when you are trying to remove an ISO that uses OS/service artifacts.
bugs.impact: The error message from these commands is unhelpful to the user and reveals internal implementation details.
bugs.fix: The fix is present in F5OS-C version 1.2.2. The error message is replaced by one of the following (or another more helpful message if more specific information is available): "Error: failed to remove controller image; may be in use" "Error: failed to remove partition image; may be in use"

bugs.title: openssl: Read buffer overruns processing ASN.1 strings
Stale interfaces are left behind upon portgroup mode change from 100GB to 40GB
bugs.symptoms: In some situations, stale interfaces are left behind in the config cdb when the portgroup mode changes from 100GB to 40GB, 4x25GB, or 4x10GB. This causes the l2-agent on the blade to exit.
bugs.conditions: -- reset-to-defaults/backup/restore OR -- live install -- change the portgroup mode from 100GB to 40GB -- commit
bugs.impact: The interfaces corresponding to portgroups are not present and stale interfaces are left behind.
bugs.workaround: Steps for mitigation: 1) Verify the issue is caused by the lack of pgindex in cdb: a) From config mode in a chassis partition, create a backup file (config)# system database config-backup name test b) Look for pgindex in the /var/F5/partition{id}/configs/test: grep pgindex /var/F5/partition{number}/configs/test c) If no entries are found, this is the issue. 2) Remove the slots corresponding to the impacted chassis partition from the system controller configuration and commit. 3) Re-add the slots corresponding to the impacted chassis partition from the system controller configuration and commit. 4) From the chassis partition CLI, ensure the system redundancy shows the blade is present and operational 5) from the chassis partition CLI, change the portgroup mode from 100GB to 40GB and commit (example below): (config)# portgroups portgroup 1/1 config mode MODE_40GB; top (config)# portgroups portgroup 1/2 config mode MODE_40GB; top (config)# commit 6) Wait for the blades to resync by monitoring 'show system redundancy'. At this point the interfaces should be republished matching the new 40GB mode.
bugs.fix: Proper interfaces are now published when portgroup mode is changed.

bugs.title: Errors related to LCD module show up in logs.
bugs.symptoms: The system controller log file can contain errors related to failed communication with the LCD module. controller-2 platform-monitor[1]: priority="Err" msg="Action Error" name="LCD Sensor Monitor" inputId="1f156c2b-0db1-11ec-bdd4-024264410634" index=0 message="unable to get LCD sensor info" interface="zmq-input"
bugs.conditions: The error message shows up when the LCD module is restarting due to initial system startup or a firmware update.
bugs.impact: The error message is not system critical and can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: Vcc-partition-software-manager logs extraneous chassis partition update records
bugs.symptoms: Following a fresh F5OS-C software install, the vcc-partition-software-manager repeatedly logs the following extraneous records: ******** <info> Dec 2 21:46:48 publish_image_thread: Controller-2 Images state not changed. <notice> Dec 2 21:48:25 main: retrying after failed operation <info> Dec 2 21:48:25 main: configuration updated; num_part: 2 <notice> Dec 2 21:48:26 main: cc.out_of_service_install(false) cc.install_stage(IDLE) ha_mode(HA_MASTER) skip_notify(true) last_failed(true) ********
bugs.conditions: Installing F5OS-C software.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, as the chassis partition configurations are not actually being changed or updated, but the lof records fill up the velos.log over time with unnecessary noise.
bugs.workaround: These messages can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: Database import fails after database reset
bugs.symptoms: An attempt to import database using "file import" in the confd/config folder fails. During a database reset operation, the config folder is deleted, which causes an import to fail
bugs.conditions: When a database reset is performed before performing an import operation.
bugs.impact: Database import fails.
bugs.fix: File import operation now creates configs folder, if missing.

bugs.title: SM2 cannot be used for creating self-signed certificates in system aaa tls
bugs.symptoms: The create self-signed certificate function allows for elliptic curves but does not work for 'SM2'.
bugs.conditions: When requesting a certificate using type ec, the curve name SM2 can be selected.
bugs.impact: Attempting to use SM2 curve name will result in an error.
bugs.workaround: Outside confd you can create the SM2 key using: /usr/bin/openssl ecparam -genkey -name SM2 The key can then be entered using system-aaa-tls-config-key and subsequently used to create a CSR. The self-signed certificate would need to be done using openssl commands and entered manually if to be stored.

bugs.title: Tenant Data path will not work correctly on downgrade to controller version 1.1.x&start;
bugs.symptoms: After a system controller downgrade to version 1.1.x, the tenant datapath will not operate correctly.
bugs.conditions: The KubeVirt software version does not downgrade to the correct KubeVirt software version needed in the 1.1.x controller release.
bugs.impact: The tenant will launch correctly, but the datapath will be broken because of a dma-agent protocol mismatch.
bugs.workaround: 1. In one root command shell window, run this command to delete the current version of KubeVirt software pods. [root@controller-2 ~]# oc delete -f /tmp/omd/scripts/kubevirt-velos.yaml 2. In another root command shell window, run this command to clear the KubeVirt namespace and install the new version of KubeVirt pods. [root@controller-2 kubevirt]# /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/omd-kubevirt-velos-install.sh /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/
bugs.fix: The tenant datapath should now work properly after a downgrade.

bugs.title: Partition_tmstat_merged container core on shutdown
bugs.symptoms: When the partition_tmstat_merged container is shutting down and it receives a message from the same container on another blade in the partition, it might crash with a core.
bugs.conditions: Container is shutting down and also receives a message from another blade.
bugs.impact: Crashes with a core file, with no other impact. You can safely ignore and remove the core file.
bugs.workaround: Remove core file.
bugs.fix: Race condition on shutdown fixed so that if message is received on shutdown, it is handled properly.

bugs.title: Sw_rbcast core file found on system
bugs.symptoms: Partition_sw_rbcast producing core.
bugs.conditions: Starting a tenant which requires the sw_rbcast container running in the following platforms: - r5x00 - r10x00 - VELOS
bugs.impact: The sw_rbcast process crashes and produces a core file.
bugs.fix: A new version of sw_rbcast correctly handles tenant broadcast packets.

bugs.title: F5OS: Some members in LACP trunks may not stand up
bugs.symptoms: When configuring an LACP trunk (aggregate link), if the trunk has interfaces on multiple blades, some members of the trunk may not join the trunk, and the peer layer-2 switch may produce warnings stating that the LACP members are not all on the same remote device. In addition, after enabling debug logging for the lacpd daemon, messages will be seen from both blades that indicate the value of "actor_oper_key". These values should be the same for all the ports within the same LACP trunk, but in this situation, the debug output may show different values for ports on different blades.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS chassis - LACP trunk with member interfaces on multiple blades
bugs.impact: One or more ports in the LACP trunk (aggregate link) will not be able to join the trunk.
bugs.workaround: Restart the LACPD container on each blade in the affected partition. For example, if the partition consists of slots 1 and 2, log in as root to the controller, and run the following command: for i in 1 2; do ssh blade-$i docker restart lacpd ; done

bugs.title: KubeVirt pods might not be installed after upgrading from F5OS-C v1.2.1 to v1.3.0&start;
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade from F5OS-C v1.2.1 to v1.3.0 the OpenShift KubeVirt pods might not be installed.
bugs.conditions: During the upgrade from F5OS-C 1.2.1 to 1.3.0, the script that installs the OpenShift KubeVirt pods might fail to install the pods.
bugs.impact: The tenants might not operate.
bugs.workaround: On the active system controller, run this command: systemctl restart orchestration_manager_container.service

bugs.title: Disk I/O stats inaccurate in snmpwalk for chassis partition
bugs.symptoms: Disk I/O stats is inaccurate in snmpwalk.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running snmpwalk on a chassis partition.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate disk I/O stats info in snmpwalk
bugs.fix: Disk I/O stats is now accurate in snmpwalk.

bugs.title: System logs this error at startup: SDK error during device programming
bugs.symptoms: During startup of the 'fpgamgr' container, this error is logged in velos.log: "SDK error during device programming." API="f5sw_port_spn_state_get" code=-1 error="parameter error"."
bugs.conditions: System startup or fpgamgr restart.
bugs.impact: Error log message with no functional impact.
bugs.fix: Fixed API call to prevent an error.

bugs.title: LAG and interface names should not contain special characters such as whitespace, asterisk, slashes, and curly braces.
bugs.symptoms: -- LAGs (trunks) not functional in system. -- LACPD daemon in a restart loop -- The "LAGs" and "Interfaces" pages in the F5OS partition GUI fail to load and report "Something went wrong. Check the web browser console for more details or contact technical support for assistance."
bugs.conditions: -- A LAG is defined that has a space in the name. When a user creates an LAG interface that contains whitespace characters, the LACPD daemon fails to read the interface information, and keeps restarting until the interface is removed or the name is changed to a regular name.
bugs.impact: All trunks in the partition are down.
bugs.workaround: Use the the F5OS partition CLI to remove the LAG, for example: ottersPart-1(config)# no interfaces interface "test lag" ottersPart-1(config)# no interfaces interface 2/2.0 ethernet config aggregate-id ottersPart-1(config)# commit and-quit Commit complete. ottersPart-1#

bugs.title: Chassis partition ConfD cluster disk usage threshold feature not functioning as expected
bugs.symptoms: When there is an update in cluster disk usage threshold configuration, the change is not reflected in the state data. default-1(config)# cluster disk-usage-threshold config critical-limit 91 default-1(config)# commit default-1# show cluster disk-usage-threshold state critical-limit cluster disk-usage-threshold state critical-limit 97
bugs.conditions: When you connect a cluster to ConfD during a firmware update and the disk-usage-threshold is updated at the same time, updates will be missed.
bugs.impact: Some changes to the chassis partition might not be performed, or they might not be reflected in the state data.
bugs.fix: Modified the cluster disk threshold subscriber to not use a shared access object in ConfD.

bugs.title: Hardware-fault alarm not cleared.
bugs.symptoms: A hardware-fault alarm triggered by RAS unknown type errors is not cleared after the errors are resolved.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with hardware fault alarms due to RAS unknown type. The alarm is not cleared after the issue is resolved.
bugs.impact: Hardware-fault alarm with severity warning will be displayed and is not cleared.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue that prevents RAS unknown errors from being cleared from the diagnostics report.

bugs.title: Tenant may not be deployed correctly after downgrade of controller to V1.2.x
bugs.symptoms: After a controller downgrade to version 1.2.x, the tenant may not deploy correctly.
bugs.conditions: The kubevirt software version does not downgrade to the correct kubevirt software version needed in the 1.2.x controller release.
bugs.impact: The tenant may not launch correctly, and if it does the datapath will be broken because of the a dma-agent protocol mismatch.
bugs.workaround: 1. In a root command shell window, run this command: systemctl restart orchestration_manager_container.service 2. Verify that kubevirt pods are created (this can take a couple minutes) If that does not work (due to a leftover kubevirt pod) then run this procedure: 2. In a root command shell window, run this command to install the kubevirt pods [root@controller-2 kubevirt]# oc apply -f /tmp/omd/scripts/kubevirt-velos.yaml

bugs.title: Networking fails on the system controller after a power cycle.
bugs.symptoms: After power cycling the active system controller, networking could go down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when power cycling the Active system controller.
bugs.impact: Networking goes down on the system controllers.
bugs.workaround: Power cycle the active system controller again.

bugs.title: QKView list and status results are difficult to parse
bugs.symptoms: The QKView list and status commands return output that can be difficult to read. Example 1 :: running the command: system diagnostics qkview list: frodo# system diagnostics qkview list result {"Qkviews":[{"Filename":"appliance-1.qkview","Date":"2022-06-15T22:59:57.704997979Z","Size":320434703},{"Filename":"cancelme.tar.canceled","Date":"2022-04-28T17:22:10.411870757Z","Size":3734340},{"Filename":"duplicate.qkview","Date":"2022-08-10T20:40:10.966027168Z","Size":490039715},{"Filename":"test.qkview","Date":"2022-06-15T23:21:23.068041954Z","Size":321199668},{"Filename":"test2.qkview","Date":"2022-07-13T19:01:32.712663042Z","Size":416706874},{"Filename":"teststatus.qkview","Date":"2022-08-23T23:27:19.283797639Z","Size":530892644}]} resultint 0 This output is easier to parse: FILENAME SIZE CREATED ON ------------------------------------------------------------------ teststatus.qkview 530892644 2022-08-23T23:27:19.283797639Z duplicate.qkview 490039715 2022-08-10T20:40:10.966027168Z test2.qkview 416706874 2022-07-13T19:01:32.712663042Z test.qkview 321199668 2022-06-15T23:21:23.068041954Z appliance-1.qkview 320434703 2022-06-15T22:59:57.704997979Z cancelme.tar.canceled 3734340 2022-04-28T17:22:10.411870757Z Example 2 :: running the command: system diagnostics qkview status: result {"Busy":false,"Percent":100,"Status":"complete","Message":"Completed collection.","Filename":"teststatus.qkview"} resultint 0 This output is easier to parse: system diagnostics qkview state status capture-in-progress false system diagnostics qkview state status percentage 100 system diagnostics qkview state status status-msg "Completed collection." system diagnostics qkview state status filename teststatus.qkview
bugs.conditions: - Running "system diagnostics qkview list" within the CLI - Running "system diagnostics qkview status" within the CLI
bugs.impact: Formatting of output makes troubleshooting more difficult.
bugs.fix: QKView output formatting is improved and easier to read, utilizing new commands. To see a list of QKView files, use the following command within the CLI: show system diagnostics qkview state files To see the current status of a captured QKView, use the following command within the CLI: show system diagnostics qkview state status

bugs.title: Partition CLI command 'show cluster nodes node' may time out
bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'show cluster nodes node' in the chassis partition CLI may cause a time-out.
bugs.conditions: Internal problem within the CLI design can trigger this situation where the CLI command fails and times out.
bugs.impact: User is unable to access the output of this command.
bugs.fix: CLI command infrastructure was redesigned.

bugs.title: After upgrading system controller to v1.2.2, there could be traffic outage&start;
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading the system controller to version 1.2.2, a traffic outage occurs.
bugs.conditions: System controller is upgraded to version 1.2.2 and the partition is not upgraded to version 1.2.2
bugs.impact: Network traffic through BIG-IP tenants is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade the partition to version 1.2.2.

bugs.title: Tcpdump on VELOS chassis blade or rSeries appliance cores when line-dma agent layer below it fails
bugs.symptoms: Line-dma agent is the underlying layer of tcpdump in the VELOS/rSeries family of chassis and appliance products When it is not running, or if it cores or is otherwise not available and a client wants a tcpdump capture, tcpdump may core.
bugs.conditions: -- line-dma-agent is not functional at start, or at some later point in time during the tcpdump capture -- a client requests a tcpdump capture
bugs.impact: Packet capture will be affected and will not work
bugs.fix: Tcpdump does not core anymore, and will retry line-dma-agent connection when clients ask for capture

bugs.title: After a software upgrade, some blades do not show the correct software version until an extra reboot occurs.
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, some blades do not show the correct version until after an extra reboot occurs.
bugs.conditions: The conditions for reproducing this issue are not definitive, but the presence of more blades makes it more likely to occur.
bugs.impact: The exact impact is unclear, but metadata might not update correctly or the system software might not upgrade completely.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blades.

bugs.title: Vcc-ConfD may fail to start new child process
bugs.symptoms: The error message <err> Oct 13 13:41:40 vcc_install_versions_failed: Vcc-ConfD-RU: popen failed => Resource temporarily unavailable occasionally appears in the /var/log_controller/cc-confd log.
bugs.conditions: Running system controller rolling upgrade.
bugs.impact: Presently the only known impact is the message appearing in the log.
bugs.fix: Vcc-ConfD processes started by popen are properly terminated with pclose.

bugs.title: Optical transceiver tuning values for OPT-0048 updated to reduce errors
bugs.symptoms: OPT-0048 might show intermittent errors.
bugs.conditions: OPT-0048 optical transceiver inserted into r10000 or r5000 appliance.
bugs.impact: System displays intermittent optical transceiver errors.

bugs.title: VLAN shared between two tenants might not pass traffic to tenant with non-default CMP hash.
bugs.symptoms: If two tenants on a VELOS chassis are configured with a shared VLAN, one tenant might not pass traffic if it has a non-default CMP hash configured for that VLAN.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS chassis -- Configure a VLAN shared between two or more tenants -- In one tenant, configure a non-default CMP hash for the VLAN
bugs.impact: No connectivity.
bugs.workaround: After configuring a non-default cmp hash, run `docker restart partition_sw_rbcast` on each blade.
bugs.fix: Fixed operation of shared VLAN when cmp hash is not the default.

bugs.title: Platform registry ports could become mismatched depending on import timing
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, it is possible for the platform registry port configuration to become mismatched between the two system controllers. This can lead to a number of cascading issues with tenant deployments later.
bugs.conditions: If a platform image import succeeds on one system controller and fails on the other, or a sync of multiple images leads to them being imported in a different order on the standby system controller compared to the active, it is possible to encounter this scenario.
bugs.impact: Tenants that reference a version of imported software with mismatched ports may attempt to pull images from the wrong registry port, resulting in tenant failure or starting up with the wrong version of platform software images.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to fix the port mismatch by removing and re-importing the images with mismatched port assignments.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where platform registry ports could become mismatched depending on import timing

bugs.title: Chassis component alarm LED shows up on active system controller
bugs.symptoms: Chassis component alarm LED activates on the active system controller instead of on the LCD module.
bugs.conditions: If a chassis component, such as a PSU, generates an alarm, the RED alarm LED activates on the active system controller instead of the LCD module.
bugs.impact: A RED alarm LED could indicate a system controller problem instead of a chassis component problem.
bugs.fix: Chassis component alarms, such as from a PSU, now activate a RED alarm LED on the chassis instead of on the active system controller.

bugs.title: If any tenant is in the 'deployed' state, you cannot downgrade the chassis partition to F5OS-C 1.1.4.
bugs.symptoms: An attempt to downgrade chassis partition services to versions older than F5OS-C 1.4.0 fails with this error: "Partition database upgrade compatibility check failed." The validation logic prior to F5OS-C 1.4.0 does not permit tenants to be in the 'deployed' state during the schema change.
bugs.conditions: Tenant is in a 'deployed' state.
bugs.impact: You cannot downgrade partition services for this chassis partition to F5OS-C 1.1.x, 1.2.x, or 1.3.x from any higher version.
bugs.workaround: 1. In the partition manager CLI or webUI, change the running-state for all tenants to 'configured' or 'provisioned'. 2. Perform the downgrade for the chassis partition. 3. When the chassis partition downgrade is complete, return the tenants to the 'deployed' state.

bugs.title: Tcpdump log level is set to default {INFO} after upgrading
bugs.symptoms: Tcpdump log severity level is not retained after upgrading.
bugs.conditions: Tcpdump log severity is set to something other than INFORMATIONAL prior to upgrading.
bugs.impact: Severity level changes to INFO after upgrading.
bugs.workaround: Reset the severity level after upgrade. controller-1(config)# system logging sw-components sw-component tcpdumpd-manager config severity DEBUG controller-1(config-sw-component-tcpdumpd-manager)# commit Commit complete.

bugs.title: Optical transceiver OPT-0043 reports unknown as media type
bugs.symptoms: The "show portgroups" command reports unknown for the media type for an OPT-0043.
bugs.conditions: OPT-0043 transceiver plugged into a system.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic - this has no functional impact. The media field is not used by any software, it is reported as information for the user.
bugs.fix: OPT-0043 now reports as a "40G BiDi" media type.

bugs.title: QKView upload to iHealth is not supported by web proxy
bugs.symptoms: The upload to iHealth feature for sending QKView data to the external F5 service is not supported by web proxy. This means that QKView files must be copied to a local computer on your intranet before the files can be uploaded.
bugs.conditions: Uploading a QKView file to the iHealth service.
bugs.impact: Several steps are required to move QKView files around before uploading to iHealth, which is inconvenient.
bugs.workaround: Copy the QKView file to a computer on the intranet. Then you can upload the QKView file to the iHealth service from that secondary computer when it has internet access.
bugs.fix: Web proxy now supports uploading QKView files to iHealth.

bugs.title: No tenant config attributes are allowed after 'storage size'.
bugs.symptoms: While configuring the tenant in the one-line command, you are unable to give any other parameters after the storage size parameter. The storage size should be given at the end of the command only.
bugs.conditions: Preferring the storage command early while configuring the tenant in one-line command.
bugs.impact: Commands fail as invalid input if any other parameters are mentioned after storage size.
bugs.workaround: Place the storage size parameter at the end of command or split the config into multiple lines.

bugs.title: Chassis admin user cannot use SCP to import controller/chassis partition ISO images
bugs.symptoms: The controller admin user cannot copy ISO images to the chassis for import.
bugs.conditions: SCP is not allowed for the admin user.
bugs.impact: User must either use root shell access or a different upload protocol that may not be convenient based on the user network configuration.
bugs.fix: The controller admin use can now use the SCP command on a client machine to upload controller or chassis partition ISOs to the chassis active or floating management IP by specifying a target directory of "IMAGES/" in the same fashion that the partition admin user can use for importing tenant images. scp F5OS-C-1.5.0-4444.PARTITION.DEV.iso admin@activeccip:IMAGES/

bugs.title: Management IP address displays incorrectly in LLDP neighbor information
bugs.symptoms: The 'show lldp' command displays the management address of the neighbor incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: -- lldp is enabled -- Run the 'show lldp' command
bugs.impact: The management address of the neighbor displays incorrectly. This is a display issue, and there is no functional impact.

bugs.title: Tpm-integrity-status is "Unavailable" for standby controller, but tpm-status reports "Valid"
bugs.symptoms: The tpm-integrity-status is "Unavailable" for the standby controller, but tpm-status reports "Valid".
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when checking TPM status: syscon-2-active# show components component controller-* state tpm-integrity-status TPM INTEGRITY NAME STATUS --------------------------- controller-1 Unavailable controller-2 Valid
bugs.impact: Wrong tpm-status will be displayed on confD.
bugs.workaround: Restart vcc-chassis-manager container. From the root prompt of the system controller: [root@controller-1 ~]# docker restart vcc-chassis-manager
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed in latest release. We are checking tpm-status in regular interval and updating correct information in confD.

bugs.title: After controller upgrade, tenant might not work correctly due to failed install of KubeVirt pods&start;
bugs.symptoms: After a system controller upgrade, a tenant might not deploy, because upgraded KubeVirt pods might have failed to install correctly.
bugs.conditions: -- System controllers were recently upgraded. -- KubeVirt pods not installed correctly
bugs.impact: Tenant will not deploy correctly.
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove existing KubeVirt pods that are incorrectly installed. 2. Manually edit the kubevirt-velos-install.sh script to point to the correct registry port. 3. Rerun the install script to install the KubeVirt pods correctly.
bugs.fix: The kubevirt-velos-install.sh script is now updated to the correct registry port, which enables KubeVirt pods to be updated correctly.

bugs.title: VLAN Listener for a VLAN shared between tenants may not upgrade properly.&start;
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from F5OS-C 1.1.4 to a 1.2 release when there are tenants configured that share VLANs, the VLAN listener is not properly upgraded.
bugs.conditions: Tenants sharing VLANs in a configuration that is upgraded from F5OS-C 1.1.4 to 1.2.x.
bugs.impact: Traffic will not pass correctly.
bugs.workaround: Remove the VLAN from the interface(s) and then add it back (no changes to the tenant are necessary). This re-creates the vlan-listener with the correct VTC value.

bugs.title: HTTP response status codes do not match the result of the file import/export operations
bugs.symptoms: HTTP response status codes do not match the result of the file import/export operations.
bugs.conditions: When the unallowed path is given in file import CLI
bugs.impact: User experience
bugs.fix: Return the proper HTTP codes in error scenarios as well.

bugs.title: MD5 cipher is allowed on RESTCONF port 8888 with FIPS-enabled license.
bugs.symptoms: When a FIPS-enabled license is installed on the system, some MD5 ciphers are allowed on RESTCONF port 8888, when they should not be allowed.
bugs.conditions: The command "openssl s_client -connect <mgmt-ip>:8888 -cipher MD5" returns a valid certificate.
bugs.impact: MD5 SSLCipher continues to work on port 8888 on both system controller and chassis partition management IP addresses.
bugs.fix: Removed MD5 SSLCipherSuites from ssl.conf when a FIPS-enabled license is installed on the system.

bugs.title: File import/export operation performed on disallowed paths is not shown in file transfer status
bugs.symptoms: When file import/export is performed on unallowed paths, the status is not shown in the file transfer status.
bugs.conditions: Performing import/export is performed on unallowed paths.
bugs.impact: The rejected transfer status is not visible in the file transfer status.

bugs.title: MIB files cannot be download or exported using file utilities.
bugs.symptoms: MIB directory is not available for download or export file utilities
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS chassis or rSeries appliance -- You would like to download the MIB file(s) via the file utilities API
bugs.impact: You are unable to download the MIBs or export them.

bugs.title: System controller will not join cluster if internal chassis network range differs from existing controller
bugs.symptoms: When using a non-default internal chassis network range, a fresh system controller running the correct software versions will not automatically join the cluster when inserted into the chassis. This will occur any time a system controller boots up with a different internal network address range.
bugs.conditions: This will occur if a system controller is booting up, and has a different configuration for the internal chassis network range from the functioning system controller. This can occur when performing an RMA replacement, or a clean install of a controller via PXE or USB drive. This can also occur when removing the standby system controller and then reconfiguring the prefix via the 'system network config network-range-type RFC1918 prefix' command.
bugs.impact: System will no longer have a redundant system controller configuration until the communication problem is resolved.
bugs.workaround: If possible, only change the network prefix with both controllers present and joined. If affected by this issue: 1. Log into the functional system controller as root and examine /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt 2. Log into the non-functional system controller as root, edit /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_override.txt, and replace it with the contents of chassis_network_active.txt from the functional system controller. 3. On the non-functional system controller, ensure that platform-services-deployment has finished starting up before proceeding (approximately 15 minutes). Monitor "systemctl status -l platform-services-deployment" or "journalctl -f -u platform-services-deployment" until it finishes starting up: systemd[1]: Started Launch platform service containers through Docker Compose. 4. Reboot the non-functional system controller.
bugs.fix: A newly inserted controller with mismatching prefix information will sync the prefix of the current active System Controller. A functioning Active system controller must be present in the chassis in order for the newly inserted/powered system controller to sync the prefix information.

bugs.title: VLAN connectivity among VELOS tenants is lost
bugs.symptoms: Inbound ARP broadcasts on VLANs shared by tenants on VELOS systems are not received, and shared VLAN connectivity among tenants is lost.
bugs.conditions: A high volume of DLF packets are handled by the VELOS software rebroadcaster.
bugs.impact: Loss of connectivity on VLANs shared among tenants.
bugs.workaround: Restart the sw_rbcast container on the affected blade: # docker restart partition_sw_rbcast
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Error shown when configuring known-host for file transfer when FIPS mode is enabled`
bugs.symptoms: "Host unreachable" error is sometimes displayed when FIPS mode is enabled, if a user tries to configure known-host. The ssh-keyscan fails, as ssh-keyscan is not using FIPS approved ciphers.
bugs.conditions: - FIPS mode is enabled - User configures known-host for file transfer
bugs.impact: "Host unreachable" error is thrown.
bugs.fix: Updated ssh-keyscan to use FIPS approved ciphers when FIPS mode is enabled.

bugs.title: Platform registry ports can become de-synchronized, impacting Openshift deployment
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, platform services on the active and standby controllers can end up residing in docker registries that use different port numbers. This can result in Openshift pods failing to start, because they expect these port assignments to be synchronized.
bugs.conditions: Varied causes, which lead to inconsistent registry port assignments on active and standby controllers.
bugs.impact: Openshift pods cannot start.
bugs.fix: Added more checks to ensure platform registry ports are synchronized between controllers.

bugs.title: Files greater then 1000 MiB are truncated in QKView
bugs.symptoms: QKView is unable to collect an untrunucated velos.log file that has been rotated.
bugs.conditions: Rotated copy of the velos.log file is greater than 1000 MiB.
bugs.impact: Logs are not complete in QKView making it difficult to troubleshoot issues.
bugs.workaround: Collect the log files manually.

bugs.title: Tenants do not launch correctly after performing a rolling upgrade to F5OS-C 1.3.0&start;
bugs.symptoms: After performing a rolling upgrade to F5OS-C v1.3.0, tenants do not launch correctly. This can be seen in the output of "oc get pods".
bugs.conditions: Rolling upgrade to F5OS-C v1.3.0.
bugs.impact: Tenants do not launch correctly.
bugs.workaround: On the active system controller: touch /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL This causes the OpenShift cluster to be re-installed using the current image registry.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: KubeVirt pods might fail when upgrading from F5OS-C v1.2.1 to v1.3.0&start;
bugs.symptoms: During a system controller upgrade from F5OS-C v1.2.1 to v1.3.0, the KubeVirt pods fail to upgrade and produce an error causing the tenant to not operate properly.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from F5OS-C v1.2.1 to v1.3.0.
bugs.impact: The KubeVirt images are not available on the VELOS system controller registry. and the tenant does not operate properly because it relies on KubeVirt pods to be installed correctly.
bugs.workaround: Follow these steps on the active VELOS system controller: 1. cp /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/omd-kubevirt-velos-install.sh /tmp 2. cd /tmp vi omd-kubevirt-velos-install.sh 3. Add these lines at line 99 of that file: else echo "Using registry port of $official_port for kubevirt install" echo "Update registry port in kubevirt yml files" sed -i -e "s@:[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]/@:$official_port/@" $WORKDIR/kubevirt-velos.yaml 4. In one Linux shell window: oc delete -f /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/kubevirt-velos.yaml 5. In another Linux shell window: /tmp/omd-kubevirt-velos-install.sh /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/
bugs.fix: This issue is resolved.

bugs.title: Removing VELOS controller images used for bare metal install can cause Openshift failures after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: VELOS system controller performance is degraded when F5OS-C software versions prior to 1.1.4 are removed and an upgrade to F5OS-C 1.3.0 is initiated.
bugs.conditions: 1. The ISO image versions prior to F5OS-C 1.1.4 used for bare metal install of controllers is removed. 3. The currently-running version of controller software is 1.2.X. 4. An upgrade to F5OS-C 1.3.0 is initiated.
bugs.impact: VELOS performance is degraded until manual intervention is taken.
bugs.workaround: Rebuild the Openshift cluster on the affected VELOS system controllers.
bugs.fix: Removing VELOS system controller images used for bare metal install no longer causes OpenShift failures after upgrade in certain cases.

bugs.title: Unable to deploy more than two instances on single blade in VELOS chassis
bugs.symptoms: Deployment fails attempting to deploy more than two instances on a single blade in a VELOS chassis.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to deploy more than two instances on a single blade
bugs.impact: Deployment of the third instance fails. This release supports only two instances on a single blade.

bugs.title: Packets are dropped on VELOS when a masquerade MAC is on a shared VLAN
bugs.symptoms: On the VELOS platform, any packets destined to a masquerade MAC address are dropped when the masquerade MAC is located on a shared VLAN (a VLAN shared between multiple F5OS tenants). On rSeries hardware platforms, all traffic for this MAC is first handled by the software-rebroadcaster and is replicated to all tenants sharing that VLAN.
bugs.conditions: -- A masquerade MAC is configured on a shared VLAN. -- Traffic to the MAC address is initiated, that is, ping a floating self-IP. -- The packets are dropped on ingress.
bugs.impact: Connectivity issues.
bugs.workaround: Configure a static FDB entry at the partition level.
bugs.fix: Packets are no longer dropped when a masquerade MAC is on a shared VLAN.

bugs.title: OpenShift cluster health can toggle between Ready and Not Ready when cluster health is not good
bugs.symptoms: When performing a rolling upgrade from F5OS-C v1.1.0 to 1.2.x, and then to v1.3.0, the cluster status toggles between Ready and Not Ready when VELOS cluster is unhealthy. Other conditions can also cause this issue.
bugs.conditions: Performing a rolling upgrade from F5OS-C v1.1.0 to v1.2.x, and then to v1.3.0.
bugs.impact: Cluster status toggles between Ready and Not Ready when VELOS cluster is unhealthy.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Downgrading VELOS from F5OS-C v1.3.0 can sometimes leave platform services in degraded state
bugs.symptoms: After downgrading a VELOS system from F5OS-C v1.3.0 to v1.2.x, various platform services might fail to start.
bugs.conditions: After upgrading to F5OS-C v1.3.0, then downgrading to an earlier version.
bugs.impact: Various platform services might fail to start.
bugs.workaround: It may be necessary to rebuild the OpenShift cluster on the affected VELOS system controllers. If that does not fix the issue, intervention from F5 might be required.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Upgrade to F5OS-C 1.3.0 failed to upgrade chassis partition
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading VELOS from F5OS-C 1.2.2 to 1.3.0 caused partition containers to go in crashbackoffloop back. This can be checked by running this command: oc get pods --all-namespaces |grep -i crash
bugs.conditions: After upgrading to F5OS-C 1.3.0, tenant datapath interfaces do not come up.
bugs.impact: Traffic is impacted.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the chassis partition, that is, disabling and enabling the chassis partition fixes the issue.

bugs.title: Removing a 'patch' version of services might remove the associated 'base' version as well
bugs.symptoms: Removing a 'patch' version (X.Y.Z, Z>0) of a platform ISO or services might, under certain conditions, lead to the unexpected removal of the 'base' version (X.Y.0) associated with that patch.
bugs.conditions: 1. A 'patch' ISO is imported when the 'base' associated with the patch is not already imported (example: An F5OS-C 1.2.2 ISO is imported, and F5OS-C1.2.0 is not already imported). 2. Some time later, the F5OS-C 1.2.2 ISO is removed. This also removes the 1.2.0 services.
bugs.impact: F5OS-C removes software that wasn't explicitly chosen to be removed.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, import the 'base' version ISO (X.Y.0) before importing any patches. If this is done, removal of a 'patch' will not remove the 'base'. If a 'base' was already removed accidentally, re-importing the 'base' ISO will also make it available again.

bugs.title: LACP interface goes down after the partition is disabled/enabled
bugs.symptoms: interface state lacp_state is LACP_DEFAULTED For example: interface 2/1.0 is one of member of an LACP interface, which works fine before the partition is disabled/enabled. After the partition is disabled/enabled, run "show interfaces interface 2/1.0 state" command; the output is lacp_state LACP_DEFAULTED. lacp_state LACP_DEFAULTED is wrong which will cause vlan-listeners missing on the blade. vlan-listeners missing on the blade will cause tenant interface failure.
bugs.conditions: 1. LACP interface is used. 2. LACP interface is configured correctly and up before the partition is disabled/enabled. 3. Disable/enable the partition.
bugs.impact: Tenant will not be able to send/receive user traffic and it will not recover automatically.
bugs.workaround: Remove the ethernet interface from the aggregation and re-attach it to the aggregation. This will recover the interface state and resolve the problem. Example: commands to recover the interface (interface 2/1.0 belongs to the LACP interface lag1 and 2/1.0 has a wrong lacp_state). 1. In the partition CLI, remove the aggregate-id for the interface. Entering configuration mode terminal default-1(config)# no interfaces interface 2/1.0 ethernet config aggregate-id ;commit Commit complete. default-1(config)# 2. Re-add the aggregate-id. default-1(config)# interfaces interface 2/1.0 ethernet config aggregate-id lag1 ;commit 3. Reboot the blade (optional step -- use only if step 1 and 2 did not fix the problem).

bugs.title: Admin console is displayed when SSH login with a new root user
bugs.symptoms: Non-root user is allowed to get root role. If any such user exist, they get an admin console instead of root console.
bugs.conditions: A new non-root user is created with root role. Example : appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication users user user_test config username user_test role root
bugs.impact: non-root user with role root is restricted. Note: In case of live upgrade from previous to current release, any non-root user with root role may cause upgrade to fail (as non-root users with root role are restricted), and you will need to either delete these users or do a bare metal install before performing a live upgrade.
bugs.fix: Current fix prevents creation of a non-root user with root role.

bugs.title: Etcd instance might not start correctly after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh might show that the etcd instance native to system controller #1 or #2 does not come up after an upgrade. This displays in the output of /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh and might occur for the .3.51 or .3.52 node: failed to check the health of member 25fa6669d235caa6 on https://100.65.3.52:2379: Get https://100.65.3.52:2379/health: dial tcp 100.65.3.52:2379: connect: connection refused member 25fa6669d235caa6 is unreachable: [https://100.65.3.52:2379] are all unreachable This can cause a longer OpenShift outage if the system controller containing the healthy instance is rebooted, and complete outage if the system controller containing the healthy instance is lost.
bugs.conditions: This is caused by a previous mount failure of the drbd file system, which causes a corruption of the etcd instance on the standby system controller. This is seen very infrequently.
bugs.impact: The local etcd instance on the affected system controller will not work correctly, compromising the high availability (HA) availability of the OpenShift cluster. The cluster will continue to work correctly while both system controllers are up.
bugs.workaround: Rebuild the OpenShift cluster by running "touch /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL" from the CLI on the active system controller. This will cause all running tenants to be taken down during the cluster reinstall, which takes 50+ minutes. Once the cluster rebuild is complete, all chassis partitions should be disabled and re-enabled, and all tenants should be cycled to provisioned and back to deployed to ensure they have restarted correctly after the cluster rebuild.
bugs.fix: This is fixed in F5OS-C 1.4.0 and later.

bugs.title: Chassis Partition/Tenant pods might not start
bugs.symptoms: Chassis Partition/Tenant pods might fail to start if the partition namespace key is missing or stale.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading to F5OS-C v1.3.1 and creating a new partition, or deleting and creating an existing partition, either which is active on the Standby VELOS system controller.
bugs.impact: Chassis Partition/Tenant pods fail to start on a partition in this condition.
bugs.workaround: Fail over the active VELOS system controller, which causes the standby controller to generate the correct partition keys. To do this, from the command line on the active system controller type: "system redundancy go-standby"
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: Timing issue with blade reboot during partition startup
bugs.symptoms: A timing issue occurs when a user creates multiple partitions and adds multiple slots to those partitions. When a user creates and configures multiple pieces of hardware in a short amount of time, the later partitions/blades don’t always get the correct values.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create multiple partitions and assign multiple separate slots to each partition, initially disabled. 2. Wait for all the blades to reboot completely. 3. Set the blade's software version to a different version. 4. Enable all the partitions from step 1 in a single commit. 5. Wait for the blades to reboot and for the partitions to start.
bugs.impact: Some partitions/blades might have the wrong version after upgrading.
bugs.workaround: Reboot each blade with the wrong version manually after the partition is enabled.
bugs.fix: The timing issue has been resolved.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next Tenant Management IP address is not reachable after a chassis power cycle.
bugs.symptoms: After a chassis is restarted during a system reboot or power cycle, the tenant cannot be reached using the management IP address.
bugs.conditions: Primarily during a chassis power cycle, tenant IP addresses cannot be reached.
bugs.impact: Tenant admins will not be able to perform management operations such as network creation/Application configuration.
bugs.workaround: If the tenant is recovered within a certain time period, toggling its state from Partition will fix it. CLI: tenants tenant <name> config running-state configured; commit; exit tenants tenant <name> config running-state deployed; commit; exit

bugs.title: Tenant deployment fails when tenant name ends with hyphen
bugs.symptoms: A tenant fails to deploy and reports "Tenant deployment failed - Server is not responding" if the user-configured tenant name ends with a hyphen.
bugs.conditions: Tenant name ends with a hyphen.
bugs.impact: Tenant will not deploy.
bugs.workaround: Delete the tenant and recreate it with a valid name, consisting only of alphanumeric characters with embedded hyphens.
bugs.fix: The configuration validation code rejects attempts to create a tenant with an invalid name.

bugs.title: Alert manager status is occasionally reported as unhealthy on startup
bugs.symptoms: When Alert manager health is reported as unhealthy, it displays system controller health as unhealthy and causes failover
bugs.conditions: On startup, if any one of the analog sensors reports a sensor fault while reading its initial state, it is causing alert manager go unhealthy.
bugs.impact: It causes controller health fault/failover
bugs.fix: Added diagnostic tasks to monitor the health of sensors, VFC and VPC periodically and raise alerts.

bugs.title: Orchestration-agent logs spurious "Warning" severity messages
bugs.symptoms: Orchestration-agent can issue warning-level log messages about "unknown tags" in velos.log, similar to this: 2022-02-09T19:57:07.444093+00:00 controller-1(p1) orchestration-agent[1]: priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x503000000000003 msg="unknown tag in operation" TAG=1013977200 OP=4.
bugs.conditions: Schema changes can result in new items being added that the code does not care about, but can result in log messages.
bugs.impact: No functional impact; these warnings an be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: The orchestration-agent no longer logs warnings about unknown tags.

bugs.title: Resource-manager pods exist after downgrade from 1.5.0 or greater release to earlier release
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to 1.5.0 release or later and then downgrading to an older release, the resource-manager pods that are spawned as a daemonset in 1.5.0 will continue to run under the older release. oot@controller-2 ~]# oc get pods -o wide --all-namespaces |grep resource partition-1 f5-resource-manager-5ltqt 1/1 Running 0 22m 100.79.2.167 blade-7.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-6ctjb 1/1 Running 0 21m 100.79.1.61 blade-8.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-7889m 1/1 Running 0 23m 100.76.3.99 blade-1.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-99phl 1/1 Running 0 23m 100.77.3.85 blade-3.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-dlfhh 1/1 Running 0 23m 100.77.5.89 blade-2.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-h96c2 1/1 Running 0 23m 100.78.3.84 blade-4.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-hcv4r 1/1 Running 0 22m 100.78.1.66 blade-6.chassis.local <none> partition-1 f5-resource-manager-vgbb9 1/1 Running 0 22m 100.76.5.93 blade-5.chassis.local <none>
bugs.conditions: Upgrading to 1.5.0 or later release and then downgrading to an older release.
bugs.impact: The pods running will have no impact while running on older releases.
bugs.workaround: The pods can be removed using the openshift client command line if desired, but they will have no impact on the system. Example: oc delete -n partition-1 daemonset.apps/f5-resource-manager

bugs.title: Newly installed license is getting replaced with old license after performing config-restore
bugs.symptoms: When database config restore is performed, the system license was getting replaced with a license that is present in the backed up database file.
bugs.conditions: Config-restore is overwriting the system license.
bugs.impact: The system license will be removed and replaced with different license.
bugs.fix: The database operations like config-restore and reset-to-default do not remove the system license. When the database config-backup is performed, the license file won't be backed up into the backup file.

bugs.title: List of running containers are not captured in host qkview
bugs.symptoms: List of running containers are not captured in host qkview
bugs.conditions: Collect qkview and look for list of containers running on the system from qkview file.
bugs.impact: Unable to get the list of running containers from qkview
bugs.workaround: Administrator needs to run 'docker ps' command on the system and share the output with support.
bugs.fix: Qkview includes list of running containers on the system

bugs.title: LACP does not transmit PDU's when creating a LAG
bugs.symptoms: The LAG interface creation will not be successful and tx packet count in 'show lacp' will be zero.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs due to a race condition while creating a LAG interface and is not reproducible every time.
bugs.impact: Link aggregation of the front panel ports will not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: 1) clear newly added lag configurations a) remove lacp interface no lacp interfaces interface <lag-name> b) remove interfaces from lag no interfaces interface <interface> ethernet config aggregate-id c) remove lag interface no interfaces interface <lag-interface> 2) create Lag interface and add interfaces to the lag
bugs.fix: Fix code to remove the race condition and read lag-type as LACP

bugs.title: Multi-node BIG-IP tenants may fail to cluster after rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP tenant instances may fail to cluster after a rolling upgrade, due to the CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO being set incorrectly in the config-map that is used to deploy the tenant instance. This can be seen in the "show tmsh sys cluster" output on the tenant showing the slots in a failed state: root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(/S1-green-P::Active)(/Common)(tmos)# show sys cluster ----------------------------------------- Sys::Cluster: default ----------------------------------------- Address 10.238.133.200/24 Alt-Address :: Availability available State enabled Reason Cluster Enabled Primary Slot ID 1 Primary Selection Time 07/21/22 01:10:47 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | Sys::Cluster Members | ID Address Alt-Address Availability State Licensed high availability (HA) Clusterd Reason ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 1 :: :: available enabled true active running Run | 2 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 3 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 4 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 5 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 6 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 7 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed | 8 :: :: offline enabled false unknown shutdown Slot Failed This condition can verified by display the config map for a tenant instance and verifying that the CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO field is empty. e.g. From the system controller shell: oc get cm -n partition-1 <tenant_name>-<blade_#>-configmap -o json | egrep CHASSIS Bad Entry: # oc get cm -n partition-1 bigiptenant1-1-configmap -o json | egrep CHASSIS; done "CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO": "", Good Entry: oc get cm -n partition-1 bigiptenant1-2-configmap -o json | egrep CHASSIS; done "CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO": "chs414616s"
bugs.conditions: This can happen during a rolling upgrade if the CHASSIS_SERIAL_NO field is not read correctly and the tenant instance is restarted as part of the rolling upgrade. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.impact: If this issue occurs, one more instance of the tenant may not communicate correctly, which can cause some or all of the data plane to not function correctly, causing an outage.
bugs.workaround: 1.) Set tenant(s) state to provisioned for BIG-IP, or configured for BIG-IP Next. 2.) Once the tenant(s) have stopped, disable the partition. 3.) Re-enable the partition. 4.) Set tenant(s) state back to deployed.

bugs.title: Local file path in file transfer-status for remote file import operation does not show appropriately
bugs.symptoms: Local file path does not show appropriately when file import operation is done from a remote URL.
bugs.conditions: File transfer from a remote URL with query params.
bugs.impact: Inappropriate file name shown in local file path.
bugs.fix: Modified file name in utils-agent code to remove unnecessary query params after file name.

bugs.title: LACP trunks are not configured automatically in BIG-IP tenant running on F5OS chassis/appliances
bugs.symptoms: When an LACP trunk is configured on an F5OS chassis/appliance and only the native VLAN is attached, the LACP trunk will not be automatically configured on the BIG-IP tenant.
bugs.conditions: This behavior is observed only when the LACP trunk is attached to a native VLAN.
bugs.impact: LACP trunk configuration will not be applied to the BIG-IP tenant automatically when only a native VLAN is attached to it on the platform.
bugs.workaround: Configure the LACP trunk in the BIG-IP tenant manually.
bugs.fix: LACP trunks are now configured automatically in BIG-IP tenant running on F5OS chassis/appliances, as expected.

bugs.title: File import should check that the target doesn't exist
bugs.symptoms: File import will fail if the same file name already exists.
bugs.conditions: Importing a file that already exists on the file system.
bugs.impact: An error occurs if the file already exists.

bugs.title: Log files collected by QKView are truncated with the newest entries removed
bugs.symptoms: If log files are exceedingly large, they may be truncated when collected by QKView from the 'bottom-up', meaning that the most recent log entries are clipped.
bugs.conditions: Log files exceed the maximum file size (default 500 MB) specified during QKView creation.
bugs.impact: Most recent log entries are clipped, making diagnosis difficult.
bugs.workaround: Collect the log files manually.
bugs.fix: QKView log files are now truncated 'top-down', preserving the most recent log entries.

bugs.title: etcd database may be corrupted on upgrade to 1.3.1 release.
bugs.symptoms: etcd instance on one of the CC's may become unresponsive after rolling upgrade to 1.3.1 due to failure to mount drbd partition. System will continue to function, but if the CC with functioning etcd instance goes offline, the openshift cluster will stop responding.
bugs.conditions: Rolling upgrade to 1.3.1 release from older software release.
bugs.impact: No immediate impact, but will cause HA failure if CC that is not affected goes offline while the etcd instance on remaining CC has hit this issue.
