bugs.impact: Packets may be forwarded to unexpected destinations, and/or new connections are unable to be offloaded to ePVA.
bugs.workaround: Don't reboot or restart TMM without also rebooting the entire appliance.
bugs.fix: Packets are behaving as expected.

bugs.title: iHealth accepts QKView files to upload without any file extension
bugs.symptoms: QKView files without any extension failed to upload into iHealth.
bugs.conditions: If the QKView files are generated without any extension.
bugs.impact: iHealth report invalid file extension.
bugs.workaround: Generate QKView files with extension.
bugs.fix: Allow to upload QKView files to iHealth without any extension.

bugs.title: nslcd start/run script may fail or log alarming messages
bugs.symptoms: The script that watches and restarts the nslcd process could sometimes fail to do so, and would sometimes log messages that appeared alarming.
bugs.conditions: Changing authentication settings that affect nslcd.
bugs.impact: The messages were benign, but the occasional failure to restart nslcd on config change could cause authentication changes to fail to propagate to the running process.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the name-service-ldap container is likely to solve the issue.
bugs.fix: The nslcd start/run script was rewritten to minimize alarming log messages and reliably start and restart the process when expected.

bugs.title: Configuring auth server-group and server requires duplicate name/address values
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a server-group from the CLI, users were forced to enter the config name and/or the config address multiple times to successfully configure the server-group.
bugs.conditions: User is attempting to configure an auth server-group using the CLI.
bugs.impact: Configuration was unnecessarily complex and error prone.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly enter the config name or config address to complete the configuration of the server-group.
bugs.fix: Server-group only requires the config name and/or config address to be entered once to successfully configure the object.

bugs.title: CLI "show interfaces summary" command doesn't provide a summary
bugs.symptoms: The "show interfaces" command is quite cluttered when displaying the state of both physical and virtual (aggregate) interfaces, making it difficult to get a high-level summary of all interfaces. The "show interfaces interface full" command displays a confusing subset of interface states, when the intent of "full" was to display all state fields, including the duplicate "name" column.
bugs.conditions: The administrator attempts to use the "show interfaces" command to diagnose networking problems.
bugs.impact: Difficult to diagnose interface configuration/connectivity problems.
bugs.fix: The new "summary" option for "show interfaces" displays a brief subset of the most important interface state information. appliance-1# show interfaces interface state summary OPER NAME TYPE MTU ENABLED STATUS --------------------------------------------- 1.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 2.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 3.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 4.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 5.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 6.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 7.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 8.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP mgmt ethernetCsmacd - true UP

bugs.title: DMA-Agent system logs preserved through system reboots
bugs.symptoms: The dma-agent log file is deleted and recreated every time the system is rebooted, this makes investigating dma-agent related issues difficult if the system had restarted since the problem occurred.
bugs.conditions: Accessing dma-agent system logs.
bugs.impact: Difficult in investigating or debugging dma-agent system logs.
bugs.workaround: Do not reboot the system in which dma-agent logs need to be investigated.

bugs.title: Qkview collects redundant log files
bugs.symptoms: Qkview collects most log files as part of its main collection, but some containers have been specified to collect log files specific to the operation of that container.
bugs.conditions: Execute system diagnostics qkview capture
bugs.impact: Redundant log files collected use extra storage space and bandwidth for transmission.
bugs.fix: Redundant log files have been scrubbed from container collection.

bugs.title: F5OS will not import system images copied with WinSCP
bugs.symptoms: F5OS will not import system images copied into /var/import/staging/ using WinSCP. The file will be present on the filesystem, but the system will not process and validate them. On older software versions (prior to F5OS-C 1.3.0 and F5OS-A 1.1.0), the image will remain stuck in an "In Queue" state.
bugs.conditions: Importing F5OS system images (F5OS-C controller and chassis partition images and F5OS-A system images) to /var/import/staging/.
bugs.impact: The images cannot be used for F5OS software installs.
bugs.workaround: After importing the images, log in to the F5OS device as root and run touch against the newly-uploaded files. For instance: touch /var/import/staging/F5OS-C-1.4.0-4112.CONTROLLER.iso
bugs.fix: F5OS will correctly import system images copied with WinSCP.

bugs.title: ConfD management IP configuration command DHCP shows unusable extra options which might confuse user
bugs.symptoms: ConfD management IP configuration command DHCP shows unusable extra options like IP address, gateway, and prefix. User do not need to pass IP address, gateway, and prefix when configuring management IP with DHCP.
bugs.conditions: User is configuring management IP with DHCP and checking command argument after DHCP over CLI.
bugs.impact: A few extra unusable options exist after the DHCP command over CLI.
bugs.workaround: Do not pass any value on the arguments passed after DHCP.
bugs.fix: Added restrictions in the ConfD CLI command, which will not display extra options after DHCP over CLI.

bugs.title: WebUI crashes when a new SSL/TLS private key is generated
bugs.symptoms: The webUI crashes when a new SSL/TLS certificate is created in the Certificate Management tab. The HTTP server has to restart to read the newly-created private keys (encrypted or un encrypted) from a configuration file. Before the HTTP server restarts, all active client connections will be closed. This will cause the webUI to crash, and the server will be unreachable temporarily.
bugs.conditions: No configuration changes required.
bugs.impact: The webUI crashes and the TCP connection with the HTTP server will be closed.
bugs.workaround: The user has to reestablish the connection to the server after waiting a few seconds.
bugs.fix: No fix required.

bugs.title: LDAP groups configurable with custom gidNumber to role mappings
bugs.symptoms: In prior releases, the group ID number representing authentication roles was hard-coded to certain values. This could cause problems since an external authentication system (for example, LDAP) may have conflicting group IDs.
bugs.conditions: External authentication system (e.g. LDAP, AD, or radius) where a group ID number conflicts with the hard-coded role IDs (for example, 9000).
bugs.impact: This could cause difficulty configuring a user with specific role assignments in an external authentication system.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure group IDs in external system such that the hard-coded group ID numbers match the role numbers required by the F5 system.
bugs.fix: Added configuration to allow the administrator to specify the group ID number in use by the external system to identify user roles. The external number will be mapped to the F5 role based on this setting.

bugs.title: User manager containers should not mount /var/log/tally as /tmp
bugs.symptoms: Unnecessary files left in /var/log.
bugs.conditions: When qkview is captured.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary files left in /var/log and collected by qkview as a result of a container using /var/log/tally as a temporary space.
bugs.fix: User manager does not mount /var/log/tally anymore.

bugs.title: Updating LDAP configuration on Auth Settings screen on the webUI having no TLS key updates it to empty string.
bugs.symptoms: When the LDAP configuration on Auth Settings is updated via the webUI, with TLS key not previously configured, it is updated to be an empty string. This is resulting in empty string encryption.
bugs.conditions: Add/Modify LDAP configuration on Auth Settings screen.
bugs.impact: TLS key is set to empty string and is encrypted.
bugs.workaround: One of the following: -- Use the F5OS CLI to modify authentication settings, rather than using the webUI. -- Use the webUI to edit authentication settings only when the TLS key is already configured, meaning, there is an encrypted value already present in TLS key field.
bugs.fix: Updating LDAP configuration when the TLS key is not configured will not create a TLS key with empty string.

bugs.title: TACACS+ remote authentication for SSH does not work when server listens on non-default port
bugs.symptoms: If remote authentication is configured to use TACACS+ and the servers use a port other than 49 (the default port for TACACS), users will not be able to authenticate via SSH. SELinux errors in /var/log/audit/audit.log similar to the following: type=AVC msg=audit(1660923433.566:3728): avc: denied { name_connect } for pid=20995 comm="sshd" dest=4949 scontext=system_u:system_r:sshd_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 tcontext=system_u:object_r:munin_port_t:s0 tclass=tcp_socket permissive=0
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries appliance running F5OS-A, or VELOS system controller; this issue does not affect VELOS chassis partitions -- TACACS+ remote authentication -- TACACS+ server listening on a port other than 49
bugs.impact: Unable to authenticate when connecting via SSH.
bugs.workaround: Configure the SELinux policy to allow this traffic. On a VELOS chassis, these instructions must be run on each system controller separately. 1. Connect to the F5OS system via SSH as root. 2. Examine the SELinux audit denials and confirm all of them are associated with traffic that should be allowed: grep denied.*name_connect.*sshd /var/log/audit/audit.log > /root/ssh-audit-denials.log cat /root/ssh-audit-denials.log Remove entries from the file /root/ssh-audit-denials.log that you do not want to allow. 3. After confirming the contents of the file /root/ssh-audit-denials.log, run the following commands to create and install an SELinux policy to allow that traffic: audit2allow -M sshd.allowtacacs < /root/ssh-audit-denials.log semodule -i sshd.allowtacacs.pp

bugs.title: CLI idle-time is not persistently configurable
bugs.symptoms: The default CLI idle-timeout is set in a non-user-modifiable configuration file, and must be set each time the user logs in.
bugs.conditions: The user desires to set an persistent idle-timeout to a value other than the pre-set default, or to disable it.
bugs.impact: User cannot select a default idle-timeout other than the predefined default.
bugs.fix: A configuration setting has been added to the configuration database as "system settings config idle-timeout" so that the administrator can configure a default idle-timeout for the CLI. The setting applies to the particular system instance (controller, partition, or appliance).
bugs.behavior: Administrator can configure the default CLI timeout value, so that it applies to all user sessions.

bugs.title: System controller components can hang during controller rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: System controller components can hang during controller rolling upgrade, resulting in failure to start the partitions correctly, and other incorrect operation. Partition instance state may show as "failed", "offline", or "running", rather than the normal "running-active"/"running-standby". This can also cause imported ISO images to not synchronize across controllers following an upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Performing a system controller rolling upgrade from a version prior to 1.5.0, to version 1.5.0.
bugs.impact: Partition instances may not reach the normal state of running-active/running-standby, and will not operate correctly.
bugs.workaround: If the system is in this state, it can be fixed by rebooting both system controllers, in sequence. Failover/go-standby is not sufficient; both controllers must be restarted to clear the issue. The problem can be avoided by performing an out-of-service upgrade, using the "out-of-service true" option with the system controller "system image set-version" command.
bugs.fix: The system controller components no longer hang during the rolling upgrade.

bugs.title: QKView obfuscation step can cause excessive disk usage
bugs.symptoms: QKView performs the obfuscation steps for capturing files, which can create temporary files the same size as the captured files. If a sufficiently large file is captured, this may cause a disk full error.
bugs.conditions: QKView captures a very large file and obfuscates it.
bugs.impact: System may be unusable.
bugs.workaround: Before executing QKView, scan the system for extraordinarily large log files and delete them. One example is telemetry.db.
bugs.fix: This bug fix truncates the file to a maximum size of 0.5 GB (or a size defined by the maxfilesize argument) before performing obfuscation. This limits the chance for a disk full error.

bugs.title: VELOS floating IP may not work properly with IPv4 prefix-length other than /24, /16, or /8
bugs.symptoms: When a VELOS device is configured with a prefix-length other than /24, /16, or /8 for IPv4 management addresses, the system may fail to install correct routes for handling reply traffic sourced from the floating management address. One of the two following situations may occur: 1. The floating management address will not be accessible from other devices on the same local network (cannot ping the floating management IP from the standby system controller). 2. The floating management address will not be accessible from another range of IPs, because the system thinks those addresses are link-local. For instance, if a device is assigned an IP address of 198.51.78.88/26: [root@controller-1 ~]# ip route show table mgmt-floating4 default via 198.51.100.126 dev mgmt-floating 198.51.100.0/26 dev mgmt-floating scope link The system will not be accessible from devices with IP address 198.51.100.0 through 198.51.100.63.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS controller -- Management network with an IPv4 management address configured, and management network prefix-length other than /24, /16, or /8.
bugs.impact: Floating system controller management IP may not be able to reply to traffic from all IPs.
bugs.workaround: On active system controller (and after any reboot or system controller failover), fix the routing rules. Log in to the active system controller as root and run the following commands: CORRECT_NETWORK=$(ip route show table main | grep mgmt-floating | cut -f1 -d' ') WRONG_ROUTE=$(ip route show table mgmt-floating4 | grep 'scope link') ip route delete table mgmt-floating4 $WRONG_ROUTE ip route add table mgmt-floating4 $CORRECT_NETWORK dev mgmt-floating
bugs.fix: The system correctly handles IPv4 management addresses with a prefix-length other than /24, /16, and /8.

bugs.title: Cannot display license information in VELOS partition webUI
bugs.symptoms: User does not have a way to see the system's license details when they are on the partition webUI.
bugs.conditions: User tries to see licensing info on the partition webUI.
bugs.impact: No way to view licensing information on the partition webUI.
bugs.fix: A new licensing navigation option has been added to the partition webUI. Clicking on it will show the system's licensing information.

bugs.title: User logon/logoff logs in audit logs, to be sent via remote syslog
bugs.symptoms: The user logon/logoff logs were not sent via remote syslog.
bugs.conditions: Releases prior to version 1.6.0.
bugs.impact: The user logon and logoff logs will not be sent to remote syslog.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: audit.log is included in remote syslog, so all the user logon and logoff logs can be sent to remote syslog.

bugs.title: Downloading QKViews directly from the System Reports screen.
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS-A webUI lacks the ability to download QKView files directly from the System Reports screen. You must navigate to the File Utilities screen to perform the action.
bugs.conditions: Download QKView files.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, you need to navigate to a different webUI screen to download QKView files.
bugs.workaround: Navigate to the File Utilities screen to download QKView files.
bugs.fix: From F5OS-A v1.8.0, QKView files can be downloaded from System Reports screen.

bugs.title: Add MAC Address to "show system mgmt ip" Command
bugs.symptoms: Show system mgmt-ip does not output the mgmt interface MAC address.
bugs.conditions: Execute show system mgmt-ip
bugs.impact: User has to execute ifconfig mgmt-fixed/mgmt-floating to determine the mgmt interface mac address.
bugs.workaround: Execute ifconfig mgmt-fixed, ifconfig mgmt-floating to determine the mac address associated with the mgmt interfaces.
bugs.fix: In releases with this fix in place the user can now get the mac address by executing "show system mgmt-ip" in the CLI.

bugs.title: After a controller upgrade, Kubevirt pods fail to upgrade due to leftover pods stuck in Unknown state
bugs.symptoms: Tenants will not move to a running state.
bugs.conditions: After a controller upgrade, it is possible that some of the Kubevirt pods from the previous software version can remain in an Unknown state. With these leftover pods, the Kubevirt install script will fail to install the newer Kubevirt pods.
bugs.impact: Tenants are not running.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the leftover Kubevirt pods in the Unknown state and rerun the Kubevirt install script.
bugs.fix: Kubevirt pods will update as expected.

bugs.title: The "hdp_dmq_stat" table is missing data for several statistics
bugs.symptoms: The TMCTL "hdp_dmq_stat" table is missing data for the following counters: hdp_dmq_stat/tpg_txpkts hdp_dmq_stat/tpg_badifh_drop_cnt hdp_dmq_stat/tpg_unsup_tag_drop_cnt
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: No valid data for the affected counters.
bugs.fix: Correctly fill in the table columns with the counter values.

bugs.title: The Tenant Deployments column on the tenant images screen is not reflecting exact purpose of that column
bugs.symptoms: The Tenant Deployments column on the tenant images screen on the VELOS chassis partition webUI is currently showing the comma separated slot numbers on which the tenant is deployed. If the image is not used for any deployment, a string 'Not In Use' is shown.
bugs.conditions: There should be a deployed tenant using the tenant image we are viewing information for.
bugs.impact: The name "Tenant deployments" on the column is confusing the user, as it indicates that the column will show the count of tenants that are deployed using that image.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: The column name is changed to "In Use" and the column will now show value "True" or "False" indicating if a tenant is deployed using that image.

bugs.title: Unexpected flow type logs
bugs.symptoms: fpgamgr docker logs will display lines such as: hdp_cap_fc_get: Unexpected flow type (17) in HDP_CAP_FC_CAP_11_REG
bugs.conditions: These lines can appear at any time, triggered with various under-the-hood API calls that need to determine hardware capabilities. Please note that despite the appearance of the log message, this isn't tied to the usage of ePVA (or lack thereof).
bugs.impact: No impact, these logs are purely cosmetic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround. However, these lines are purely cosmetic and can safely be ignored.

bugs.title: Adding ConfD status command's output to QKView logs
bugs.symptoms: ConfD --status command's output was not collected as part of QKView.
bugs.impact: ConfD status is needed in QKView logs for debugging during an issue.
bugs.workaround: Added the command output to QKView.
bugs.fix: ConfD --status output is added to QKView logs.

bugs.title: When TACACS+ users are assigned the same UID, the first-time SSH session closes abruptly
bugs.symptoms: When two or more TACACS+ users are assigned the same UID, one of the user's SSH session closes abruptly.
bugs.conditions: Two or more TACACS+ users are assigned the same UID.
bugs.impact: The SSH session of one of the users will be closed abruptly.
bugs.workaround: Do not assign the same UID for two or more TACACS+ users. If you have already assigned two or more users the same UID and the the SSH session closes abruptly, try to re-authenticate the user.

bugs.title: DNS warning on cluster status is ambiguous
bugs.symptoms: If the F5OS configured DNS server is not reachable then the cluster summary status displays 'Check DNS server configuration'. This warning is not specific enough to quickly identify the problem due to it appearing as if the cluster DNS is problematic, rather than the F5OS configuration.
bugs.conditions: The DNS server that was configured on F5OS is not reachable.
bugs.impact: The DNS warning on the cluster summary status slows the process of identifying the cause of the message.
bugs.workaround: Configure reachable DNS servers on F5OS. For example: syscon-2-active# config Entering configuration mode terminal syscon-2-active(config)# system dns servers server 10.1.1.1 syscon-2-active(config)# show cluster The output of "show cluster" may take a short time to update, assuming the configured DNS IP(s) is reachable.
bugs.fix: Delete the "Check DNS server configuration" cluster summary and change the event log as well.

bugs.title: Alerts not generated in ConfD when dma-agent is unhealthy
bugs.symptoms: Alerts not generated in ConfD alarms and events when dma-agent health is unhealthy.
bugs.conditions: Only when dma-agent service reports health as unhealthy and severity critical.
bugs.impact: No alerts will be displayed in ConfD, but health will be displayed in ConfD "show system health".
bugs.fix: Alerts and events will be generated and visible in ConfD.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants created before F5OS-C 1.5.1 or F5OS-A 1.3.0 may be allocated a smaller disk than required
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP tenant disk space is fully used by creating multiple software volumes within the tenant, it will generate disk errors.
bugs.conditions: - A tenant originally deployed from an “ALL-F5OS” tenant image (i.e., BIGIP-15.1.6.1-0.0.10.ALL-F5OS.qcow2.zip.bundle) originally created from one of the following: -- 14.1.5 or above in the 14.1.x branch of code -- 15.1.6.1 or above in the 15.1.x branch of code - The tenant is configured to use 76G of disk space (the default)
bugs.impact: Software installs within the tenant may fail.
bugs.workaround: Beginning in F5OS-A 1.3.0, the system detects the minimum size of a disk created from a tenant image file, and enforces that minimum on newly-created tenants. If a customer has a tenant affected by this issue and upgrades their system to F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later, set the tenant to "configured", and then deploy the tenant again. If the disk size is not right, the system will show the minimum size, then adjust the tenant disk size to what is advised by the system or larger. From 1.4.0, user does not need to adjust the size unless the user needs a bigger size. The right/minimum size will be auto-allocated when the state is changed.
bugs.fix: The tenant disk size will be detected and auto-allocated.
bugs.behavior: There are two behaviors. 1.3.x: If the disk size is smaller than it has to be, it warns the user and doesn't start the tenant until the user specifies the right/minimum size. 1.4.0: It auto increases the size to the right/minimum size if the user didn't specify the disk size.

bugs.title: Wrong route table names in host-config qkview file
bugs.symptoms: Wrong routing policy tables used to collect the data from the vcc-host-config in controller qkview. vcc-host-config - ip route list table mgmt-floating Error: argument "mgmt-floating" is wrong: table id value is invalid vcc-host-config - ip -6 route list table mgmt-floating Error: argument "mgmt-floating" is wrong: table id value is invalid The actual table names are "mgmt-floating4" and "mgmt-floating6".
bugs.conditions: Qkview data collection from vcc-host-config at the controller.
bugs.impact: Qkview is unable to collect the expected data.

bugs.title: Egress traffic is dropped on interface 1/1.1
bugs.symptoms: Egress traffic on interface 1/1.1 is dropped. If that interface is configured as part of a LAG with LACP enabled, the interface will remain in an LACP_DEFAULTED state.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS-C partition using the blade in slot 1. -- The port group for the interfaces in slot 1 are configured in 4x25GbE or 4x10GbE mode.
bugs.impact: All traffic that the system tries to transmit out of interface 1/1.1 is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Do not use interface 1/1.1 in affected software versions.
bugs.fix: Do not use interface 1/1.1 in affected software versions.

bugs.title: Mixed front panel port speed configurations are unsupported on F5OS-C v1.5.0
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to set the blade front panel ports into a 100:10/25G or 40:10/25G configuration will result in a non-functional data path. The blade may appear to be linked at the physical layer, but no traffic will pass through the blade until the front panel port speed configuration is the same for both ports (for example, 2x100g, 2x40G, 2x 4x10G).
bugs.conditions: Setting a mixed speed configuration on the front panel ports (for example, one port at 100G and the other at 4x10G, or one port at 40G and the other at 4x10G).
bugs.impact: No traffic will pass through the blade. Tenants will not deploy.
bugs.workaround: If mixed front panel port speeds are required, update to the next version when it becomes available.
bugs.fix: If mixed front panel port speeds are required, update to the next version when it becomes available.

bugs.title: Front panel interface status is not reported in alarms or events
bugs.symptoms: Front panel interface flap events are not displayed in alarms or events CLI/GUI.
bugs.conditions: Front panel interface is down or oper-status changes.
bugs.impact: Interface status is not shown in alarms or events.
bugs.workaround: View interface with "show interfaces interface state oper-status".

bugs.title: Application error while using the CLI command "show components"
bugs.symptoms: The user receives an error message using the CLI (show components -> Error: application error) when there is a faulty sensor in the hardware.
bugs.conditions: When the system has the faulty sensor.
bugs.impact: Application error seen in the ConfD CLI while trying to execute "show components". The webUI is affected as well.
bugs.fix: We have added a check at diag-agent to not throw the application error; it will show data for the healthy components.

bugs.title: VELOS high availability (HA) cluster transitions into an active-active configuration after the upgrade
bugs.symptoms: VELOS high availability (HA) cluster transitions into an active-active configuration after the upgrade.
bugs.conditions: After upgrading.
bugs.impact: As the two nodes are in active-active configuration, a failover cannot be performed.
bugs.workaround: https://docs.f5net.com/display/~boli/Workaround+for++the+%27f5-avcl-keepalive%27+subsystem+status+is+%27ACTIVE%27+on+standby+node+after+VELOS+HA+standby+upgrade

bugs.title: Opensource Updates
bugs.symptoms: Opensource libraries used in previous versions were potentially susceptible to:
bugs.conditions: This addresses different problems. Multiple common vulnerabilities are fixed.
bugs.impact: Strengthens System Security
bugs.fix: Multiple common vulnerabilities are fixed to make system more secure. RPM libraries have been upgraded to the following versions. rpm-4.11.3-48.el7_9.x86_64 rpm-build-libs-4.11.3-48.el7_9.x86_64 rpm-libs-4.11.3-48.el7_9.x86_64 rpm-python-4.11.3-48.el7_9.x86_64 rsync-3.1.2-11.el7_9.x86_64 java-1.8.0-openjdk-headless-1:1.8.0.342.b07-1.el7_9.x86_64 tzdata-2022a-1.el7.noarch tzdata-java-2022a-1.el7.noarch systemd-219-78.el7_9.7.x86_64 systemd-libs-219-78.el7_9.7.x86_64 systemd-sysv-219-78.el7_9.7.x86_64 podman-1.6.4-36.el7_9.x86_64 runc-1.0.0-69.rc10.el7_9.x86_64 expat-2.1.0-15.el7_9.x86_64

bugs.title: QKView now collects data from unassigned but active blades
bugs.symptoms: If a blade in a chassis is unassigned from a partition, qkview ignores it, and will not collect any data from it.
bugs.conditions: -- Taking a partition qkview -- You wish to see qkview data for a blade that was recently removed from that partition
bugs.impact: Diagnostics data is not collected from unassigned blades.
bugs.workaround: Run qkview-collect on an unassigned blade. 1. ssh blade-n 2. qkview-collect 3. resulting qkview data will be in qkview.tgz
bugs.fix: Chassis qkviews will now contain the results of qkview-collect for unassigned blades.

bugs.title: Directory indexing enabled for management webUI
bugs.symptoms: Directory indexing is enabled for management webUI.
bugs.conditions: When the management IP is followed by the name of any directory that is contained in the webUI, the build directories and file contents are visible on the browser.
bugs.impact: The webUI build directories and file contents are visible on the browser.
bugs.fix: Disabled directory indexing.

bugs.title: Tcpdump may not capture large packets
bugs.symptoms: The tcpdump utility may not capture packets larger than 1371 bytes.
bugs.conditions: Large packets, chassis platform.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting network issues by running tcpdump in the partition may not work effectively.

bugs.title: Using MAC Masquerade in a BIG-IP tenant causes traffic issues when re-deploying the tenant
bugs.symptoms: If the tenant has configured MAC Masquerade, when the tenant is moved to a Configured or Provisioned state, then back to Deployed, the tenant may experience loss of traffic.
bugs.conditions: The tenant has configured MAC Masquerade and redeploys the tenant.
bugs.impact: The tenant may experience loss of datapath traffic.
bugs.fix: Using MAC Masquerade in a BIG-IP tenant no longer causes traffic issues.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenant intermittently showing wrong status
bugs.symptoms: Due to the order and data with events received from Kubernetes, TPOB is failing to determine the latest status of the BIG-IP tenant status and temporarily displaying a wrong status. The wrong status will be auto-corrected.
bugs.conditions: A tenant recovered from a error state randomly displays wrong status temporarily and then auto-corrects.
bugs.impact: Intermittent wrong status displayed with BIG-IP tenants.

bugs.title: etcd database may be corrupted in certain failure scenarios
bugs.symptoms: /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh might show that the etcd instance native to system controller #1 or #2 does not come up after an upgrade. This displays in the output of /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh and might occur for the .3.51 or .3.52 node: failed to check the health of member 25fa6669d235caa6 on https://100.65.3.52:2379: Get https://100.65.3.52:2379/health: dial tcp 100.65.3.52:2379: connect: connection refused member 25fa6669d235caa6 is unreachable: [https://100.65.3.52:2379] are all unreachable This can cause a longer OpenShift outage if the system controller containing the healthy instance is rebooted, and complete outage if the system controller containing the healthy instance is lost.
bugs.conditions: This can happen if both system controllers are rebooted at the same time.
bugs.impact: The local etcd instance on the affected system controller will not work correctly, compromising the high availability (HA) of the OpenShift cluster. The cluster will continue to work correctly while both system controllers are up.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to rebuild the OpenShift cluster by running "touch /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL" from the shell as root on the active system controller. This will cause all running tenants to be taken down during the cluster reinstall, which takes 90+ minutes.
bugs.fix: This is fixed in F5OS-C-1.5.1 and later. With this fix, the impacted etcd instance will be recovered automatically, restoring full high availability support in etcd.

bugs.title: The chassis partition webUI should show the partition name on the application header
bugs.symptoms: Partition name is not shown on application header.
bugs.impact: Users find it difficult to differentiate between multiple sessions.
bugs.workaround: The partition name is visible on the tab title and dashboard screen.
bugs.fix: Partition name is added to the application header on the chassis partition webUI.

bugs.title: Packet loss caused by failure of internal hardware bus
bugs.symptoms: All or 50% of from-network packets arriving at a front panel port are dropped in hardware prior to delivery to tenant(s) running on the CPU. Packet loss is caused by CRC errors on an internal bus connecting two hardware components leading to eventual failure of the bus.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs randomly, but is most commonly seen soon after bootup when packets first start to be handled by fastL4 hardware acceleration, hardware per-virtual server syn cookie protection, or AFM hardware protection.
bugs.impact: Total loss of from-network to CPU packets on r5900, r5800, and r5600 appliances, and either total loss or loss of 50% of from-network to CPU packets on r10900, r10800, and r10600 appliances. The r4800, r4600, r2800, and r2600 appliances are unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the appliance and disable fastL4 acceleration, per-virtual syn cookie hardware protection, and AFM hardware protection before re-enabling ingress traffic.
bugs.fix: This issue has been corrected.

bugs.title: F5OS install may partially fail, leaving system with mismatched OS and services
bugs.symptoms: After an attempted upgrade, administrators are unable to access the system via management UI, or log into the system as any user other than "root". A message such as the following in the platform log: priority=Fatal msgid=0x3501000000000021 msg=OStree rebase to version 1.2.0-10139 failed.
bugs.conditions: The first part of an F5OS software upgrade fails, but the system continues on and performs subsequent steps of the upgrade.
bugs.impact: The system may be completely inoperative, or the system may be running with different OS and services versions, which could lead to unknown problems. On VELOS systems, "show system image" will report a failed install, and one of the system controllers may report a running OS version that is not aligned with the OS version and services versions, as can be seen on system controller 2 here: syscon-1-active# show system image SERVICE ISO INSTALL NUMBER OS VERSION VERSION VERSION STATUS ---------------------------------------------------- 1 1.8.0-18829 1.8.0-18829 - failed 2 1.6.1-19136 1.8.0-18829 - failed
bugs.workaround: If this issue occurs, contact F5 Support for assistance. Note: This issue exists in the starting software version. It can affect upgrades to versions where this issue is fixed, i.e. upgrades to F5OS-A 1.7.0 or later or F5OS-C 1.8.0 or later.

bugs.title: Boot marker logs do not provide enough information
bugs.symptoms: Boot marker logs should provide version and product information in the log.
bugs.conditions: After a reboot.
bugs.impact: It can be difficult to determine which version of VELOS a system was booting into.
bugs.fix: The boot marker logs were updated to show product and OS version information.

bugs.title: System generated events will be logged in platform.log, which is sent to remote logging
bugs.symptoms: All the system-generated events are displayed using "show system events" and these events were not sent to remote logging.
bugs.workaround: All the system events are logged and displayed using "show system events" and the system alarms are displayed using "show system alarms".
bugs.fix: The system events are logged in platform.log. The platform.log has the capability to send it for remote logging.

bugs.title: Correcting /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh script
bugs.symptoms: /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh was wrongly run inside the OMD container. This needs to be run from host-os to collect the correct status.
bugs.impact: /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh script was wrongly run.
bugs.workaround: The script was corrected to run from host-os.
bugs.fix: Corrected /etc/etcd/dump_etcd.sh to run from host-os to collect the correct status.

bugs.title: Updating libraries on F5OS-C to resolve CVEs
bugs.symptoms: F5OS-C 1.5.0 is vulnerable to the following CVEs: These CVEs affect the following packages: url-parse shell-quote merge-deep minimist json-schema eventsource node-tar LibSass serialize-javascript Ramda immer object-path
bugs.impact: F5OS-C 1.5.0 is affected by the listed CVEs.
bugs.fix: Dependencies have been upgraded to non-vulnerable versions.

bugs.title: Intermittent ingress broadcast traffic failure for tenants on shared VLAN
bugs.symptoms: Traffic on the affected VLAN does not function correctly. Affected tenants are able to respond to ARP requests or other broadcast traffic. Pings may intermittently fail. On an affected F5OS rSeries appliance, even though the VLAN is shared between multiple tenants, the VLAN is missing from the software rebroadcaster, as observed by looking at: docker exec system_tmstat_zmq tmctl -Sd blade rbcast_vlan_stat
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple tenants configured with access to the same VLAN. -- The VLAN is assigned to multiple interfaces, and then removed from one interface.
bugs.impact: Traffic on the affected VLAN does not function correctly. Inbound broadcast traffic is not delivered to tenants.
bugs.workaround: If a system is already affected, remove the VLAN from the interface or trunk, and then re-add it.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Tenant health in the partition shows additional entries that are not part of the tenant configuration
bugs.symptoms: When the admin upgrades the system software from 1.3.x to 1.5.0, the platform updates the tenant's table with additional entries that are not running as part of the tenant's original configuration.
bugs.conditions: Power cycle or system software upgrades from 1.3.x to 1.5.0.
bugs.impact: There will not be any impact on the critical functionality of the tenant, and traffic continues to work. However, it does show some unwanted information in the health which could be confusing.
bugs.workaround: Toggling the affected tenant's running state from "Deployed" to "Provisioned" and back to "Deployed" will fix the state of the tenant in the table.
bugs.fix: During the power cycle/system upgrade, the platform re-populates the tenant oper status from Openshift and publishes it to Partition. If the REST response of the tenants from Openshift is incomplete, the platform is populating entries under the wrong key/value. As a result, the partition tenant's table ends up with some unwanted entries. It is a cosmetic issue and will not impact any tenants.

bugs.title: Upgrading to F5OS-A v1.3.1 requires increasing the minimum tenant Virtual Disk Size to 77GB from 76GB of to allow editing of existing tenants in the webUI
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to F5OS-A v1.3.1 from an earlier version, when you attempt to edit the attributes and parameters of an existing tenant, the Save button on the screen will not become selectable.
bugs.conditions: Applies to upgrading from an earlier F5OS-A version to F5OS-A v1.3.1 and preexisting configured, provisioned, or deployed tenants are present.
bugs.impact: If the Virtual Disk Size for any of the preexisting tenants is not increased to a minimum Virtual Disk Size of 77GB you will be unable to edit and save the tenant configuration via the webUI.
bugs.workaround: Increase the minimum tenant Virtual Disk Size to 77GB on the Add/Edit Tenant screen in addition to any other configuration elements and the Save button will become enabled. Alternatively, tenants can be edited via the CLI interface.
bugs.fix: Subsequent versions of F5OS will provide an inline validation warning that will be displayed near the Virtual Disk Size webUI element calling attention that the Virtual Disk Size minimum is insufficient if it is set to any value below 77GB.

bugs.title: 'system aaa' command in ConfD fails with "Error: application communication failure"
bugs.symptoms: -- System fails to change password and renders system in a degraded state where user management no longer works. -- System fails to provide proper user feedback to the user about failed password changes. As per testing, user password change either times out or fails with application communication failure, depending on 'system aaa password-policy config retries' value. When 'system aaa password-policy config retries 0' -> the error is "application timeout". When 'system aaa password-policy config retries 3' -> the error is "application communication failure". Note : On 1.5.0, the issue is fixed when 'retries' value is configured for values equal or greater than 2
bugs.conditions: Changing 'system aaa password-policy config retries' from the default
bugs.impact: F5OS user password cannot be changed.
bugs.workaround: Change 'system aaa password-policy config retries' back to the default: system aaa password-policy config retries 3

bugs.title: The "test media" option during USB install may be interrupted by the hardware watchdog
bugs.symptoms: During USB booting there is an option for "Test this media & install F5OS". If this is selected then the system verifies the media for only 5 minutes before the hardware watchdog reboots the device and the verification is interrupted.
bugs.conditions: USB booting, "test media" option selected.
bugs.impact: The "test media" option does not work.

bugs.title: Radius server secret key should not be empty
bugs.symptoms: When setting up a Radius server without specifying a secret key, an entry for the server is made that has a missing secret key, thus it creates an invalid configuration file.
bugs.conditions: Normal
bugs.impact: The system has an invalid configuration.
bugs.workaround: Don't make an entry without a secret key.
bugs.fix: In the fixed version, if no secret key is entered, then the configuration files are not generated.

bugs.title: Radius server secret-key should not be empty
bugs.symptoms: On add server screen of radius server group, the secret key field is not a mandatory field, which allows the user to add a server without any secret key.
bugs.conditions: User created a server group of type radius and tries to add a server in that group.
bugs.impact: If no secret key is provided by user as the field is not mandatory, the timeout value is read as a secret key for server, which is not correct.
bugs.workaround: User can provide a secret key even though it is not mandatory on the webUI.
bugs.fix: Secret key field is made a mandatory field now, so the user must enter a secret key before saving the form.

bugs.title: "Warning: Invalid HW_TYPE_MINOR: 01." is observed in BIOS banner during the controller restart
bugs.symptoms: A warning occurs, "Warning: Invalid HW_TYPE_MINOR: 01.", in the BIOS banner.
bugs.conditions: A system controller (CX16xx variant only) that is at hardware minor type of 01 with a BIOS earlier than BIOS version 2.03.171.1
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Only the warning in the banner.
bugs.workaround: Requires a BIOS update to BIOS version 2.03.171.1 or later
bugs.fix: The HW_TYPE_MINOR of 01 is supported in BIOS version 2.03.171.1 and later. With this BIOS version there is no warning in the BIOS banner.

bugs.title: Tenants fail to start after bare metal install
bugs.symptoms: If the system reboots without an ISO imported after bare metal install, it will try to set up the port 2000 registry as a mirror of itself, which is not correct and results in the registry being empty. Because of this, the tenants are not being deployed.
bugs.conditions: In bare metal install ISO is not imported.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not deploy.
bugs.workaround: Import the version of the ISO that matches the version of the image used to perform the bare metal installation.
bugs.fix: When patch release is being installed, the correct 'active version of services' is taken which makes the registry not empty. Hence the tenants will be deployed without any issue.

bugs.title: Inactivity-timeout for Console
bugs.symptoms: Console session is not expiring after certain time.
bugs.conditions: Log into system using console. This console session will remain active for a long time.
bugs.impact: Log into system using console. This console session will remain active for a long time.
bugs.fix: We have introduced timeout API for console and ssh connection timeout. If a session is active longer than its configured timeout value and has had no interactions, then that session will be automatically terminated. appliance-1(config)# system settings config sshd-idle-timeout 40 appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1# show system settings state system settings state sshd-idle-timeout 40

bugs.title: F5OS installer does not indicate progress or completion state
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS installer does not indicate the process or completion state of upgrade/installation.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade/reboot the system.
bugs.impact: You are unable to identify the readiness state of system.
bugs.fix: The upgrade, installation or initialization detail is now included in the system's bash prompt.

bugs.title: New role named "user" with read-only access to non-sensitive system level data
bugs.symptoms: To meet security requirements, you need to create a user account on F5OS that cannot access sensitive data, such as platform logs, system events, login activities, and more.
bugs.conditions: Create user account with roles available on the F5OS using the following CLI command: system aaa authentication users user <user_name> config role <role_name>
bugs.impact: F5OS is unable to meet defined security requirements.
bugs.fix: A new user role named “user” is provided on F5OS to have a role with no access to the sensitive data such as platform logs, system events, and login activities and meet security requirements.

bugs.title: Race condition in platform bringup can result in incorrect Openshift images in local registry after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade to F5OS-C controller OS version 1.5.x, it is possible for the docker registry from which the Openshift platform pulls container images to have the wrong contents. This can result in necessary images to be missing from the registry, and lead to failures in Openshift cluster bringup after a cluster re-install.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading F5OS-C controller OS from a pre-1.5.x version to 1.5.x and triggering a cluster re-install after upgrade.
bugs.impact: Openshift cluster does not come up after re-install.
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove the controller ISO version used to USB install the system. This version can be determined by running the following in a bash shell on either system controller: grep ^version: /var/platform-services/VERSION | cut -d' ' -f2 2. Reboot both system controllers.
bugs.fix: Fix for race condition in platform bringup that can result in incorrect Openshift images in local registry after upgrade.

bugs.title: LACPD fails to read system-priority at container starting time
bugs.symptoms: Error logs occur when LACPD starts.
bugs.conditions: Occurs every time LACPD starts up.
bugs.impact: User is not able to configure system-priority and the system-priority remains with the default value.
bugs.fix: LACPD is now able to read system-priority properly. User is able to configure system-priority and see the field in the CLI.

bugs.title: F5OS - "system config hostname" change not reflected in SNMP MIB
bugs.symptoms: Configure hostname using CLI: appliance-1(config)# system config hostname <name> appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. Check system name in SNMPv2-MIB: appliance-1# show running-config SNMPv2-MIB system sysName SNMPv2-MIB system sysName appliance-1.chassis.local Hostname configuration is not reflecting to SNMPv2-MIB.
bugs.conditions: Configure hostname using CLI: appliance-1(config)# system config hostname <name> appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. Check system name in SNMPv2-MIB: appliance-1# show running-config SNMPv2-MIB system sysName SNMPv2-MIB system sysName appliance-1.chassis.local Hostname configuration is not reflecting to SNMPv2-MIB.
bugs.impact: Configured hostname will not be synced in SNMPv2-MIB.
bugs.workaround: Configure same hostname for SNMPv2-MIB: appliance-1(config)# SNMPv2-MIB system sysName f5-stsu-kzps appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1# show running-config SNMPv2-MIB system sysName SNMPv2-MIB system sysName f5-stsu-kzps
bugs.fix: Hostname synced with SNMPv2-MIB sysName.

bugs.title: Terminal window not reflecting configured hostname
bugs.symptoms: The title of the terminal window does not have the configured hostname. Currently, all open windows with root login either from PuTTY or any application display as appliance-1.
bugs.conditions: Connecting to the device using ssh clients like PuTTY.
bugs.impact: This causes difficulty for a user trying to juggle multiple open SSH sessions during a maintenance window.

bugs.title: WebUI server error when opening entry for added NTP server created with FQDN
bugs.symptoms: When the user creates an NTP server with FQDN, the NTP server data table on the time settings screen shows the resolved IP address instead of the FQDN. If the user clicks on the hyperlinked IP address in order to launch the edit screen for the NTP server, the webUI throws an error as a record with the IP address is not found.
bugs.conditions: For an NTP server created with FQDN.
bugs.impact: The edit screen for the NTP server does not launch.
bugs.workaround: If the user replaces the IP address in the browser URL with the FQDN of the NTP server, they are able to view the Edit screen and make the required changes.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next tenant configuration defaults to 15GB virtual disk size upon creation
bugs.symptoms: When initially configuring a BIG-IP Next tenant, the virtual disk size always defaults to 15GB regardless of whether you specify a larger size at the time of initial creation.

bugs.impact: The issue requires you to subsequently edit the tenant's configuration, specify the desired virtual disk size, and to save the changes.
bugs.workaround: Change the tenant's state to Configured, edit the tenant's virtual disk size to the desired value, save the tenant's configuration changes and redeploy.

bugs.conditions: Use the AOM command menu "I --- Display chassis information" option to report the current serial console baud rate configuration.
bugs.impact: Use the AOM command menu "I --- Display chassis information" option to report the current serial console baud rate configuration.
bugs.fix: The current serial console baud rate configuration can be reported by the AOM command menu "I --- Display chassis information" option.

bugs.conditions: When changing password at the time of first SSH login. bugs.impact: No impact on any of the features due to this issue. The user just needs to log in again with the changed password as the current SSH session will be closed after password change.

bugs.title: Adding or removing nodes from a running BIG-IP tenant instance can cause data plane and management IP access issues
bugs.symptoms: If nodes are added to the tenant, then tenant management IP may bounce between nodes of a tenant instance. There may also be data plane issues where traffic will not be routed to the nodes added to an existing tenant instance. This occurs because the slot masks are not being updated in the existing tenant instances.
bugs.conditions: - Nodes are added or removed from a BIG-IP tenant instance on F5OS.
bugs.impact: Data plane traffic may be impacted, and management access to the tenant IP may be unreliable.
bugs.workaround: - If the node population of a tenant has already been modified, then as a workaround configure the tenant to provisioned and then back to deployed. This will restart all the tenant instances and make the node masks consistent across all instances. If a node population change is planned, then the as a workaround configure the tenant to provisioned, configure the different node population on the tenant and then configure back to deployed.
bugs.fix: Dynamic updates of the node population are allowed.

bugs.title: During an upgrade from 1.3 to 1.5.1, a core file may be created from the diag-agent
bugs.symptoms: A core file can be generated by the diag-agent during the upgrade process from 1.3 to 1.5.1.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade of F5OS-C from 1.3 to 1.5.1.
bugs.impact: A Linux core file is generated by the diag-agent service. The service will automatically restart. No functional impact is visible.
bugs.workaround: No workaround; the service will restart automatically and function normally.

bugs.title: The root-causes of F5OS upgrade compatibility check failures are hidden in /var/log/sw-util.log.
bugs.symptoms: When performing a live upgrade, if the upgrade compatibility check fails, users can only see "System database upgrade compatibility check failed" error message. The applicable information about what failed is neither displayed nor shown in platform.log/velos.log.
bugs.conditions: 1. Perforrm a live-upgrade. 2. If the upgrade compatibility check fails, users can only see "System database upgrade compatibility check failed" error message. The applicable information about what failed is neither displayed nor shown in platform.log/velos.log.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failure logs are not logged in platform.log/velos.log.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed and displays the error scenarios in platform.log/velos.log.

bugs.title: RADIUS remote authentication uses internal system IP address as system identifier in requests
bugs.symptoms: When configured for RADIUS remote authentication, the F5OS systems send internal system IP address as Network Access Server (NAS) system identifier (NAS-IP-Address or NAS-IPv6-Address), rather than a system management IP. On VELOS systems, the NAS-IPv6-Address will be a link-local IPv6 address in fe80::/64. On rSeries appliances, the NAS-IP-Address will be an address in the internal address range (RFC6598 by default), e.g. 100.65.60.2.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS remote authentication for system users.
bugs.impact: RADIUS authentication servers may ignore or reject authentication requests due to an unknown system identifier in the requests.

bugs.title: LACP daemon restarts when changing lag-type of the aggregation
bugs.symptoms: LACP daemon restarts. The system will be unable to process LACPDUs until LACP daemon starts up again.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs from changing the lag-type of an aggregation interface that does not have an associated LACP interface.
bugs.impact: All LACP link aggregations may go down and be unable to process traffic for a short time. The down time, if it occurs, should be less than a few seconds.
bugs.workaround: Only change an aggregation's lag-type while an associated LACP interface exists.
bugs.fix: LACP daemon will not restart when changing an aggregation's lag-type while an associated LACP interface does not exist.

bugs.title: Chassis partition ConfD may fail to start completely during controller rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Following a controller rolling upgrade, one or both of the chassis partition controller instances may fail to start completely. This can be seen by running the "show partitions" command. Normal status is that one controller instance will show "running-active" and one will show "running-standby". If any other status is shown (running, offline, failed, or no status), then the database is not operating correctly.
bugs.conditions: At database startup, it is possible for a chassis partition to hang retrieving the database primary key. The presence of this defect confirmed by observing this message at the end of the partition devel.log file: ERR> 6-Jan-2023::17:51:49.205 partition1 confd[109]: confd encryptedStrings command timed out after 300000 ms inactivity
bugs.impact: One or both instances of the chassis partition control plane are not operating. This will prevent the chassis partition rolling upgrade, and may stop tenant traffic.
bugs.workaround: If the chassis partition is in this state, it can be recovered by disabling the partition, waiting for both instances to transition to "disabled", and then re-enabling. The error state is unlikely to occur unless the partition startup happens during a controller failover.

bugs.title: Packet loss on VELOS due to congestion caused by interfaces that are down or disabled
bugs.symptoms: An interface that is down or disabled can cause dropped packets on another port due to internal congestion. This leads to bi-directional packet loss that affects tenants. The packet drops due to VOQ congestion can be seen in the vqf_voq tmctl table in the cos_fill_drop column.
bugs.conditions: VELOS chassis. One or more interfaces on a blade in a partition is down or disabled. Packets generated internally like lldp packets being sent to a down or disabled interface.
bugs.impact: Congestion occurs, which causes packet loss that also affects tenants.
bugs.workaround: The mitigation is to disable sources of internally generated packets which are sent to a down or disabled interface. This can be done by disabling LLDP on a down or disabled interface.
bugs.fix: This change will disable queueing packets to a down or disabled interface queue. This will prevent the internal congestion and dropped packets.

bugs.title: Disabling Basic Authentication does not block the RESTCONF GET requests
bugs.symptoms: When basic authentication is disabled by user, RESTCONF GET requests are not getting blocked.
bugs.conditions: User disables basic authentication. RESTCONF GET requests never get blocked.
bugs.impact: No effect on configuration. Some of the APIs data will be displayed in RESTCONF GET requests, even when basic authentication is disabled.
bugs.fix: The GET operation for the APIs has been blocked when basic authentication is disabled.

bugs.title: The default value of virtual disk size is 77GB and user is not allowed to have a tenant with disk size smaller than 77GB on the webUI
bugs.symptoms: Depending on the tenant image type, the virtual disk requirements vary. Although the user can make necessary changes if the required disk size is greater than 77GB, they cannot make it lesser than 77GB on the webUI.
bugs.conditions: Deploying a tenant with image types that have virtual disk size requirement lesser than 77GB, such as T1 and T2 type images.
bugs.impact: The tenant will be not deployed with the virtual disk size as required for the tenant.
bugs.workaround: Users can edit the tenant from the CLI and update the virtual disk size as required, and can manage this tenant from the CLI.
bugs.fix: With the fix, there will be no inline validation for lower or upper limit on the Virtual Disk Size input field on the webUI form, and the default value is set to 0. If and when the configuration is saved with the default value, it will scale up to the minimum default Virtual Disk space required for that specific image.

bugs.title: Unable to remove unused ISOs or services if used by openshift
bugs.symptoms: Even if an imported version of a controller service says it is not in use in ConfD, it is possible under certain conditions for Openshift to still depend on that version of services. In such cases, it will not be possible to remove that version of services until Openshift is re-installed.
bugs.conditions: Openshift was rebuilt on a version of the controller OS earlier than 1.5.0, and user attempts to remove services that openshift relies on after rebuild.
bugs.impact: Unable to remove some ISOs and services that indicate they are unused.
bugs.workaround: Rebuild openshift cluster.
bugs.fix: Added more informative removal messages for case where removal is blocked due to openshift usage.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next fails to come up intermittently upon system power cycle/reboot
bugs.symptoms: Every tenant gets its own storage space and F5OS applies the right permissions for BIG-IP Next to access the necessary paths to generate certs/database/etc. When the system goes for a reboot, F5OS will have to remount the storage path from volume. But when it does, F5OS is skipping those permissions back, hence tenant containers are failing to access the path and go for a crash loop.
bugs.conditions: When the system goes for power cycle or blade reboot.
bugs.impact: The tenant will not be available functionally or pass any traffic since the majority of containers are in the restart loop due to permission issues.
bugs.workaround: Please run the following commands from the blade shell setfacl -Rdm u:7053:rwx /mnt/disks/<tenant-name>/ setfacl -Rm u:7053:rwx /mnt/disks/<tenant-name>/
bugs.fix: Containers and pods.

bugs.title: F5OS dashboard in webUI displays the system root file system usage, not the entire disk
bugs.symptoms: The Dashboard page displays disk usage information that can be misleading. For example, on an r5900 the following information may be shown: Storage Capacity: 109.4GB System Storage Free: 89.1GB System Storage Used: 15% However, the storage capacity is a value taken from the root (/) filesystem. It does not represent the entire 800GB disk, and does not show information about the file systems where tenant images reside.
bugs.conditions: View Dashboard page in webUI.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.workaround: Linux commands such as "df -hl -t ext4" will provide detailed information about disk usage. Another breakdown of the disk partition use can also be seen using "lsblk /dev/nvme0n1". Note that nvme0n1 is the physical disk of interest. Example from rSeries appliance: # lsblk /dev/nvme0n1 NAME MAJ:MIN RM SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINT nvme0n1 259:0 0 683.5G 0 disk |-nvme0n1p1 259:1 0 1G 0 part /boot/efi |-nvme0n1p2 259:2 0 1G 0 part /boot |-nvme0n1p3 259:3 0 455.3G 0 part | `-partition_tenant-root 253:2 0 455.3G 0 lvm /var/F5/system/cbip-disks |-nvme0n1p4 259:4 0 113.9G 0 part | `-vdo_vol 253:3 0 227.7G 0 vdo | `-partition_image-export_chassis 253:4 0 227.7G 0 lvm /var/export/chassis

[root@controller-1 ~]# oc get pods -n partition-3 --token="`cat /tmp/omd/tokens/partition-3/tokens/partition-3-saToken`" No resources found. error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized) [root@controller-1 ~]#

bugs.title: Persistent alarm for "Fault detected in PSU controller health" due to PSU I2C fault in VELOS PSU controller runtime status
bugs.symptoms: The two PSU controllers in a VELOS 8-slot chassis are redundant. Both PSU controllers have access to a shared I2C bus connected to the 4 power supplies. The AOM on the active controller selects one of the 2 PSU controllers to use for PSU management and directs all PSU accesses through that PSU controller. When a PSU controller indicates a runtime fault, then the AOM fails over to using the other PSU controller. The PSU controller runtime status fault is recorded in the event log and asserts an alarm. Unfortunately, this behavior leaves an active alarm for the PSU controller reporting a runtime status fault once it occurs. That PSU controller is no longer being used for PSU management, thus there is no opportunity for it to clear its own reported PSU I2C fault. The associated alarm remains active indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: When a VELOS PSU controller indicates a runtime status fault, then the AOM fails-over to using the other PSU controller. The PSU controller runtime status fault is recorded in the event log and asserts an alarm.
bugs.impact: No system impact is expected because the two PSU controllers are redundant. The active alarm for a VELOS PSU controller runtime status fault may persist indefinitely because that PSU controller is no longer being used for PSU management.
bugs.workaround: The PSU controller reporting a persistent alarm for a runtime status fault can be reset to clear the alarm. Log in to a controller as the root user and execute either of these two commands at the host prompt. For PSU controller 1: docker exec -it platform-hal psf call POST:lop/object/reset-device destSlot=PsuCtrl1 device=Vpc For PSU controller 2: docker exec -it platform-hal psf call POST:lop/object/reset-device destSlot=PsuCtrl2 device=Vpc
bugs.fix: Fixes to this issue are available with VELOS PSU controller firmware v2.00.806.0.1 and later: - Automatically expire a PSU controller's PSU I2C fault runtime status fault after 120 seconds, so that the persistent alarm is cleared - Increase the PSU I2C fault threshold from 5 to 10 consecutive faults, to reduce the chance of an unnecessary occurrence - Write a PEL (to both CC-LOPs) on assertion and deassertion of PSU I2C channel runtime status errors, to assist with trouble-shooting similar issues

bugs.title: QKView is not collecting core files in /var/crash
bugs.symptoms: QKView was designed to collect core files in /var/core only. The operating system kernel can create core files in /var/crash. SEs need to know about these files.
bugs.conditions: OS kernel creates a core file.
bugs.impact: Core file not collected by QKView.
bugs.workaround: Core file can be manually copied from /var/crash.
bugs.fix: QKView takes a directory listing from /var/crash and collects core files in that directory.

bugs.title: Neighbor interface description is not updated in LLDP neighbor details
bugs.symptoms: Port Description TLV is not displayed under LLDP interface neighbors.
bugs.conditions: 1) enable LLDP on device and on switch 2) enable port description TLV 3) set port description on interface in switch side
bugs.impact: No impact.
bugs.fix: Fixed code to display port description.

bugs.title: HAL message output for non-existing blade in velos.log
bugs.symptoms: LOP RX timeout error messages seen in velos.log for non-existing blade.
bugs.conditions: As part of background-monitoring, we are running a task to monitor the power on hours of each blade. This task is creating the errors in velos.log.
bugs.impact: Error messages will be logged in velos.log once in every hour.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: LopBladePresentNotification is sending slotID as 1 based index, which causes the monitoring of the subsequent blade, as diag-agent expects it to be 0 based index. Updated LopBladePresentNotification to 0 based index.

bugs.title: exclude-cores "true" option still includes the core files in webUI/CLI
bugs.symptoms: Collecting a QKView with "exclude-cores true" results in a QKView that still has core files in it.
bugs.conditions: If QKView is collected with "exclude core true" option.
bugs.impact: Core files are not excluded part of QKView file.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround as cores files always included with any option.
bugs.fix: As "exclude-core" is a boolean type, modified the qkview.sh scripts to pass actual value as user entered.

bugs.title: Blade reporting VQF and VOQ packet drops as errors
bugs.symptoms: VQF and VOQ packet drops are being reported as errors. These are relatively normal occurrences.
bugs.conditions: No particular conditions.
bugs.impact: This accumulation of errors from drops causes the blade to be unnecessarily flagged as unhealthy. This can create confusion as to whether the blade is operating normally or not.
bugs.fix: Dropped VQF and VOQ packets are now notices, instead of errors. This prevents the blade from being put in an unhealthy state.

bugs.title: Invalid L4 checksum packet drop in ATSE
bugs.symptoms: Small number of L4 checksum drops reported in NETC_L4C_DRPS counters on all 4 NETC lanes. The L4 checksum drops were found to be invalid.
bugs.conditions: This can happen any time L4 checksum validation FPGA offload is enabled.
bugs.impact: Small number of valid packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Logic issue was fixed in this bitfile update. Refer to Bug ID 1259493.
bugs.fix: There was a flow control logic issue in the pipeline among the modules in the VQF FPGA. The logic is fixed in Bitfile v8.9.5.9 and all the new VQF bitfiles.

bugs.title: The set-password action now reports a 'success' message
bugs.symptoms: When a user sets a password via the set-password action, no response is returned when the operation is successful.
bugs.conditions: A user sets a password via the CLI or REST API.
bugs.impact: It is unclear if the operation is successful so a user may try to 'commit' the changes or retry the command.
bugs.fix: F5OS now reports a 'success' message when a password is set to indicate no further action must be taken.

bugs.title: Memory capacity and utilization details are confusing / misleading
bugs.symptoms: The memory statistics do not provide a clear or accurate representation of the total memory and how it is being utilized.
bugs.conditions: Using ConfD to retrieve information about memory capacity and utilization.
bugs.impact: There are no clear, easy-to-understand statistics for memory capacity and utilization.
bugs.fix: More detailed, granular memory statistics are provided to give user a clear understanding of total memory and how it is being used.

bugs.title: Modification of STP path cost with value 0 on appliance/chassis does not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: User is allowed to set path cost as 0 but it does participate in port role selection. > Port role is dependent on path cost; port with lesser path cost becomes root. > In the current issue, though port has a lesser value of path cost (0), it is not becoming root.
bugs.conditions: STP is enabled on F5OS enabled platforms and > Path cost of any of the interface is set to some number > One of the interface has default value or value 0.
bugs.impact: Interface with path-cost as 0 does not become root or it does not restrict user to set path cost value as 0.
bugs.workaround: Don not keep path-cost value as 0.
bugs.fix: > Default value of path-cost is modified to 1. > Range of the path-cost is updated, it starts from 1 instead of 0.

bugs.title: F5OS OID SNMPv2-MIB::sysDescr provides meaningless information for system controller
bugs.symptoms: After setting up snmpwalk on older version and live upgrading to another version, the snmpwalk is still showing older service version.
bugs.conditions: 1. configure SNMP 2. upgrade system with live upgrade 3. check system version using SNMPv2-MIB::sysDescr (it will be pointing to older version) example: SNMPv2-MIB::sysDescr.0 = STRING: Linux 3.10.0-1160.62.1.F5.1.el7_8.x86_64 : Appliance services version <older_version>
bugs.impact: sysDescr will be displaying older version.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in latest release.

bugs.title: Issue when Management IP address is configured to have public internet access on F5OS
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS webUI allows web crawlers access to all content when the Management IP address is configured to have public internet access.
bugs.conditions: If the Management IP address is configured to have public internet access.
bugs.impact: This impedes the ability to satisfy internal security compliance mandates.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate the issue, you can manipulate the contents of the robots.txt file inside the webUI container as demonstrated below: $ ssh root@10.238.160.60 root@10.238.160.60's password: [root@appliance-1 ~]# docker exec -it vanquish-gui bash [root@d6303361e100 /]# cd /app/build [root@d6303361e100 build]# echo "User-agent: *" > robots.txt [root@d6303361e100 build]# echo "Disallow: /" >> robots.txt [root@d6303361e100 build]# cat robots.txt User-agent: * Disallow: / [root@d6303361e100 build]# exit exit [root@appliance-1 ~]# exit logout Connection to 10.238.160.60 closed.
bugs.fix: Robots.txt now disallows web crawlers access to any content.

bugs.title: Not allowing special characters "/*!<>^,/" in SNMP community/user/target name
bugs.symptoms: Currently, we are allowing all characters to configure SNMP community/target/user. Because of that someone can use this configuration to inject script and system can be compromised.
bugs.conditions: Try to configure SNMP community/target/user with below command: r10900-1(config)# system snmp communities community <script>alert(1)</script config security-model v2c r10900-1(config-community-<script>alert(1)</script)# commit Commit complete. r10900-1(config-community-<script>alert(1)</script)# r10900-1# show running-config system snmp system snmp engine-id config value mac system snmp communities community <script>alert(1)</script config security-model [ v2c ]
bugs.impact: We are allowing all characters to configure SNMP community/target/user. Because of that someone can use this configuration to inject script and system can be compromised.
bugs.fix: We are restricting special characters /*!<>^,/ (identified as invalid input) as SNMP community/target/user name configuration. Note: Upgrade will fail if user already has SNMP configuration with restricting special characters /*!<>^,/

bugs.title: F5OS systems send incomplete DDoS stats response to the tenants
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP tenants on F5OS systems receive incomplete/corrupted DDOS stats response, which leads to TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: Undetermined circumstances on a BIG-IP tenant with AFM provisioning.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes on the tenant, which affects application traffic. Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes.

bugs.title: sPVA hardware offload not working correctly on r10k
bugs.symptoms: The DOS attack traffic is distributed unevenly on different TMMs, and some DOS attack traffic is not handed off to hardware due to a misconfigured DOS group.
bugs.conditions: Any DOS vector traffic going through the r10k device
bugs.impact: Reduced performance for DOS attack and hardware offload is not active.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for older F5OS releases. Need to upgrade to any latest F5OS version from F5OS-A 1.6.0 or later.
bugs.fix: Implemented per ATSE DOS group support in F5OS that enables DOS group configuration at individual hardware offload engines.

bugs.title: Authentication fails via the webUI when “:” is at the end or beginning of the password
bugs.symptoms: After modifying the user's password to include ":" either at the beginning or the end of the password, the user is not able to log in via the webUI. The user is able to log in via the CLI (SSH).
bugs.conditions: The password includes ":" at the beginning or end of the password string.
bugs.impact: User not able to log in via the webUI.
bugs.workaround: Do not use ":" at the beginning or end of the password string. Since it is possible to log in via the CLI, modify the password accordingly.

bugs.title: SNMP OIDs to monitor serial number of the device, type of hardware and hostname
bugs.symptoms: Device serial number, type, and hostname are not available for the SNMP interface.
bugs.conditions: Install the F5OS-A/F5OS-C version and run SnmpWalk. You cannot find the device’s serial number, type, and hostname.
bugs.impact: You are not able to poll for device serial number, type, and hostname through the SNMP interface.
bugs.fix: Added support for device serial number, type, and hostname for SNMP interfaces.

bugs.title: Some firewall rules do not generate denial logs
bugs.symptoms: system_latest_vers network namespaces are disabled by default to prevent host kernel log flooding from inside a container.
bugs.conditions: By default, all network namespace logs are disabled except for init namespace.
bugs.impact: When traffic is denied from an IP, we do not get a message saying traffic from a particular IP is denied.
bugs.workaround: Command to enable system_latest_vers network namespace denial logs: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_log_all_netns=1 (not-persistent) Persistent solution: 1) Create a file: /etc/sysctl.conf 2) Run the command: echo "net.netfilter.nf_log_all_netns = 1" >> /etc/sysctl.conf

bugs.title: tcam-manager may get stuck using 100% CPU
bugs.symptoms: After running a QKView or tcam-dump by itself, tcam-manager does not clean up the diagnostic socket, which results in a tight loop and pegging the CPU at 100% utilization. This in turn starves other platform processes (such as dma-agent), which causes performance degradation.
bugs.conditions: A QKView or tcam-dump, which is included in QKView, is run.
bugs.impact: Performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: The issue can be avoided by not running QKView.
bugs.fix: After tcam-dump completes, the corresponding socket is properly removed.

bugs.title: VELOS system controller fails to PXE boot when network-range-type is RFC1918
bugs.symptoms: If the network-range-type is set to RFC1918, a VELOS system controller will fail to PXE boot from its peer system controller, reporting an error message "Unable to locate configuration file".
bugs.conditions: - The Internal Chassis Networking range (network-range-type) is set to RFC1918 (the default is RFC6598).
bugs.impact: Unable to PXE boot the system controller.
bugs.workaround: Log into the peer controller (the one NOT being PXE booted) as root, and navigate to the /var/images/pxelinux.cfg directory. In the directory, locate the file whose name is six hex characters ("0a", followed by two digits, followed by "07"), and rename the file to uppercase. For example: [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active ~]# cd /var/images/pxelinux.cfg/ [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]# ls -l 0a* -rwxr--r--. 2 root root 352 Oct 7 15:14 0ae107 [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]# mv 0ae107 0AE107 [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]#

bugs.title: FPGA update status in ConfD may show error even though it was successful
bugs.symptoms: The ConfD CLI "show components component blade-N" could show that the update of the FPGA-generated error, even though the FPGA loaded successfully.
bugs.conditions: In very remote cases, when blades are removed and then added back into a chassis, the status may fail to update correctly.
bugs.impact: The error message does not impact the operation of the product.
bugs.workaround: There is currently no way to remove the error message from the ConfD logs unless the chassis is power-cycled.

bugs.title: Once TACACS server-group is configured on a non-default port, on downgrade virt-handler pod gets into a crash loopbackoff state because of SELinux corruption
bugs.symptoms: Virt-handler pod is crashing upon downgrading from F5OS-A 1.4.0 to F5OS-A 1.3.2, and a tenant is stuck in pending state.
bugs.conditions: Configure TACACS server-group on a non-default port (that is, other than port 49) and downgrade from F5OS-A 1.4.0 to F5OS-A 1.3.2.
bugs.impact: Tenant becomes stuck in pending state.
bugs.workaround: Two workarounds: 1. Configure standard port (49) for the TACACS server instead of a non-standard port. Using the standard port should not trigger these issues. Releases older than F5OS-A 1.4.0 do not correctly support any port other than 49 for the TACACS server. 2. Fix SELinux policy on the appliance: a. cp selinux module from /usr cp /usr/etc/selinux/targeted/active/modules/400/f5_appliance to /etc/selinux/targeted/active/modules/400/f5_appliance b. Reboot the device reboot
bugs.fix: Enforce closure of non-standard port every time configuration is updated or system is shut down. This avoids leaving ports open for which SELinux may not have exceptions. Note this does not address the non-standard port in older releases when downgrading. Non-standard ports for TACACS are still not properly supported in the older release.

bugs.title: TPM status may not reporting during PXE install
bugs.symptoms: The tpm-integrity-status parameter may incorrectly be displayed as "Unavailable" when running the ‘show components component platform command’.
