bugs.conditions: When performing a PXE install downgrade, SIRR DB does not persist across OS updates. This leads to mismatch SIRR and BIOS version; SIRR DB may not have the info about the newer BIOS version, causing inconsistencies in TPM validation.
bugs.impact: This may impacting TPM integrity validation.
bugs.workaround: Contact F5 support for further assistance and more details.

bugs.title: Removing or manually adding TLS Certificate & Key on webUI removes whole TLS configuration
bugs.symptoms: Manually adding TLS Certificate & Key on webUI instead of storing through Self-Signed Certificate or removing Certificate & Key removes TLS configuration, which includes verify-client and verify-client-depth.
bugs.conditions: - When there is an existing Verify Client and Client Depth configuration, and user tries to remove TLS Certificate & Key on Certificate Management screen on webUI. - When user fills the TLS Certificate & Key on Certificate Management screen on webUI.
bugs.impact: Verify Client and Client Depth configuration of Certificate Authentication will be changed to default values which disables verification of httpd client certificates.
bugs.workaround: - Remove or Add TLS Certificate & Key through CLI. - While creating Self-Signed Certificate, set "Store TLS" field as true - Re-add Verify Client and Client Depth after removing or manually adding TLS Certificate & Key.

bugs.title: Operational and Configurational prompts do not persist through user sessions
bugs.symptoms: prompt1 (Operational) and prompt2 (Configurational) do not persist over user sessions and logins once configured.
bugs.conditions: Configure both prompts, exit from session and re-login. It can be observed that the configured prompts are reset to default.
bugs.impact: Hard to identify the terminal session without configured prompts when working with multiple terminal sessions with new logins.
bugs.fix: Operational (oper-prompt) and Configurational (config-prompt) prompts can be configured which persist over sessions and logins.

bugs.title: A manual license install does not log success message
bugs.symptoms: When a user is installing a license manually, the manual license installation process does not log the success message in velos.log.
bugs.conditions: Always occurs when license is manually installed.
bugs.impact: Successful installation message is not captured in velos.log.
bugs.fix: Successful log message is captured when license is manually installed.

bugs.title: Notification streams are sometimes empty using 'restconf/streams/platform-stats/json' API endpoint
bugs.symptoms: When using the 'restconf/streams/platform-stats/json' API endpoint, the JSON object could be empty instead of being populated with platform stats.
bugs.conditions: The initial discovery of platform-stat had a logic flaw which prevented drive information from being correctly discovered. This caused the rest of the JSON object from being populated.
bugs.impact: The platform-stats notification stream endpoint would return an empty object instead of platform-stat data.
bugs.fix: The logic flaw has been resolved and the platform-stat notification stream is fully populated with stat information.

bugs.title: WebUI and shell admin access unavailable after upgrade to when one of the previously installed images is no longer present
bugs.symptoms: 1. WebUI or CLI inaccessible via admin account (that is, ConfD is not up): [root@appliance-1(XXXXXXXXX) log]# su admin Failed to connect to server 2. sw-mgmt.debug file will have a line similar to this one (with image version changing depending on which image is missing): DEBUG: Source file /var/export/chassis/import/.mounts/iso/R2R4/1.1.1-9159/m3/*-services/F5OS*.img does not exist, removing from all_sw. 3. Containers stuck in ImagePullBackOff. For example, system_network container cannot be pulled, and the following error is observed in messages log: appliance-1 dockerd-current: time="2023-03-24T15:09:26.631359235Z" level=error msg="Not continuing with pull after error: Error: image system_network:1.4.5-f5os-a-1-4-0-candidate.2023-02-14-15-09-15.S9b340f7e not found" An error message may occur that reads "System database upgrade compatibility check failed"
bugs.conditions: Both of the below conditions: 1. Certain ISO image has been ungracefully removed from the /var/import/staging folder. Examples of ungraceful removals: -- Deleted via bash (after running chattr -i <image name>) -- Image name had parentheses in it and as per ID1273021 it is wiped out upon reboot. 2. /var/import/import.json file includes reference to removed image that is listed BEFORE the reference to currently used image.
bugs.impact: Device webUI is inaccessible. Cannot access ConfD. Root access is working.
bugs.workaround: Two workarounds: 1. Re-import the deleted image and reboot the box. 2. Remove the whole section that references the deleted image from import.json file and reboot the box.

bugs.title: When no parameter is given for 'system aaa tls create-self-signed-cert', encrypted key-type does not ask for passphrase
bugs.symptoms: When requesting a self-signed-cert, if the key-type is encrypted, then a passphrase is required. However, if no parameters are supplied, the key-type is then requested as a mandatory parameter, but won't ask for passphrase if encrypted type is selected.
bugs.conditions: No parameters passed to the config: system aaa tls create-self-signed-cert.
bugs.impact: An error indicates that the passphrase wasn't supplied, but it never was asked for in these conditions.
bugs.workaround: Specify key-type as a parameter and then if encrypted, the passphrase will be requested.
bugs.fix: The key-type is no longer a mandatory field and simply defaults to RSA. There is no conflict with not passing any parameters.

bugs.title: The error message is not correct when enabling client-cert (Client Certificate Authentication) before setting verify-client (Client Certificate Verification) to true
bugs.symptoms: An error on the ConfD CLI occurs when the user tries to enable Client Certificate Authentication before setting Client Certificate Verification to true. The error message given by this condition is not correct.
bugs.conditions: - User trying to enable Client Certificate Authentication when Client Certificate Verification is set to false.
bugs.impact: Due to the incorrect error message, the user is not able to enable Client Certificate Authentication.
bugs.fix: Provide a proper error message when user tries to enable Client Certificate Authentication before setting Client Certificate Verification to true.

bugs.title: Hashed/encrypted passwords are getting logged
Unable to restore backup file containing expired TLS certificate
bugs.symptoms: If a user attempts to restore a configuration backup whose contents include a TLS certificate that has expired, the configuration restore will fail.
bugs.conditions: User attempts to restore a configuration backup file which contains an expired TLS certificate.
bugs.impact: User is unable to restore their backed up configuration.
bugs.workaround: While there is no workaround for the issue, once the backup has been collected, this can be avoided by de-configuring any TLS certificates before collecting a configuration backup, and re-setting them manually after the configuration backup has been restored.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where configuration backup files containing expired TLS certificates could not be successfully used for configuration restore.

bugs.title: Users are seeing prompt cannot identify you when password expires.
bugs.symptoms: When a user uses SSH to connect to the system with an expired password, the system will show a prompt indicating it cannot identify the user.
bugs.conditions: User's password has expired.
bugs.impact: Only users whose password has expired. Impact is negligible.
bugs.workaround: Reset password.
bugs.fix: The behavior is controlled through nss-pam-ldapd interactions with sshd. Now users will see the correct message indicating that the password has expired.

bugs.title: Some aggregation interface names can cause ethernet interfaces in LACP aggregations to be erroneously down
bugs.symptoms: One or more interfaces in LACP aggregations may be considered down when they should not be.
bugs.conditions: Internally, LACPD hashes interfaces to an integer, and some aggregation interface names hash will collide with ethernet interface name hash. Changes to the these aggregation interfaces can impact the ethernet interface.
bugs.impact: Traffic through the affected ethernet interface in LACP aggregations may be disrupted. This can cause either degraded performance or traffic failure for LACP aggregations that the interface is a member of.
bugs.workaround: Only use aggregation interface names that don't hash to the same port numbers as ethernet interfaces. In order to determine if an existing aggregation interfaces port number conflicts with an ethernet interface, review the lacpd_interface_stat table. For a VELOS partition, use the lacpd container on any blade in the partition to run tmctl. For an appliance, use system_lacpd container to run tmctl. The following example from a rSeries appliance shows the aggregation interface "vlag" with the same port number as interface 1.0 [root@appliance-1 ~]# docker exec -it system_lacpd bash [root@appliance-1 partition]# tmctl lacpd_interface_stat -s name,port_num name port_num ---- -------- 1.0 1024 10.0 10240 2.0 2048 3.0 3072 4.0 4096 5.0 5120 6.0 6144 7.0 7168 8.0 8192 9.0 9216 mgmt 43008 vlag 1024 If an aggregation interface hashes to the same port number an Ethernet interface: 1. Delete the conflicting aggregation interface 2a. You can either restart the lacpd containers or 2b. Reboot the appliance, or for VELOS reboot each blade in the partition.
bugs.fix: Aggregation interface names will never impact ethernet interfaces in a LACP aggregation.

bugs.title: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces when virtual wire is enabled
bugs.symptoms: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces although virtual wire is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1) Enable virtual wire on interface. 2) Attach interfaces to a lag. 3) Enabled LLDP on the interfaces.
bugs.impact: When virtual wire is enabled, BIG-IP will function in transparent mode and is not expected to see interfaces on either side. With this issue, F5 interfaces will be visible when LLDP is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure LLDP on the interfaces when virtual wire is enabled.

bugs.title: Error logs while generating the qkview
bugs.symptoms: System logs following errors under platform.log while capturing qkview --- 2023-04-09T13:21:23.774606+00:00 appliance-1 tcam-manager[78]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6b01000000000007 msg="ERROR" MSG="handle_dbg_cmd_snapshot: bad tcam id 2". 2023-04-09T13:21:32.905003+00:00 appliance-1 tcam-manager[78]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6b01000000000007 msg="ERROR" MSG="handle_dbg_cmd_snapget: bad row id 512". ---
bugs.conditions: Generating a qkview
bugs.impact: The errors are false alarms, they don't have any functional impact.

bugs.title: ISO with special characters in name will not import
bugs.symptoms: An ISO named with special characters like "()" will not be imported and gets deleted from the import directory silently.
bugs.conditions: Only when the ISO name contains special characters.
bugs.impact: User will not have any status on the imported image with a name that contains special characters.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The "show system image" API will display the status as "Import error. File name is incorrect."

bugs.title: DAGD component crashes during live upgrade or downgrade
bugs.symptoms: The DAGD component crashes occasionally during live upgrade or downgrade. However, these incidents won't affect the overall system, and the DAGD component will restart automatically without requiring any user action.
bugs.conditions: The DAGD component crashes occur rarely during live upgrade or downgrade.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on the overall health of the system.

bugs.title: Provide ability to manage services through systemd/docker commands from F5OS CLI
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to start/stop/check service status for systemd units or docker containers.
bugs.conditions: -- Confd CLI -- You would like to check status of specific containers
bugs.impact: You are unable to check service status for specific containers.
bugs.fix: You can now start/stop/check service status for systemd services or docker containers: system diagnostics os-utils docker [start|stop|restart] node platform service <name>

bugs.title: Interface vlan configured while corresponding vlans/vlan deleted
bugs.symptoms: When a VLAN is deleted while being referenced by an interface or LAG, it cannot be de-referenced from the interface/LAG.
bugs.conditions: Delete the VLAN before removing the VLAN from the interface.
bugs.impact: Cannot add the interface to a LAG after deleting VLAN(s) that used the interface.
bugs.workaround: Recreate the removed VLAN, then edit the interface which shows defined VLAN, remove the defined VLAN, then remove the recreated VLAN.
bugs.fix: With the fix, the user will be able to view and remove the VLAN in the Add/Edit Interface/LAG screen even if the VLAN was deleted, and thus will be able to detach it from the interface/LAG.

bugs.title: Ability to suppress the proceed warning generated when portgroup mode is changed
bugs.symptoms: When the user commits portgroup mode changes, the system generates a proceed warning to inform the user of the potential consequences.
bugs.conditions: When committing portgroup mode changes.
bugs.impact: While the proceed warning is present, the user needs to input “yes” or “no” before the transaction is committed.
bugs.fix: Now you have the option to suppress the proceed-warning for the entire system. The setting is called portgroup-confirmation-warning and can be disabled in confd with the following command: system settings config portgroup-confirmation-warning off

bugs.title: Display option "universal-time" is not supported
bugs.symptoms: The display option "universal-time" is a built-in third-party command that F5OS does not support.
bugs.conditions: User attempts to access the built-in third-party command "universal-time."
bugs.impact: The correct output for "universal-time" is not displayed. Proper documentation for this third-party command also cannot be found.
bugs.fix: F5OS has suppressed this display option.

bugs.title: Some log messages/timestamps do not observe configured timezone
bugs.symptoms: Some logfiles and timestamps report the time as UTC even when the system is configured with a non-UTC timezone.
bugs.conditions: The orchestration-manager is not aware of the configured timezone, so Openshift/Kubernetes/Ansible log files produced by this component are reported as UTC. Also, the 'user login/last login' times reported by the CLI are always in UTC.
bugs.impact: Difficult to correlate timestamps across log files.
bugs.fix: Orchestration Manager recognizes the current timezone setting, and produces all timestamps as localtime using RFC3339 format (localtime + offset). All debug logfiles produced by this component are now timezone aware. The sshd/login programs report login/last login times as localtime, not UTC. The CLI no longer (incorrectly) reports login time.

bugs.title: Multus ansible-playbook run could hang if blades rebooted
bugs.symptoms: After blades are added to the Openshift cluster, Multus is installed on the blades via an ansible-playbook. If the blade/blades are rebooted during the playbook run, it is possible that the playbook run could hang, possibly for several hours. During this time, the blade will not be available in the Openshift cluster.
bugs.conditions: Adding a new blade, or re-adding an existing blade to the Openshift cluster, and the blade is rebooted during the install of Multus.
bugs.impact: Blade will not be available in the Openshift cluster and will not be able to run tenants.
bugs.workaround: If the blades are rebooted during the Multus install and they do not finishing joining the cluster after reboot, the active CC can fail over, which will cause the blade to be added to the cluster again.
bugs.fix: Orchestration manager has been updated to run the Multus playbook with a hard timeout, after which it will be retried.

bugs.title: Tenant with crypto enabled does not deploy correctly
bugs.symptoms: With crypto enabled, tenant deployment may sometime be in pending state.
bugs.conditions: Randomly during tenant deployment.
bugs.impact: With crypto enabled, tenant deployment may sometime be in pending state.
bugs.workaround: When this issue occurs, the "qat-device-plugin" program automatically restarts and recovers itself.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with qat-device-plugin process. This allowed the tenant to transition to the Running state.

bugs.title: AAA server group Port and Type are not displayed on ConfD
bugs.symptoms: When a server group is created on an F5OS appliance, "show system aaa server-groups" does not display the Port and Type of the server group.
bugs.conditions: When a AAA server group is created (LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS).
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. Port and Type information is not displayed on ConfD: appliance-1# show system aaa server-groups NAME TYPE ADDRESS PORT ------------------------------------------- ldap-group - 10.50.5.25 -
bugs.workaround: The Port and Type information can be viewed via Web UI.

bugs.title: LAG interface status is not updated on the BIG-IP tenant
bugs.symptoms: Symptom 1: Trunk is down in tenant but the LAG is up in F5OS-A. Symptom 2: LAG is down in F5OS-A but the trunk is up in tenant. Symptom 3: LAG is down in VELOS partition but the trunk is always up in tenant.
bugs.conditions: For symptom 1: 1. Set up new rSeries device. 2. Config static LAG and VLAN. 3. Deploy new tenant. 4. In tenant, LAG will be shown as down but interfaces shown as up. 5. This happens only at initial tenant deployment. For symptom 2: 1. LAG is shown as down in F5OS-A. 2. Trunk is shown as up in tenant. For symptom 3: 1. LAG is shown as down in VELOS partition. 2. Trunk is always shown as up in tenant.
bugs.impact: Symptom 1: On r2x00/r4x00 platforms, as LAG will be in DOWN state, datapath will not be working. Symptom 2: On r2x00/r4x00 platforms, LAG status is shown as UP but it's actually DOWN on the platform. Datapath will not be UP, but as LAG is UP in tenant we expect Datapath to be UP. Symptom 3: If trunks are used for HA Group the scores associated to the trunks are not deducted from the overall health scores regardless of whether the interfaces in the trunks are up or not.
bugs.workaround: For symptom 1: Restarting "system_api_svc_gateway" service on host. #docker restart system_api_svc_gateway For symptom 2: Restarting "system_api_svc_gateway" service on host. #docker restart system_api_svc_gateway For symptom 3: Restarting "partition_api_svc_gateway" on blades have no effect. Request an EHF on VELOS controller and partition/s.

bugs.title: When OCSP is disabled, configurations are not accurately shown outside of 'config' mode
bugs.symptoms: When the OCSP feature is disabled, making any changes to OCSP configurations (i.e. nonce request, override-responder) are not being updated outside of 'config' mode on the ConfD CLI. When the OCSP feature is enabled, there is no issue.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when OCSP is set to 'disabled' and changes are made to the OCSP configurations. Running 'show system aaa authentication ocsp' will display incorrect information.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. User will not be able to see an accurate display of the OCSP configurations while the feature is disabled.
bugs.fix: Starting in F5OS 1.8.0, OCSP configurations are accurately displayed even if the feature is disabled.

bugs.title: WebUI header shows FQDN for IP address field instead of management IP
bugs.symptoms: The IP Address field displayed on the login page and on the top section of the GUI displays the hostname, not the IP address.
bugs.conditions: Accessing the F5OS GUI via the FQDN and not the IP address.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on functionality but the FQDN is displayed, not the management IP.
bugs.workaround: To view the management IP address, navigate to the Management IP screen.
bugs.fix: Login using FQDN shows the IP address on the header instead of the FQDN. Additionally, the IP address label on the login screen is renamed to Address.

bugs.title: Ability to change SNMPD listening port
bugs.symptoms: When using default 161 SNMP listening port, user was not able to change/configure this to another port.
bugs.conditions: snmpwalk was working only on default 161 port.
bugs.fix: Added below API to configure SNMP port. Configuration: CLI# system snmp config port <port_num> Show: CLI# show system snmp state port

bugs.title: qkview may capture log files truncated in a reverse way
bugs.symptoms: qkview captures log files, but may truncate them if too large (greater than 100 MB). A regression was introduced such that the most recent log entries would be truncated rather than the oldest.
bugs.conditions: Collection of qkview.
bugs.impact: Log entries may be missing in qkview capture.
bugs.workaround: When running a qkview capture, specify the maxfilesize argument to 1000 (1 GB). system diagnostics qkview capture maxfilesize 1000
bugs.fix: QKview now collects the tail end of log files.

bugs.title: Large core files can cause system instability
bugs.symptoms: When a system generates and stores large core files, it can cause the system unstable.
bugs.conditions: F5OS generates a large core file.
bugs.impact: F5OS core-writing script does not check filesystem availability before writing a core file and can fill up the filesystem, causing catastrophic system instability until disk-space is reclaimed. For more information of other impacts see 1185577 - F5OS-A memory leak in ImageAgent process on rSeries hosts may affect tenant performance or lead to unexpected restarts of tenant or host https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1185577.html 1284705 - Appliance Orchestration Manager core file may consume entire root filesystem https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1284705.html 1290949 - Invalid memory read in appliance orchestration manager https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1290949.html 1327701 - Space in SNMP community/user/target name causing snmpd container restart https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1327701.html
bugs.fix: F5OS now takes into account the available filesystem space before writing a core file. If the core file is too large then it will be truncated and deleted to maintain system stability. The system log message will indicate if the core file was too large to safely write.

bugs.title: Domain Name Service takes more time to come up on bare-metal installation
bugs.symptoms: In case of bare-metal install, initially DNS is not up as port 53 is consumed by named service. While Openshift is initializing, OpenShift resolves the port conflict by restarting the service with different addresses. So the issue won't be observed after a few minutes.
bugs.conditions: Issue won't be seen in a live upgrade. It will be seen only on bare-metal install, during the first few minutes.
bugs.impact: No impact to end user. As issue won't be seen in live upgrade. It will be seen only in the manufacturing stage during the first few minutes.
bugs.workaround: Wait for the openshift cluster to be available; you can check "oc get nodes" to confirm.

bugs.title: Tightening controls on uploading files to F5OS
bugs.symptoms: The File Upload Manager permits arbitrary file types to be uploaded by an admin user.
bugs.conditions: -- Uploading files -- User role is admin
bugs.impact: Arbitrary file types can be uploaded.
bugs.workaround: Do not upload untrusted files to the F5OS system. Reduce access to the management plane to trusted users.
bugs.fix: Only .iso, .os, .img, and .patch files are permitted to be uploaded.

bugs.title: WebUI authentication does not follow best practices in some situations
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, the WebUI interface and RestConf requests do not follow best practices when handling authentication-related requests.
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed.
bugs.impact: Undisclosed.
bugs.workaround: Secure access to the F5OS GUI and expose only to trusted users and networks.
bugs.fix: WebUI and RestConf requests now follow best practices.

bugs.title: Upgrade compatibility issue from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C
bugs.symptoms: As a part of this bug fix: We are not allowing webUI banner text and color detail when webUI banner is disabled. We are only allowing to configure/show webUI banner test and color when webUI banner is enabled. After this fix, We have some upgrade compatibility issue from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C (or latest). If we enable webUI banner without providing values for color and text in 1.6.0-A/C and 1.7.0-C build and if we upgrade to latest version(1.7.0-A build and 1.8.0-C) from 1.6.0-A/C and 1.7.0-C where we cannot enable banner without text, upgrade will fail with compatibility issue.
bugs.conditions: If webUI banner is enabled without text and color details then upgrade from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C will fail with compatibility error.
bugs.impact: We will not be able to upgrade from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C, and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C with webUI banner enabled and color and text fields empty.
bugs.workaround: Either disable the webUI banner or enable the webUI banner with color and text fields.
bugs.fix: We are not allowing webUI banner's text and color details when webUI banner is disabled. We are only allowing to configure/show webUI banner's text and color when webUI banner is enabled.

bugs.title: Syslog target files do not use the hostname configured via system user interface.
bugs.symptoms: Syslog target files, for example: /var/F5/system/log/platform.log, use a fixed nodename (appliance-1) for every device as a hostname.
bugs.conditions: Viewing syslog files, especially on a remote syslog server.
bugs.impact: In a remote log collector, source IPs are the only way to differentiate among devices.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to do an iRule workaround that replaces custom strings in syslog traffic depending on the client's IP address. This iRule is applied to the virtual server on another LTM that consumes the syslog traffic and load balances. when CLIENT_DATA { switch [IP::client_addr] { "10.10.10.10" { UDP::payload replace 38 11 "ABCDC01F5OS01" } "10.10.10.20" { UDP::payload replace 38 11 "ABCDC01F5OS02" } } } Below is the example message after irule workaround. Jul 31 03:33:50 10.10.10.10 2023-07-31T07:33:50.181136+00:00 appliance-1 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 0 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )". to this Jul 31 06:00:01 10.10.10.10 2023-07-31T10:00:01.356324+00:00 ABCDC01F5OS01 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 1 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )". Jul 31 06:00:04 10.10.10.20 2023-07-31T10:00:04.983677+00:00 ABCDC01F5OS02 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 0 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )".
bugs.fix: Infrastructure to use the system hostname user configuration in the syslog target logs has been added with the setting 'system logging config include-hostname'. It is enabled by default, and can be turned off if old behavior is preferred.

bugs.title: Initial Password Settings insufficient for security certifications
bugs.symptoms: When an admin-role user sets another user's password using set-password, the user was not always forced to change their password on first login with the new credentials. Modern security standards all require that users establish their own credentials.
bugs.conditions: If a user set their own initial password, and an admin-role user later changed it to some other value, the user was not always forced to reset it on first use.
bugs.impact: Credentials are not always required to be set upon initial access.
bugs.fix: The 'set-password' command now always resets the password last-change time to zero, which forces a password change on next login.

bugs.title: A remote admin user is not able to enter the ConfD config mode when logged in from SSH
bugs.symptoms: When a remote user's GID is mapped to the F5OS system's local GID, the GID mapping is not parsed correctly by the system. If the remote GID is known to the F5 system, there is no issue. For example, a mapping of the form 9000:9000 works fine. However, mapping of the form 5555:9000, 6666:9000 etc. will not work.
bugs.conditions: Local GID is being mapped to a remote GID.
bugs.impact: The admin user mapped to a remote GID cannot access the ConfD config mode.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Update the system to the version with the fix.

bugs.title: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partition or appliance services from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0
bugs.symptoms: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partitions or appliances from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0. If there are running tenants at the time the downgrade is attempted, it will be blocked.
bugs.conditions: A downgrade of a VELOS partition or rSeries appliance from ISO version 1.6.0+ to <1.6.0 is attempted.
bugs.impact: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' for the downgrade to succeed.
bugs.workaround: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' for the downgrade to succeed.
bugs.fix: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partition or appliance services from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0

bugs.title: Unable to set local user's password if the same user exists on a remote LDAP server
bugs.symptoms: If a user exists locally (in F5OS) as well as on a remote LDAP server, and LDAP-based authentication is configured as an accepted authentication method, attempting to set the user's local password in F5OS will fail. In the ConfD CLI, an error like the following will be observed: syscon-1-active(config)# system aaa authentication users user ldap_user config set-password Value for 'password' (<string>): **************** Error: Rejected, Configured password-policy: min-length:6 required-differences:8 max-letter-repeat:3 policy applies to root:true It should be emphasized that in the case of such duplicate user definitions locally/remotely, the local user's credentials will need to be used to login even if remote authentication is preferred.
bugs.conditions: A user exists locally (in F5OS) as well as on a remote LDAP server, and LDAP-based authentication is configured as an accepted authentication method.
bugs.impact: Unable to set the local user's password.
bugs.workaround: Temporarily remove LDAP as an authentication method, set the user's password, and then re-configure the preferred authentication method(s).
bugs.fix: Fixed issue with setting a local user's password when an identically named user exists on a remote LDAP server and LDAP is enabled as an authentication method

bugs.title: Tcam-manager does not support all the possible system network subnets
bugs.symptoms: The connection from the tenant (TMM) to the tcam-manager is continuously restarts. tcam-mgr logs show the wrong tenant-id and hence rejected connection from the tenant: msg="INFO" MSG="Connection from client address:10.245.3.1". msg="ERROR" MSG=" Confd access error obtaining tenant info for tenant:12291 slot:1". msg="INFO" MSG="neuron_handle_responses: dropping resp to non-existent client". TMM periodically logs neuron client errors, such as: notice hudproxy_neuron_client_closed_cb: Neuron client connection terminated notice pva_sc_frs_neuron_stopped_cb/2373: FRS SC: Neuron client stopped.
bugs.conditions: The 'system network' configuration is changed from its default setting in F5OS to an affected RFC1918 subnet.
bugs.impact: TCAM based features don't work.
bugs.workaround: Select either the default RFC6598 subnet or any of the unaffected RFC1918 subnets (prefix: 0, 4, 8, 12).
bugs.fix: Tcam-manager now correctly calculates the tenant-id for all possible system network subnets.

bugs.title: Implements duplicate port check and fix logic on standby controller
bugs.symptoms: An edge case that duplicates registry causes different controller level images to be incorrect and causes the live upgrade to hang in the standby controller in the middle of the live upgrade.
bugs.conditions: This condition might happen during live upgrade, where the standby was upgraded first. Since it was unable to even deploy services due to the duplicate port conflicting with the active CC services port, it never went active and was never able to fix itself.
bugs.impact: Live upgrade fail on the old standby controller.
bugs.workaround: Please contact F5 Support if this issue occurs. The workaround requires F5 Support to intervene to manually fix the file.
bugs.fix: Fix the duplicate port assignment edge case on standby cc.

bugs.title: A remote LDAP user with an admin role is unable to make config changes through the F5 webUI
bugs.symptoms: When a remote user's GID is mapped to the F5OS system's local GID, the GID mapping is not parsed correctly by the system. If the remote GID is known to the F5 system, there is no issue. For example, a mapping of the form 9000:9000 works fine. However, mapping of the form 5555:9000, 6666:9000 etc. will not work.
bugs.conditions: Local GID is being mapped to a remote GID.
bugs.impact: The admin user mapped to a remote GID cannot access the ConfD config mode.
bugs.fix: Update the system to the version with the fix.

bugs.title: F5OS file download API does not work with basic authentication
bugs.symptoms: File upload and download using basic auth is not supported.
bugs.conditions: When trying to upload or download the file from F5OS using basic auth.
bugs.impact: Upload/download failed with authentication error.
bugs.fix: File download API work with basic auth and x-auth-token.

bugs.title: Error handling in F5OS file-download API
bugs.symptoms: Upon file download failure, API is returning an Apache error page that isn't an F5OS-specific error and isn't aligned with other F5OS API errors. This is a negative user experience.
bugs.conditions: Due to unhandled errors, when data not in the FormData format are passed through a Curl request, an Apache error page is thrown, misaligning from other F5OS APIs errors.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. It is a negative user experience.
bugs.fix: All errors are handled in the file-download API and aligned with other F5OS APIs errors with no more Apache error pages in error cases.

bugs.title: Multiple CVEs in SQLite package
Tenants may not return to running state when upgrading from 1.1.4 to 1.6.0
bugs.symptoms: When a system is updated from the 1.1.4 release to the 1.6.0 release, it is possible that the tenants that were running may not come up in the running state after the upgrade is complete.
bugs.conditions: When system is upgraded from 1.1.4.
bugs.impact: Tenant traffic will be interrupted if the tenant does not come back to the running state.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the tenant running-state of the tenant from deployed to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: Tenant CPU assignments are not populated on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Tenant CPU assignments are not populated on upgrade from older releases, so they will not be viewable in the CLI or webUI.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade with a deployed BIG-IP tenant.
bugs.impact: Tenant CPU assignments will not be viewable in the CLI or webUI.
bugs.workaround: If the tenant is configured to Provisioned and back to Deployed, the CPU assignments will be populated into the database and viewable from the CLI and webUI.

bugs.title: LLDP details of some interfaces are not shown after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: LLDP details of all the interfaces are not shown after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: When a user upgrades to version 1.6.0 with LLDP configured, the LLDP details will not show up after the upgrade.
bugs.impact: The "show lldp" command will not show neighbor details even if the interfaces/ports are connected to peer switch.
bugs.workaround: The issue arises when all LLDP interfaces are configured simultaneously. However, if the LLDP interfaces are disabled and then enabled one by one, the issue is generally not observed.

bugs.title: The file download API is not working with the x-auth-token header
bugs.symptoms: The x-auth-token in the header of the request is not working for file download.
bugs.conditions: Try to download a file using the file download API with the x-auth-token header.
bugs.impact: The file download fails when using the file download API with the x-auth-token header.
bugs.workaround: Pass x-auth-token as part of the form-data of the API instead of in the header.

bugs.title: Add more resilience to the file download API
bugs.symptoms: If basic authentication is being used in place of the x-auth-token, then the system blocks the requests and eventually stales in the request queue.
bugs.conditions: Use of basic authentication instead of the x-auth-token causes this situation in file download.
bugs.impact: No new download requests can be made.
bugs.workaround: Restart the platform-services.

bugs.title: Tenant service-id mismatch between fdb mac-table and service-instance entries
bugs.symptoms: The tenant service-instances IDs are not matching with the fdb mac-table service-ids. This happens when the system attempted to read a field that does not exist in the /services table.
bugs.conditions: Configuring tenants on F5OS-A.
bugs.impact: Fails to add all the additional services of a tenant to the service instance.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for older F5OS releases. Need to upgrade to F5OS-A 1.6.0 or later.
bugs.fix: The system no longer attempts to read a field that does not exist in the /services table. The tenant service-instances IDs are now matching with the fdb mac-table service-ids.

bugs.title: Datapath is broken when LAG type is changed from LACP to Static on r2000/r4000 platforms
bugs.symptoms: After changing the LAG type to Static, the datapath on the BIG-IP tenant starts failing and the BIG-IP tenant reports the LAG is DOWN.
bugs.conditions: -- r2000 and r4000 platform -- The LAG type is changed from LACP to Static.
bugs.impact: Datapath is completely broken while using the LAG configured.
bugs.workaround: Bring the members of the LAG DOWN and back to UP: interfaces interface <ifc name> config admin disable interfaces interface <ifc name> config admin enable
bugs.fix: Datapath no longer breaks when changing the LAG type from LACP.

bugs.title: Unable to delete the static LAG from webUI
bugs.symptoms: User is unable to use the webUI to delete the static LAG that is created through the CLI.
bugs.conditions: a) If lag is created with LACP type and later changed to STATIC. b) User is trying to delete lag from webUI. LAG can not be deleted from webUI. commands > interfaces interface lag1 aggregation config lag-type LACP > once lag1 is created change the lag1 type to STATIC
bugs.impact: LAG can not be deleted from webUI.
bugs.workaround: Delete the lag from the CLI: > no lacp interfaces interface lag2 > commit > no interfaces interface lag2 > commit

bugs.title: The snmp table F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::platformMemoryStatsTable is not available on a partition.
bugs.symptoms: Snmpwalk for F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::platformMemoryStatsTable is failing on partition.
bugs.conditions: Snmpwalk for platformMemoryStatsTable is executed on partition.
bugs.impact: PlatformMemoryStatsTable data will be available with snmp.
bugs.fix: Code modication done to support snmpwalk for platformMemoryStatsTable on the partition.

bugs.title: Partition config-restore failed after reset-default-config is performed
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs when running 'system database config-restore name my-backup-partition proceed yes' Error: Database config-restore failed.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to restore the partition database after an upgrade using 'system database config-restore'.
bugs.impact: Partition's database config restore is not possible.
bugs.workaround: Partition config-restore won't work until all the blades have started up at least once (usually takes around 5 minutes from when the partition containers start). Use 'show system redundancy' to see when the blades have finished starting.
bugs.fix: Added fix for not to delete the system generated configuration during database reset-default-config.

bugs.title: RSA-1024 SSH public keys should not be allowed in FIPS mode
bugs.symptoms: When logging into an F5OS or BIG-IP system that is in FIPS mode, RSA-1024 SSH public keys should not be allowed to make the connection. Users should instead be prompted for a password.
bugs.conditions: User creates a RSA-1024 SSH public key and uses it to connect to the system, while the system is in FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: The user is allowed to authenticate with the key, which should not be allowed.
bugs.fix: Users cannot authenticate with a RSA-1024 SSH public key while the system is in FIPS mode.

bugs.title: Key migration failure and potential corruption updating to 1.5.0 or later with deployed tenants
bugs.symptoms: When setting a new primary key after upgrading from an older release (such as 1.1.1 or older), where tenants are deployed, to 1.5.0 or newer, the key migration may fail. The migration failure may cause configuration database corruption for the entire system.
bugs.conditions: Tenants are deployed on release 1.1.1 or older. Upgrade to 1.5.0 or newer (including through intermediate upgrades, such as 1.1.1 -> 1.3.2 -> 1.5.1). Set new primary key.
bugs.impact: Setting a new primary key may fail. When this failure occurs, system configuration corruption may occur.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation to prevent failure: - Change all tenants to the configured state - Set a new primary key - Wait for key migration to complete - Return tenants to deployed state. Recovery for corruption: - Reset device to default configuration - Set the primary key to the known primary key for a known-good backup - Restore with known-good backup
bugs.fix: Fix known causes of database corruption on primary key migration failure. While the primary key configuration may still fail if tenants are in deployed state, it should no longer cause system corruption.

bugs.title: Users authenticated via TACACS+ cannot log in via serial console
bugs.symptoms: If remote authentication is configured to use TACACS+, users authenticated via TACACS+ cannot log in via the system serial console. SELinux errors in /var/log/audit/audit.log similar to the following: type=AVC msg=audit(1691528610.427:121): avc: denied { name_connect } for pid=13249 comm="login" dest=49 scontext=system_u:system_r:local_login_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 tcontext=system_u:object_r:reserved_port_t:s0 tclass=tcp_socket permissive=0
bugs.conditions: -- TACACS+ remote authentication. -- Attempting to log in to system via serial console.
bugs.impact: Only locally-defined users can log in to the system via serial console.
bugs.workaround: Configure the SELinux policy to allow this traffic. On a VELOS chassis, these instructions must be run on each system controller separately. 1. Connect to the F5OS system via SSH as root. 2. Examine the SELinux audit denials and confirm all of them are associated with traffic that should be allowed: grep 'denied.*name_connect.*comm="login"' /var/log/audit/audit.log > /root/login-audit-denials.log cat /root/login-audit-denials.log Remove entries from the file /root/login-audit-denials.log that you do not want to allow. 3. After confirming the contents of the file /root/login-audit-denials.log, run the following commands to create and install an SELinux policy to allow that traffic: audit2allow -M login.allowtacacs < /root/login-audit-denials.log semodule -i login.allowtacacs.pp
bugs.fix: A missing SELinux exception has been added. Users authenticated via TACACS+ are now able to log in via serial console without having to manually add the exception or turning off SELinux.

bugs.title: "Hardware datapath fault" alarm triggered by empty dma-agent health file
bugs.symptoms: An empty dma-agent health file causes the system to display an unhealthy status for the dma-agent service in "show system health" within ConfD, along with the generation of a "Hardware datapath fault" alarm.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the dma-agent health file is empty.
bugs.impact: "show system health" indicates an unhealthy state for dma-agent in ConfD, and the system generates a Hardware datapath fault alarm.
bugs.fix: The system will set dma-agent health based on non-empty health file contents.

bugs.title: Manual Configuration of FEC for 25G ports
bugs.symptoms: FEC configuration was automatic prior to this change. FEC can now be configured manually.
bugs.conditions: When using a 25G port FEC can be configured manually.
bugs.impact: FEC can be configured manually for a 25G interface.
bugs.fix: FEC can be configured manually for a 25G interface.

bugs.title: LAGs not programmed when adding VLAN to LAG
bugs.symptoms: Traffic from a LAG is not reaching the tenant.
bugs.conditions: 1) Add a VLAN to a LAG and add that VLAN to a tenant in the same commit. 2) Configuration read following blade reboot.
bugs.impact: LAGs are not programmed; traffic doesn't reach tenant.
bugs.workaround: Workaround for condition (1): Add the VLAN to the LAG, commit; then add the VLAN to the tenant.
bugs.fix: Fix usage of mutexes to prevent deadlock with LAG programming is happening in parallel with VLAN programming.

bugs.title: Sluggishness in SSH access to system on VELOS system controllers
bugs.symptoms: User experiencing delays and slowness in SSH access to system on VELOS system controllers.
bugs.conditions: By default in controller grep UseDNS /etc/ssh/sshd_config UseDNS yes
bugs.impact: Slowness in SSH to access system controller.
bugs.workaround: Set UseDNS to no in file /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
bugs.fix: This is fixed in F5OS-C 1.7.0.

bugs.title: Cannot use WAF modules on VELOS on deploying tenant with 10 CPUs
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use WAF functionality on a BIG-IP Next tenant installed on VELOS when the number of CPUs assigned to tenant is not one of these values: 4, 8, 12, 18, 22.
bugs.conditions: Install a BIGIP-Next tenant on VELOS with an unsupported CPU core count. Supported CPU values are [4, 8, 12, 18, 22].
bugs.impact: Cannot configure WAF policies for a BIG-IP Next tenant.
bugs.workaround: Install a BIG-IP Next tenant with CPUs of the following values: [4, 8, 12, 18, 22 ]

bugs.title: F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::diskPercentageUsed not available.
bugs.symptoms: The diskPercentageUsed OID is not available. snmpwalks/getnext of diskUtilizationStatsTable will not return diskPercentageUsed. snmpget of diskPercentageUsed will fail with a no Such instance error. snmptable of F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB:diskUtilizationStatsTable shows a question mark (?) for diskPercentageUsed.
bugs.conditions: Snmpget of diskPercentageUsed
bugs.impact: The disk percentage used statistic is not available via SNMP.
bugs.fix: Support for disk percentage used statistic is added via SNMP.

bugs.title: Peer controller compatibility verification failed
bugs.symptoms: During a downgrade of the chassis from 1.6.0 to 1.5.1, the partition downgrade will succeed, but the controller downgrade may show a message indicating that compatibility verification failed. This is due to missing certain firewall rules in the controllers.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently in downgrades, controller configuration indicates that compatibility verification failed.
bugs.impact: Intermittently in downgrades.
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart the iptables-config.service in both controllers $ systemctl restart iptables-config.service 2. Reboot the chassis

bugs.title: After downgrading from version 1.6.0 to 1.5.1 and then upgrading back to 1.6.0 both packages are installed and install status is set to none.
bugs.symptoms: "PACKAGE INSTALLED" and "INSTALL STATUS" are none after downgrading from 1.6.0 to 1.5.1 and upgrading back to 1.6.0.
bugs.conditions: 1. Install the optics package. 2. Downgrade from 1.6.0 to 1.5.1 2. Upgrade back to 1.6.0
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact with this. The previously installed packages will still be available in the system. And optics will be updated.
bugs.workaround: There is no functional impact. As a workaround, switch to an alternative package version and then revert to the previous package version. The package installed and install status field would be updated.

bugs.title: Failed to start launch platform service containers during upgrade of Standby cc
bugs.symptoms: The software upgrade status of the standby cc while rolling upgrade happens is stuck at "in progress". The platform-service (docker containers) don't come up after the reboot of the stand by CC.
bugs.conditions: The software upgrade status of the standby cc while rolling upgrade happens is stuck at "in progress". The platform-service (docker containers) don't come up after the reboot of the stand by CC. The import status of the installed version in /var/import/import.json is in error state without port assignment.
bugs.impact: The upgrade process is stuck and we will not be able to trigger another upgrade.
bugs.workaround: As part of recovery/WA. Please follow these steps: 1) Copy the contents of active cc's /var/import/import.json to stand-by cc's /var/import/import.json. 2) Reboot the standby cc.
bugs.fix: Fix has been made to handle port assignment failure in case of communication failure between CCs while rolling upgrade is in progress.

bugs.title: A vqfdm system software core file is occasionally observed on system reboot
bugs.symptoms: The line-dma-agent or vqf-dm occasionally hits a cosmetic failure state as the entire system is rebooting, leading to a core file being produced prior to shutdown. There is no problem with the state of the system.
bugs.conditions: Due to left over data on a communication buffer from the tcpdump daemon to the line-dma-agent, on live-upgrade reboot the line-dma-agent can segfault during its shutdown after the tcpdump daemon already has gone down.
bugs.impact: A core file is observed on the system after the system finishes rebooting. This will happen during an upgrade from a version that is affected by this bug. The core file can be ignored.
bugs.fix: The memory for the communication buffer between the line-dma-agent and the tcpdump daemon has been refactored so this is no longer a possibilty during shutdown. The only way this core care be seen now is if a system is live-upgrading from a version without the fix in the line-dma-agent to a new version with this fix, even then the core is completely cosmetic. Once the system is updated to a version with the fix the core will never be reproduce again on sequential upgrades/reboots.

bugs.title: RADIUS authentication fails if F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute is not specified
bugs.symptoms: Authenticating F5OS users against an external RADIUS server fails if the server does not specify an F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute. The F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute is supposed to be optional.
bugs.conditions: F5OS system authenticating against a RADIUS server
bugs.impact: F5OS authentication fails even if the server sends back the required F5-F5OS-GID attribute.
bugs.workaround: Configure the RADIUS server to include an F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute with a value of "/tmp"

bugs.title: Unable to generate SNMP Trap for IPV6
bugs.symptoms: Generating SNMP traps for IPv6 is not working.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure SNMP traps for an IPv6 address: appliance-1# show system snmp system snmp engine-id state engine-id 80:00:2f:f4:03:00:94:a1:38:33:02 system snmp engine-id state type mac system snmp state port 5000 system snmp targets target v1_target state name v1_target state community c1 state security-model v1 state ipv6 address 2620:128:e8:49:f816:3eff:fe9:248e state ipv6 port 5011 SECURITY NAME NAME MODEL ---------------------- c1 c1 [ v1 ] 2. Try to collect SNMP traps on targeted system: [root@testvm ~]# snmptrapd -Lof 2620:128:e008:4009:f816:3eff:fe09:248e:5011 NET-SNMP version 5.7.2
bugs.impact: SNMP traps for IPv6 addresses won't work.
bugs.fix: We corrected the code for generating SNMP traps for IPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: FIPS-enabled tenant inoperative after in-tenant reboot.
bugs.symptoms: After performing an in-tenant reboot, the tenant did not come back to a healthy state. The tenant management IP was not reachable, and the tenant would not pass traffic. This issue is intermittent.
bugs.conditions: An in-tenant reboot of a FIPs enabled tenant.
bugs.impact: Tenant did not recover from the reboot, and thus cannot be logged in to, or pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: A toggle of the tenant running-state to configured and back to deployed restarts the tenant.

bugs.title: Manually remove root and user keys before entering Appliance Mode
bugs.symptoms: In order to enter appliance mode, the root and other user public keys must be removed from /root/.ssh/authorized keys.
bugs.conditions: Configuring appliance mode on an F5OS device.
bugs.impact: Misconfiguration within Appliance Mode.
bugs.workaround: If any keys were manually added prior to enabling Appliance Mode, remove them. https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000140791 As a best practice, deny network access to the control plane to trusted users. Note: Users may disable Appliance Mode in order to perform the mitigations above.
bugs.fix: Appliance Mode is configured as expected.

bugs.title: Space in SNMP community/user/target name causing snmpd container restart
bugs.symptoms: When there is a space in any SNMP community/user/target name configuration, this will cause an F5OS snmpd service restart.
bugs.conditions: When there is a space in an SNMP community/user/target name configuration.
bugs.impact: F5OS snmpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the SNMP community/user/target without a space in the name.
bugs.fix: Added a space restriction in SNMP community/user/target name configuration so the user can no longer configure with a space.

bugs.title: Deleting tenants may not release MAC address allocations
bugs.symptoms: In a partition, it is possible to see allocated MAC addresses that have not been freed back to the pool.
bugs.conditions: When the number of deployed tenants on a chassis has exhausted resources, it is possible that when all tenants are removed, the allocated MAC addresses are not freed back to the free pool.
bugs.impact: MAC addresses may not be available for tenant creation.
bugs.workaround: A failover of the partition recovers the MAC addresses; they are returned to the free pool.

bugs.title: F5OS system stopped generating tmstat snapshots
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS system is not generating the tmstat snapshots, which helps us in diagnosing issues.
bugs.conditions: System is running an affected version of F5OS software (F5OS-A 1.2.0 and above, or F5OS-C 1.6.0 and above).
bugs.impact: Impacts the supportability of the device; the support teams usually rely on the snapshots while working on field issues.

bugs.title: Unexpected "Optic REMOVED" or "Unable to read optic EEPROM - device is unusable" messages
bugs.symptoms: Inauthentic "Optic REMOVED" or "Unable to read optic EEPROM - device is unusable" messages appear in the VELOS log, even for interfaces that have nothing plugged in.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system -- Portgroups configured in 4x10GB or 4x25GB mode
bugs.impact: Temporary loss of connectivity on port group interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that all interfaces, used or unused, are enabled.

bugs.title: In non-FIPS mode, added support for the SSH-RSA host key algorithm
bugs.symptoms: Not able to establish an SSH connection using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.conditions: Connect to the device from the SSH client using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: The SSH connection to the device could not be established.
bugs.fix: Added SSH-RSA host key algorithm support in non-FIPS mode.

bugs.title: Missing days-valid, store, and key type logging items of a certificate
bugs.symptoms: Logging most of the certificate request fields but not logging days-valid, store, and key type fields. This was because some fields were added for the creation of the certificate and the logging was done as part of the certificate request.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: The user will still see logging of all items used in the creation of a self-signed certificate, except for a few that are not necessary for the certificate request.
bugs.workaround: Check the history and observe the values that were entered.
bugs.fix: The key type and days-valid will now be logged. The store-tls is a logic value and not loggged.

bugs.title: RADIUS user logs in through the WebUI without configuring the F5-F5OS-UID, will be disconnected after 10 minutes
bugs.symptoms: When a RADIUS user is configured without F5-F5OS-UID and then logged in through the WebUI, they will be disconnected after 10 minutes. This problem has also been observed with other remote authentication methods where the UID and GID are configured.
bugs.conditions: 1) Create a RADIUS user without F5-F5OS-UID configured 2) Logged in as the RADIUS user through WebUI
bugs.impact: If logged in as the RADIUS user through the WebUI, they will be disconnected after 10 minutes. This problem has also been observed with other remote authentication methods where the UID and GID are configured.
bugs.workaround: To avoid encountering this problem, the F5-F5OS-UID should be provided. Additionally, the UID for every user (which spans across all remote users as well as local users) should be unique (or have the same GID).
bugs.fix: UID is not defaulting to 1001 for RADIUS and TACACS+ users anymore. UID is assigned from the range 40,000 - 65,000 for remote users.

bugs.title: LLDP neighbors are not getting discovered
bugs.symptoms: When a user configures LLDP at one time, the LLDP details will not show up.
bugs.conditions: Configure LLDP interfaces at one time.
bugs.impact: The "show lldp" command will not show neighbor details even if the interfaces/ports are connected to a peer switch.
bugs.workaround: The issue arises when all LLDP interfaces are configured at one time. However, if the LLDP interfaces are disabled and then enabled one by one, the issue is generally not observed.

bugs.title: Interfaces removed from LACP trunk due to traffic congestion
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces repeatedly removed and added to a LACP LAG due to dropped LACP PDUs.
bugs.conditions: High traffic volume resulting in weighted-random-early-drop (WRED) being invoked.
bugs.impact: LACP PDUs dropped resulting in loss of LACP state.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade.
bugs.fix: Adjust traffic management settings for Class-of-Service '0' (highest priority) so it is never dropped due to weighted-random-early-drop.

bugs.title: Interfaces removed from LACP trunk due to traffic congestion
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces repeatedly removed and added to a LACP LAG due to dropped LACP PDUs.
bugs.conditions: High traffic volume resulting in weighted-random-early-drop (WRED) being invoked.
bugs.impact: LACP PDUs dropped resulting in loss of LACP state.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade.
bugs.fix: Modify LACP, STP and LLDP to use class-of-service 0 (highest priority) for PDUs.

bugs.title: Tcpdump performed with an interface filter on VELOS or rSeries will show broadcast traffic from all interfaces
bugs.symptoms: When performing a tcpdump in VELOS or an rSeries appliance, a traffic capture limited to a specific interface will show broadcast traffic hitting other interfaces.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS platform or r5000 / r10000 / r12000 series appliance - Running a packet capture on a specific interface (e.g. 1/1.0 or 1.0)
bugs.impact: This can cause confusion or impede troubleshooting when unexpected broadcast traffic is seen in a capture such as ARP or Miscabling Protocol traffic.
bugs.fix: This issue is now corrected.

bugs.title: A remote user with the same username as the local F5OS user will be granted the local user's roles
bugs.symptoms: If you create a remote user on the RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP servers with the same username as a local F5OS user, the remote user will be granted the local user's roles upon authentication.
bugs.conditions: A remote user is created with the same username as a local user and remote authentication is enabled.
bugs.impact: Remote user will take the local user's privileges.
bugs.workaround: Do not create a remote user with the same username as the local user. If you have created already, change the username for either the local user or the remote user.
bugs.fix: If a remote user is created with the same username as a local user, the remote user's authentication will be rejected. Only the local user will have access to the F5OS system.

bugs.title: Unable to login when accessing F5OS GUI through a network proxy on a port other than 443.
bugs.symptoms: Users are not able to log in to the UI when trying to access F5OS GUI through a network proxy running on a port other than 443.
bugs.conditions: GUI should be accessed via a network proxy running on a port other than 443.
bugs.impact: Users are not able to log in to the GUI.
bugs.fix: After the fix, GUI now reads the port along with the hostname from the URL and can use the port in making API calls (including login API calls).

bugs.title: Incorrect subnet mask returned for GET call for /systems
bugs.symptoms: Subnet mask returned from Get call for /systems returns the wrong netmask for the management IP on VELOS and rSeries.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Next instances on VELOS and rSeries.
bugs.impact: Does not impact any functionality. GET API call for /systems returns the wrong subnet mask for the management IP.
bugs.workaround: Log in to the machine/tenant and check the management IP address by using the ip addr show command.

bugs.title: Issues with liveness probe during tenant deploy/re-deploy causing incorrect identification of container health status
bugs.symptoms: Occasional error messages may appear, indicating unhealthiness during tenant deploy and re-deploy due to liveness probe misidentification.
bugs.conditions: The issue may occur during tenant deploy/re-deploy.
bugs.impact: These error messages are false indications of an issue. If the tenant is operational, these messages can be disregarded. They should resolve themselves within two hours.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the false status report messages.
bugs.fix: The issue is resolved by implementing additional checks to ensure that the data remains up-to-date, thereby excluding stale positives from the results.

bugs.title: VELOS interfaces flapping if an interface is disabled
bugs.symptoms: After disabling an interface on a VELOS blade: -- Interfaces intermittently start flapping UP/DOWN. -- "Optics removed" is found in fpgamgr logs for 4x10G or 4x25G port groups -- LACP links go down randomly
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system -- Port groups configured in 4x10GB or 4x25GB mode. -- One or more interfaces on the blade are disabled.
bugs.impact: Interfaces are intermittently marked DOWN and then UP. Traffic is disrupted while the interface is marked DOWN.
bugs.workaround: Enable all physical interfaces on the blade, even interfaces that may be unplugged or unused.

bugs.title: libpng: underflow read in png_check_keyword()
Appliance-setup-wizard traceback on invalid NTP input
bugs.symptoms: Appliance setup wizards throw an uncaught Python traceback if you enter non-numeric input for the NTP port [root@appliance-1 ~]# appliance-setup-wizard Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 1355, in <module> curses.wrapper(main) File "/usr/lib64/python2.7/curses/wrapper.py", line 43, in wrapper return func(stdscr, *args, **kwds) File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 1329, in main if scene.setting.is_valid(input_string) is not True: File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 282, in is_valid_ntp_port int(input_string) < MIN_NTP_PORT or ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'
bugs.conditions: Giving non-numeric value as NTP port configuring via wizard-setup
bugs.impact: Throws an uncaught Python traceback.
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A 1.8.0

bugs.title: GUI virtual server CLI has different limitations for days-valid
bugs.symptoms: The range of acceptable values for days-valid for a certificate had inconsistent range limits between the GUI and CLI.
bugs.conditions: Creating a self-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Possible to enter a value that cannot be reflected in both the GUI and CLI.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of days-valid to the smaller of the two limits (65535).
bugs.fix: Both the CLI and the GUI now have the same range limits.

bugs.title: Rolling software upgrade is stuck with one system controller in an "in-progress" state, and a "No such file or directory" error in sw-mgmt.debug
bugs.symptoms: While performing a rolling software upgrade on VELOS system controller software, one controller completes the installation process, but the other remains stuck in an "in-progress" state, and is not reachable on its management IP. 1. One of the two system controllers is "stuck" and largely inaccessible after a rolling upgrade: a. Cannot connect to system controller's management IP. b. Cannot connect to the system controller as root from the active system controller, e.g. "ssh controller-#"). The controller should be accessible over the "ccpeer" link. c. Platform services are not running. 2. When you access the stuck system controller (via console or connection over the "ccpeer" link): a. Some subset of the files in /var/docker/config/ are broken symlinks (env_var, env_var.patch, platform.yml, platform.patch.yml) b. A log message similar to this is in /var/log/sw-mgmt.debug with the error "No such file or directory": 19-Oct-23 14:55:34 - ERROR: sw-mgmt: priority=error msgid=0x3501000000000153 msg=Unexpected error importing controller services 1.6.1-19136: ('Connection aborted.', FileNotFoundError(2, 'No such file or directory'))
bugs.conditions: Performing a rolling system update of VELOS system controller software.
bugs.impact: The upgrade process is stuck, and one controller remains inoperative.
bugs.workaround: To avoid running into this issue during an upgrade, either: 1) perform an out-of-service upgrade, rather than a rolling upgrade. Refer to https://techdocs.f5.com/en-us/velos-1-5-0/velos-systems-installation-upgrade/title-install-upgrade-software.html for more information. 2) add a systemd drop-in file for the sw-mgmt service on each controller, by logging into each controller as root and doing the following: a. Create a systemd drop-in file for the sw-mgmt service by running the following commands: mkdir /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/ echo -e '[Unit]＼nWants=docker.service＼nAfter=docker.service' > /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/deps.conf cat /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/deps.conf The output of displaying the file should look like this: [root@controller-2 ~]# cat /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/deps.conf [Unit] Wants=docker.service After=docker.service [root@controller-2 ~]# b. Activate the modified configuration: systemctl daemon-reload c. Verify that the service is in a functioning state, and now has an explicit dependency on docker: systemctl status -l sw-mgmt systemctl list-dependencies sw-mgmt | grep docker To remove the workaround, run the following on each system controller individually: a. Log into the system controller as root b. Rename the systemd drop-in file to have a ".disabled" extension mv /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/deps.conf /etc/systemd/system/sw-mgmt.service.d/deps.conf.disabled c. Reload systemd: systemctl daemon-reload If a system has encountered this problem: 1. Log into the active system controller via SSH as 'root'. 2. SSH to the offline system controller over the internal 'ccpeer' link. By default, if a chassis uses RFC6598 IP addressing, the IP addresses of the system controllers on this network will be: controller-1: 100.65.7.51 controller-2: 100.65.7.52 The IP address of the peer controller on the ccpeer link can be found by running this command: echo "peer controller: $(ifconfig ccpeer | grep -Po '(?<=inet )([^.]+＼.){3}')$(( 53 - $(grep Slot /etc/PLATFORM | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')))" 3. Verify that both system controllers have the same set of software images present, by comparing the output of "ls /var/import/staging/*.iso" on both system controllers. 4. On the offline system controller, stop the sw-mgmt service systemctl stop sw-mgmt 5. On the offline system controller, make a backup copy of import.json: cp /var/import/import.json ~/import.json.bak 6. On the offline system controller, copy import.json from the working controller over the ccpeer link. If controller-1 is working, and controller-2 is offline: scp 100.65.7.51:/var/import/import.json /var/import/import.json If controller-1 is offline, and controller-2 is working: scp 100.65.7.52:/var/import/import.json /var/import/import.json 7. On the offline system controller, start the sw-mgmt service systemctl start sw-mgmt 8. Wait about 5 or 10 minutes (you can monitor progress by tailing /var/log/sw-mgmt.debug), and then run this command to list the controller services versions that the sw-mgmt service has imported: echo list cc_iso | nc -U /var/sw-mgmt.unix 9. If that works as expected, reboot the offline system controller. reboot After the system controller reboots, it should progress further in the installation process. If there are pending firmware upgrades, the system controller may reboot automatically again to complete those upgrades.

bugs.title: Partition s/w upgrade compatibility check doesn't use correct target version
bugs.symptoms: When performing the partition database compatibility upgrade check (check-version/set-version), the check logic does not always use the correct target version. This potentially can cause the compatibility check to pass, but the actual database upgrade can fail and automatically roll back.
bugs.conditions: When the target partition version is a patch release (such as 1.5.1, 1.6.1), the compatibility check will use the wrong (base release) version.
bugs.impact: The check-version/set-version database compatibility check might pass even though the actual upgrade would fail.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade the controller s/w to version F5OS-C 1.6.1 or later prior to attempting upgrade to a partition patch release.
bugs.fix: The controller OS services uses the correct partition patch version for the compatibility check.

bugs.title: Setup wizard script gives an "All IP addresses must be unique" error when NTP and DNS servers match
bugs.symptoms: When the given IP addresses of NTP and DNS servers match, the setup wizard script gives the error, "All IP addresses must be unique" even though it is a valid configuration.
bugs.conditions: The IP addresses of NTP and DNS servers given to the Setup wizard tool are the same.
bugs.impact: Through the setup wizard tool, the user is not able to provide the same IP address for NTP and DNS servers, which is a valid configuration.
bugs.workaround: The same IP address for NTP and DNS servers can be configured using the webUI or CLI instead of the setup wizard tool.

bugs.title: Setup wizards fails and immediately exits if it is given incorrect credentials.
bugs.symptoms: If incorrect credentials are entered while using the setup wizard tool, it fails and exits immediately without allowing the user to correct the given credentials. The setup wizard utility should make it clear that only non-root admin accounts can be used.
bugs.conditions: Incorrect credentials are passed to the setup wizard tool.
bugs.impact: User is not given the chance to correct incorrect credentials.

bugs.title: Unable to remove the ISO images that share the same minor version with the running version
bugs.symptoms: Removal of ISO (controller/partition/appliance) fails when a same minor version is shared. Example: Import 1.5.1 and upgraded the system to 1.6.1. Later import 1.6.2(1.6.*) and upgraded the system to 1.6.2. When the system is on 1.6.2 unable to delete 1.6.1.
bugs.conditions: The major and minor version of the current ISO must be same as the ISO version that is being removed/deleted.
bugs.impact: Unable to remove the unused ISO.
bugs.workaround: For controller/appliance, you must remove the ISO on a software version that includes different minor release. For example, you can remove 1.6.1-5555 while running ISO version 1.5.X or 1.7.X. For partition, disable and unset the ISO versions of any partitions that use the same minor version of the ISO that needs to be removed. For example, you can remove 1.6.1-5555 by disabling all the partitions running on 1.6.X and de-configure the SW versions.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next tenant will not deploy with mac-block-size set to medium or large
bugs.symptoms: TMM pod gets stuck in a pending state if you try to deploy a BIG-IP Next tenant with mac-block-size set to medium or large.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Next tenant deployed with mac-block-size set to medium or large.
bugs.impact: There is no known use case with BIG-IP Next to be deployed with medium or large mac-block-size, so the impact is minimal.
bugs.workaround: Deploy tenant without mac-block-size specified or specify it as one or small.

bugs.title: ConfD Logging 'Failed to change working directory' Error Message
bugs.symptoms: When running the tcpdump client from the ConfD command line interface, ConfD logs 'failed to change working directory /var/roothome' error message in the devel.log file.
bugs.conditions: Running tcpdump client from the ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: No known impact.
bugs.workaround: No work around.
bugs.fix: When ConfD executes external commands, the working directory is set to the user home directory by default. ConfD logs error if unable to find the user's home directory.

bugs.title: Remove integrity-check configurable option from CLI
bugs.symptoms: In F5OS systems, root and admin users are allowed to toggle the integrity-check option from the CLI. When in FIPS mode, integrity-check should always execute on system startup and when demanded. Since the integrity-check option is configurable, users can disable it which puts the integrity of the system at risk.
bugs.conditions: The configurable integrity-check option is visible when the device is in FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: An admin or root user could access the CLI and disable integrity-check. This could replace files and packages which could impact the integrity of the system.
bugs.fix: We have removed the enable/disable integrity-check option from the CLI.

bugs.title: iHealth upload is failing with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use the QKView upload feature, the upload may fail with the message "certificate signed by unknown authority". This is due to a recent change in certificate authority that is inconsistent between F5OS and iHealth.
bugs.conditions: Always, after mid-September 2023.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload QKView files to iHealth with a single click.
bugs.workaround: Users may use the File Export feature to download QKView files to their PCs, and then upload those files to iHealth. You can find the qkview files in the GUI at System Settings :: File Utilities, then choose "diags/shared" as the base directory, then select "qkview".
bugs.fix: Certificate authorities used by the iHealth upload feature in F5OS will be updated.

bugs.title: Some internal log content may not appear in external log server
bugs.symptoms: When a remote log server is configured, some internal log content may not appear in the logs on the remote server. Notable are logs related to audit login failures.
bugs.conditions: Remote logging server is configured. Log messages do not appear on remote server for user trying to log in with wrong password repeatedly, causing account lockout.
bugs.impact: Brute-force password attack indications may not be seen on external log server.
bugs.workaround: For logs of this type, consult the log files directly on the appliance.

bugs.title: tcpdump service improvements
bugs.symptoms: When 'system diagnostics tcpdump' is run on the system-manager container, sometimes incorrect behavior is observed.
bugs.workaround: Restrict access to the control to trusted users.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump improvements have been applied.

bugs.title: Configure admin/operator roles in LDAP without uidNumber or gidNumber attributes
bugs.symptoms: In previous versions of F5OS, when using LDAP for third-party authentication, having uidNumber and gidNumber LDAP attribute mappings was required. These attributes are common on unix systems and unix-based directories, but are optional in Windows environments. In Windows environments (For example, Active Directory), admin may be required to manually add uidNumber attributes to users, and gidNumber attributes to admin/operator groups.
bugs.conditions: Third-party LDAP authentication using Active Directory or other LDAP directory where uidNumber and gidNumber attributes are not provided by default.
bugs.impact: In the above conditions, administrators are required to add uidNumber attributes to users in the directory, and gidNumber attributes to admin/operator groups.
bugs.workaround: Create uidNumbmer/gidNumber attributes if not present in directory.
bugs.fix: A feature was added to map LDAP groups to F5OS roles using LDAP filter (group names) instead of numeric IDs. Additionally, code was added to use objectSid mapping instead of uidNumber/gidNumber to eliminate the need to create missing attributes in Active Directory environments.

bugs.title: Snmpd daemon stuck in loop deleting and recreating 'system snmp communities community' entry after recreating and deleting SNMP config a few times
bugs.symptoms: Snmpd daemon stuck in loop deleting and recreating 'system snmp communities community' entry after recreating and deleting SNMP config a few times.
bugs.conditions: 1. Put an SNMP configuration, e.g.: curl -sku admin:admin -H "content-type: application/yang-data+json" https://localhost/api/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-snmp:snmp -XPUT -d @put2.json # jq -c . <put2.json {"f5-system-snmp:snmp":{"targets":{"target":[{"name":"i10_2_108_100","config":{"name":"i10_2_108_100","community":"verynicecommunity","security-model":"v2c","ipv4":{"address":"10.2.108.100","port":162}}},{"name":"i10_2_108_101","config":{"name":"i10_2_108_101","community":"verynicecommunity","security-model":"v2c","ipv4":{"address":"10.2.108.101","port":162}}}]},"communities":{"community":[{"name":"verynicecommunity","config":{"name":"verynicecommunity","security-model":["v2c"]}}]},"engine-id":{"config":{"value":"mac"}}}} # 2. Wait 10 seconds or so 3. Delete/clear the SNMP config, using one of the two methods: a. curl -sku admin:admin -H "accept: application/yang-data+json" https://localhost/api/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-snmp:snmp -XDELETE b. from the confd CLI in config mode: no system snmp ; commit no-confirm 4. Wait 15 seconds, while monitoring /var/log/messages for repeating audit messages related to the SNMP config. 5. Repeat first three steps.
