bugs.impact: High CPU and inconsistent state (SNMP community string comes and goes from 'show running-config system snmp' output while the user is watching it).
bugs.workaround: Restart snmpd container using docker command.
bugs.fix: We obsoleted old SNMP configuration commands.
bugs.behavior: In latest F5OS releases (from F50S-A-1.2.x and F5OS-C-1.6.x onwards) SNMP configuration commands have been simplified. For backward compatibility, the old style SNMP configuration works until F5OS 1.7.0 and keeping a confirmation warning in the CLI asking user to use new simplified snmp commands and the old style commands will be obsolete in future releases. In latest release (from F50S-A-1.8.x and F50S-C-1.8.x), the old SNMP configuration commands are obsolete.

bugs.title: Tenants running on VELOS chassis will restart as part of a rolling upgrade of the system controllers
bugs.symptoms: As part of the rolling upgrade of the system controllers to F5OS-C 1.6.0 (or later), tenants running on that chassis will restart.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading system controller software from a version prior to F5OS-C 1.6.0 to F5OS-C 1.6.0 (or later).
bugs.impact: Tenants will reboot as part of the upgrade of the controller software.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade system controller software during a maintenance window when tenants can also be offline.

bugs.title: False indication of Always-On Management (AOM) Power-On Self-Test (POST) failure for I2C1 interface
bugs.symptoms: The Always-On Management (AOM) may report a false indication of a Power-On Self-Test (POST) failure for the I2C1 interface.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system controller.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Although the AOM reports a Power-On Self-Test (POST) failure, the I2C1 interface is functional.
bugs.fix: Fixed in VELOS system controller AOM/LOP firmware v2.01.1282.0.1 and later.

bugs.title: System controller can configure an invalid chassis network prefix
bugs.symptoms: If a booting system controller receives invalid chassis network prefix information from its peer, it may use that information and configure an invalid network prefix for the chassis.
bugs.conditions: Chassis startup.
bugs.impact: Docker fails to start because the configured prefix info is invalid.
bugs.workaround: Netowrk prefix info validation is added to ensure network prefix info received form the peer system controller is valid. If not, the receiver will reboot expecting to receive valid network prefix info on the next startup.
bugs.fix: After validating network prefix info received duing startup, docker startup failures caused by overlapping network prefixes are no longer seen.

bugs.title: Controller-manager pods fail to start with status of CrashLoopBackOff
bugs.symptoms: When the controller-manager pods are unable to start and have a status of CrashLoopBackOff, tenants may fail to start. oc get pods -o wide --all-namespaces NAMESPACE NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE default docker-registry-1-qf79w 1/1 Running 0 4d 100.77.0.44 controller-1.chassis.local <none> default registry-console-1-dflwj 1/1 Running 0 4d 100.77.0.49 controller-1.chassis.local <none> default router-1-cdb9h 1/1 Running 0 4d 100.76.0.43 controller-2.chassis.local <none> default router-1-vtkv6 1/1 Running 0 4d 100.77.0.42 controller-1.chassis.local <none> kube-service-catalog apiserver-5xz4z 1/1 Running 0 147d 100.77.0.46 controller-1.chassis.local <none> kube-service-catalog apiserver-ltnkh 1/1 Running 6 147d 100.76.0.42 controller-2.chassis.local <none> kube-service-catalog controller-manager-hkpz2 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 8 18m 100.76.0.209 controller-2.chassis.local <none> kube-service-catalog controller-manager-zw9kx 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 3 1m 100.77.0.240 controller-1.chassis.local <none>
bugs.conditions: This issue is caused under the following conditions: - VELOS chassis - Upgrade
bugs.impact: Tenants fail to start.
bugs.workaround: Reinstall Openshift.

bugs.title: Unable to access tenant through console access.
bugs.symptoms: Admin can create a user with 'tenant-console' as its primary role from the ConfD CLI. This may create tenant console access issues if a tenant gets created with the same name as the user. The 'tenant-console' role is only for tenant and a new user with 'tenant-console' role cannot be created.
bugs.conditions: Admin has created a user with the 'tenant-console' role and then created a tenant with the same name as the 'tenant-console' user.
bugs.impact: Console access to the tenant (with the same name as a user, which is created earlier with tenant-console role) won't be working.
bugs.fix: Added a warning to be displayed during user creation with the 'tenant-console' role from ConfD CLI. Example: appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication users user test_1 config role tenant-console appliance-1(config-user-test_1)# commit Aborted: 'system aaa authentication users user test_1 config role': tenant-console role cant be assigned to users other than tenant users.

bugs.title: Changing a VLAN from trunked (tagged) to native (untagged) on a LAG in a single transaction can cause traffic outage
bugs.symptoms: Traffic outage after changing a VLAN assigned to a LAG from Trunk to Native in a single commit.
bugs.conditions: Changing a VLAN assigned to a LAG from Trunk to Native in a single commit.
bugs.impact: Traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: First remove the Trunk VLAN from the LAG, then commit the change. Then add the Native VLAN to the LAG and commit the change.

bugs.title: Stale trunk data after trunk deletion
bugs.symptoms: - There could be mismatching actor key for interfaces in the same aggregation. - The non-selected LACP members could be marked as LACP_UP.
bugs.conditions: This happens every time after trunk deletion.
bugs.impact: LACP members and LACP aggregation might be in an unexpected state.
bugs.workaround: Restart lacpd container.
bugs.fix: Appropriately clean up the trunk data after deletion.

bugs.title: Incorrect Vlan Listeners when a Static FDB is configured
bugs.symptoms: When a Static FDB is configured on an interface, Vlan Listeners associated with that interface will have an extra Service ID configured for Service ID 1.
bugs.conditions: A Static FDB is configured on an interface.
bugs.impact: Extra broadcast traffic will be generated on the system, which could affect performance.

bugs.title: System controller fails over when mgmt ports are aggregated
bugs.symptoms: After aggregating mgmt ports failover can happen if active mgmt link goes down.
bugs.conditions: -- Aggregated system controller management ports -- The active management link goes down
bugs.impact: An unexpected failover occurs
bugs.fix: In releases with this fix, if user aggregates mgmt ports and active system controller link goes down, no failover will occur.

bugs.title: Non-root users unable to download or pull qkview/pcap/core files via SCP
bugs.symptoms: Remote auth and non-root users are unable to download qkview/pcap/core files via SCP or pull files while specifying the local path.
bugs.conditions: When a non-root user tries to download/pull files (qkview/pcap/core) they don't have required permissions.
bugs.impact: Accounts with non-root remote access will not be able to download/pull the files using scp.
bugs.fix: Added support virtual paths with permissions using which a non-root user will be able to download/pull files using scp.

bugs.title: Partition is not reachable after performing multiple powercycles
bugs.symptoms: During boot up, there is a possibility that the primary key can cause the key logic to create a new key, thus making the partition unreachable.
bugs.conditions: The normal state of the primary key is to not change unless there is an error in reading the key incorrectly. Attempting multiple reboots where there is a possibility of interruption with the key storage access can cause the key logic to create a new key.
bugs.impact: Once a new key is generated, the existing encryptions no longer can be decrypted and the partitions in particular become unreachable because of this condition.
bugs.fix: The retry logic was enhanced and no longer creates a new key based on recourses being temporarily unavailable.

bugs.title: Unexpected log messages in /var/log/boot.log post-integrity recovery
bugs.symptoms: Users may observe the following inappropriate log message in /var/log/boot.log after recovering from integrity failure: Sep 28 08:45:08 appliance-1 journal: FIPS Integrity Check: This system has been placed in an error state. Try to recover the system using /usr/libexec/ostree_recover utility or reinstall the system. On many devices pressing the escape key followed by '(' key will bring up a menu that allows the system to be restarted.
bugs.conditions: The integrity failure occurs when the device is in FIPS mode, and a user alters or removes a file, subsequently executing an on-demand integrity test or a boot-up integrity test.
bugs.impact: There are no noticeable performance issues or anomalies associated with these log messages, and the issue does not affect the overall system performance or user experience. There are no potential risks or security concerns related to the inappropriate log messages.
bugs.fix: The code has been modified to provide more user-friendly log messages.

bugs.title: Container daemons running as PID 1 cannot be cored on-demand
bugs.symptoms: - kill -QUIT (or any other core-producing signal) to a container process running as PID 1 does not cause a core file. - Actual runtime errors do generate cores as expected.
bugs.conditions: Containers that run their services directly as PID 1.
bugs.impact: Not possible to force a core file for diagnostic purposes.
bugs.fix: Containers that were running directly as PID 1 have been modified to use a minimal "init" process to catch and forward signals to the real service process. The command: "docker exec {containername} kill -QUIT 1" can be used to core a daemon running as a child of /dev/init. More complicated containers that have multiple processes running under 'bash' script may need to use "docker exec {containername} kill -ABRT -1" Note that if the "docker kill" or "docker stop" commands are used instead of "docker exec", the container will not restart, resulting in an inoperative system.

bugs.title: GID role mapping may not work with secondary GID
bugs.symptoms: When a user in an external authentication system (LDAP, Radius, TACACS) is given a GID for an F5 role, and that GID is a secondary GID, the role assignment may not be discovered. This would result in the inability to access the system or be able to configure the system for that user.
bugs.conditions: - User in an external authentication system (LDAP, Radius, TACACS) - GID corresponding to F5 role is a secondary GID (for example, it is not the user's default GID, rather a GID from a group to which the user belongs)
bugs.impact: Inability to log into the system, or inability to configure the system for the user in question.
bugs.workaround: The GID for the desired role should be the GID directly mapped to the user in the external authentication system (for example, in LDAP, the gidNumber on the user object should be the F5 role GID), rather than a secondary GID (for example, in LDAP, the gidNumber on a group of which the user is a member).
bugs.fix: All GID role mappings are properly considered when discovering role assignments for users in external authentication systems.

bugs.title: Warning needed about creating tenant with same name as existing user account name
bugs.symptoms: When a tenant is created with the same name as an existing user account, the end user will not be able to log into the tenant console with that user account. A warning is not included.
bugs.conditions: Creating the tenant with the same name as an existing user account.
bugs.impact: The end user will not be able to connect to the tenant mgmt-ip with the user account.
bugs.workaround: Delete and re-deploy the tenant again with a different name.
bugs.fix: A warning that a console user won't be created if it matches the same name as a user account has been added.

bugs.title: Long BIG-IP tenant names will cause not having virtual console access
bugs.symptoms: No access to the BIG-IP tenant virtual console.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant name is longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The creation of the tenant-console user fails, preventing access to the virtual console for that tenant.
bugs.workaround: Use tenant names that don't exceed 32 characters in length.
bugs.fix: Warn the user when using BIG-IP tenant names that exceed 32 character in length.

bugs.title: Import of a system controller image fails on standby system controller during removal
bugs.symptoms: Import will fail on the Standby controller with previous releases when done during Software removals in progress.
bugs.conditions: Importing while removal is in progress
bugs.impact: Standby import fails.
bugs.workaround: On the standby system controller. run the linux command touch on the ISO that failed to import. ex. touch /var/import/staging/F5OS-C-1.6.0-18695.CONTROLLER.iso
bugs.fix: Import will not fail in 1.8.0 release. Import is delayed for 20 mins if imported while software removals are in progress. Now you will see log message in VELOS regarding the same. <number of removals>:Removal of software is in progress, Import will take sometime, please wait...

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next tenants are not getting deleted when Openshift API is down
bugs.symptoms: When the system is rebooted/power-cycled, Openshift API will take a few minutes to come up online. During this period, Create/Delete operations with regard to tenants will be failed since Openshift API is down. We have the necessary code in place to retry the operations, but there is functionality missing to retry deletions in case an earlier one failed due to API unavailability.
bugs.conditions: Tenant deletion when a cluster is being re-installed/system is power-cycled and cluster is yet to initialize.
bugs.impact: Tenant pods keep running and using resources even when there is no tenant in the ConfD Config Database.
bugs.workaround: Exec into a partition docker container from one of the controller shells. docker exec -it partitionX_TPOB bash --- X is replaced with partition-ID helm delete <tenant-name> -n partition-X --kubeconfig /tmp/omd/tokens/partition-1-kubeconfig

bugs.title: Controller Upgrade Failure Reported by ConfD
bugs.symptoms: During a rolling upgrade, the system controller image may display a completed status, but both controllers report running the new image.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading system controller images.
bugs.impact: The user's system functions as expected. To proceed with another upgrade, the user must execute the system image install-abort command. To clear the status and continue running the same image, the user must downgrade to the old image and then upgrade to the desired one.
bugs.workaround: Abort the failed upgrade using the system image install-abort command. Up/downgrade to a different version than the one currently running. After completion, upgrade to the desired version.
bugs.fix: After an upgrade where both controllers run the updated version, the "show system image" command will display an install-status of "success" for both controllers.

bugs.title: Error occurs when changing LAG type for an existing LAG interface on webUI
bugs.symptoms: On the webUI, if a LAG type changes from LACP, an error displays when that LAG type changes back to LACP.
bugs.conditions: The error occurs when attempting to change the LAG type on an existing LAG interface to a previously used type. (i.e. Creating a LAG interface with type LACP, changing that type to Static, and then changing it back to LACP)
bugs.impact: This issue does not affect functionality; however, an unnecessary "Object Already Exist" error pop-up appears.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the pop-up, change the LAG type to LACP using the CLI in this scenario.
bugs.fix: Changing the LAG type on an existing LAG interface to a previously used type no longer triggers an error pop-up on the webUI.

bugs.title: Observing QKView start from 100% and then going back to 1%
bugs.symptoms: On a second execution of QKView, it is possible that the percent complete reported by the system diagnostics QKView status command will remain at the previous setting until the QKView collection set-up has been completed. This has no effect on the QKView collection, but it can be confusing.
bugs.conditions: QKView is executed two or more times.
bugs.impact: Confusing percent-complete number for a few moments.
bugs.workaround: Wait for a few moments until QKView capture set-up has finished (up to 30 seconds).

bugs.title: Changing the max-age attribute in password policy is not reflecting immediately
bugs.symptoms: Even after setting max-age value (maximum age, in days, after which password will be expired) less than 7 days, the warning for password expiration is not displaying at the time of next login.
bugs.conditions: Set max-age attribute to less than 7 (days) and check if password expiration warning is prompted at the time of next login.
bugs.impact: Password expiration feature is not working as expected.
bugs.fix: Fix is provided to sync the max-age value, updated from ConfD CLI, with the user's password expiration attribute in the /etc/shadow on the system.

bugs.title: Cluster IP is unavailable for some time during tenant reboot
bugs.symptoms: Cluster IP/Floating IP becomes inactive, causing API calls failure temporarily.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently when the system/tenant is rebooted. When tenant running-state is toggled (deployed->configured->deployed).
bugs.impact: API calls are failing temporarily. CM will not be able to get the status of the HA.
bugs.workaround: 1. Login to the rSeries device on which the current ACTIVE HA node is running. 2. execute the below command with appropriate changes, docker exec -it node-agent arping -q -c 5 -W 0.01 -U -P -I <tenant mgmt interface> -S <tenant mgmt VIP> <tenant mgmt VIP> tenant-mgmt interface can be found using 'ip a s | grep mgmt' on the root.

bugs.title: Opening and closing preview pane is causing the page scrollbar to disappear on View Tenant Deployments screen
bugs.symptoms: On the "View Tenant Deployments" screen, when there are a significant number of tenants on the tenant data table, there will be a page level scroll. Opening and closing the preview pane by clicking on any row makes the page level scroll bar disappear.
bugs.conditions: User should be on the "View Tenant Deployments" screen and there should be many tenants configured on the system so that user can see a page level scroll bar.
bugs.impact: Opening and closing preview pane is causing the page level scrollbar to disappear making it impossible for a user to scroll down and see the tenants that are out of scroll view.
bugs.fix: The issue is now fixed and opening and closing preview pane no longer hides the page level scrollbar. The user can scroll down to see the tenants that are hidden in scroll view.

bugs.title: Most recent login information is not displayed in F5OS webUI
bugs.symptoms: The most recent login information is not available in the F5OS webUI. These details can only be accessed through the CLI.
bugs.conditions: When using F5OS webUI.
bugs.impact: To access the most recent login information, you must use the CLI.
bugs.workaround: Use CLI command 'show last-logins' to access the recent login information.
bugs.fix: From F5OS-A 1.8.0, the most recent login information can be found in the User & Roles screen of the F5OS webUI.

bugs.title: Additional password policy settings
bugs.symptoms: Youa are unable to configure min-days, warn-age, and remember when configuring a password policy. min-days: a limit on how many days a user must wait between password changes warn-age: indicates how many days before their password expires a user will be warned remember: indicates the number of previous user passwords that will be saved in the system
bugs.conditions: Configuring the password policy.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to configure mid-days, warn-age, remember.
bugs.fix: You can now configure warn-age, min-days, and remember when setting a password policy.

bugs.title: LDAP external authentication fails if there is no group definition for user's primary GID
bugs.symptoms: LDAP external authentication (e.g. REST API or GUI; but not ssh) fails in the following scenario: - User is defined in external auth system (e.g. LDAP) - User has a primary GID assigned - There is no group definition for user's primary GID While this is legal, because the numeric GID should be sufficient, when we try to look up the group info and fail, this short circuits authentication resulting in an error.
bugs.conditions: - User is defined in external auth system (e.g. LDAP) - User has a primary GID assigned - There is no group definition for user's primary GID
bugs.impact: Externally defined users may not be able to log in.
bugs.workaround: Define a group for the user's primary group ID. system aaa authentication roles role <group name> config remote-gid <group ID>
bugs.fix: LDAP external authentication no longer fails if there is no group definition for user's primary GID. The numeric GID is sufficient.

bugs.title: On VELOS, utils-agent generates "item is not writable" errors every fifteen minutes
bugs.symptoms: The "utils-agent" daemon generates a number of error messages every 15 minutes: utils-agent[18]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x5e01000000000011 msg="utils-agent : failed get value for cdb" COMPONENT="/file/transfer-operations" ERROR="item is not writable" LASTERROR="Not allowed in slave mode" ERRORNO=4. These error messages are generated on the standby node.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system controller or VELOS partition
bugs.impact: These error messages can be ignored.

bugs.title: Egress ARP requests are dropped on native-vlan interfaces on the BX520 blade
bugs.symptoms: On a VELOS chassis with BX520 blades, if an interface is configured for native vlan tagging (i.e. an untagged interface), small egress packets like ARP requests may be sent with a frame size smaller than the Ethernet minimum frame size of 64 bytes. Such frames are known as runts, and the peer device is likely to discard runt frames as an interface input error.
bugs.conditions: - BX520 blade. - Native vlan configured on the interface. - Egress ARP requests (or other egress frames that are smaller than or just barely larger than the Ethernet minimum frame of 64 bytes.)
bugs.impact: Failure to resolve MAC addresses using ARP requests.
bugs.fix: For frames egressing an interface on a vlan configured as a native vlan, the FPGA will add padding to the frame if its size is less than 64 bytes after the vlan tag is stripped.

bugs.title: Default GID group mapping authorized even when GID mapped to different group ID
bugs.symptoms: When a role (group) is mapped to a custom remote group ID (GID), the default GID (e.g. 9000 for admin) is also authorized for the same group.
bugs.conditions: The admin role (GID 9000), operator role (GID 9001), user role (GID 9002), or the resource-admin role (GID 9003) are assigned non-default GID.
bugs.impact: Remote users with GIDs 9000, 9001, 9002, or 9003 maintain the default access for their user role.
bugs.workaround: Do not assign the F5's default admin, operator, and resource admin role IDs (GID) to the remote user groups. These GIDs are 9000, 9001, and 9003 respectively. For a customer who uses the versions with the issue, if higher privilege user group IDs are anything different from 9000, 9001, and 9003, do not assign 9000, 9001, and 9003 GIDs to any other group in the external directory, and do not assign default F5 role GIDs to any user. The default GIDs 9000, 9001, and 9003 should be entirely unassigned in the directory, or assigned to placeholder groups that are prohibited from user assignment. See the role GIDs in ConfD CLI with the following command: show system aaa authentication roles role See the 'GID' column in the command output and don't assign those GIDs to users.
bugs.fix: If a remote-GID is configured for a role, the default GID will no longer authenticate for that role.

bugs.title: Partition configuration database locks up, preventing database changes
bugs.symptoms: At times, the partition HA cluster fails to start up correctly, leading to issues with database replicas and the secondary controller instance not reaching "standby". The "show system redundancy" command at the partition CLI can confirm this issue. Blades will be either "offline" or "failed", with a reason of "reconnecting" or "database disconnected" for an extended period (more than a few seconds).
bugs.conditions: Write transactions occurring during HA cluster formation can sometimes interfere with database initialization/replication, most often observed when multiple blades reboot together during a rolling upgrade.
bugs.impact: Blades fail to initialize, causing tenants to not restart correctly.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable the partition. If both partition controller instances are healthy (active/standby), in the partition CLI, enter config mode and use the "system redundancy go-standby" command.
bugs.fix: The HA framework recognizes the database replication lockup and automatically resets the cluster.

bugs.title: Controller upgrade failed with certificate bundle
bugs.symptoms: System controller upgrade failed with "Compatibility verification failed" error in CLI and webUI.
bugs.conditions: If certificate bundle is configured.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failed.
bugs.workaround: Delete the certificate bundle.

bugs.title: Error log: "PINGLOOP Failed to ssh to 127.0.0.1"
bugs.symptoms: "PINGLOOP Failed to ssh to 127.0.0.1" logged in platform.log by Appliance Orchestration Manager.
bugs.conditions: 1. root user locked with expiry status set to "locked". 2. Appliance rebooted after locking root user.
bugs.impact: Internal processes relying on root user may malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Avoid locking the root user account by not setting the expiry status to "locked". Use appliance mode for root user lockdown.

bugs.title: Partition fails over on link fault when mgmt ports are aggregated
bugs.symptoms: After aggregating management ports, failover can occur if the active controller's management link goes down.
bugs.conditions: -- Aggregated system controller management ports -- The active controller management link goes down
bugs.impact: An unexpected failover occurs
bugs.fix: In releases with this fix, if user aggregates mgmt ports and active system controller link goes down, no failover will occur.

bugs.title: On adding a member to an existing LAG on webUI, the newly added member's speed does not add up to the LAG's "Current Speed" instantly and requires a reload to see the expected response
bugs.symptoms: The status for the newly added member shows as "down" in the REST response and the newly added member's speed does not add up to the "Current Speed" of the LAG on the webUI/REST response.
bugs.conditions: Occurs on the webUI when adding a member to an existing LAG.
bugs.impact: "Current Speed" for the LAG appears stale as it does not reflect the newly added member's speed.
bugs.workaround: The issue only stays momentarily. If the user refreshes the screen, it shows the LAG's Current Speed appropriately.

bugs.title: Vcc-lacpd can intermittently core dump when disconnected from system database
bugs.symptoms: Vcc-lacpd unexpectedly restarts, leaving a core file on the related system controller.
bugs.conditions: Vcc-lacpd can disconnect from the system database while the process is running. A disconnect of this nature is hard to predict and is not typical. When the connection is reestablished, the process typically crashes.
bugs.impact: A core file for vcc-lacpd process is generated. Vcc-lacpd process restarts and recovers. Chassis backplane LACP aggregations may go down for a few seconds while the process restarts, briefly interrupting mgmt traffic to blades. User dataplane traffic is unaffected.
bugs.fix: Vcc-lacpd does not crash during this case.

bugs.title: Rare LACPD crash during process termination
bugs.symptoms: LACPD crashes, generating a core file.
bugs.conditions: While the LACPD process terminates, it may crash. Operations such as a host reboot and software upgrade cause the process to terminate.
bugs.impact: A core file is generated. No functional impact to the system.
bugs.fix: LACPD no longer crashes during process termination.

bugs.title: Upon configuration changes, the l2-agent container restarts with a core.
bugs.symptoms: On systems running F5OS-A or F5OS-C, wen the owner field of the fdb entry is updated by the system, for L2_LISTENER entries, l2_agent crashes.
bugs.conditions: Configuration changes triggered by system for L2_LISTENER fdb entries. Note that this field is not used by STATIC fdb entries, but the problem can be reproduced easily with STATIC entries.
bugs.impact: When l2_agent crashes there is a potential disruption to configuration processing.
bugs.fix: The fix will avoid the crash, and the update of the owner leaf will be processed accordingly.

bugs.title: Unable to add blade to Openshift cluster if VELOS partition root password is expired or locked
bugs.symptoms: If a VELOS partition root password is expired or locked, the system may be unable to add the blade to the Openshift cluster (or manage the cluster). The "show cluster" command output will report that a blade is reachable ("able to ping"), but will not be able to connect to it ("able to SSH"): ABLE ABLE IN READY TO TO PARTITION INDEX NAME INSERTED CLUSTER CLUSTER PING SSH STATE LABEL -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 blade-1.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster 2 blade-2.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster 3 blade-3.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS partition -- root account in partition is expired or locked
bugs.impact: - Blade will not join Openshift cluster. - Unable to deploy Tenants to blade.
bugs.workaround: Re-enable the root user account for the partition: system aaa authentication users user root config expiry-status enabled

bugs.title: F5OS-A:"Use of libssh2 in utils-agent restricting to add known-hosts entry in host"
bugs.symptoms: - Unable to add a known host as ssh-rsa is disabled and libssh acccepts only ssh-rsa.
bugs.conditions: - Add a known-host with any algorithm other than ssh-rsa.
bugs.impact: - Unable to add known-host.

bugs.title: Etcd scale-up operation fails after PXE boot of VELOS system controller
bugs.symptoms: When PXE booting a controller, the Kubernetes cluster may not form properly. This happens during the etcd scale-up operation, and the following log message will be seen repeatedly in the active controller's /var/log/openshift.log file: "Failed to scale ETCD instances" In addition, the following log will be seen repeatedly in the PXE booted controller's /var/log/messages file: etcdmain: rejected connection from "100.65.3.51:50788" (error "tls: ＼"100.65.3.51＼" does not match any of DNSNames [＼"etcd3.chassis.local＼"] (lookup etcd3.chassis.local on 100.65.3.52:53: no such host)", ServerName "", IPAddresses ["100.65.3.50"], DNSNames ["etcd3.chassis.local"]
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system/F5OS-C. -- PXE booting one of the controllers.
bugs.impact: The system cannot add the PXE booted controller to the Kubernetes cluster, and the cluster fails to become healthy.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the /etc/hosts file on the standby controller (i.e., the controller that is being PXE booted). -- If the active controller is controller-1, ensure the following lines are present: 100.65.3.51 controller-1.chassis.local etcd3.chassis.local 100.65.3.52 controller-2.chassis.local -- If the active controller is controller-2, ensure the following lines are present: 100.65.3.51 controller-1.chassis.local 100.65.3.52 controller-2.chassis.local etcd3.chassis.local -- Note: There may already be entries for 100.65.3.51 and 100.65.3.52 in /etc/hosts; these lines should be replaced by the above lines. An in-progress etcd scaleup operation will continue to fail after editing the /etc/hosts file. After three failures, the PXE booted controller will be totally removed from the cluster. At this time, a message similar to the following will be observed in the active controller's /var/log/openshift.log: "Failed to scale ETCD instances after 3 retries.Removing new controllers from the cluster" The controller will be added back. The next run of the etcd scaleup operation should succeed at that point. This part may take up to an hour.

bugs.title: SNMP ifTable data missing for some interfaces when ports unbundled
bugs.symptoms: SNMP interface data is not returned for all interfaces on the system when the device is configured with unbundled interfaces (4x10Gb or 4x25Gb modes).
bugs.conditions: Configure device with unbundled interfaces. default-1(config)# portgroups portgroup 1/2 config mode MODE_4x25GB default-1(config-portgroup-1/2)# commit The following warnings were generated: 'portgroups portgroup': VLAN, LAG, FDB, L2 protocols configuration is lost for the interfaces corresponding to the changed portgroups. Blade(s) 1 will reboot. Proceed? [yes,no] yes Commit complete. default-1(config-portgroup-1/2)# top default-1(config)# portgroups portgroup 2/2 config mode MODE_4x25GB default-1(config-portgroup-2/2)# commit The following warnings were generated: 'portgroups portgroup': VLAN, LAG, FDB, L2 protocols configuration is lost for the interfaces corresponding to the changed portgroups. Blade(s) 2 will reboot. Proceed? [yes,no] yes Commit complete. Check the SNMP output. it will not list all the interfaces.
bugs.impact: SNMP will not list all the unbundled (subports) interfaces.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with SNMP not listing all unbundled interfaces.

bugs.title: F5OS permits non-existent ethernet interfaces to be configured
bugs.symptoms: F5OS allows you to manually type in non-existent interfaces of type "ethernetCsmacd" when adding an interface component. The system later prohibits you from deleting this non-existent interface while the type is ethernetCsmacd.
bugs.conditions: User-triggered command for non-exposed interface type.
bugs.impact: The configuration contains a non-existent ethernet interface with no actual activity. Attempting to delete the interface from the Partition CLI will result in the following error : Partition-1(config)# no interfaces interface 1/1.1 Warning: Some elements could not be removed due to NACM rules prohibiting access. From the Partition GUI The Network-> interfaces Page will show blank "There are no items to show in this view."
bugs.workaround: Delete the non-existent interface. Depending on the type of the created interface , there are 2 ways to delete it . In case the interface is not a valid interface for the blade such as 25.0 or even a fake name like "example" you can delete it using "no interfaces interface 25.0" If the interface is for a real interface, for example you have created interface 1/1.1 while the portgroup is in 100G mode (only 1.0 is valid) you will need the following procedure to delete it : From from the Controller running the Active Partition Login to controller that is the active one for the needed partition (can be seen via "show partitions" command on the controller). Also from "show partitions" on the controller check the partition ID. From controller bash: docker exec -it partition2_manager bash (assuming the partition ID is 2) From inside the partition run the following: confd_cmd -c "mdel /interfaces/interface{1/1.1}"
bugs.fix: With this fix, F5OS will reject the creation of ethernetCsmacd.

bugs.title: Non-patch version of orchestration may start on controller after RMA replacement or rolling upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: In a patch release after an RMA or rolling upgrade, the orchestration-manager version that is started may be from the base build of the patch release, rather than the version from the patch release, if orchestration-manager was updated in the patch release.
bugs.conditions: An RMA of a system running a patch release, or a rolling upgrade to a patch release.
bugs.impact: Base version of orchestration-manager may run on either controller instead of the patch version, until the controller is rebooted. This means that the patch release will not take affect until the controller is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected controller.
bugs.fix: Orchestration manager code was updated to wait for the patch registry to be created and populated before launching orchestration-manager.

bugs.title: OpenTelemetry exporters may not produce data upon first tenant being added to system
bugs.symptoms: Telemetry streaming stops when the first tenant is configured.
bugs.conditions: When OpenTelemetry exporters are configured before the first tenant is configured within F5OS, this can lead to a condition where the exporters stop streaming metrics and logs.
bugs.impact: OpenTelemetry exporters stop producing metrics and logs.
bugs.workaround: The work-around is to disable and re-enable all exporters from the ConfD CLI. system telemetry exporters exporter <name> config disabled system telemetry exporters exporter <name> config enabled

bugs.title: Incorrect slot info may cause blade backplane link errors
bugs.symptoms: In VELOS v1.7.1, the system controller relies on the slot width of each blade in order to configure the backplane portfor the blade. When the slot width is set to "1", the system controller configures for Bx110. If it is set to "2", system controller configures the BX520 blade. If the ConfD slot info is not available, the resulting backplane port configuration may be unsuitable for the blade occupying the given slot.
bugs.conditions: A Bx110 or Bx520 blade is present in the chassis.
bugs.impact: Blade will fail to send /receive traffic over the backplane.
bugs.workaround: This defect is addressed in 1.8.0 by changing chassis manager, so that it updates confD with slot info provided by platofmr-ha before processing other HA info that might result in an error which skips the processing of the slot info.
bugs.fix: Blade backplane port link errors no longer observed when suitable slot info is present in system controller ConfD.

bugs.title: Modifying a remote server with multiple selectors from the web UI removes the AUTHPRIV configuration.
bugs.symptoms: The AUTHPRIV option is not available on the webUI. Modifying a remote log server, which has multiple servers, from the webUI removes the AUTHPRIV configuration
bugs.conditions: Modifying a remote server with multiple selectors from the webUI.
bugs.impact: The AUTHPRIV selector has been removed from the configuration.
bugs.workaround: To modify the configuration of a remote server with more than one selector, use the CLI.
bugs.fix: Added AUTHPRIV option to the webUI. Modifying the configuration of a remote server with more than one selector from the web UI will not remove AUTHPRIV from the configuration

bugs.title: Copying BIG-IP ISO to /var/import/staging/, leaves ISO loopback mounted
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs: ERROR: sw-mgmt: priority=error msgid=0x3501000000000154 msg=Unexpected error processing "import /var/export/chassis/import/iso/<image>.iso": [Errno 30] Read-only file system: 'ace-1.1.7-0.0.3.i686.rpm'
bugs.conditions: Copying a BIG-IP ISO to /var/import/staging/ (rather than /var/F5/system/IMAGES or /var/F5/partition<num>/images)
bugs.impact: An error occurs and the ISO loopback remains mounted
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A/C 1.8.0

bugs.title: Memory leaks in tcam-manager
bugs.symptoms: TCAM Manager leaks a small amount of memory at each rule add or delete operation.
bugs.conditions: Memory leak happens with rule add/delete operations. These rules are generated by TMM during hardware offload.
bugs.impact: High memory utilization and eventual OOM.
bugs.fix: Allocated objects are now properly freed.

bugs.title: SNMP IF-MIB misreport the status and speed of LACP LAGs
bugs.symptoms: SNMP polling on IF-MIB provides incorrect status and speed of LACP Lag interfaces.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen only on SNMP interface. The correct status and speed display on CLI or GUI.
bugs.impact: The user will see inappropriate status and speed details when polled for IF-MIB details on SNMP for LACP LAG interfaces.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue to display the correct values of LACP LAG interfaces in IF-MIB SNMP polling.

bugs.title: The "MAC exhaustion" error message during tenant creation may be caused by configuration processed during startup initialization
bugs.symptoms: If tenant configuration is processed before startup initialization has completed then there may be a MAC exhaustion error issued.
bugs.conditions: If startup initialization has not completed then the available MAC addresses are not known and a MAC exhaustion error is issued.
bugs.impact: The tenant configuration fails.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the tenant once startup has completed.
bugs.fix: The configuration code is now gated to not run until startup initialization has completed.

bugs.title: When more than one PCIe AER error has occurred, diag-agent reports this as a "RAS AER 'unknown' error" instead of the individual AER errors.
bugs.symptoms: When more than one PCIe AER errors are occurred simultaneously, diagnostics will not report the events.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when more than one PCIe AER errors occur simultaneously.
bugs.impact: You are unable to see the individual PCIe errors.
bugs.fix: Updated diagnostics to consider and report more than one PCIe AER errors when occurred simultaneously.

bugs.title: Enhanced the upgrade prompt for better understanding the impacts of upgrade on tenants
bugs.symptoms: Older upgrade prompt didn't include information about impacts of upgrade on tenants.
bugs.conditions: An upgrade is triggered.
bugs.impact: Upgrading does not warn you that tenants will be started and traffic will be disrupted.
bugs.fix: Fixed in 1.8.0

bugs.title: Display a GUI warning to let user know tenants might be affected/reboot
bugs.symptoms: User is not informed about tenants getting temporarily affected when an F5OS upgrade operation is performed.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a F5OS system
bugs.impact: User can be unaware that tenants will be affected/rebooted by performing a system upgrade.
bugs.fix: Added a warning message which will be displayed in the confirmation popup before triggering system upgrade. This new warning message conveys upgrade operation may lead to temporary downgrade of tenants.

bugs.title: Watchdog resets during PSU management may cause AOM/LOP to remain in bootloader mode
bugs.symptoms: The system controller AOM/LOP may encounter a watchdog reset while doing PSU management. If multiple watchdog resets occur in succession, then the AOM/LOP may remain in bootloader mode and be unavailable. When this occurs, the PEL log will indicate a LOP watchdog reset in the LopPsuManagement task, for example: 07/17/2024 06:27:14 | 36644 | AOM | 128 | Network Access | 5 | LopPsuManagement task 100% of watchdog period, resettin 07/17/2024 06:27:20 | 36645 | AOM | 190 | Network Access | 5 | watchdog reset, successive watchdog resets: 9 When there have been 10 successive watchdog resets then AOM/LOP remains in bootloader mode and needs to be reprogrammed.
bugs.conditions: - A VELOS system controller, in either the CX-410 or CX-1610 chassis.
bugs.impact: If multiple watchdog resets occur in succession, then the system controller's AOM/LOP may remain in bootloader mode and be unavailable.
bugs.workaround: At the system controller host prompt, verify that the AOM/LOP is in bootloader mode. [root@controller-1 ~]# lsusb Bus 002 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0003 Linux Foundation 3.0 root hub Bus 001 Device 002: ID f5f5:df11 Bus 001 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0002 Linux Foundation 2.0 root hub An AOM/LOP in bootloader mode will enumerate as USB device f5f5:df11 as shown above. To reprogram the AOM/LOP firmware, first locate the latest firmware version provided by F5OS-C. For example: [root@controller-1 ~]# ls $(docker container inspect platform-fwu -f '{{ range.Mounts}}{{.Source}}{{printf "＼n"}} {{end}}' | grep config_fw-volume) | grep ^lop-chassis-controller lop-chassis-controller-v2.01.1238.0.1.dfu Then reprogram the AOM/LOP using the firmware version located above, for example: [root@controller-1 ~]# docker exec -it platform-fwu dfu-util -D /usr/lib/firmware/lop-chassis-controller-v2.01.1238.0.1.dfu It will take approximately 2 minutes to reprogram the AOM/LOP firmware image. The AOM/LOP will enumerate as USB device f5f5:3000 after reprogramming, as shown: [root@controller-1 ~]# lsusb Bus 002 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0003 Linux Foundation 3.0 root hub Bus 001 Device 002: ID f5f5:3000 Bus 001 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0002 Linux Foundation 2.0 root hub
bugs.fix: Fixed in lop-chassis-controller-application-2.01.1276.0.1 and later.

bugs.title: VELOS backplane packet priority issue
bugs.symptoms: A packet priority issue was discovered during internal testing.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions.
bugs.impact: No impact has been reported.
bugs.workaround: Fixed in VQF bitfiles v8.10.1.3 and newer.
bugs.fix: Updated priority of backplane traffic in VQF bitfile.

bugs.title: Audit log entries are missing when creating or deleting objects via UI or API
bugs.symptoms: When creating or deleting multiple remote-server related objects via UI or API, multiple restart happens causing log message drop.
bugs.conditions: While creating or deleting multiple objects related to remote-server, rsyslog restart everytime to apply new configuration. Due to the restart, some log messages are dropped.
bugs.impact: Log messages are dropped due to multiple restarts of the rsyslog.

bugs.title: VELOS ATSE v7.10.4.12 firmware
bugs.symptoms: VELOS ATSE v7.10.4.12 firmware
bugs.conditions: VELOS CX410 blades.
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.workaround: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes RRDAG issues. See ID1347997 or ID1785385 for more information.

bugs.title: SCP as non-root user does not report errors correctly for bad/non-existent files.
bugs.symptoms: Using SCP to retrieve files from F5OS as "admin" or other non-root users should report a proper error when attempting to access an invalid directory or non-existent file. Instead, the SCP command does nothing, reports no error, and exits with an on-zero exit status.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to read a non-existent/inaccessible file via SCP.
bugs.impact: The user is not informed about the failed SCP operation and the reason for the failure.
bugs.fix: SCP server software now reports errors the invalid/inaccessible filenames.

bugs.title: Appliance management plane egress traffic from F5OS-A host going via BIG-IP Next tenant management interface instead of host management when both are in same subnet
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP Next tenant is installed, a default route rule is added on host. If tenant management and host management IPs are on same subnet, then two similar rules are created with destination as same subnet. The tenant route rule is created with higher priority (metric 0) resulting any management egress traffic destination belonging to same subnet is going through tenant management interface instead of host management interface.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Next tenant is deployed on appliance.
bugs.impact: End users receiving traffic from appliance, will observe sender IP as tenant management interface instead of host management interface. Note: a. This issue will be observed only when host management & tenant management subnet is same and also destination to which data is sent is on same subnet. b. This impacts management plane traffic within the appliance's management subnets.

bugs.title: F5OS upgrades fail when SNMP configuration contains special characters.
bugs.symptoms: As part of some security fixes, added a special character restriction in SNMP configuration in F5OS-A 1.5.1. This resulted in an upgrade failure to 1.5.1. If an upgrade to 1.5.1 is successful, the SNMP configuration will get deleted implicitly.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to 1.5.1 fails when the SNMP configuration contains any special characters. The restricted special characters are: /*!<>^,/
bugs.impact: If the user encounters this issue, the system will go to an inaccessible state and require a forced downgrade.
bugs.workaround: Delete the SNMP configuration (community, target, or user) containing special characters before performing an upgrade to 1.5.1.
bugs.fix: The special characters in the SNMP configuration do not inject any security issues and can have special characters. Hence, the special characters restriction is removed in F5OS-A 1.5.2 and F5OS-A 1.8.0.

bugs.title: Partition go-standby command sometimes fails to change active instance
bugs.symptoms: The partition "go-standby" command is sometimes too slow to finish taking over. When this happens usually the system briefly goes active/active and then resolves to the preferred node.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to force the partition active instance location using the go-standby. Normal HA framework initiated failovers work properly.
bugs.impact: When the confd instances are failing back & forth, the control plane daemons will be disconnected.
bugs.workaround: Allow the HA framework to manage instance locations and don't use "go-standby" to attempt to force instance location. If necessary, the "mode" can be set temporarily to "prefer" the desired location.
bugs.fix: Performance of yield/takeover operation has been improved.

bugs.title: Slow execution of ansible-playbooks on cluster reinstall caused timeouts and retries for many hours.
bugs.symptoms: A openshift cluster rebuild kept failing and retrying do to timeouts while running the ansible-playbooks to rebuild the cluster. This caused the cluster rebuild to fail for 8 plus hours, during which time not tenants could be started.
bugs.conditions: An openshift cluster rebuild was issued after upgrade the system. Unable to reproduce this issue locally.
bugs.impact: While the ansible-playbook runs were timing out, it was not possible to launch tenants on the chassis.
bugs.workaround: The playbooks stopped timing out after 8 plus hours, no workaround is known.
bugs.fix: 1.) Enhanced code that generates and corrects the /etc/hosts file to make sure all the necessary entries are always present and correct. 2.) Enhanced the code the handles the SSH connection caching to make sure it always cleared during ansible-playbook runs, so it won't get affected by a stale connection 3.) Playbook timeouts will be increased after a timeout failure up to 3x to try and allow the system to complete it's work even if something is slowing down the playbook runs.

bugs.title: Tcpdump on F5OS does not honor the -c flag
bugs.symptoms: When using Tcpdump on F5OS with the -c flag, Tcpdump will not stop after receiving the given number of packets.
bugs.conditions: A Tcpdump session is started with the -c or --count flag.
bugs.impact: The Tcpdump session will not terminate after receiving the requested number of packets and will continue until manually terminated.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump now honors the -c flag and will terminate after receiving the given number of packets.

bugs.title: renew_nodes.sh script may leave omd pause if aborted during running of script
bugs.symptoms: The renew_nodes.sh script may leave a /tmp/omd/pause file behind if abort during execution, which causes orchestration manger (OMD) to stop taking actions while the file exists.
bugs.conditions: This can happen if the renew_nodes.sh script is aborted via a ctrl-c while it is being run by the user.
bugs.impact: This will cause orchestration manager (OMD) to stop taking actions while the /tmp/omd/pause file exists on the controller. This can impact cluster rebuilds, adding and removing blades/controllers from the cluster, creation of new partitions in openshift associated with new partitions configured in confd, and other openshift associated actions.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to manually remove /tmp/omd/pause on both controllers if the renew_nodes.sh is interrupted during it's run via ctrl-c or some other method.
bugs.fix: The fix adds a signal handler to renew_node.sh so that it will catch any signal and correctly clean up the /tmp/omd/pause files before exiting.

bugs.title: On a rSeries appliance, config-backup proceed is broken
bugs.symptoms: On a rSeries appliance, system database config-backup 'proceed' is broken. It is about overwriting an existing backup file, but it prompts you to proceed even if a file does not exist.
bugs.conditions: System database config-backup always prompts for the user to proceed even if a file does not exist.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. When you provide input 'yes', the backup file will be generated.
bugs.workaround: When prompted to 'proceed', you must respond with 'yes'.
bugs.fix: The system database config-backup prompts the user with ‘proceed’ option only when the file exists and the user is not provided ‘proceed yes’ in the input CLI command.

bugs.title: CC takes time to come up after reboot is triggered in active CC.
bugs.symptoms: Containers take time to come up after reboot when active CC is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: Reboot should be triggered in active CC.
bugs.impact: Current standby CC takes time to come up after reboot.

bugs.title: Platform-deployment script logs are now captured in both its dedicated log file and the systemd journal
bugs.symptoms: The platform-deployment script used bare echo statements for all output, meaning log messages were not persisted to a dedicated log file and were not captured in the systemd journal. This made it difficult to troubleshoot platform service deployment issues (e.g., container startup failures, registry setup, OS rebase errors) after the fact, as the output was only visible in the service status and could be lost on rotation or reboot.
bugs.conditions: Any F5OS-A or F5OS-C system running the platform-services-deployment service during upgrade/downgrade, reboot, or service start/stop operations.
bugs.impact: Reduced observability during platform service deployment. Operators had limited ability to diagnose historical deployment failures, Docker Compose errors, or registry setup issues because log messages were transient and not written to a persistent, searchable location.
bugs.workaround: Prior to this fix, operators could manually inspect systemctl status platform-services-deployment.service -l for recent output, but historical logs were not reliably available.
bugs.fix: Added structured logging to the platform-deployment script. All output is now timestamped and written to a dedicated log file (/var/log/platform-deployment.log) with logrotate support, and simultaneously forwarded to the systemd journal via StandardOutput=journal on the service unit. This enables operators to use both journalctl -u platform-services-deployment and the persistent log file for troubleshooting platform service deployment issues

bugs.title: LDAP authentication is consuming several minutes to authenticate via GUI and SSH.
bugs.symptoms: LDAP authentication is working fine. However, authentication takes several minutes, which lacks a user-friendly experience.
bugs.conditions: - Configure LDAP server-group. - Configure LDAP_ALL as an authentication-method. - Log in using LDAP user via GUI or SSH.
bugs.impact: The user is forced to wait for several minutes to get the result of LDAP authentication.
bugs.fix: Removed unnecessary GID lookup to speed up LDAP authentication.

bugs.title: VELOS management LAG may bridge traffic between management interfaces during LACP negotiation
bugs.symptoms: When the management interfaces of VELOS system controllers are configured in a LACP LAG, the VELOS system may incorrectly forward some ethernet frames ingressing one management interface out the other management interface. This behavior occurs during the period between when an interface links up and when the system completes LACP negotiation and adds the interface to the LAG. This can result in management switches incorrectly learning non-VELOS MAC addresses as being present on the VELOS management LAG interface.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system - Management interfaces configured in LACP LAG
bugs.impact: VELOS management interfaces incorrectly forward non-VELOS frames from one management interface out the other, causing upstream switches to learn non-VELOS MAC addresses as being present on the VELOS management LAG interface.
bugs.workaround: Configure the upstream switch to be an LACP lag first, then configure the VELOS system MGMT interfaces to use an LACP lag.

bugs.title: GUI freezes during LDAP user authentication if no remote GID mapped locally.
bugs.symptoms: The LDAP remote user authentication freezes for a long time (more than a minute).
bugs.conditions: When trying to authenticate a remote LDAP user through the GUI without mapping any of the remote user GIDs to the F5OS local roles.
bugs.impact: Authentication freezes for a long period before rejecting the user.
bugs.workaround: One of the remote GIDs should be mapped to the local F5OS roles.
bugs.fix: Map the remote GID(s) to the F5OS role(s) to authenticate remote LDAP users successfully.

bugs.title: Tenants may be in a failed state after downgrade from VELOS v1.7.1 to v1.7.0 and then back to 1.7.1
bugs.symptoms: After a VELOS software downgrade from v1.7.1 to v1.7.0 and then upgrading back to a v1.7.1 VELOS version may put the tenants into a failed state.
bugs.conditions: The VELOS v1.7.0 software is intended to be an initial manufacturing build in which the user upgrades to the released v1.7.1 VELOS version. Downgrading back to the VELOS v1.7.0 version is not supported.
bugs.impact: Tenants may be in a failed state.

bugs.title: Failure of BX110 10G Links to recover after going DOWN
bugs.symptoms: If the 10G link on the BX110 experiences a disruption, such as a cable pull or peer device shutdown, it may occasionally fail to re-establish connectivity even after the issue is resolved.
bugs.conditions: The 10G link on the BX110 experiences a disruption, such as a cable pull or shutdown on the peer device, leading to a DOWN state.
bugs.impact: Loss of connectivity.
bugs.fix: Regularly reset the 'DOWN' link to clear the failure state and enable the establishment of the connection.

bugs.title: LDAP authenticated admins logging in via the serial console may have trouble disabing appliance mode during system instability
bugs.symptoms: If ConfD is not running, F5OS offers an emergency option to disable appliance mode when an administrator logs in successfully via the serial console.
bugs.conditions: The admin role has been configured with a remote-gid that is not 9000 and the admin successfully authenticates via LDAP on the serial console while ConfD is not running.
bugs.impact: Remotely-authenticated admin users cannot disable appliance mode if ConfD is offline.
bugs.fix: Remotely-authenticated admin users can disable appliance mode if ConfD is offline.

bugs.title: BX110 blade VQF v8.9.2.3 datapath lockup
bugs.symptoms: Datapath lockup in host to network direction. VOQ reports drops in the cos_lo_drops and/or cos_hi_drops counters.
bugs.conditions: Random. No known data pattern or specific datapath configuration.
bugs.impact: Datapath lockup. Requires BX110 blade reboot to clear.
bugs.workaround: Update to VQF bitfile v8.9.5.9 or newer.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing datapath lockup.

bugs.title: Debug output is missing from qkview
bugs.symptoms: NSE debug registers missing from qkview output.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system -- A qkview is taken
bugs.impact: Qkview file is missing some desired component output.
bugs.workaround: Without this fix, manually read desired debug registers with existing tools under the guidance of F5 support.
bugs.fix: With the current fix in place, all NSE debug registers are included in the standard QKView output.

bugs.title: Configuring Expiry-status of root and admin users should not be allowed
bugs.symptoms: Expiry-status of root and admin users are allowed to be configured and there is a chance of locking out these users.
bugs.conditions: If Expiry-status of any root or admin user is marked as Locked, that root or admin user cannot log in to the system.
bugs.impact: There is a chance that default users, such as root and admin, become locked out.
bugs.fix: You cannot edit the ‘Expiry-status’ field in webUI for admin and root users. Thus, it cannot be configured. The 'Expiry-status' field for root and admin users will now always display the default value as 'Enabled'.

bugs.title: Partition dagd cores during system startup
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, the partition dagd component triggers an assert and cores due to loss of connectivity with the internal system database. The partition dagd component will automatically restart.
bugs.conditions: The system database experiences a loss of connectivity during the startup of the partition.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.

bugs.title: Monitor Error Event logged on controller and partition
bugs.symptoms: The system may periodically log platform-monitor errors in the velos.log on the controller: <timestamp> controller-1 platform-monitor[8]: priority="Err" msg="Monitor Error Event" kind="service:monitor-error" error="Get ＼"http://localhost:10080/v3/qkviewd/health＼": dial tcp [::1]:10080: connect: connection refused" interface="console-output" <timestamp> controller-1 platform-monitor[8]: priority="Err" msg="Monitor Error Event" kind="service:monitor-error" error="ReadyRequest failed for 'platform-hal' @ 'tcp://127.0.0.1:1046', Inner -> 'receive timeout'" interface="console-output" The VELOS system may also log these errors in the partition's velos.log: <timestamp> controller-1(p2) platform-monitor[8]: priority="Err" msg="Monitor Error Event" kind="service:monitor-error" error="HealthRequest failed for 'partition2_tcpdumpd_manager' @ 'tcp://127.0.0.1:3510', Inner -> 'receive timeout'" interface="console-output" <timestamp> 100.65.18.52 controller-2(p2) platform-monitor[9]: priority="Err" msg="Monitor Error Event" kind="service:monitor-error" error="HealthRequest failed for 'partition2_tcpdumpd_manager' @ 'tcp://127.0.0.1:3510', Inner -> 'receive timeout'" interface="console-output" The platform-monitor events normally only occur on tcpdump monitors. The log messages can occur even on an idle VELOS system.
bugs.conditions: VELOS system with partition enabled.
bugs.impact: The issue is transient and cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Platform-monitor does not miss monitors under normal operating conditions.

bugs.title: A linkUp and linkDown traps are sent when an up interface is disabled, and vice versa
bugs.symptoms: When F5OS system is configured with SNMP Targets for managing the Trap notifications, linkUp and linkDown traps will be sent when interface state is toggled.
bugs.conditions: Always two traps (linkUp and linkDown) will be sent even when the interface state is toggled from UP to DOWN or DOWN to UP.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but when two traps are sent, the interface state over SNMP can be misleading.
bugs.fix: The appropriate trap, that is, linkDown trap when F5OS interface state is down and linkUp trap when F5OS interface state is up, will be sent.

bugs.title: Non-root, local authentication fails when LDAP is configured with chase referrals and an invalid DNS server is configured
bugs.symptoms: Local and remote authentication to F5OS will timeout and fail. Running commands as root may take 60 seconds before each command returns.
bugs.conditions: LDAP authentication is configured with chase-referrals set to true and an invalid or non-responsive DNS server is also configured.
bugs.impact: Users cannot successfully authenticate via the GUI. Local admin users cannot successfully authenticate. Logging in as root takes 2 minutes and many system commands will take at least 60 seconds to complete.
bugs.workaround: Set 'system aaa authentication ldap chase-referrals false' or ensure a working DNS server is always configured.

bugs.title: User with operator role is not having read-access to all pages
bugs.symptoms: - User experiences unauthorized error when trying to access "Tenant Images", "Software Management", "File Utilities", "Configuration Backup", and "System Report" - User sees no items when trying to access "File Utilities", "Configuration Backup", and "System Report" pages
bugs.conditions: User has operator role.
bugs.impact: User is not able to view certain pages.

bugs.title: Config-restore fails when backup file has expiry-status field for admin or root user
bugs.symptoms: For a root or admin user, if the value for Expiry-status in the backup file is not set to enabled, then config-restore fails.
bugs.conditions: During backup, if the "Expiry-status" value for admin or root user is not set to enabled, then restore fails with the backup.
bugs.impact: Database config-restore fails.
bugs.workaround: For admin and root user, comment expiry-status, expiry-date in the backup file and try to restore.
bugs.fix: Added NACM rules in ConfD for successful config-restore.

bugs.title: Allowing user to configure HostKeyAlgorithms parameters
bugs.symptoms: A new config CLI (system security services service sshd config host-key-algorithm) is implemented to allow HostKeyAlgorithms configuration.
bugs.conditions: In non FIPS mode, to enable or disable ssh-rsa HostKeyAlgorithm, this newly implemented CLI can be used.
bugs.impact: HostKeyAlgorithm usage was not configurable.
bugs.fix: This is a new CLI that can be used to enable or disable ssh-rsa HostKeyAlgorithm

bugs.title: ConfD Application Error when tenant interface stats are not available
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to get tenant interface stats, the system displays "Error: application error".
bugs.conditions: The creation or modification of tenants may result in inaccurate handling of historical data by the tenant interface-stats logic. This could lead to the display of an “Error: application error” message when queried. For example: appliance-1# tenants tenant cbip-tenant-b state interface-stats down-sample-to 10 average 10s-avg Error: application error
bugs.impact: Confd reports the error on the command line and logs the error in platform logs. 2024-01-24T20:12:37.123437567Z: [Error]: confd: msg="Action Point reply error" error="confd error: 'Unknown error', last='Invalid confd_vtype value: 0', errno=5"
bugs.fix: The problem has been resolved in more recent versions of F5OS-A. To resolve it, upgrade to a more recent version of F5OS-A. It will resolve once all interfaces are enabled.

bugs.title: Allowing entry of a Subject-Alternative-Name (SAN) for certificate and CSR creation
bugs.symptoms: There is no method available for inputting the SAN field during the creation of certificates or CSR.
bugs.conditions: While creating a CSR through system aaa tls create-csr in ConfD.
bugs.impact: The option to include the SAN field in certificates and/or certificate request is not available.
bugs.workaround: To add an SAN, you need to edit the /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf file and add it. However, this may not be effective for certain software that does not accurately read the configuration file.
bugs.fix: A new SAN field has been implemented, which is mandatory, and allows users to enter a value in the field. However, if the value “none” is used, the field can be omitted. Additionally, to allow entry of the SAN, a default tls certificate is created in /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert that has the SAN populated with the hostname and management-ip values. In the absence of a user-provided self-signed certificate, the http-server will automatically use the default certificate. As this is a new feature, back-porting to older versions has not been implemented and would be difficult and complex.

bugs.title: User-manager's ConfD socket getting closed.
bugs.symptoms: After repeating the change of network type and device reboot, the device goes into a state where the user-manager is not interacting with ConfD.
bugs.conditions: - Change remote GID role and check '/etc/gid-map.txt' file if the value is reflected. - Switch network type and reboot the device. Repeat the above process until '/etc/gid-map.txt' file is not been updated correctly.
bugs.impact: Any ConfD configuration change that goes through user-manager fails. This includes any of the user’s password changes, or remote GID changes.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the system will get the correct GID value from the ConfD and update the '/etc/gid-map.txt' file.
bugs.fix: The user-manager has no reason to use NSS to lookup any PW/group info, as it deals exclusively with the local user database. Additionally, there is a ZMQ service that belongs in authentication-mgr (which understands remote authentication) that is in the user-manager container. It forces user-manager to use an ‘/etc/resolv.conf’ that can reference remote sources. If the user-manager trips over a lookup that goes to LDAP (usually a local-db miss), it can be very slow and time out. The ConfD->user-manager channel is sensitive of slow responses, and shuts down subscriber/callpoint handler/daemon that takes over 15 to 30 seconds to respond. When this happens, the user-manager is going to see an EOF on its ConfD sockets. This fix forces the user-manager to only lookup on local databases.

bugs.title: Third etcd instance can get into an error state on controller upgrade from 1.5.1 to 1.6.1
bugs.symptoms: The internal datastore of third Openshift etcd process has become out of sync with the etcd processes on the other two controllers.
bugs.conditions: A split brain situation occurred in the lower level database of the third etcd instance on each controller and is unable to recover.
bugs.impact: The user may notice inconsistencies with the display of tenants due to this condition.

bugs.title: Remote GID mappings to F5OS roles are disconnected for TACACS+/RADIUS authentication methods.
bugs.symptoms: Remote GID mappings (on a TACACS+ or RADIUS server) to F5OS GIDs/roles are not working correctly. When attempting to configure a remote mapping, it results in the access rejection with a message similar to below: [root@system ~]# ssh radius_or_tacacs_user@<F5OS system mgmt IP> Password: Last login: <date> from <source IP> No valid role group found in user groups: '9000' Connection to <mgmt IP> closed.
bugs.conditions: A remote GID mapping is configured for a role in F5OS and the authentication method used for remote users is RADIUS or TACACS+.
bugs.impact: Remote users cannot log in to the system.
bugs.workaround: Configure remote user's GIDs in a way that they correspond to the GIDs in F5OS for the desired role(s). Then, remove any remote GID mappings in the F5OS configuration.
bugs.fix: Fixed remote GID mapping to F5OS roles for TACACS+/RADIUS authentication methods.

bugs.title: Support for SSH-RSA host key algorithm for partitions added in non-fips mode
bugs.symptoms: Unable to establish an SSH connection to the partition using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to connect to the partition from an SSH client using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm while in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: SSH connections to the partition cannot be established using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.fix: Support for the SSH-RSA host key algorithm has been added in non-FIPS mode.

bugs.title: F5OS SNMP IF-MIB::ifAlias missing from snmpwalk
bugs.symptoms: The following SNMP MIB OID from IF-MIB table is missing on F5OS-A and F5OS-C. 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 Example snmpwalk result: ~ % snmpwalk -c public -v 2c 10.10.10.33 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 IF-MIB::ifAlias = No Such Instance currently exists at this OID
bugs.conditions: Snmpwalk -c public -v 2c 10.10.10.33 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 IF-MIB::ifAlias = No Such Instance currently exists at this OID
bugs.impact: Cannot get results for MIB OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18
bugs.fix: We have added the support for OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 (IF-MIB::ifAlias), which will represent the value for interface description.

bugs.title: First SSH login after editing remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user privileges will still apply old privileges
bugs.symptoms: The first SSH login after editing role-based privileges for a remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user will still give the user their prior privileges (or, if the user is newly created, login will be rejected with a message saying "This account is currently not available"). Subsequent logins will apply the updated user privileges.
bugs.conditions: 1. RADIUS or TACACS+ Authentication is enabled. 2. A new user is created in one of the above auth systems, or an existing user’s role-based access is modified. 3. The affected user SSHs into F5OS for the first time after the change in step #2.
bugs.impact: First login to system after creation fails, or first login after modification of user privileges gives the user incorrect privileges.
bugs.fix: Fix issue where first SSH login after editing remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user privileges will still apply old privileges.

bugs.title: Log flooded with "Error found in chassis platforms response"
bugs.symptoms: The system controller velos.log is flooded with messages from chassis-manager: msg="Vcc-HAL-lib: Error found in chassis platforms response."
bugs.conditions: This can happen temporarily while a blade is updating the LOP firmware, or if a blade LOP is unreachable for any other reason
bugs.impact: Logging noise in velos.log
bugs.fix: Fixed by improving how a blade LOP communication error is handled when chassis-manager is gathering chassis platform data.

bugs.title: Unable to deport previously referenced ISO of now-disabled partition
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading a partition to a new ISO in a disabled state does not completely switch the partition’s OS from the previous version to new, in turn, the system is failing to deport the previously referenced ISO file from the system.
bugs.conditions: - Enable a partition with version A. - Disable the partition. - Upgrade the partition to new version B. - Attempt to deport version A. Version A deport fails claiming it is still in use.
bugs.impact: You cannot remove the previously referenced ISO from the system.
bugs.workaround: Enable the partition, which was upgraded to a new version. Now deport the previously referenced ISO.

bugs.title: Learned L2 entries in data-plane L2 forwarding table may disrupt some traffic flows between tenants
bugs.symptoms: While a tenant transitions from active to standby, an egress packet in flight may trigger a L2 learn event in the FPGA data-plane. This can occur for tenants that transmit using a different MAC address while active, such as when MAC masquerading is enabled. If so, a dynamic L2 entry is created from the source MAC address of the egress packet. These dynamic entries also enable the service DAG without setting a service ID, which causes matching packets to be dropped in the VOQ system due to an invalid service DAG lookup result. This can disrupt egress traffic for another tenant on the same device, attempting to transmit to the destination MAC address that was recently relinquished by the standby tenant. These drops increment the 'ic_voq_drops' counter in the tmctl vqf_global table. These L2 entries will not be corrected by subsequent L2 learn events for the same MAC address from a different location. Thus, traffic disruption may persist until entries age out.
bugs.conditions: - MAC masquerade configured on the traffic-group of an HA pair of tenants. - A failover from tenant A to tenant B. - Another tenant running alongside tenant 'A' attempts to transmit to the MAC masquerade address that is now owned by tenant 'B'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption from one tenant to another in specific directions.
bugs.fix: L2 entries that are created from host generated L2 learn events, no longer enable the service DAG for matching packets.

bugs.title: If accidentally import bad ISO images, it may not removed automatically
bugs.symptoms: When you accidentally import ISO images from a faulty URL, they cannot be removed or replaced with the correct URL.
bugs.conditions: User accidentally imports faulty ISO images to the system.
bugs.impact: Deleting and importing system ISO images might have an impact.
bugs.workaround: Login to the command line with root user access and remove the image via 'rm' under '/var/import/staging', and import the correct ISO.
bugs.fix: Please refer to the workaround and further detail.

bugs.title: Partition image removal message is truncated
bugs.symptoms: If a partition is enabled and then disabled while running version A, and then upgraded to version "B", attempting to deport partition image "A" fails, the CLI throws truncated error messages.
bugs.conditions: The partition is upgraded with the state is disabled.
bugs.impact: Incomplete error messages for the failure reason. The error that is reported is: "Error: Failed to remove software: 1.5.1-14085, error message: Standby removal failed for following reason: OS version".

bugs.title: During remote logging server configuration, selectors help menu does not display when using Tab key.
bugs.symptoms: While configuring the remote logging server, using the Tab key does not display selector help menu.
bugs.conditions: While configuring the remote logging server, using the Tab key does not display selector help menu.
bugs.impact: No help menu is displayed
bugs.workaround: Use ? key to get help in selectors menu, while configuring remote server.

bugs.title: Subject-Alternative-Name (SAN) feature now supports client-side SSL Validation
bugs.symptoms: Since no SAN was allowed to be inserted into the http-server’s self-signed certificate, client-side SSL validation was not supported. This impacts Central Manager's VELOS/rSeries provider. The missing SAN field causes the certificate to be rejected.
bugs.conditions: Using the default self-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Client-side SSL validation is not supported.
bugs.workaround: To add an SAN, you need to edit the /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf file and add it. However, this may not be effective for certain software that does not accurately read the configuration file.
bugs.fix: A new SAN field has been implemented, which is mandatory, and allows users to enter a value in the field. However, if the value “none” is used, the field can be omitted. Additionally, to allow entry of the SAN, a default tls certificate is created in /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert that has the SAN populated with the hostname and management-ip values. In the absence of a user-provided self-signed certificate, the http-server will automatically use the default certificate.

bugs.title: VELOS Blade BX520 USB host controller not working, resulting in LOP USB device not present at either /dev/ttyAOM or /dev/ttyACM0
bugs.symptoms: Random soft lockup trace due to corrupt USB drive
bugs.conditions: Corrupt USB Drive.
bugs.impact: Seldom seen stack strace and soft lock error seen , which is not reproducible.
bugs.workaround: Not reproducible ever after in any other environment , it was seen once in a particular environment having suspected corrupted flash drive.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenant reports blank interface
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP tenant reports a blank ("") interface member in the trunk when removing one or more interfaces from an aggregation.
bugs.conditions: When removing one or more interfaces from an aggregation.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP tenant has an empty member in the trunk.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
