And in the vqf_voq_stat table output, the remaining VOQ stat requests starting from 13 do not return data although the tmstat table for some other blades are intact.
bugs.conditions: One of the intermediate blades from the list of show components is faulty and leads to skipping of processing the vqf voq stat requests for rest of the blades that are properly functional.
bugs.impact: Improper output for the 'show fpga-tables vqf_voq_stat' command.
bugs.fix: Added a code change to get the stats completion for rest of the functional blades when one of the blades is faulty.

bugs.title: If 'ldap-group is configured for a role but LDAP search fails, users with the default GID for the role can still get those privileges
bugs.symptoms: When an 'ldap-group' mapping is configured for a F5OS role, and the mapping fails (because the filter is invalid or the LDAP query of remote groups fails for some other reason), the default mapping for the role (or, what is configured in 'remote-gid' for the role) is still used. For example, if you were attempting to map the F5OS role 'admin' (default GID 9000) to an LDAP group 'CN=my-ldapgroup', and the LDAP search for that group failed (because the provided filter was invalid, the group does not exist, etc.), users with GID 9000 would still be able to authenticate and login with 'admin' privileges.
bugs.conditions: 1. LDAP authentication is enabled. 2. A role mapping is applied via the 'ldap-group' configuration for a F5OS role. 3. The provided 'ldap-group' filter is invalid or another unexpected issue is encountered when querying the LDAP server.
bugs.impact: Users can login with privileges in excess of what one might expect given the system configuration.
bugs.workaround: If the LDAP group/users have Posix attributes ('gidNumber'), it is possible to map the F5OS role using this GID number by specifying it in the 'remote-gid' configuration under the role. If this is not feasible, it is possible to directly validate the 'ldap-group' mapping was successful by inspecting this file from a bash shell: [root@appliance-1(test):Active] ~ # cat /etc/ldap-gid-map.txt 1108:=9000 If there is an entry that has the default GID for the role on the right-hand side of ':=' in this file, it means the mapping was applied successfully and users with the default or 'remote-gid' GID will not be able to obtain the role permissions. If such an entry is missing, you will need to fix the 'ldap-group' filter so an LDAP query of the group can be successful.
bugs.fix: If a configured 'ldap-group' mapping fails, deny all role-based access for the mapped role until it is fixed or de-configured.

bugs.title: Component fpgamgr in restart loop with segmentation fault after failed FPGA firmware update
bugs.symptoms: Component fpgamgr experiences segmentation fault after failed FPGA firmware update and persists in a reboot loop. The CLI command "show cluster nodes node state platform fpga-state" indicates that FPGA_STATE persists in FPGA_INIT and never reaches the state FPGA_RDY.
bugs.conditions: FPGA firmware update fails and one or more of the FPGA devices does not show up on the PCI bus. This causes a FPGA SDK segmentation fault upon the fpgamgr component startup, and perpetual reboot loop so long as the FPGA issue persists.
bugs.impact: A failure in the FPGA firmware update process results in one or more FPGA devices not being detected on the PCI bus. This, in turn, causes a segmentation fault in the FPGA SDK upon the startup of the fpgamgr component, leading to a continuous reboot cycle until the FPGA issue is resolved.
bugs.workaround: None. Perpetual reboot loops after trying to load FPGA firmware that do not recover typically indicates a hardware error and requires an RMA.
bugs.fix: One of the BARs fails to initialize when the PCIE speed does not load at the intended Generation. This issue was causing a segmentation fault in the SDK, but it has now been resolved by having the SDK notify the fpgamgr of the missing BAR instead. While the device may still fail to load, the fpgamgr will no longer experience a crashing loop as a result.

bugs.title: CPU data for standby-controller is not displayed in the dashboard
bugs.symptoms: After a controller failover(maybe during live upgrade or otherwise) (or) standby controller reboot, sometimes CPU stats are not displayed in the webUI.
bugs.conditions: A controller failover occurs - maybe during live upgrade or otherwise standby controller reboot
bugs.impact: CPU stats not displayed in the webUI
bugs.workaround: CPU usage can still be collected/monitored from F5OS confD CLI with 'show components component controller-X cpu'

bugs.title: Restoring a backup with an SNMP user on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID will duplicate the SNMP user
bugs.symptoms: If you restore a backup containing an SNMP user, but the SNMP user’s SNMP Engine ID does not match the current system, a new SNMP user will be created with the same name and the current system’s SNMP Engine ID. However, this is only seen when the database is later backed up.
bugs.conditions: -- Restoring a database backup that contains an SNMP user. -- Doing the restore on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID.
bugs.impact: Two SNMP users with the same name (but different SNMP Engine IDs) are saved to subsequent backups. SNMP will not work.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup. SNMP will work after configuring passwords.
bugs.fix: When backup is restored on a system with a different EngineID, SNMP might not work for SNMP users. However, it can be mitigated by reconfiguring the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup.

bugs.title: DDM system alarms triggered when interface is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Running 'show system alarms' reports "Portgroup <N> ERROR Lanes: 1 Transmitter power low alarm"
bugs.conditions: Disabling an interface locally
bugs.impact: Transmitter power low and transmitter bias low alarms occur.
bugs.workaround: To clear the alarms, workaround provided in article K000150155 can be followed.

bugs.title: Fpgamgr failing to clear alarms when unplugging and replugging SFPs combined with disabling/enabling interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Fpgamgr fails to clear the {transmit,receive} {power,bias} {low high} alarms, even though the values are within tolerance.
bugs.conditions: -- Unplugging and replugging SFPs -- Disabling/enabling interfaces at the same time
bugs.impact: The {transmit,receive} {power,bias} {low high} alarms do not clear.

bugs.title: Arrow keys do not work in the GRUB edit screen of the console
bugs.symptoms: The arrow keys do not work as expected in the GRUB edit screen in the console.
bugs.conditions: -- Connected via console. -- In the GRUB edit screen. -- Attempting to use arrow keys on the keyboard.
bugs.impact: Unable to select a GRUB image.
bugs.workaround: If connected via SSH, ctrl-p and ctrl-n can be used for up (previous) and down (next). ctrl-b and ctrl-f can be used for left (back) and right (forward). And ctrl-h can be used to delete a character left to the cursor when backspace key does not work. In addition, the grub.cfg file can be modified to make the arrow keys work. Change: serial --speed=115200 terminal_input serial console terminal_output serial console to terminal_input console terminal_output console
bugs.fix: Remove serial port configurations from grub.cfg. Our BIOS supports serial port console emulation that conflicts to the serial port config.

bugs.title: Daemons that handle ZMQ messages may crash under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: Certain allowed IP configurations on partitions may cause crash scenarios when handling zmq messages
bugs.conditions: Configurations that allow all IPs as part of Allowed IP settings.
bugs.impact: With the said condition, handling certain ZMQ messages may cause daemon crash scenarios.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using allow all IPs as part of Allowed IP configuration.
bugs.fix: Daemons no longer crash in partitions while handling zmq messages

bugs.title: Orchestration Agent process may core
bugs.symptoms: User may see the Orchestration Agent process on the active controller core. Users may find logs with message ID 0x401000000000027. They shall look like the following. network-manager[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x401000000000027 msg="Failed to parse ZMQ message header" session_id="<sessionid>".
bugs.impact: Tenants that are currently running are not affected. New tenants that are deployed when this condition is occurring may be delayed in coming to a running state.
bugs.fix: The Orchestration Agent behaves correctly.

bugs.title: Daemons that handle ZMQ messages may crash under certain conditions.
F5OS chassis switchd core dump
bugs.symptoms: The switchd process experiences crashes that generate core dumps.
bugs.conditions: These crashes are typically observed during certain interface queries or other operations involving statistics updates.
bugs.impact: The switchd process crashes and generates core files. Temporary service disruptions may occur for functionalities reliant on the switchd process.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed, ensuring switchd includes proper handling for TMSTAT query.

bugs.title: Timeout for the Ansible playbook during cluster install cannot be retried.
bugs.symptoms: If there are other issues on the chassis that cause the ansible playbooks to run slowly during Kubernetes cluster install, the playbook cannot be retried correctly if it reaches timeout.
bugs.conditions: This can occur, if there are other issues on the chassis that cause the ansible playbooks to run slowly, such as DNS or remote auth issues when a Kubernetes cluster rebuild is executed.
bugs.impact: The Kubernetes cluster install may fail repeatedly because it will not correctly recognize the timeout, and raise the amount of time it will wait.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation is resolve the issue(s) causing the playbooks to run slowly. This may involving removing bad DNS servers or remote auth servers that may be causing the slow down.
bugs.fix: The orchestration-manager code has been updated to correctly recognize the timeout error, and handle it correctly.

bugs.title: The meaning of the interface phyport internal field changed from phyport to DID. This will break functionality that is using phyport
bugs.symptoms: Two different symptoms surfaced after the meaning of phyport changed: - reset-counters for an specific interface - lag members association with a lag in fpgamgr
bugs.conditions: You configure LAGs while running 1.6.2, with LAG members spanning multiple blades (e.g. blade-1 and blade-3), and then perform a live upgrade to 1.8.0 and above. You attempt to reset counters for a specific interface (e.g. 1/1.0) after a live upgrade from 1.6.2 into 1.8.0 and above.
bugs.impact: For the lag members mismatch, the data packets will be forwarded to the wrong port. For the reset counters, the counters are not reset for the specified interface.
bugs.workaround: For the reset-counters issue, execute reset counters for all interfaces. This will clean up the counters. For the LAG member mismatch, reboot the blades after live install ends successfully.
bugs.fix: The fix addresses the mismatch in interface phyport values. This will allow reset counters per interface to work. This will allow the lag members to be properly handled after live upgrade.

bugs.title: When FIPS license is applied and telemetry enabled, some of the containers metrics will be missing in exporter data
bugs.symptoms: When FIPS license is applied and telemetry enabled, randomly some of the containers metrics will not be transmitted to exporter.
bugs.conditions: Happens only when FIPS license is applied and telemetry is enabled and only when instrument type "all" or "container" is selected in F5OS.
bugs.impact: Randomly some of the containers metrics will not be transmitted to exporter.

bugs.title: Zero is not allowed as Prefix Length for allowed IPs
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to save a prefix length with a value of ‘0’.
bugs.conditions: Prefix Length value is configured to '0'.
bugs.impact: Allowed IPs cannot be created with prefix value '0'.
bugs.workaround: Works from CLI.
bugs.fix: Fixed to accept '0' as prefix length value.

bugs.title: Tenant may not come to Running state after quick movement of slots between partitions
bugs.symptoms: After quick movement of a slot between different partitions, it is possible that tenants on that slot will not come back to the Running state.
bugs.conditions: This situation can occur if nodes are moved from current partition to another partition and then back to original partition.
bugs.impact: Tenant may not come to Running state.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the running-state of the tenant from deployed to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: BX520 Port LED solidly illuminated indicating link up while system software reports link down.
bugs.symptoms: The BX520 Port LED may be solidly illuminated indicating link up while system software reports link down. This is typically a transient condition during initial port bringup. If it persists, it could be an indication of a problem with the fiber or at the link partner.
bugs.conditions: The BX520 Port LED is illuminated solid when the associated port has achieved RX alignment. The system software indicates port status UP when the BX520 port has achieved RX Alignment AND the link partner has also signaled it has achieved RX Alignment through the 802.3 Remote Fault Indicator protocol. It is expected that there may be transient cases of this during port bringup. If it persists, it can be an indication that the BX520 was able to achieve RX alignment but the link partner was not.
bugs.impact: Differences in Link status as reported by HW LED and SW Status can cause confusion.

bugs.title: LDAP Remote user may show as a different user after logging in to the system
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Remote user may show as a different user after logging in to the system and using the 'who' command.
bugs.conditions: LDAP auth is not configured at the time the local user is created, then LDAP auth is configured.
bugs.impact: If LDAP auth is not configured at the time the local user is created, the account could potentially end up with the same local user's UIDs. However, the permissions will not be be determined by the UIDs, therefore the account is required to have the correct permissions.

bugs.title: Error log does not contain all needed information.
bugs.symptoms: An "Interface data differ" log is logged by l2-agent, but all of the compared fields in the log message are identical.
bugs.conditions: L2-agent logs an error message that the interface data differs.
bugs.impact: The lack of some data such as interface type and slot ID in the log entry makes troubleshooting more complex.
bugs.workaround: Save the backup configuration file, and inspect the file for hidden fields. For example, search for pgindex under the interface entry.
bugs.fix: With this change, the log ERROR will display all required data.

bugs.title: Partition upgrade or creation fails on controller
bugs.symptoms: Partition upgrade or creation fails due to missing partition_image volume. vcc-confd - /confd/scripts/f5_confd_run_cmd show partitions install # show partitions install INSTALL INSTALL BLADE OS SERVICE BLADE OS SERVICE INSTALL INSTALLING NAME ID VERSION VERSION VERSION VERSION STATUS CONTROLLER ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ none - - - - - - - controller-1 1 1.8.0-26321 1.8.0-26321 1.8.0-26321 1.8.0-26321 success - controller-2 2 1.6.2-26579 1.6.2-26579 1.8.0-26321 1.8.0-26321 in-progress 2 You may see below messages in /var/log/sw-util.log: /usr/libexec/sw-mgmt/sw-util.sh nodename=controller-2 resize 1 10 15 10: priority=Error msgid=0x3501000000000074 msg=Failed to create LV for partition 1. /usr/libexec/sw-mgmt/sw-util.sh nodename=controller-2 enable_partition 2 10 15 10: priority=Error msgid=0x3501000000000074 msg=Failed to create LV for partition 2
bugs.conditions: The partition upgrade or creation is unsuccessful because the partition_image volume is not present. This is a rare problem that may occur due to a mismatch in metadata while converting the LVM to VDO volume.
bugs.impact: The partition upgrade or creation is unsuccessful.
bugs.workaround: Do PXE clean installation of the affected system controller. K000152443: VELOS PXE clean install of system controller https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000152443

bugs.title: F5OS LLDP details page cannot display information about neighbors with matching port IDs
bugs.symptoms: On the LLDP Details page in the F5OS GUI, clicking on a neighbor row expands to show information about the neighbor system. If the F5OS system is connected to the same interface on multiple peer switches, the F5OS GUI will always show neighbor information for the first matching interface. For example: F5OS interface 3.0 => switch 1 xe-0/0/38 F5OS interface 4.0 => switch 2 xe-0/0/38 The F5OS system is connected to port xe-0/0/38 on two different switches, and attempting to use the F5OS GUI to view neighbor information for the neighbor on interface 4.0 will show the information from interface 3.0.
bugs.conditions: F5OS system with LLDP enabled. Multiple interfaces on the F5OS system connected to the same port ID on distinct switches.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the GUI to view neighbor information about some LLDP
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI or API to retrieve information about LLDP neighbors. For example, log into the CLI as an admin user and run "show lldp interfaces interface neighbor"
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed in new look and feel, now preview pane shows correct data even of the ids are same for two neighbours.

bugs.title: Missing internal interface pgindex field causes l2-agent to restart
bugs.symptoms: Upon upgrade from 1.1 -> 1.6 -> 1.8, l2-agent on blade will exit due to interface data mismatch. This mismatch happens because the pgindex hidden leaf is missing from cdb, but the l2-agent on blade expects it.
bugs.conditions: Chain upgraded from 1.1 -> 1.6 -> 1.8. Version 1.8 is the version where l2-agent added more logic to check interface data inconsistency.
bugs.impact: Dataplane is not functioning.
bugs.workaround: Work around is to delete the blades from the partition and re-add them. This will require user to reconfigure interface data (vlans, lag members).
bugs.fix: With this fix, the upgrade into 1.8 will work as expected, and l2-agent on the blade will find matching interface data.

bugs.title: Standby tenant is unreachable after F5OS partition upgrade to 1.7.x or higher.
bugs.symptoms: - The `tmsh show net arp` may show arps with an unknown status. - The confd CLI `show dag-states` command shows dag tables consisting of only zeros.
bugs.conditions: * Multi-slot tenant in a device group * Connection mirroring enabled * Upgrade F5OS partition from 1.6.x to 1.7.x or greater
bugs.impact: Standby tenant is inaccessible.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed in F5OS partition upgrades to 1.7.x or higher.

bugs.title: Version option is not need when creating Certificate Signing Request
bugs.symptoms: GUI is showing a version field that you can fill in when creating a Certificate Signing Request. But this option is not required.
bugs.conditions: Creating a Certificate Signing Request via the GUI.
bugs.impact: The option is not needed, the field value is ignored.
bugs.fix: The field is removed now from the Certificate Signing Request form.

bugs.title: Users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured
bugs.symptoms: - CLI/GUI access for all roles other than admin and root is denied - The GUI permit user authentication and then immediately terminate the session; for more information, refer to https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1933645.html. - Repeated log messages from user-manager in platform.log / velos.log with an error of "Lost connection to ConfD" / "Socket to ConfD is closed": user-manager[17]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6802000000000001 msg="cdb_get failed for" ATTRIBUTE="rolename" ERRNOSTR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="Socket to ConfD is closed" ERRNO=45.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication is enabled - A LDAP group is defined for a role in the system - Queries to the LDAP server take a long time, for example due to connection timeouts or LDAP referral chasing. This issue can also occur when the system is rebooted if user-manager tries to perform LDAP queries before the management network is accessible.
bugs.impact: Users with roles other than admin and root cannot login using CLI or GUI
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart the appropriate user-manager container (system_user_manager on rSeries appliances, controller-userman for VELOS system controllers, and partition<ID>_user_manager for VELOS partitions) 2. Disable LDAP system authentication or remove the LDAP group definitions, and then restart the user-manager container. This will restore connectivity for locally-defined users.
bugs.fix: Fix users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured

bugs.title: Inconsistency with network interface alarms
bugs.symptoms: An example of the issue: Both portgroup 3/1 and 3/2 have state ddm rx-pwr instant val-lane4 = -40.0, but only one reports an alarm. There also seems to be a discrepancy regarding the alarms and the logs The alarm log from velos.log reports an error from Portgroup 3/1: fpgamgr[13]: nodename=blade-3(p3) priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x304000000000012 msg="DDM low warning set" PORTGROUP="3/1" ALARMTYPE="receive power" LANE1=-0.029600 LANE2=-0.008900 LANE3=-0.046900 LANE4=-0.400000. But the alarm is reported for Portgroup 3/2: # show system alarms ID RESOURCE SEVERITY TEXT TIME CREATED ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 262401 Portgroup 3/2 ERROR Lanes: 4 Receiver power low alarm 2025-02-12 09:10:19.603552427 UTC
bugs.conditions: Both interfaces enabled, but disconnected (no cables inserted). Affects both VELOS and rSeries (r5000, r10000, r12000)
bugs.impact: Inconsistent alarms may be reported for only one of the Portgroups when both Portgroups have low rx-power values.

bugs.title: VELOS partition Allowed IP rule restrictions
bugs.symptoms: Configuring a "system allowed-ips allowed-ip" rule in a VELOS partition without limiting it to a specific port (22, 80, 443, 7001-7032, 8888, or SNMP) allows access to more than expected.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS partition - Allowed IP Address rules configured to use port 'All' in the GUI (or that do not specify a specific port when configured via the CLI)
bugs.impact: Permits more traffic than it should.
bugs.workaround: Instead of creating an 'All' port allowed IP address rule, create individual rules for each specific port.
bugs.fix: Expected behavior is performed when using port 'All'.

bugs.title: Memory leak in l2_agent daemon on F5OS
bugs.symptoms: - Large memory consumption by the l2_agent. - Tenant disruption on F5 rSeries appliance.
bugs.conditions: - An F5OS system with SNMP configured and a LAG (Link Aggregation Group) with more than 1 member. - SNMP monitoring in use. We can check the l2_agent memory consumption by using `top` command. Ex: Top output showed a 15GB l2_agent process: PID USER PR NI VIRT RES SHR S %CPU %MEM TIME+ COMMAND 19454 root 20 0 17.3g 14.9g 1788 S 0.0 5.9 174:04.57 /confd/bin/l2_agent -s appliance-1
bugs.impact: Eventually the system experience OOM (Out of Memory). On an F5 rSeries appliance, a tenant might experience disruptions and slowness, up to and including a TMM SIGABRT core.
bugs.workaround: Restart the L2_agent process on the F5OS host. On an rSeries appliance, one of the following: - as root, run the command 'docker restart system_L2' - as an administrative user from the F5OS CLI, enter config mode and then run 'system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service system_L2' On a VELOS system, restart the partition<ID>_L2 instance on each controller. Log into the system controller as an administrative user, enter config mode, and then run: system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node controller-1 service partition1_L2 system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node controller-2 service partition1_L2 (Adjust 'partition1' to the partition ID for the partition in question)
bugs.fix: The l2_agent process no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: CVE 2020-27743: pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes().
bugs.symptoms: libtac in pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes(). This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id.
bugs.conditions: The current version pam_tacplus from version 1.6.0 doesn't have the fix as this was added in version 1.6.1 source package.
bugs.impact: This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id which means an adversary could gain access.
bugs.fix: By updating the pam_tacplus source code to 1.7.0 where the vulnerability was fixed in 1.6.1, the new code does not have this issue.

bugs.title: F5OS LDAP operations from authentication-manager and user-manager do not respect timeouts or chase-referrals
bugs.symptoms: LDAP queries performed by authentication-manager and user-manager do not respect some of the LDAP configuration, in particular chase-referrals and connection and bind timeouts. LDAP queries take an extensive period of time. This can result in user-manager losing its connection to confd, resulting in the problems described in https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication - authentication-manager trying to query the directory, which will occur if active_directory is enabled and unix_attributes is disabled. - user-manager trying to query the directory, which will occur if an LDAP group mapping is defined for a user role.
bugs.impact: Remotely-authenticated users will not work. Further problems may occur as described in https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html

bugs.title: REST API for Docker Restart command fails
bugs.symptoms: The endpoint restconf/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:diagnostics/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:os-utils/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:docker/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:restart can be used (with POST) to restart some Docker containers. However it will fail with the message "restart aborted", e.g.: { "f5-system-diagnostics-docker:output": { "result": "snmpd restart aborted" } }
bugs.conditions: Attempting to restart a Docker container using the REST API.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the REST API to restart a Docker container.
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI instead: config system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node <node> service <service>

bugs.title: The network-manager container crashes when it fails to create FDB entry in database
bugs.symptoms: Network-manager container crashes.
bugs.conditions: The issue may occur when there is an upgrade/downgrade, tenant creation/deletion, or reset/restore the database.
bugs.impact: The network-manager container will restart.
bugs.fix: The network-manager will not crash when it fails to create FDB entry in database.

bugs.title: Duplicate lag members in show interfaces interface lag output
bugs.symptoms: The show lag output may display multiple occurrences of the same members within a lag.
bugs.conditions: In some instances, after an upgrade, some members show up twice.
bugs.impact: No functional impact is identified at this time. This is considered to be cosmetic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround identified at this time.

bugs.title: Health summary is not reported for some nodes in controller and partition ConfD
bugs.symptoms: System health summary is missing for some nodes.
bugs.conditions: It is observed when iso is upgraded to 1.8.1 branch
bugs.impact: System health summary is not reported for some nodes. It throws error while fetching summary.
bugs.fix: Updated Node tag in components properly. Since GET:health api is fixed in diag-agent, Show system health summary reports etails properly for all nodes.

bugs.title: F5OS password policy's "max-letter-repeat" description is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In the CLI, the description for "max-letter-repeat" in the password policy ("system aaa password-policy") has an incorrect description. Currently it states that it, "Reject passwords with this many repeating lower-case letters in the password". It actually applies to any repeating consecutive characters, not just lower-case letters.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the CLI's online help for the password policy's "max-letter-repeat" setting.
bugs.impact: The incorrect description may lead to an unintended password policy.

bugs.title: Traffic over a LAG not working after upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1, the internal LAG programming may become faulty, resulting in incorrect configuration of interfaces within the LAG. This issue disrupts the proper flow of traffic.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.impact: Traffic over the LAG does not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blades hosting the members of the LAG.

bugs.title: Traffic over a LAG not working after upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1, the internal LAG programming may become faulty, resulting in incorrect configuration of interfaces within the LAG. This issue disrupts the proper flow of traffic.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.impact: Traffic over the LAG doesn’t work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blades hosting the members of the LAG.

bugs.title: High memory utilization by NetworkManager
bugs.symptoms: After a VELOS system controller, blade, or rSeries appliance has been running for several hundred days, the NetworkManager service may start leaking memory. This will eventually result in system instability including a failover between system controllers, or instability to tenants. Log messages similar to the following occurring in /var/log/messages or the systemd journal: controller-2.chassis.local NetworkManager[180091]: gsignal.c:2642: instance '0x564069a2be40' has no handler with id '34120' Prior to these log messages being generated, there is no way to tell if the issue is close to occurring.
bugs.conditions: The NetworkManager service has been running for a substantial period of time (i.e. more than 500 days).
bugs.impact: NetworkManager service utilizes high memory in the system, which leads to controller failover.
bugs.workaround: Restart NetworkManager by logging in to the appropriate device as root (system controller, blade, or appliance) and running the command "systemctl restart NetworkManager".

bugs.title: When attributes are added under exporters for Open Telemetry, the keys are not visible in the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: When attributes are added under exporters for Open Telemetry, the keys are not visible in the GUI. If any exporters have existing attributes and you try to edit the exporter from the GUI, the attributes get deleted.
bugs.conditions: Adding or updating attributes to an open telemetry exporter through the GUI.
bugs.impact: -- New attributes created under exporters don not have their keys visible in the GUI. -- Editing the exporter from the GUI will delete existing attributes.
bugs.workaround: Add attributes to exporters or update existing exporters via the CLI.

bugs.title: Blades are not upgraded after partition upgraded to 1.8.1 from 1.8.0 EHF build
bugs.symptoms: Blades are still running on the previous version of F5OS even after the partition upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Control plane network connectivity to the blades has been lost due to incomplete internal trunk / VLAN programming.
bugs.impact: Blades report that they are not running the current version of F5OS software and/or control plane Connectivity may be lost between CC and one or more blades over unprogrammed vlans.
bugs.workaround: Recommended recovery path is to perform a staggered reboot of both System Controllers: 1. Reboot the standby system controller. 2. After the standby is rebooted, run the SC confd configuration command system redundancy go-standby. 3. After the go-standby completes, reboot the new standby System Controller.

bugs.title: During partition software upgrade dagd process may crash and dump a core
bugs.symptoms: During partition software upgrade (or when multiple blades are restarted simultaneously), dagd process crashes and produces a core dumpump a core.
bugs.conditions: One of: -- Partition software version is upgraded. -- Multiple blades are restarted at the same time.
bugs.impact: This has no impact except for the core dump.
bugs.workaround: Prior to a partition software upgrade, manually move your tenants into provisioned running state.
bugs.fix: Fixed dagd core dump during partition software upgrade.

bugs.title: LDAP role mappings may not update after LDAP configuration changes.
bugs.symptoms: User role mappings may become outdated or incorrect after changes to LDAP configuration settings.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when LDAP settings are modified after roles are already configured, such as changes to bind credentials, server groups, unix-attributes, authentication method, or other LDAP options.
bugs.impact: Users may receive incorrect roles or experience authorization issues until role mappings are refreshed.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure or refresh LDAP role mappings after making LDAP configuration changes. appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication roles role <role> config ldap-group <ldap-group>
bugs.fix: Improved LDAP change detection and remapping logic so role mappings are automatically updated when LDAP configuration settings change.

bugs.title: Openshift cluster rebuild can timeout when LDAP is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When the user initiates a cluster reinstall while LDAP is enabled, the operation may time out.
bugs.conditions: The timeout during a cluster reinstall may occur due to slowness in the LDAP queries.
bugs.impact: The cluster reinstall may not complete due to the timeouts.
bugs.workaround: User needs to disable LDAP before issuing cluster reinstall.

bugs.title: "Failed to write to cdb" and "Unable to set STP VLAN state" error logs are seen with MSTP configuration deletion via CLI
bugs.symptoms: Stpd and FPGA error logs are observed while doing MSTP configuration. In platform.log: stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance mst-id" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance designated-root-address" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="WriteTenantOperMSTInstance failed" ERRNO=0 ERRNOSTR="Unknown error".
bugs.conditions: 1. Create VLANs. 2. Attach VLANs to the interfaces. 3. Enable MSTP using webUI. Select Network Settings > STP configuration and select MSTP. 4. Create an instance(1) and attach a VLAN to it (created VLANs). 5. Add the interfaces to instance 1. 6. Delete mstp instance. 7. You will observe errors under platform.log.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on MSTP behavior and convergence.

bugs.title: GUI immediately logs user off with "User Session Terminated" error and "validator" process cores
bugs.symptoms: After logging into the device, the GUI immediately reports "User Session Terminated. You will be logged out of the application." Core files generated from the "validator" process in the confd container (system_manager, vcc-confd, or partition<X>_manager).
bugs.conditions: Trying to login to the GUI, and the "limited" group is missing from /etc/group. The "limited" group is an internal role that should always be defined and cannot be deleted by a user. The most likely reason for it to be missing is https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.impact: Users are not able to access the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Apply a workaround for https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.fix: Even if the "limited" group goes missing, users should still be able to access the GUI.

bugs.title: Interface remain down in F5OS after removing and reinserting SFP modules
bugs.symptoms: After SFPs are removed and reinserted in a VELOS blade, the interface will remain down in F5OS until the blade is rebooted. The peer switch may report the interfaces as having a link.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS chassis running F5OS-C 1.8.0 - SFPs in blade are removed and reinserted.
bugs.impact: F5OS interfaces remain reported as operationally down until the blade is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: After SFP modules are removed and reinserted on a blade, reboot the blade.

bugs.title: OpenShift 3.11 Control Plane Memory Growth on Controllers (master-api/master-controllers)
bugs.symptoms: Over time, controller memory utilization steadily increases due to growth in OpenShift 3.11 control-plane processes (openshift start master api and openshift start master controllers). Initially, the Chassis and pods generally remain operational. However, prolonged uptime can lead to elevated load, reduced performance margin, and eventual need for controller reboot to reclaim memory.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs during normal long-running operation on systems using embedded OpenShift 3.11 control-plane components. As uptime increases (days to weeks), the openshift start master api and openshift start master controllers processes exhibit gradual RSS memory growth.
bugs.impact: Steady rise in the memory usage of the controller and higher sustained system load over time.
bugs.workaround: Perform a controller reboot to temporarily reclaim memory.

bugs.title: Logging doest work properly if wrong tls is configured for remote log servers
bugs.symptoms: Logging is halted qkview generation fails
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS configured for remote log server authentication for secure log forwarding. -- TLS settings are missing or incorrect
bugs.impact: F5OS logging will be stopped.
bugs.workaround: Fix the wrong or missed tls configuration for remote logging servers.

bugs.title: Telemetry exporter attribute values are not showing in CLI
bugs.symptoms: Telemetry exporter attribute values are not showing in CLI.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when user creates new exporter and attributes together.
bugs.impact: Telemetry attribute values will not be displayed in the CLI.
bugs.workaround: Create the exporter first and add attributes. Alternatively, exporters and attributes can be added from the GUI.

bugs.title: Partitions can leave stale tenant pods when controller configuration reset to default is issued
bugs.symptoms: Partition tenants that are configured with slots greater than max-nodes can fail to come back when resetting the controller configuration and restoring it back via save configuration for controller and partition.
bugs.conditions: Occurs typically when - Partition with ID 1 - Tenant uses virtual slots that do not match the physical slot. - Controller reset-to-default is issued
bugs.impact: Stale tenant pods for partition 1 tenants will still show after restoring the controller configuration and partition configuration, but the impacted tenants may not came back up fully (multinodes case).
bugs.workaround: - Bring partition tenants down if planning to do controller configuration reset-to-default. or - Manually delete default partition 1 after reset-to-default before restoring the save controller configuration. This should take care of removing everything associated to the namespace before the config-restore happens. Partitions with ID different than 1 should clear the namespace automatically, since they don't get recreated as part of reset-to-default.
bugs.fix: Startup stale cleanup logic has been adjusted to manage multinode and virtual slots tenants appropriately.

bugs.title: QKView creation status does not update automatically in the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: When generating a QKView via the web UI, the progress status remains at "Collecting - 0% completed" and does not update automatically.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the GUI to generate a system diagnostics report (QKView). The status updates only if the user manually refreshes the page or switches windows.
bugs.impact: Users cannot track the real-time progress of QKView creation through the GUI. The display may incorrectly suggest the process is stalled at 0%.
bugs.workaround: Manually refresh the browser page or navigate to a different GUI screen and back to update the status.
bugs.fix: The GUI now correctly reflects the real-time progress of QKView generation without requiring a manual page refresh.

bugs.title: F5OS does not clear OpenShift certificate expired/expiring alarms
bugs.symptoms: If F5OS raises "One or more openshift certificates has expired or is expiring." alarm, it won't successfully clear it when show_certs.sh no longer reports expiring certs.
bugs.conditions: -- OpenShift certificate expiring/expired alarm has been raised. -- The condition triggering the alarm was resolved.
bugs.impact: Stale critical alert.
bugs.workaround: Run this command to manually clear the alarm: docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert --source controller-1 --name openshiftCertificatesExpiring --report clear --id 524289 --severity critical

bugs.title: When running a tenant with more than 72 VCPUs / cores, adminstall crashes
bugs.symptoms: When running a tenant with more than 72 VCPUs / cores, adminstall crashes.
bugs.conditions: When ASM provisioned and running a Tenant with more than 72 VCPUs / cores per blade.
bugs.impact: DOSL7 (BADOS) is not functioning. Core created.

bugs.title: Qkview-collect crashes while collecting a QKView
bugs.symptoms: Qkview-collect may crash when collecting a QKView.
bugs.conditions: This happens intermittently when collecting a QKView.
bugs.impact: Unable to collect a QKView.

bugs.title: When setting "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" to false, trying to change user password fails and triggers application timeout
bugs.symptoms: - The GUI reports a Server Error 'application timeout' when attempting to change a user's password. - Attempting to load the "Users & Roles" page fails with the error "Failure for data/openconfig-system:system/aaa/authentication/f5-system-aaa:roles/role API. The server or an underlying service is unreachable."
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - The local password policy "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" option (referred to as "apply-to-root" in the CLI and API) is set to "false". The default for this option is "true". - Attempt to change a user's password.
bugs.impact: The user manager daemon is temporarily unresponsive. It should recover after approximately five minutes. Attempts to change user's password does not take effect and authentication fails when using the new password.
bugs.workaround: Set the "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" / "apply-to-root" option to "true".

bugs.title: Controller-manager pods in CrashLoopBackOff state
bugs.symptoms: After a controller restart, controller-manager pods enter CrashLoopBackOff state, if the API server certificate has expired. This can occur when the API server certificate reaches a 2-year expiry.
bugs.conditions: -- API server certificate is expired -- A controller is rebooted.
bugs.impact: The controller-manager pods crash repeatedly and new blades can not be added. Expired API server certificate does not cause traffic disruption on an otherwise healthy running device, only failures to change configuration or add/remove blades.
bugs.workaround: To check if cert is expired, run as root: oc get secret apiserver-ssl -n kube-service-catalog -o jsonpath='{.data.tls＼.crt}' | base64 --decode | openssl x509 -noout -enddate To renew the certificate and fix the issue: As the root user: docker exec -it orchestration_manager ansible-playbook -v -i /tmp/omd/etc_ansible_hosts playbooks/openshift-service-catalog/config.yml This script takes about 5 minutes to run and then the pods are fixed
bugs.fix: The API server certificate has had its expiry changed to 10 years to align with the other certificates on the system.

bugs.title: Partition may fail to come online on one controller after it is created
bugs.symptoms: A new partition that is created may fail to come online as one of the controllers is seen in the Failed state.
bugs.conditions: While this error log is seen it is not clear what causes this condition to occur.
bugs.impact: The partition is not in a Ready state.
bugs.workaround: The partition state will need to be toggled to disabled and then to enabled.

bugs.title: SSH configuration file on the active controller can be corrupted
bugs.symptoms: It is possible that the SSH configuration file on the active controller can become corrupted.
bugs.conditions: The SSH configuration file is not protected correctly from the multi-threaded orchestration-manager process.
bugs.impact: Host names that do not correspond to the correct IP addresses are observed.
bugs.workaround: The corrupted configuration file required to be fixed manually.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: High CPU or increased translation errors following upgrade or restart when DAG distribution changes
bugs.symptoms: Dagv2 tables are randomized and may change when a tmm is restarted. This can result in a change of traffic distribution, which in some cases may lead to traffic disruption. The specific condition when this option was introduced is using a CGNAT pool that is not large enough.
bugs.conditions: - tmm is restarted (or chassis rebooted)
bugs.impact: - dag distribution changes which may cause a traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: You can restart tmm until the distribution is good, which can be checked using tools like cmp_dest.
bugs.fix: ID 1966941 added two DB variables to control dagv2 behavior - sdag.runtime.hashtable sdag.runtime.mirror.hashtable. This adds F5OS-side support to this solution.

bugs.title: "Show cluster" may incorrectly log a system controller as not present
bugs.symptoms: When running "show cluster", it may show a message like this, even though a system controller is present: Controller 2 is NOT present. A service incorrectly reads that a system controller is not present, but correctly reads it as present immediately after.
bugs.conditions: This happens very rarely. There are no specific conditions that will cause this issue.
bugs.impact: This only causes a message to be logged and does not affect the stability of the chassis.

bugs.title: Confd.smp memory consumption spikes high with snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled
bugs.symptoms: When config-restore is performed on a RMA system, with the configuration of SNMPv3 users and targets and snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled, observed confd.smp process memory spikes increase and causes OOM after system reboot.
bugs.conditions: Restoring the configuration onto an RMA replacement system.
bugs.impact: Confd's RSS memory begins to grow rapidly and causes restart of ConfD process.
bugs.workaround: The available workarounds, 1. After performing config-restore on a RMA system, disable snmpEnableAuthenTraps 2. Reset all SNMPv3 users and passwords right after performing config-restore.
bugs.fix: Disabling snmpEnableAuthenTraps when the engine-id of the database backup and the system engine-id. This will prevent confd.smp process memory hike in case of any sudden reboot of the system. User can reconfigure the snmpEnableAuthenTraps after reseting the SNMPv3 users authentication and privacy password.

bugs.title: iHealth upload is failing with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use the QKView upload feature, the upload may fail with the message "certificate signed by unknown authority". This is due to a recent Entrust certificate authority shutdown resulted inconsistency between F5OS and iHealth.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to upload a qkview file to iHealth after 30 June 2025.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload QKView files to iHealth with a single click.
bugs.workaround: You can use the File Export feature to download QKView files, and then log into iHealth and upload the files via the iHealth page. You can find the QKView files in the GUI at System Settings > File Utilities, then choose "diags/shared" as the base directory, then select "qkview".
bugs.fix: Certificate authorities used by the iHealth upload feature in F5OS will be updated.

bugs.title: Can't upgrade F5OS-C 1.8.x FIPS-licensed chassis to F5OS 2.x
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-C-1.8.0 and 1.8.1, the "check-version-fips" and "set-version-fips" commands fail with a compatibility check failure.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade chassis from 1.8.0 or 1.8.1 to 2.0 or later w/ FIPS licensed.
bugs.impact: Cannot upgrade to F5OS 2.x
bugs.fix: Upgrade compatibility check succeeds.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Tenant's VM will be patched/relaunched everytime after system reboot/upgrade/failover/TPOB restart
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from F5OS v1.6.1/1.7.0 to v1.8.x, tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and recreated, VM patches also not being properly applied.
bugs.conditions: - System upgraded from F5OS-C v1.6.1 or v1.7.0 to v1.8.x. - System reboot, failover, or TPOB restart occurs.
bugs.impact: Tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and relaunched after every reboot.
bugs.workaround: None. Recommended to upgrade to F5OS-C v1.8.3 which includes this fix.
bugs.fix: These changes prevent unnecessary VM patching and recreation after system upgrades, reboots, or TPOB restarts while ensuring legitimate patches are properly applied.

bugs.title: In IPv6-only environment, remote authentication using RADIUS server by hostname may not work
bugs.symptoms: F5OS remote authentication does not work. Administrator can observe F5OS performing DNS resolution of the configured RADIUS server, but F5OS never transmits RADIUS Access-Request packets to the server.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS host is configured with only an IPv6 management IP address. - RADIUS remote authentication configured with a RADIUS server specified via hostname. - RADIUS server hostname has both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (i.e. both A and AAAA records in DNS)
bugs.impact: Remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: Create a separate hostname for the RADIUS server that only resolves to an IPv6 address.

bugs.title: Logging from PAM modules only seen for SSH authentication, and not GUI/API authentication
bugs.symptoms: Logging from PAM modules (e.g. pam_unix, pam_radius_auth, or pam_unix) is only captured in system logs when a user attempts to authenticate via SSH; no such logging occurs when authenticating via the F5OS GUI or API.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - Attempting to troubleshoot issues related to authentication
bugs.impact: PAM module log messages are not logged anywhere. The system does generate authentication success/failure messages that are captured in the audit.log, e.g.: audit-service[12]: priority="Notice" version=1.0 msgid=0x1f03000000000012 msg="User authentication failed" reason="Invalid login attempt, user-id/password is incorrect" failcount=8 user="otters".
bugs.workaround: When troubleshooting authentication issues, attempt to log in via SSH. PAM modules will generate log messages that are captured in /var/log/secure and the systemd journal.

bugs.title: Unable to change F5OS primary key with LDAP TLS client cert+key set
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to set the system's primary key ("system aaa primary-key set") aborts and fails. System log shows: authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x7b01000000000075 msg="OpenSSL Keys and Certificates must start with -----BEGIN ...".
bugs.conditions: -- LDAP TLS certificate and key are configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to change primary key on device.
bugs.workaround: 1. Make sure you know the unencrypted value of the LDAP TLS cert and key. 2. Remove the LDAP TLS cert and key values 3. Rotate the system primary key 4. Re-configure the LDAP TLS cert and key values.

bugs.title: OPT-0056 QSFPO Rev 1C showing as "40G/100GBASE-FR" in "show portgroup" output
bugs.symptoms: OPT-0056 QSFPs have 100G media speed. The Rev 1A shows this when running "show portgroups", but the Rev 1C versions show "40G/100GBASE-FR".
bugs.conditions: -- OPT-0056 Rev 1C QSFP installed in the system. -- Running "show portgroups" on the CLI.
bugs.impact: Misinformation.

bugs.title: WebUi does not display warning about Zeroization during FIPS license installation or removal
bugs.symptoms: When adding or removing a FIPS license through the webUI, no notification is provided to alert that this action will initiate zeroization and results in the deletion of all partitions and the primary key.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during the installation or removal of a FIPS license using the webUI.
bugs.impact: The absence of this warning can lead to unintentional data loss.
bugs.workaround: The CLI provides a warning during this operation. Additionally, the Admin Guide documents this behaviour and its implications.

bugs.title: VOQ IMM watchdog does not resolve
bugs.symptoms: VOQs do not sync after an IMM watchdog. Backplane traffic may be disrupted.
bugs.conditions: IMM VOQ watchdog occurs.
bugs.impact: Backplane traffic may be disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected blade.

bugs.title: OTel telemetry data for a system controller or blade stopped after its reboot
bugs.symptoms: If a system controller is rebooted or a blade is rebooted or removed and inserted back, OTel telemetry data is stopped for it.
bugs.conditions: System controller or blade reboot, blade removed and inserted back.
bugs.impact: OTel telemetry data is stopped after a blade or system controller reboot.
bugs.workaround: Blade reboot scenario - making changes in the exporter path like disabling and enabling back, change in instrument list might help. Restartinig diag-agent on the active system controller might help. In a system controller reboot scenario - restart diag-agent on the active system controller.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing OTel telemetry data to stop being collected after a reboot.

bugs.title: No egress traffic from front-panel interface for port 1/2.1 in 4x100G mode on CX1610/BX520 blades
bugs.symptoms: Symptom is no traffic from front-panel interface for port 1/2.1 in 4x100G mode.
bugs.conditions: CX1610/BX520 blade front panel ports have to be configured in 4x100G mode.
bugs.impact: Loss of traffic routed to front panel.
bugs.workaround: This has been fixed with a TAM bitfile update in F5OS-C-1.8.1 EHF2 and newer. This issue is fixed in TAM FPGA bitfile version 73.80.18.66 and newer.
bugs.fix: FPGA logic fix in TAM FPGA bitfile version 73.80.18.66 (or newer).

bugs.title: VLAN cannot be deleted after removing all tenant and interface references
bugs.symptoms: If a box experiences hitting Bug ID 1759761, sometimes the workaround for that bug does not always work. The currently published workaround for that bug is: "The [vlan] deletion operation can be retried, or wait a moment after unassigning the VLAN before deleting it." However, in some cases the vlan delete will always fail because the vlan-listener for the tenant is never removed. Which means every attempt to delete the vlan will fail until the vlan-listener is removed, and any lingering fdb entries. You will see one or even a handful of vlan listeners that should not exist anymore.
bugs.conditions: Sometimes it will take several iterations for the vlan-listener to not be deleted in time. It's possible enabling network-manager and api-svc-gw debug logging increases the probability of hitting this bug. 1. Create and deploy a tenant 2. Copy the bash script vlan.tenant.tort.bsh to an external client 3. Modify the script to match rseries or partition mgmt ip, username, password and tenant name: ex. PARTITION_MGMT_IP=172.12.12.12 USERNAME=admin PASSWORD=admin TENANT=rdt1 4. run show vlan-listener | repeat 1 on the rSeries 5. run the script: while :;do date;bash vlan.tenant.tort.bsh 1;echo "sleeping for 10";sleep 10;done 6. As soon as the script reports it's sleeping for 10 seconds, check to see if the vlan-listener still exists from the output of #5. If its still there for 2+ seconds; kill the bash script to leave the device in that state.
bugs.impact: VLAN-listener does not get deleted, and will show disabled.
bugs.workaround: There are two delays needed, which I know is less then ideal. One for Bug ID 1759761 which is before removing the vlan entirely. and A second one for Bug ID 1983061 before removing the vlan from the tenant. And both bugs are resolved by the change for 1759761 which is fixed in F5OS v2.0.0 and is unfortunately not backportable.
bugs.fix: Fixed in version 2.0.0.

bugs.title: System uptime misreported when uptime is 7 days or more
bugs.symptoms: The "show system uptime" command and uptime reported for controllers and blades in the F5OS GUI will report incorrect uptime values when it has an uptime that is 7 days or more, e.g.: [root@controller-1:Active ~]# f5sh show system uptime NAME UPTIME --------------------------------- controller-1 0d, 21h, 36m, 55s controller-2 3d, 5h, 37m, 27s [root@controller-1:Active ~]# uptime 15:41:54 up 21 days, 21:36, 1 user, load average: 6.73, 7.01, 6.56 [root@controller-1:Active ~]#
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system
bugs.impact: The "show system uptime" command output fails to include the number of weeks of uptime.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and run "uptime" on the appropriate system controller or blade.

bugs.title: Add output of "show system uptime" for Qkview data
bugs.symptoms: Uptime data was missing from QKView data.
bugs.conditions: No ConfD repo changes for collecting output of uptime.
bugs.impact: No uptime data about devices for debugging and records.
bugs.workaround: Changes to ConfD repo for collecting output for uptime.
bugs.fix: Qkview will have output of "show system uptime".

bugs.title: After upgrade, non-default F5OS logging is set to INFORMATIONAL despite configuration
bugs.symptoms: After a software upgrade, daemons may revert to logging at the INFORMATIONAL log level, regardless of what is actually configured. For example, the configuration may indicate that authentication manager has debug logging enabled, but it will not generate any debug logs.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system upgrade - A component has a non-default log severity configured.
bugs.impact: System does not generate debug logs when expected.
bugs.workaround: Set the log level to INFORMATIONAL and then set it back to the desired severity. For example, from the F5OS CLI: config system logging sw-components sw-component authd config severity INFORMATIONAL ; top ; commit system logging sw-components sw-component authd config severity DEBUG ; top ; commit
bugs.fix: An order in which conditions are checked was changed to not skip updating the severities that the individual components use to know at what level they are logging.

bugs.title: F5 VELOS BX520 TAM firmware v73.80.18.66
bugs.symptoms: F5 VELOS BX520 TAM firmware v73.80.18.66
bugs.conditions: F5 VELOS BX520 Platform.
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes issue with 4x100G mode. See ID1983021 for more information.

bugs.title: File download failing from log/system
bugs.symptoms: File download failing from log/system using GUI and RESTCONF both.
bugs.conditions: While trying to to download audit.log or the file from host directory from log/system, 500 internal server error will display
bugs.impact: Not able to download the log file.
bugs.workaround: Instead of download use file export utility

bugs.title: VOQs don't recover after window error on own slot
bugs.symptoms: Traffic outage after a VOQ window error occurs on a the blade's own slot. The VQF_CORE_GLOBAL_ACTIVE_BLADES_REG (0x1024) on the blade will not have the bit for itself asserted.
bugs.conditions: VOQ window error occurs on a the blade's own slot.
bugs.impact: Traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blade with the VOQ window error.

bugs.title: System controller may not update IP range for docker0 network after changing internal chassis network range
bugs.symptoms: When using a non-default internal chassis network range, a VELOS system controller may keep using 100.64.10.0/16 for the IP range for the docker0 network.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when performing an RMA replacement, or a clean install of a controller via PXE or USB drive.
bugs.impact: Some internal containers running on the system controller will continue to be addressed in 100.64.0.0/16 (RFC6598 address space) rather than the RFC1918 space configured.
bugs.workaround: 1. Log into the system controller as root 2. Edit /etc/sysconfig/docker and update the "--bip" parameter in the OPTIONS line. This can be done automatically by running the following commands from a root shell: source /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt prefix=${network_prefix:-"100.65"} chassis_id=${chassis_id:-1} first_octet=${network_prefix%%.*} second_octet=${network_prefix##*.} (( second_octet=second_octet - chassis_id )) sed -i.bak -E "s@--bip[ =][0-9]*＼.[0-9]*＼.@--bip=${first_octet}.${second_octet}.@g" /etc/sysconfig/docker Or all on one line: ( source /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt; prefix=${network_prefix:-"100.65"}; chassis_id=${chassis_id:-1}; first_octet=${network_prefix%%.*}; second_octet=${network_prefix##*.}; (( second_octet=second_octet - chassis_id )); sed -i.bak -E "s@--bip[ =][0-9]*＼.[0-9]*＼.@--bip=${first_octet}.${second_octet}.@g" /etc/sysconfig/docker ) 3. Reboot the system controller.

bugs.title: A TACACS+ server secret with a newline breaks PAM configs and blocks all user logins, including root.
bugs.symptoms: When a TACACS+ server secret contains a newline character, the PAM configuration files (/etc/pam.d/password-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-auth) become corrupted. This causes PAM to report "illegal module type" and "expecting return value" errors, preventing all user authentication, including root login via SSH and console.
bugs.conditions: A TACACS+ server is configured with a secret-key value that contains a literal newline character (U+000A). This can occur either by directly submitting a secret containing a newline via the REST API or when the system's primary key is corrupted, causing the decrypted secret value to contain unexpected characters.
bugs.impact: TACACS+ authentication to the system is broken.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5 v2.0 version.

bugs.title: F5OS SCP hardening
System health may show a transient alert during controller firmware updates that does not clear automatically
bugs.symptoms: During or shortly after a controller firmware update, system health can display an error indicating the controller’s hardware alert handler failed to initialize. The health view may suggest a fan or power controller monitoring failure even though all components later report Healthy/Ok. The error may persist in health/status after the firmware update completes, creating the impression of a controller health problem.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when controller firmware updates, controller failover, or a restart of the diagnostics service temporarily interrupts hardware health monitoring at startup.
bugs.impact: Misleading controller health alarms may remain visible after updates complete, causing confusion and unnecessary investigation. Firmware updates themselves complete successfully.
bugs.workaround: - After the firmware update, confirm that fans/power controllers report Healthy/Ok in system health. - If an initialization error persists, restart the diagnostics service or perform a controller failover to clear the stale alert.
bugs.fix: Diagnostics alert handlers now automatically retry during transient outages and recover initial alert states once hardware monitoring becomes available. As a result, the initialization error no longer appears, and system health clears correctly after firmware updates.

bugs.title: Privilege Escalation to Admin via SSH Port Forwarding
Tcpdump may crash with "malloc(): corrupted top size" when using complex BPF filters
bugs.symptoms: Running tcpdump with complex or long BPF filter expressions may result in a crash with the error message: malloc(): corrupted top size
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when tcpdump is invoked with a filter expression containing multiple conditions or a long filter string, especially when run via the system diagnostics
bugs.impact: Packet capture operations fails and no data is collected. This may impact troubleshooting or monitoring activities that rely on tcpdump.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump has been updated to reliably support complex and long filter expressions. The utility now validates filter input to prevent errors, ensuring stable and consistent packet capture operations

bugs.title: Platform registry failures on standby partition
bugs.symptoms: This issue can manifest in several ways, including: - Tenant deployments fail. - Partition upgrade fails. - Partition fails to join the cluster after a PXE boot. This issue is due to overridden port assignments for platform registry services on the partition's standby controller.
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system. -- An active controller's port assignment replaces one on the standby controller.
bugs.impact: This issue can manifest in several ways, including: - Tenant deployment fails. - Partition upgrade fails. - Partition fails to join the cluster after a PXE boot.

bugs.title: F5OS qkview fails to collect log files due to journal logs
bugs.symptoms: When generating a host qkview on F5OS, some of the journal log files are not handled properly, resulting in the output qkview missing expected log files, and the following example error log is observed in the platform.log file: panic: runtime error: index out of range [327713] with length 128
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when qkview is generated using the standard qkview-collect on F5OS with the software version 1.8.x and lower, and the system contains binary systemd journal files in /var/log/journal folder.
bugs.impact: -- Resulting qkview archive is incomplete and missing log files. -- Diagnostic and support efforts may be hindered due to missing data.
bugs.workaround: Edit the qkview-collect.config.yml to not collect /var/log/journal files before running qkview using the below steps and commands to collect the qkview -- Edit the file /etc/qkview-collect/qkview-collect.config.yml and add the line "- /var/log/journal" under the “excludes:" section, ensuring it follows the existing YAML syntax and indentation. -- Generate a qkview: f5sh 'system diagnostics qkview capture' -- Check the qkview status using the below command and wait for the qkview collection to complete: f5sh 'system diagnostics qkview status'

bugs.title: IPv6 NDP Neighbor Advertisements may get dropped at the VELOS platform layer when tenant transitions from Standby to Active during a failover
bugs.symptoms: -- Some IPv6 NDP Neighbor Advertisements (NA) from a tenant does not egress the VELOS platform when the tenant becomes active during failover. -- When a failover occurs, drop_pkt_cnt increases when observing the counters from the controller using the following command: for i in blade-{1,2}; do echo $i; echo '====='; ssh $i docker exec -i partition_fpga fpgatool -c ＼"nsms hdp_drop_pkt_cnt 1＼"; done
bugs.conditions: -- Tenant running on VELOS v1.8.1, v1.8.2. -- IPv6 floating self-IPs and many IPv6 floating virtual addresses are configured in VLANs on the tenant. -- Failover occurs.
bugs.impact: Upstream devices do not receive the IPv6 NDP NAs that should have indicated that the new tenant has taken over for the affected IPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: Tenant deletion may fail when a transient internal communication timeout occurs on the system controller
bugs.symptoms: After a tenant is deleted, the tenant instance may remain running on one or more blades.
bugs.conditions: The delete request was issued, but a transient internal timeout prevented the instance from being stopped and removed, and the request was not retried.
bugs.impact: After the tenant delete is issued, the user assumes the tenant was removed but it is still present.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the tenant running-state from deployed to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: BX520 blade eDAG masking issue causes redirections with ipv6-prefix-len not equal to 128.
bugs.symptoms: This issue can cause lower overall system performance because of bad disaggregation to service endpoint. Host software recognizes that packets are not at the correct endpoint and redirects the packets to the correct endpoint. The extra packet hop can cause lower overall system performance.
bugs.conditions: ipv6-prefix-len not equal to 128. ATSE v75.3.23.00 or earlier.
bugs.impact: Variable packet performance and latency impact.
bugs.workaround: Update to ATSE v75.3.25.00 or newer bitstream release for BX520 blade.
bugs.fix: Logic issue in disaggregation masking found and fixed in ATSE v75.3.25.00 bitstream release for BX520 blade.

bugs.title: F5 VELOS BX520 ATSE firmware v75.3.25.00
bugs.symptoms: F5 VELOS BX520 ATSE firmware v75.3.25.00
bugs.conditions: F5 VELOS BX520 Platform
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes disaggregation issue. See ID2034661 for more information.

bugs.title: Blade interface presence/stats are getting wiped because of bad power event during system controller failover
bugs.symptoms: After inserting a blade in the chassis, the blade interface state may be wiped out on the next system controller failover. Interfaces will be shown as "NOT_PRESENT" even though the blade is present and running. default-1# show interfaces interface state oper-status NAME OPER STATUS -------------------- 1/1.0 DOWN 1/2.0 DOWN 2/1.0 NOT_PRESENT 2/2.0 NOT_PRESENT 3/1.0 DOWN 3/2.0 DOWN
bugs.conditions: Physically inserting a blade in the chassis, followed by a controller failover after the blade finishes booting.
bugs.impact: After the controller failover, the incorrect 'power off' event causes the partition software to erase the blade dataplane state, resulting in the blade dataplane being inoperative.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the issue: After inserting a blade in the chassis, cause a controller failover and then reboot the blade. To recover if the problem is encountered: Reboot the blade.
bugs.fix: Inaccurate power events are not generated during system controller failover.

bugs.title: The confd-key-migrationd logs may display incorrect error messages during migration failures
bugs.symptoms: The confd-key-migrationd logs may display incorrect or misleading error messages during migration failures.
bugs.conditions: When confd-key-migrationd encounters errors during migration, the logged error messages may not accurately reflect the actual cause.
bugs.impact: The logs don't provide enough detail to identify the underlying problem.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that caused confd-key-migrationd to log incorrect error messages during migration failures.

bugs.title: VELOS controller cannot change primary key if there is an NTP key configured
bugs.symptoms: If an NTP key is configured, attempts to change the system's primary key will fail and log these errors: confd-key-migrationd[9]: nodename=controller-1 priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x1b01000000000010 msg="Failed to set element in cdb" path="/system/ntp/ntp-keys/ntp-key{1}/state/key-value" error="" errno="Interrupted system call". confd-key-migrationd[9]: nodename=controller-1 priority="Crit" version=1.0 msgid=0x1b01000000000002 msg="Key Migration failed, attempting to restore" stage="RESTORE_SECURE_ELEMENTS"
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system controller running F5OS-C. -- NTP encryption key configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to change primary key.
bugs.workaround: -- Remove the NTP key from the configuration. -- Perform the key migration. -- Re-add the NTP key to the configuration.

bugs.title: Changing LDAP configuration via the GUI results in an unexpected error
bugs.symptoms: Changing LDAP configuration on GUI errors out with the following error message - "object is not writable: /oc-sys:system/oc-sys:aaa/oc-sys:authentication/f5-aaa-ldap:ldap/f5-aaa-ldap:state"
bugs.conditions: When using a Windows Active Directory (AD) server and LDAP settings are configured with Active Directory authentication enabled (true) and Unix Attributes disabled (false).
bugs.impact: You are unable to make LDAP configuration changes via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Make the configuration change from CLI.
bugs.fix: GUI will not modify the read-only state part of the LDAP configuration and allow user to save the LDAP configuration changes.

bugs.title: Setting the primary key on VELOS will intermittently cause a failover and primary key inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: When performing a "system aaa primary-key set" operation, sometimes the controller will fail over prior to updating the database values, resulting in an inconsistent decryption key. The set key operation remains in 'IN_PROGRESS' and does not recover.
bugs.conditions: Retry timing problem in the key retrieval logic sometimes causes the database to hang for over 30 seconds during configuration reload, resulting in the hardware watchdog expiring and causing a failover.
bugs.impact: Configuration database will not be usable, partitions will not start correctly. System must be restored from backup.
bugs.workaround: Prior to attempting to change the primary-key, ensure that a controller, partition, and tenant backups with a known primary-key are available. If the problem occurs, perform a "system database reset-to-default", reset the primary key to the previous known value corresponding to the backup and restore the backups.
bugs.fix: Setting the primary key does not cause a failover.

bugs.title: The fpgamgr process crashes after reconnecting to the ConfD
bugs.symptoms: The fpgamgr process crashes.
bugs.conditions: fpgamgr reconnects to the ConfD.
bugs.impact: Potential temporary datapath outage.
bugs.workaround: Wait for the fpgamgr process to restart. If that doesn't resolve the datapath issue, reboot the blade.

bugs.title: PlatformStatsBridge process crash
bugs.symptoms: The PlatformStatsBridge process crashes on SIGSEGV, creates a core file. The associated Docker container goes into "Exited" state. SNMP failures and webUI errors occur, indicating the server or underlying service is unreachable.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs occasionally, when an snmp request tries fetching diskUsagePercentage on platform stats.
bugs.impact: The Docker container does not restart automatically as expected.
bugs.fix: The support for diskUsagePercentage MIB has been reverted.

bugs.title: FCS or FEC uncorrected errors seen continuously on the system
bugs.symptoms: FCS (Frame Check Sequence) and FEC (Forward Error Correction) error statistics for chassis/blade backplane ports were incorrectly reported as unhealthy because the system interpreted raw (non-zero) counter values as errors.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when switch reports FCS or FEC errors greater than 0
bugs.impact: System will display switch port status alarms and events.

bugs.title: Chassis control-plan LAG interface presence/status may be incorrect after failover
bugs.symptoms: Chassis system controller "show lacp interfaces interface" show interfaces present on the standby controller when the standby is not present and/or powered-off.
bugs.conditions: LAG interface state is not always properly propagated when a controller transitions to 'standby'. If that standby controller becomes 'active' prior to update, the data persists.
bugs.impact: LAG member mismatch may cause blade control-plane connectivity problems.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the active controller.
bugs.fix: Operational data is properly synchronized across active/standby transitions.

bugs.title: OPT-0056 100G link intermittently fails to come up after reboot or hot plug insertion due to incorrect Media Side FEC programming
bugs.symptoms: An OPT-0056 100G link intermittently fails to come up after a reboot or hot plug insertion.
bugs.conditions: Having an OPT-0056 100G link and after a system reboot or hot plug inserts the optic into the system.
bugs.impact: Intermittent link issues.

bugs.title: F5OS GUI/CLI "Available Storage" displayed when creating tenants not accurate due to thin provisioning
bugs.symptoms: The "Available Storage" field in the F5OS GUI/CLI shows “0 GB” available after several tenants are deployed, even though more tenants can still be created due to thin provisioning. This behavior leads to confusion as users may mistakenly believe that no additional tenants can be deployed.
bugs.conditions: * Deploy tenants on an F5OS appliance (e.g., r5k or r10900). * Observe the "Available Storage" field in the GUI/CLI after creating multiple tenants; it may display "0 GB" despite sufficient resources for additional tenants.
bugs.impact: Misrepresentation of available storage in the GUI/CLI causes users to incorrectly interpret system limits and subsequent loss of trust in the storage metric as a reliable reference.
bugs.workaround: No current workaround exists to adjust the displayed storage value.

bugs.title: Loss of System Controller <-> Blade control plane link can result in loss of communication with blade lop
bugs.symptoms: In the event the System Controller <-> Blade control plane link goes down on the active controller, the controller will no longer be able to communicate with the blade lop.
bugs.conditions: Active Controller <-> Blade control plane link goes down.
bugs.impact: Blade LOP is unable to communicate with the active controller.
bugs.workaround: Fail over the active System Controller.

bugs.title: Ansible Service Broker process may communicate with External Docker Hub
bugs.symptoms: It is possible that the Ansible Service Broker process which is part of the Openshift installation may communicate with an external Docker Hub.
bugs.conditions: The Ansible Service Broker (ASB) process is configured by default to communicate with a possible external Docker Hub.
bugs.impact: The user will not notice anything unsusal.
bugs.fix: Only localhost is now used.

bugs.title: Axios is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
bugs.symptoms: When a manipulated string is provided as input to the format method, the regular expression exhibits a time complexity of O(n^2). Server becomes unable to provide normal service due to the excessive cost and time wasted in processing vulnerable regular expressions.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: It will lead to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Axios has been upgraded to non-vulnerable version.

bugs.title: Axios is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
bugs.symptoms: When a manipulated string is provided as input to the format method, the regular expression exhibits a time complexity of O(n^2). Server becomes unable to provide normal service due to the excessive cost and time wasted in processing vulnerable regular expressions.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: It will lead to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Axios has been upgraded to non-vulnerable version.

bugs.title: Authentication of LDAP Remote user in AD server may fail
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Remote user authentication in F5OS may fail when the Unix attributes is set to false.
bugs.conditions: If LDAP authentication is configured with an Active Directory (AD) server, remote users will not be able to authenticate successfully on F5OS.
