bugs.impact: Remote user may not be able to login to F5OS.

bugs.title: Controllers lose connectivity to blades with stale LACP members in member table
bugs.symptoms: LACP member table has stale members and controllers lose connectivity to blades.
bugs.conditions: Issue can happen when the following are performed. - Manually failover the controllers. - Power down active controller. - Reboot active controller. - Physically remove active controller from the chassis.
bugs.impact: Controllers lose connectivity to blades and stale LACP members cannot be cleaned up.
bugs.workaround: Restart cc-lacpd container on the active controller, or reboot active controller.
bugs.fix: Debug log is added to help debugging the issue. Enable cc-lacpd debug log and look for msgid=0x3301000000000050 from velos.log. This debug log prints the cache of current confD member table data.

bugs.title: Blade cpu-usage and memory-usage stats not populated after a cluster rebuild
bugs.symptoms: After rebuilding the OpenShift cluster (as documented in K000139870), the cpu-usage and memory-usage stats will be empty.
bugs.conditions: -- A chassis system with OpenShift. -- OpenShift was rebuilt (K000139870).
bugs.impact: Unable to get values for the cpu-usage and memory-usage blade statistics.
bugs.workaround: After rebuilding the OpenShift cluster completes, run the following command: docker exec orchestration_manager /usr/omd/scripts/metrics-server-install.sh

bugs.title: Dagd may crash if a malicious message is sent from the tenant
ServiceCatalogInstall status may show as failed in "show cluster"
bugs.symptoms: Due a race condition on update the apiserver certificate during upgrade, the ServiceCatalogInstall status in the "show cluster" output may show as failed.
bugs.conditions: This can happen on upgrade from a pre 1.8.1-EHF-6 release to 1.8.1-EHF-6.
bugs.impact: The ServiceCatalogInstall status in the "show cluster" output will show as failed, and several pods may show in error state.
bugs.workaround: As the root user from the active controller: docker exec orchestration_manager sed -i.bak s/force=0/force=1/ /usr/omd/scripts/check_apiserver_certs.sh; sleep 300; docker exec orchestration_manager sed -i.bak s/force=1/force=0/ /usr/omd/scripts/check_apiserver_certs.sh This will cause orchestration-manager to re-run the certificate updates, which will re-run the ServiceCatalogInstall playbook and fix the status in show cluster
bugs.fix: Orchestration-manager has been updated to wait until rolling upgrade is done before updating the apiserver certificate.

bugs.title: Partitions created on VELOS v1.1.x will have configuration wiped during controller upgrade to VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2
bugs.symptoms: A partition's configuration can get wiped out and reset to default when the controller is upgraded to VELOS 1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2.
bugs.conditions: If a partition was created while the system controller was running VELOS v1.1.x, the partition configuration volume may have been created with as an LVM "thin pool" rather than a logical volume. The problem does not occur with partitions created on VELOS 1.2.0 or later. In VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, and v1.8.2, the partition startup logic incorrectly fails to recognize that these filesystem volumes are already initialized, and reinitializes them resulting in data loss. The reinitialization error is persistent, and will be repeated any time the partition instance is restarted, until the volumes are recreated without "thin provisioning".
bugs.impact: -- The partition configuration data is wiped and reset back to default.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading to the system controllers to VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2, check if the partition logical volumes on either system controller are incorrectly provisioned. To do this, run the "lvs" command from a bash shell on both controllers. "Thin provisioned" volumes will have numeric entries in the "Data%" and "Meta%" columns, and will have the "t" flag in the "Attr" column In this example, partitions 1 is effected: [root@controller-1:Active log]# lvs LV VG Attr LSize Pool Origin Data% Meta% Move Log Cpy%Sync Convert partition1 partition_config twi-a-tz-- 10.00g 0.00 10.61 partition3 partition_config -wi-ao-z-- 10.00g export_chassis partition_image -wi-ao---- 256.12g partition1 partition_image twi-a-tz-- 15.00g 0.00 10.57 partition1_shared partition_image -wi-a----- 10.00g partition3 partition_image -wi-ao-z-- 15.00g partition3_shared partition_image -wi-ao---- 10.00g ... If this condition exists, do not upgrade to these versions and contact support for assistance for non-destructively converting these volumes.
bugs.fix: In VELOS v1.8.3, the partition startup logic correctly recognizes that these partition logical volumes are already initialized, and does not wipe and recreate them.

bugs.title: LLDP neighbor details may not update with a low switch update timer.
bugs.symptoms: When neighbouring switches are configured with a low LLDP update timer (around 1 to 10 seconds) and LLDP is enabled on multiple interfaces (more than five), the LLDP details in F5OS ConfD may eventually either get wiped out or fail to update.
bugs.conditions: A low LLDP update timer (1 to 10 seconds) combined with LLDP being enabled on multiple interfaces.
bugs.impact: LLDP info will be lost and/or failed to update.
bugs.workaround: Update the LLDP update timer on the neighboring switch to more than 30 seconds and wait for some time to allow the system to stabilize and return to normal. For an immediate resolution, delete the LLDP pod in the cluster using the following steps: [root@controller-1:Active ~]# kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep lldp partition-1 lldpd-7d7f465488-s7pw5 1/1 Running 0 17h [root@controller-1:Active ~]# kubectl delete pod lldpd-7d7f465488-s7pw5 -n partition-1 pod "lldpd-7d7f465488-s7pw5" deleted

bugs.title: A partition's "show system events" no longer updates after multiple partition failovers
bugs.symptoms: After a partition is failed over more than once it will no longer list new events when running "show system events".
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis system with at least one partition. -- The partition must have failed over at least twice.
bugs.impact: New events are no longer seen when running "show system events".

bugs.title: LLDP errors are logged when no IPv4 management address is configured
bugs.symptoms: If a partition (F5OS-C) does not have an IPv4 management address configured, errors like the following will be logged in the partition's velos.log file: lldpd[9]: nodename=blade-1(p1) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6001000000000015 msg="Unable to start confD session." ERROR="item does not exist" LASTERR="/oc-sys:system/state/f5-partition:mgmt-ipv4 does not exist" ERRNO=1. fpgamgr[11]: nodename=blade-5(p2) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x302000000000005 msg="cdb_get failed for" COMPONENT="/voq-states/voq-state{1 5}" ERROR="item does not exist" LASTERR="/f5-voq:voq-states/voq-state{1 5}/voqs_enabled does not exist" ERRNO=1.
bugs.conditions: A partition's IPv4 management address is not configured. Systems with only an ip6 address will also exhibit the same messages.
bugs.impact: These logs are benign and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: To prevent these logs, configure an IPv4 management IP address.

bugs.title: F5OS not able to handle changes to LDAP tls_reqcert configuration
bugs.symptoms: Changes to an LDAP server's tls_reqcert configuration are not handled by F5OS, resulting in authentication-manager and user-manager communication failures with the LDAP server
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication configured to authenticate against an Active Directory Server - Under the system Authentication Settings configuration in the Common LDAP Configuration section, "Authenticate with Active Directory" set to True and "Unix Attributes" set to False - LDAP group filters specified for one or more roles - The LDAP server's tls_reqcert configuration is modified while F5OS is actively running.
bugs.impact: Changes to the LDAP server's tls_reqcert setting will cause communication failures with the LDAP server.
bugs.workaround: Restart authentication manager and user manager after making configuration changes to the tls_reqcert configuration option.

bugs.title: Possible that a node may not be added to cluster after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: During a partition upgrade to version 1.6.4, a node may be removed from the cluster and fail to rejoin automatically.
bugs.conditions: During a partition upgrade, one of the nodes may be removed from the OpenShift cluster by OMD and fail to rejoin the cluster afterward.
bugs.impact: The node is not in the cluster.
bugs.workaround: The node can be rebooted to add it back to cluster.

bugs.title: Openshift Metrics Server pod can get stuck in the ContainerCreating state
bugs.symptoms: The Openshift Metrics Server pod may launch but get stuck in the ContainerCreating state.
bugs.conditions: Not clear what causes this issue.
bugs.impact: No noticable issues unless the 'oc get pods' command is run at the shell level.
bugs.workaround: Follow these steps: 1. Delete the metrics server pod and it will restart. 2. Retrieve the name of the metrics server pod by running the following command: 'oc get pods --all-namespaces | grep metrics'. 3. Delete the pod using the following command: 'oc delete pod <pod-name> -n kube-system'

bugs.title: Observing FCS Errors on system controller Peer HG Links
bugs.symptoms: The symptom of this issue is FCS error counters incrementing on control plane system controller peer HG links.
bugs.conditions: Run a system with 1.8.1+ that has the 6.5.26 version of the broadcom SDK.
bugs.impact: Error counters increment, no system impact is observed aside from the counters incrementing.
bugs.fix: Had to modify SDK at init time to properly set advertisements to disable FEC on the peer links when running 6.5.26 SDK.

bugs.title: LLDP may core when ConfD restarts or reconnects
bugs.symptoms: LLDP may core when ConfD restarts or reconnects. Log messages similar to the following may be soon in velos.log (F5OS-C) or platform.log (F5OS-A) around the time of the core: 2025-06-04T01:09:47.357839+03:00 blade-1(p1) lldpd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6001000000000015 msg="Unable to start confD session." ERROR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="EOF on socket to ConfD" ERRNO=45. 2025-06-04T01:09:47.357842+03:00 blade-1(p1) lldpd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6001000000000015 msg="Unable to start confD session." ERROR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="EOF on socket to ConfD" ERRNO=45.
bugs.conditions: -- LLDP in use. -- ConfD restarts or reconnects.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Thread processing has been improved to enable smoother restarts and reconnections.

bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed chassis is rebooted after an upgrade to 1.8.2.
bugs.impact: The impact will be related to inter-blade traffic. If imm_enabled is 0 for an affected destination blade, ingress traffic entering the chassis on one blade destined to the tenant deployed on the affected blade will not reach the tenant.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade, on partition issue: cluster nodes node blade-X reboot X being the number of the affected blade.

bugs.title: Multicast traffic can be dropped by Host DLF rate-limiter
bugs.symptoms: Multicast traffic from a tenant can be dropped by the host DLF rate-limiter, causing traffic loss.
bugs.conditions: Egress multicast traffic exceeding 2500 packets per second.
bugs.impact: Loss of multicast traffic.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the multicast MAC address.
bugs.fix: We changed the behavior of the FPGA code to remove multicast packets that miss the L2 table from being classified as DLF.

bugs.title: Logs in /var/confd/log are not rotated on system controllers
bugs.symptoms: Log files in /var/confd/log are not rotated on system controllers. Upgrades may fail due to a timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- A chassis-based system.
bugs.impact: If the files get too large, there can be disk space issues. It can also cause upgrades to fail due to a timeout.
bugs.workaround: If these files get too large, they can be pared down using the Linux "truncate" command. Note that this will remove log messages from these files.

bugs.title: Prompt-statusd process occasionally cores
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the prompt-statusd daemon will core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in prompt-statusd during normal operation.
bugs.impact: After core, service will restart the operation

bugs.title: TACACS External Authentication Failure after a software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: TACACS users are not able to login to the device.
bugs.conditions: TACACS+ server sends back an authorization reply with an auth status of 'PASS_REPL' (pass + *replace all attributes*) instead of 'PASS_ADD' (pass + *add* to attributes)
bugs.impact: TACACS users will be unable to log in when the server is configured under the specified conditions.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using PASS_REPL on Tacacs server.
bugs.fix: After upgrading device to latest EHF build, the issue is not reproduced.

bugs.title: BX110 ports configured for 40G can fail to link with OPT-036 optics
bugs.symptoms: BX110 front panel interface configured for 40G with OPT-0036 optic fails to achieve link.
bugs.conditions: BX110 front panel interface configured for 40G and using an OPT-0036 optic.
bugs.impact: Front panel interface remains DOWN, preventing traffic from flowing.
bugs.fix: Implement a software workaround that first writes a reset bit to '0' before writing it to a '1'.

bugs.title: The "system aaa tls config passphrase" command does not validate whether or not the new passphrase correctly decrypts the current key file
bugs.symptoms: If the GUI is configured to use a custom key and certificate ("system aaa tls config certificate" and "system aaa tls config key") and use an encrypted key file protected by a passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase"), the system fails to perform validation for subsequent changes to the passphrase (and the system is not decrypting and re-encrypting the key file).
bugs.conditions: -- System is configured to use a custom key and certificate for GUI access. -- They key is encrypted with a passphrase, and "system aaa tls config passphrase" is used to set this passphrase in F5OS. -- "system aaa tls config passphrase" is later used to change the passphrase, but the underlying key is not changed.
bugs.impact: -- Key migration fails -- HTTP GUI and API are rendered unusable
bugs.workaround: Using the CLI: -- Manually re-encrypt the key to use the new passphrase. OR -- Change the passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase") back to the one that matches they key.

bugs.title: The port of Allowed IP Addresses is shown as "Select" on GUI instead of port number.
bugs.symptoms: While editing Allow List Entry under System Settings -> System Security -> Allowed IP Addresses in the "Port" field you see "Select" instead of port number e.g. "22".
bugs.conditions: You configured Allowed IP Address Entry for port other than SNMP (161).
bugs.impact: The word "select" is incorrectly displayed, but it otherwise has no effect.

bugs.title: VELOS controller unhealthy if it is rebooted after clean install while platform-services-deployment still starting
bugs.symptoms: A newly-installed controller running the correct software version is inaccessible from the network or peer controller, even though it is booted into F5OS. Log messages in /var/log/messages or "journalctl -u platform-services-deployment" indicating that it failed to pull docker images, and the initial registries were set as a mirror of themselves: platform-deployment: Initial registry (port 2000) setup as mirror of port 2000 registry complete platform-deployment: Initial registry (port 2500) setup as mirror of port 2500 registry complete [...] platform-deployment: Pulling repository localhost:2500/vcc-partition-software-manager platform-deployment: Error: image vcc-partition-software-manager:7.2.7-f5os-c-1-8-1-candidate.2025-02-11-05-55-35.S383ff41b not found platform-deployment: Unexpected error encountered while starting platform services via docker-compose. platform-deployment: Nov 12 11:57:57 controller-2.chassis.local platform-deployment[3342]: Error: image vcc-partition-software-manager:7.2.7-f5os-c-1-8-1-candidate.2025-02-11-05-55-35.S383ff41b not found platform-deployment: Platform services done
bugs.conditions: A fresh install of software on a VELOS system controller (an RMA replacement system controller, or a clean install via PXE or USB). During the initial boot into F5OS, the new system controller is rebooted while platform-services-deployment is still running in the background.
bugs.impact: The VELOS system controller remains inoperative.
bugs.workaround: Perform a clean install of the VELOS system controller software again, and do not reboot the controller while platform-services-deployment is still running.

bugs.title: Disabled ports or port mode mismatches can cause bad register reads.
bugs.symptoms: When a Front panel port is disabled or the port mode is mismatched, it can cause incorrect register reads. This may manifest as port interface flapping on other unrelated ports.
bugs.conditions: Front Panel Port is disabled or a port mode mismatch, such as a 100GE optic installed when the port is configured for 40GE operating mode.
bugs.impact: The status on other interfaces may incorrectly show ‘down’ when the interface is ‘up’ or other unexpected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Enable all Front Panel ports, even those not in use, and ensure there are no port mode mismatches.
bugs.fix: Updated FPGA firmware is required for the fix.

bugs.title: Application level DOS via improper configuration of the look aside memory allocator.
Tenant Disk can be removed as a result of misinterpreting system state.
bugs.symptoms: A tenant disk will be removed from compute nodes when the tenant appears to be running from partition ConfD CLI. As a result, the VM pods cannot be started because the disk is gone. The orchestration software will notice this and recreate the tenant with a new disk, but all configuration and other data associated with the original tenant will be lost.
bugs.conditions: - Power Cycle is performed on the a controller, forcing the partition go to the one staying up if it was not already there - Cause a fault in the system that is up (like unplug mgmt interface cable). This is to cause the controller that was power cycled to take over as soon as it is able to. - When the node that was down takes over (because the one that became active is at fault after unplugging cable) the tenants in the partition could end up getting wiped. This is intermittent since it is cause by a race condition at failover time. When the failover occurs, the other partition instance is running on controller node that will take a number of seconds to become active on the controller side and take over the kubernetes layer.
bugs.impact: The orchestration software that takes over because the other node is at fault could end up running the reconciliation logic to add and remove tenants with no data because the DB read is not done and/or the kubernetes layer is not ready for queries. If the reconciliation tenant list is empty, orchestration software end up misinterpreting it as if there were no tenants, causing tenants to be removed. But the DB does have the tenants. Subsequent iterations will detect there is a tenant that needs to be created, but at this point the disk is gone and a new disk gets created.
bugs.workaround: Because this is a race condition that occurs when a double fault happens (powercycle on one controller node and not having the mgmt interface up on the other controller node), the only way to try avoid it is to be ahead of the faults reported by the system.
bugs.fix: Orchestration software that was meant to reconcile what was missed should not take any action if the information is not available.

bugs.title: Rsync.log files on blades are not rotated
bugs.symptoms: The rsync.log files on VELOS blades are not rotated.
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system. -- Large (several GB) rsync.log file on at least one blade.
bugs.impact: This can cause disk space issues on blades, which can cause various issues, including the failure to run tenants.
bugs.workaround: Manually truncate the rsync.log file. 1. From the active controller, ssh to the blade with the large log file, e.g.: ssh blade-1 2. Truncate the rsync.log file: truncate -s0 /var/F5/partitionN/log/rsync.log ... where N is the ID of the partition with the large rsync.log file. NOTE: This will remove all the contents of the rsync.log file. If you wish to keep this data, back it up before performing this operation.

bugs.title: After a controller upgrade, out-of-sync etcd processes can lead to unhealthy cluster
bugs.symptoms: After a controller upgrade, it is possible that the controller etcd processes can be out of sync causing the cluster to go into an unhealthy state.
bugs.conditions: The etcd processes require a quorum of three and the third etcd process is not being launched which leaves the etcds on both controllers in an inconsistent state.
bugs.impact: The cluster will remain in an unhealthy state.
bugs.workaround: On the active controller, manually launch the third etcd instance, by running this command at the root shell /etc/etcd/launch_etcd.sh Then issue a controller failover.

bugs.title: Tenant outage caused by deletion of VLAN in the tenant and unassignment of the VLAN from F5OS
bugs.symptoms: When a VLAN inside the tenant is deleted and the VLAN is un-assigned from F5OS, a service for the tenant could be deleted. Deletion of service will cause an outage on the tenant. Here are the two log messages on F5OS datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000045 msg="Confd Event Update:" EVENT="DELETE_SERVICE_ID" FROM="CONFD" TENANTNAME="" ATSE=0 SUBMODULE=0. datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000034 msg="Service Instance Update Success." TENANTNAME="tenant-1" DOSGRP="[2]" SVCGRP="[7]" SVCID=22.
bugs.conditions: -- Deletion of the VLAN inside the tenant. -- Un-assignment of the same VLAN from the F5OS.
bugs.impact: Because the service is removed, all VLANs on that service will be inaccessible for the tenant and cause an outage in the tenant.
bugs.workaround: If a VLAN is going to be deleted from the tenant, first un-assign the VLAN inside the tenant from F5OS. Then after a 2 second delay, delete the VLAN inside the tenant.

bugs.title: DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant
bugs.symptoms: An error is found in platform.log platform-stats-bridge[10]: nodename=controller-1(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x4305000000000008 msg="" msg="DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant".
bugs.conditions: -- Tenant is in configured or not deployed completely -- tcp-cop stats are queried when there are not yet any stats. (show tenants tenant tcp-cop tcp-cop)
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The log message is logged at the error level and should be logged at the warning level.
bugs.fix: The Err log is changed to Warning log in the latest versions (from 2.0+ and C-1.8.3)

bugs.title: The Virtual Server is not receiving traffic due to an incorrect VLAN update from F5OS platform
bugs.symptoms: When a specific native VLAN is configured for a port in virtual-wire, the incoming packets still arrive with VLAN ID 4094, while the Virtual Server expects traffic with the configured VLAN ID.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a specific native vlan on a port and then configuring it in virtual-wire.
bugs.impact: When enabling/disabling virtual-wire mode on a port with a configured native VLAN, the port default VLAN was being set with values (4094 for vwire enable, 4095 for vwire disable), ignoring any existing native VLAN configuration.
bugs.workaround: Once the virtual-wire is configured on the port, if the remove and re-add the native vlans to the interfaces, the hardware should get programmed correctly.
bugs.fix: Added a fix such that ensure native VLAN configuration is respected and preserved throughout the virtual-wire lifecycle.

bugs.title: Switchd may process blade slot operational data updates that are not intended to trigger any action
bugs.symptoms: On software upgrade v1.7.x to v1.8.x and later releases following with a firmware upgrade, it is observed that the power field in the slot operdata may fluctuate. This behavior can cause switchd to incorrectly detect that the slot's dataplane ports require reconfiguration, resulting in a link flap on the affected blade dataplane port(s) This will show up in the blade fpga manager as VOQ watchdog timeouts.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.7.x to v1.8.x and later that also involve a firmware update.
bugs.impact: Degraded dataplane performance and TMM HA failovers.
bugs.workaround: Reboot system controllers and / or impacted blades.
bugs.fix: Switchd configures the dataplane ports of a slot only in response to changes in slot presence or blade type

bugs.title: Tenant disk can get removed when there is a double fault scenario
bugs.symptoms: Tenant disk will be recreated from scratch, prompting for changing the password from the default one.
bugs.conditions: When a controller is booting and is required to become the active role (including all partition active instances) due to the other controller being unavailable, a race condition may occur. This can result in the orchestration daemon removing tenant disks, as it has not have acquired the latest system state.
bugs.impact: Tenant disk is lost. No way to recover it.
bugs.workaround: Whenever possible, perform a power cycle on the controllers following a partition failover to the active controllers. Additionally, verify that there are no faults in the controller hosting the active partitions. This approach helps mitigate race conditions that may occur when the standby controller, during startup, is required to take over due to an unhealthy active controller.
bugs.fix: Removed the race condition that could cause prematurely removing tenant disks.

bugs.title: Vqf bitstream failed to load on blade
bugs.symptoms: When there is a power outage/down without power backup then sometime a blade's usb drive will be disconnected. That will cause the vqf bitstream to fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Install the 1.8.2-C build on the system and perform power cycle. (This is highly intermittent issue)
bugs.impact: Blade will be in an inoperative state.
bugs.workaround: Power cycle will bring the system back
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: The runc library version in F5OS-C v1.8.2 causes issues with OpenShift after an upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The runc library in F5OS-C v1.8.2 was upgraded to version that causes issue with OpenShift. This manifested as occasional issue with adding new blades to the cluster, and problems around other OpenShift operations.
bugs.conditions: These issues could occur when upgrading to F5OS-C v1.8.2
bugs.impact: It can impact operation of the Openshift cluster, which can impact tenants, and the ability to add new blades and tenants to the system.
bugs.workaround: There is no viable workaround.
bugs.fix: The runc library has changed to version that is compatible with the OpenShift version being run in the chassis.

bugs.title: LLDP core found while upgrading chassis
bugs.symptoms: LLDPD process terminated unexpectedly(core file) during database connection establishment due to an unhandled exception.
bugs.conditions: -- ConfD Connection Timeout. -- ConfD not running when LLDPD started.
bugs.impact: LLDP crashes and restarts. No functionality impact.

bugs.title: Observed ctrlplane0x interface missing & ixgbe load errors after Active System Controller power cycle test
bugs.symptoms: After performing a power cycle of active system controller, an error of loading ixgbe diver is observed which results in ctrlplane0x port missing in team0. Errors: [ 5.611594] ixgbe: probe of 0000:06:00.0 failed with error -5
bugs.conditions: Install v1.8.X-C/v1.7.C-X build on the system and perform active system controller power cycle. (This is intermittent issue) On the failure case, dmesg logs will point: [ 5.611594] ixgbe: probe of 0000:06:00.0 failed with error -5
bugs.impact: A malformed trunk between the control plane switch and controller host can lead to unpredictably unreliable traffic flows between the controller host and control plane switch.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the controller.
bugs.fix: The failed PCI device has been reinitialised.

bugs.title: Traffic outage after simultaneously rebooting both controllers before FPGA_RDY is asserted
bugs.symptoms: Traffic outage occurs when both controllers are rebooted simultaneously before the FPGA_RDY signal is asserted, leading to a disruption in data flow.
bugs.conditions: Simultaneous reboot of both controllers after a partition upgrade before FPGA_RDY is asserted.
bugs.impact: Traffic outage occurs.
bugs.workaround: Wait until FPGA_RDY is asserted after a partition upgrade before rebooting controllers. If possible reboot controllers one at a time.

bugs.title: Controller stuck with continuous Software Management service restart post power down event
bugs.symptoms: After a power down event, in a rare occurrence, the Software Management service can keep on restarting leaving the controller in bad state with ConfD down and Openshift install stuck.
bugs.conditions: It can occur on a fully loaded chassis if any of the ISO's *_state or *_mount file contents are missing after power down event.
bugs.impact: Platform services will be down, resulting in the controller being in a bad state. ConfD will not be accessible.
bugs.workaround: Check for the empty *_state or *_mount files under /var/import. Delete the empty files and restart Software Management service.
bugs.fix: Controllers will no longer be stuck with Software Management service restart after power down event.

bugs.title: Improper VM Tenant Thread CPU pinning may cause overlap with dma-agent threads
bugs.symptoms: Symptoms would be loss of performance.
bugs.conditions: During tenant deployment, two mechanisms attempt to pin the tenant's KVM CPUs. 1.Custom code added to the KubeVirt virt-launcher pod. 2. The libvirt daemon responsible for launching the QEMU process. While our code performs CPU pinning, the libvirt daemon occasionally unpins the CPUs. In some cases, the Libvirt unpinning takes precedence, resulting in tenant threads being left unpinned. This is more likely to happen on large systems with large tenants, or many tenants.
bugs.impact: This can lower system performance, if the kvm threads try to run on the same processor as other datapath-critical threads (like dm-worker threads from the dma-agent).
bugs.workaround: There is no reliable workaround, but one could try toggling the tenant from deployed -> configured -> deployed and give another chance to the two entities that are pinning/un-pinning the kvm threads.

bugs.title: FDB entries may expire when multiple entries hash to the same FPGA table index and traffic is intermittent
bugs.symptoms: L2/FDB entries may expire even when traffic is arriving at the FPGA of the Appliance or VELOS Blade.
bugs.conditions: L2 entries which internally hash to the same table index inside the FPGA can lead to the expiration of the entry when traffic is arriving on intervals of more than 30 seconds from that MAC address. On each interval, an age refresh message might be lost, leading to decrement the age of the entry on 30 seconds. When the entry reaches the last period it will expire, and then it will be re-learnt again.
bugs.impact: The expiration of the FDB entry can lead to Destination Lookup Failures that are rate-limited, i.e. traffic loss. Depending on the scenario this could lead to intermittent potential outages between the entry expires, and it is learnt again.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the MAC address that suffers expiration issues. See K000152328. Ensure that traffic from the MAC address expiring arrives continuously under 30 seconds intervals. Open a Support case and request an EHF.

bugs.title: Swapping controllers between slots in the same chassis will not operate correctly
bugs.symptoms: Removing both controllers from the chassis and swapping their slots is not supported, as this will prevent the cluster from functioning properly and result in an unhealthy state.
bugs.conditions: There is very specific openshift information stored within each controller based on the slot. Physically swapping these slots will result in the cluster entering an unhealthy state.
bugs.impact: Cluster will remain in an unhealthy state.
bugs.workaround: Issue a manual cluster reinstall.

bugs.title: Controller upgrade struck in in-progress after upgrading the chassis from 1.7.1 EHF1 to 1.8.2 EHF3
bugs.symptoms: When performing a rolling System controller upgrade from 1.7.1 to 1.8.x it is possible on of the upgrading System Controllers does not complete its upgrade and show system image displays "in-progress" for that system controllers upgrade status indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Problem is known to occur on a fully loaded CX1610 chassis.
bugs.impact: Dataplane should continue to function at a reduced rate. However, the System Controllers will not form a ConfD HA pair until both System Controllers are running the same System Controller version and management communication may be lost with the upgrading controller.
bugs.workaround: Perform a manual switch of both service and os versions to match the peer System Controller. Example: echo "switch cc_os <iso-version> " | nc -U /var/sw-mgmt.unix echo "switch cc_serv <iso-version> no_restart" | nc -U /var/sw-mgmt.unix where <iso-version> is the version the peer System Controller is currently running. Then reboot the system reboot the system controller
bugs.fix: Ugrades from 1.7.1 to releases 1.8.x and later are no longer subject to becoming stuck in the "in-progress" state.

bugs.title: Chassis partition go-standby command does not work correctly after Active/Active resolution
bugs.symptoms: If an internal chassis network partition causes the chassis partition HA pair to go active/active, the HA pair will resolve to the current preferred controller when the network partition is fixed. But future attempts to manually fail over to the other controller using the 'go-standby' command will immediately fail back to the original controller.
bugs.conditions: If an internal controller network partition causes partition HA pair to go active/active the internal failover state is left inconsistent.
bugs.impact: The go-standby command will not work.
bugs.workaround: Proper operation can be restored by restarting the partition HA on the non-preferred controller (controller-2 if in 'auto' mode): syscon-1-active(config)# system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node controller-2 service partition1_ha Restarting container affects configuration and data path. Do you want to proceed? [yes/no] yes result partition1_ha restarted successfully syscon-1-active(config)#
bugs.fix: The go-standby command works correctly after active/active resolution.

bugs.title: After Power Cycle testing on 1.8.2 EHF-3, observed partition mgmt interface stuck DOWN
bugs.symptoms: Access to partition management can be permanently lost if the System Controller is power cycled.
bugs.conditions: Power cycle the system controller on which the active instance of a partition is running.
bugs.impact: Management access to partition CLI / webUI lost.
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the partition management interface from the System Controller ConfD partition configuration. config# no partitions partition <name> config mgmt-ip config# commit config# partitions partition <name> config mgmt-ip <ipv4 | ipv6> address <ip address> prefix-length <length> gateway <gateway address>
bugs.fix: Reconnection to partition CLI/webUI through the management IP can be reliably reestablished after power cycling the system controller hosting the active partition instance.

bugs.title: Interblade traffic outage after simultaneous reboot of both controllers
bugs.symptoms: Interblade traffic outage occurs following the simultaneous reboot of both controllers, resulting in disrupted communication between blades.
bugs.conditions: Simultaneous reboot of both controllers.
bugs.impact: Interblade traffic outage occurs.
bugs.workaround: Reboot controllers one at a time.

bugs.title: iHealth upload is failing with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use the QKView upload feature, the upload may fail with the message "certificate signed by unknown authority". This is due to a recent Entrust certificate authority shutdown resulted inconsistency between F5OS and iHealth.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to upload a qkview file to iHealth after 30 June 2025.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload QKView files to iHealth with a single click.
bugs.workaround: You can use the File Export feature to download QKView files, and then log into iHealth and upload the files via the iHealth page. You can find the QKView files in the GUI at System Settings > File Utilities, then choose "diags/shared" as the base directory, then select "qkview".
bugs.fix: Certificate authorities used by the iHealth upload feature in F5OS is updated as fix. Qkview upload to ihealth should work in 1.8.3 and 1.8.2-EHF (1.8.2-29612) version

bugs.title: FPGA firmware health status reported as unhealthy/error
bugs.symptoms: Shortly after a VELOS BX520 blade boots up, the health status of the blade shows an error for one of the FPGAs, it never clears, and the blade still successfully runs traffic. There are also verification errors in velos.log. For example, in confd: "blade/firmware/fpga/atse1 firmware:update-status unhealthy error error" In velos.log, entries such as: "FWU response error." ... "PCI slot ca:00.0 width is 4; expected 8." FWU atse2 Verification failed, retrying (also appears in the blade PEL) FWU atse2 Verification failed (also appears in the blade PEL)
bugs.conditions: Booting up a VELOS BX520 blade.
bugs.impact: One or more of the FPGA-to-CPU (PCIe) links may be running in a degraded state and could affect the bandwidth of traffic between the blade's FPGA and CPU.
bugs.workaround: The blade can be rebooted to retry the FPGA load process, which will retrain all the FPGA PCIe links.
bugs.fix: Retries were increased for the FPGA load process to make it more reliable.

bugs.title: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available
bugs.symptoms: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available. You may see below error from logs "Disk usage exceeded threshold."
bugs.conditions: When there is sufficient space available, tenant image upload fails.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload tenant image
bugs.fix: Fixed in 2.0

bugs.title: Stale cache info can cause inaccurate tenant orchestration operations
bugs.symptoms: - A tenant is showing as deployed, has no running pods. - A tenant that is supposed to be running is not running while a deleted tenant is trying to come up (in terms of pods in the system).
bugs.conditions: Sequence of failover operations on the partition when tenant configuration changes were being processed
bugs.impact: Tenants may not reflect the latest committed configuration state.
bugs.workaround: Failover the partition or recreate the tenant.
bugs.fix: Updated standby cache regularly and cleared the stale info before orchestration daemon becomes the active one.

bugs.title: Controller platform-services can crash/restart at startup
bugs.symptoms: Conflicting volume mount points in the system controller platform-services can cause a crash/restart at startup.
bugs.conditions: A race condition exists between the vcc-confd container and the velocity-rsyslogd container that can cause velocity-rsyslogd to crash early in the platform-services startup.
bugs.impact: All platform-services containers restart, which can leave some services in an inconsistent state, including an unreachable partition management-IP.
bugs.fix: The volume mount point no longer conflict, so no startup race occurs.

bugs.title: Invalid or unresponsive rsyslog remote servers for log forwarding can exhaust system memory.
bugs.symptoms: System memory usage will increase over time without boundaries.
bugs.conditions: Remote-syslog servers configured with TCP protocol that cannot establish a connection (or has a unreliable connectivity).
bugs.impact: The rsyslog daemon will retry, and memory will continue to increase. This could potentially exhaust system memory.
bugs.workaround: Fix the connection, remove the invalid or flaky servers from config, OR use the UDP protocol.
bugs.fix: The new syntax used for rsyslogd remote-servers forwarding configuration requires specifying for each forwarding action a linked list queue type. This will implicitly use the default queue size of 1000 messages (or lower for earlier versions of rsyslogd).

bugs.title: F5OS web UI fails to load upon refreshing the page
bugs.symptoms: After performing a live upgrade of F5OS, refreshing the browser while on the appliance/partition/controller web UI returns a "404 Not Found — The requested URL was not found on this server" error. The web UI does not recover until the browser navigates back to the root URL manually.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS-based platforms (chassis and appliances) when a user refreshes the browser page.
bugs.impact: Access to the webUI may be lost when the browser is refreshed.
bugs.fix: Added a client-side fallback in the F5OS http-server to redirect stale deep-link requests back to the application root on page reload.

bugs.title: F5OS Backplane connectivity issues: 'TMM Not Ready', VoQ EMMs disabled for Blades due to VQF-CC link failures
bugs.symptoms: Dataplane switch interfaces corresponding to the even slot of a BX520 blade may be incorrectly disabled, causing a link outage to the Dataplane port of the even slot BX520 blade.
bugs.conditions: The Platform HAL sends a chassis platform response to the Chassis Manager indicating lop_ok is 0 for the even slot of a BX520 blade. Consequently, the Chassis Manager registers the blade as 'not present' (present = 0), prompting switchd to disable the port associated with the even-numbered slot.
bugs.impact: VQF IMM watchdog timeouts appear in the FPGA manager log.
bugs.workaround: Reboot both CCs. Can be performed in service if standby is rebooted first, followed by lsystem redundancy go-standby and then rebooting the new standby.
bugs.fix: The Chassis Manager will not publish a loss of presence specifically for the even slot of BX520 blades, ensuring that the corresponding dataplane port is not inadvertently disabled by switchd.

bugs.title: The platform-stats-bridge-cc restarted unexpectedly on VELOS controllers
bugs.symptoms: In some rare cases, the platform-stats-bridge-cc container restarts unexpectedly on VELOS controllers.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions are unknown and this occurs rarely.
bugs.impact: The platform-stats-bridge-cc container can quickly restart by itself. When the container is not running, the platform stats for the system controllers cannot be viewed temporarily. A core file is generated. There is no impact on production traffic or system health.

bugs.title: Intermittent webUI startup failure after F5OS v1.8.x upgrade caused by SSL certificate generation issue
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases after upgrading to F5OS v1.8.x, the Web GUI (httpd) may fail to start. System logs may show a missing ServerName directive, and the /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert file may be missing or zero bytes.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur in certain scenarios where the upgrade process fails to properly generate or retain the f5os.cert certificate file, and the authentication-manager does not recover from the missing or empty certificate, resulting in an invalid httpd configuration.
bugs.impact: The webUI is completely unavailable. CLI and API access remain functional.
bugs.workaround: Restart the authentication-mgr and http-server services using the following CLI command: system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service authentication-mgr system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service http-server

bugs.title: Removing the active controller does not trigger an immediate tenant failover
bugs.symptoms: On a VELOS chassis setup where the BIG-IP tenant is active for a traffic group and the HA score includes a weighted value for F5OS_INTERNAL_TRUNK. Removing the active controller does not result in an immediate failover.
bugs.conditions: The tenant is active for a traffic group and is running on the controller that is currently active for the partition hosting the tenant. The active system controller is removed or powered off using AOM.
bugs.impact: Tenant failover is delayed upto 4min when an active controller of the active tenant is pulled out .
bugs.fix: Reduce the polling interval for lost VQF-link confD events to shorten the event detection time.

bugs.title: Snmpwalk misses LAG interface stats intermittently
bugs.symptoms: Though the LAG interface is configured in system, some stats for the LAG interface will be missed in snmpwalk output intermittently.
bugs.conditions: Issue is rarely observed when running snmpwalk in a loop continuously.
bugs.impact: Snmpwalk may not display all statistics for the LAG interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Run snmpwalk after a 20 second delay.
bugs.fix: Ensured all LAG interface statistics are properly reported in SNMP walk output.

bugs.title: VELOS tenant pods unexpectedly restart after the active system controller is physically removed
bugs.symptoms: Removing the active system controller from a VELOS chassis causes all BIG-IP tenant pods across the blades to restart. The Multus reinstalls unintentionally, triggering the restart of all running tenant instances. The chassis recovers after the process completes, but tenant availability is disrupted during the process.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following are true: * The VELOS chassis is running in a redundant system controller configuration. * The active system controller is physically removed or powered down (e.g., for maintenance or certification testing).
bugs.impact: All BIG-IP tenants on the affected VELOS chassis restart after an active system controller failover event. This results in a temporary loss of tenant availability and traffic processing until the tenants return to a healthy running state. The chassis itself recovers automatically, but the tenant restart introduces unplanned downtime that exceeds the expected duration of a standard controller failover.
bugs.workaround: There is no permanent software workaround prior to upgrading to the fixed release.

bugs.title: Long BIG-IP tenant names will prevent virtual console access
bugs.symptoms: Creating a BIG-IP tenant in the GUI with a name longer than 32 characters will prevent virtual console access to the tenant.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant name is longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The creation of the tenant-console user fails, preventing access to the virtual console for that tenant.
bugs.workaround: Use tenant names that don't exceed 32 characters in length.

bugs.title: Configuration loss when using a preferred redundancy mode
bugs.symptoms: When the redundancy mode is set to "prefer-1" or "prefer-2", replacing or reinstalling the preferred system controller can result in configuration loss.
bugs.conditions: A preferred redundancy mode is configured during controller maintenance or a software upgrade.
bugs.impact: The system configuration can be lost, resulting in service disruption.
bugs.workaround: Use the "auto" redundancy mode for normal operation. Use "prefer-1" or "prefer-2" only temporarily under guidance from F5 Support, and restore "auto" mode before controller maintenance or software upgrades.

bugs.title: The dnsmasq_t SELinux violation
bugs.symptoms: Observing the seliux warnings related dnsmasq ausearch -m avc -ts boot type=AVC msg=audit(1768957848.741:27): avc: denied { write } for pid=2965 comm="dnsmasq" name="lock" dev="dm-0" ino=13501463 scontext=system_u:system_r:dnsmasq_t:s0
bugs.conditions: It is seen when running F5OS 1.8.x version
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: The dnsasq functionalies is not affected.

bugs.title: After clean install, VELOS controller may be unable to start third etcd instance
bugs.symptoms: After a controller is freshly-installed and Openshift is installed on it, that controller will be unable to launch the third etcd instance due to errors in the /etc/etcd/etcd-3.conf configuration file. If this controller becomes active, this may result in the Openshift cluster becoming unresponsive and unhealthy. /var/log/openshift.log will be logging repeating error messages such as the following: displayClusterStatus: skip display since the last query nodes failed queryNodes: oc get nodes command failed - Do not parse output file Controller 1 is inserted, pingable, sshable, InCluster, and cluster is initialized and 3rd etcd was installed Controller 2 is inserted, pingable, sshable, InCluster, and cluster is initialized and 3rd etcd was installed ETCD: No controllers are currently active - reset delay in launch of the third etcd docker container
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system controller - Freshly installed (i.e. via USB install or PXE install) - non-default internal chassis network range (something other than RFC6598)
bugs.impact: Openshift cluster unhealthy. Unable to manage tenants.
bugs.workaround: On the newly-installed controller, edit /etc/etcd/etcd-3.conf and modify the references to "100.65." to the correct internal chassis network prefix. See /etc/etcd/etcd.conf. This can be done automatically by running the following commands in a bash shell on the controller. (source /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt && [ -n "${network_prefix:-}" ] && sed -i.ID2216701.backup -e "s,100＼.65＼.,${network_prefix}.,g" /etc/etcd/etcd-3.conf )

bugs.title: Controller can incorrectly be removed from the OpenShift cluster during rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After a rolling upgrade of the controller software, one of the controllers may incorrectly be removed from the OpenShift cluster. This leaves the OpenShift cluster in a state where there is only one leader node in the cluster.
bugs.conditions: This can happen during a rolling upgrade due to a race condition on checking the status of the standby controller.
bugs.impact: If this occurs the affected controller will no longer be in the OpenShift cluster, so HA availability of the OpenShift cluster between the controllers will be compromised.
bugs.workaround: To protect against a controller being removed from the cluster during the rolling upgrade while the active controller is still running the older software, it is recommended to do a "touch /tmp/omd/pause" on the active controller before starting the rolling upgrade. This will keep the down rev controller from removing the newly upgraded controller if the bug is hit. The pause file be automatically removed when the controller is upgraded after the newly upgraded controller becomes active. The workaround to recover once the controller has been removed from the cluster is to manually retrigger the addition of the removed controller to the Openshift cluster. If controller-1 was removed, on controller 2 the user would do a touch /var/omd/CONTROLLER1_REINSTALL If controller-2 was removed, on controller 1 the user would do a touch /var/omd/CONTROLLER2_REINSTALL
bugs.fix: The race condition that led to the controller being incorrectly removed from the cluster has been fixed, so that a controller will no longer be removed from the cluster during rolling upgrade once the controllers have been upgraded.

bugs.title: Tenant management IP may be inaccessible until ARP entries timeout after controller failover
bugs.symptoms: After a controller failover, or reboot of the active CC mode, Stale ARP entries may cause the tenant management IPs to not be accessible. GARP packets are sent, but there was a race between the management port on the new CC becoming active and the tenant orchestration layer sending the GARPs
bugs.conditions: This can happen after reboot/power cycle of the active controller, or manual failover the system controllers.
bugs.impact: The tenant management IP will become inaccessible until the ARP entries in the upstream switch times out, or the tenant generates outbound traffic on the management port that causes an update of the ARP table.
bugs.fix: GARPs are now sent for a longer time after the controller failover to make sure they reach the upstream network device.

bugs.title: Updated the restconf token's idle timeout configuration
bugs.symptoms: The default idle-timeout of the restconf-token was 1 minute, and was configurable up to a maximum of 5 minutes.
bugs.conditions: This is a change in the configurable values and default value of the restconf token.
bugs.impact: Not a bug
bugs.workaround: Not a bug.
bugs.fix: Updated the default idle-timeout of the restconf-token to 5 minutes. It can now be configured anywhere between 1 and 1,440 minutes (24 hours) maximum.

bugs.title: Controller boot up in rare conditions can impact blade management network after failover
bugs.symptoms: A rare race condition in the vcc-lacpd process can prevent a system controller failover correctly setting the LACP status for LACP based link aggregations. This condition is easily identifiable if the log msgid=0x6602000000000003 originating from vcc-lacpd process is seen since the last controller reboot.
bugs.conditions: Controller reboot. It is more likely though still extremely rare to occur if vcc-lacpd process restarts independently of a controller reboot.
bugs.impact: Blade management network can be impacted which can cause a variety of issues, including blade reboot loops on partition upgrade. If a management aggregation on the controller front panel management ports is configured for LACP, this aggregation may also be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Restart the affected vcc-lacpd process via docker restart cc-lacpd.
bugs.fix: While you may still see msgid=0x6602000000000003, the log no longer indicates a problem as the vcc-lacpd process will appropriately recover.

bugs.title: Empty File path in upload api leads to core
bugs.symptoms: The utils-agent service crashes
bugs.conditions: Provide an empty file path to the upload api
bugs.impact: Utils-agent crashes and generates a core.
bugs.fix: Empty/Null check added for file path field in upload api to make sure no crash in utils-agent service.

bugs.title: F5OS image import fails with 'Signature verification failed' error
bugs.symptoms: When F5OS ISO certificates were rotated for the first time in October 2025, certificate validity was set to 6 months. Consequently, importing affected images fails after expiration. This issue is limited to image import.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when attempting to import an F5OS ISO image published on or before October 2025.
bugs.impact: F5OS ISO images published on or before October 2025 cannot be imported.
bugs.workaround: Use F5OS ISO images published after October 2025 for import.
bugs.fix: F5OS ISO certificate expiration period has been extended to 39 months.

bugs.title: L2 table become inconsistent after reseating VELOS blades
bugs.symptoms: After reseating blades, L2 tables become inconsistent and traffic is sent to wrong interfaces despite static FIB entries being present.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when multiple VELOS blades are removed and reinserted. L2-agent fails to connect to confd during blade initialization, preventing proper interface/portgroup configuration updates.
bugs.impact: Traffic misdirection, inconsistent L2 tables, SNMP and CLI interface commands may fail.
bugs.workaround: Perform partition failover, disable/re-enable partition, or reseat affected blades.

bugs.title: TCP Packet loss after upgrade with AFM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, disabled hardware DOS vectors may use old values.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS tenant -- Upgrade -- AFM provisioned
bugs.impact: DOS thresholds may be incorrectly set or set too low resulting in packet loss that causes poor throughput.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable the disabled DOS vectors. Log into the BIG-IP GUI and navigate to Security ›› DoS Protection : Device Protection Filter attack vectors: tcp click the "Network" text Enable all the disabled vectors by clicking on the vector name and changing state from "disabled" to "mitigate". Then disable the vectors by clicking on the vector name and changing state from "mitigate" to "disabled".

bugs.title: PSU alarms getting cleared during controller failover
bugs.symptoms: PSU fault alarms were not triggered during controller failover.
bugs.conditions: When PSU alarms are present in the system and are followed by a controller failover.
bugs.impact: When PSU health status is displayed as faulty, the corresponding alarm notification does not appear.
bugs.fix: Updated diag-agent service so that any psu alarms won't be cleared by standby controller boot up.

bugs.title: Corrected Typo "tenanat" to "tenant" in Logging
bugs.symptoms: When searching log archives or examining journalctl outputs, the word "tenant" is misspelled as "tenanat" in log messages generated. This prevents support engineers and diagnostic tools from finding relevant log entries when searching or grepping logs for the keyword "tenant".
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on all supported platforms (including version A-1.8.3) when log entries are written by network-manager or appliance-network-manager.
bugs.impact: Although the spelling error is minor, it directly hinders supportability. Standard diagnostic tools, automated scripts, search queries, or grep commands targeting the word "tenant" will fail to locate these logging records. This can lead to frustration and extended troubleshooting times for support teams.
bugs.workaround: To locate these logs prior to applying the fix, search or grep for the misspelled term tenanat instead of tenant.
bugs.fix: The spelling of "tenant" has been corrected.

bugs.title: PSU alarm disappears intermittently when PSU issues exist
bugs.symptoms: The PSU alarm gets stuck when PSU hardware is faulty and frequent controller switchovers (or power cycle followed by switchovers) that can generate more LOP events and trigger the issue.
bugs.conditions: Faulty PSU hardware and frequent controllers switchover.
bugs.impact: No functional impact but PSU alarm gets stuck in ConfD.
bugs.workaround: Need to replace faulty PSU hardware. For more information on Platform maintenance, refer to Platform Guide: VELOS CX Series. For further assistance, contact F5 Support.

bugs.title: Partition VLAN traffic may dropped for a noticeable period of time during standby initialization
bugs.symptoms: LACP PDUs will be exchanged between the system controller and blade before switchd processes ConfD lagg membership and partition configuration (needed to setup partition vlans). As a result, LACP negotiation between blade and system controller completes before the lagg is actually ready for traffic. The delay between these events is typically ~10 seconds but may be up to 30 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Standby initialization after a reboot or power cycle.
bugs.impact: Services depending on partition connectivity between blade and System Controller are delayed until the System Controller switch daemon configures hardware trunks and partition vlans on the BCM control plane switch.
bugs.workaround: None. Partition traffic between blade and system controller requires successfull LACPD negotiation and trunk/vlan configuration of the control plane switch.

bugs.title: The snmpwalk fails with timeout after system upgrade on controller
bugs.symptoms: The snmpwalk gets timeout without response.
bugs.conditions: On upgrade, multiple services try to update iptable rules. Due to timing, there is rare chance of missing SNMP DNAT iptable rules update causing the connectivity issue with the SNMP port.
bugs.impact: The snmpwalk fails with timeout.
bugs.workaround: Run command "systemctl restart iptables-config.service " on the controller to reapply iptable rules (or) On controller reboot, iptable rules gets re-applied and fix the connectivity issue with SNMP port.

bugs.title: VELOS BX520 ATSE Datapath lockup causes blade to report unhealthy and stop passing traffic
bugs.symptoms: This failure looks like an RQM lockup. An RQM lockup can show up as a DMA receive failure or a DMA transmit failure. Receive failure because the receive queue will not accept HBM memory writes. Transmit failure because loopback health check packets will back up and flow control the transmit data-path.
bugs.conditions: No known conditions. This typically happens on initialization, but has been seen at runtime.
bugs.impact: This causes a data-path lock-up and traffic will not be passed by the affected blade.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: HBM calibration has been fixed.

bugs.title: 'Show NTP' Command Displays Incorrect Server IP Information
bugs.symptoms: The 'show ntp' command does not indicate an error when a server DNS name cannot be resolved. Additionally, if multiple NTP servers are configured, sometimes it displays the IP address of the synchronized time source as the IP address of all configured servers.
bugs.conditions: Configure multiple NTP servers, possibly with some with unresolvable domain names.
bugs.impact: NTP server information is inaccurate.
bugs.fix: NTP server status display has been corrected.

bugs.title: Kubervirt is stuck in unhealthy state due sw-mgmt port differences on controllers
bugs.symptoms: Kubervirt is stuck in unhealthy state due to port mismatch on different CCs. If cluster was brought up using one CC assigned port, it is stuck in unhealthy state if the same port is used to pull containers from the other CC.
bugs.conditions: Sw-mgmt port assignment to the service version must be different on differnt CCs. When the CCs were baremetal installed , import of ISO failed on one CC due to signature verification failure. Because ISO got imported on one CC and not the other this led to port mismatches.
bugs.impact: Kubervirt is stuck in unhealthy state.
bugs.workaround: As the port mismatch in this case is due to signature verification failure. Please check the ISO import status after baremetal and in case of failure copy the ISO from healthy CC to the other. OR Perform a HA failover in this case the CC with unimported state becomes stand by and syncs it self with active and will get the same port assignment.

bugs.title: AOM and fan alarms persist on rSeries appliance persist after hardware replacement and cannot be cleared
bugs.symptoms: After replacing a faulty fan tray via RMA, critical fan and AOM fault alarms remain visible in show system alarms even though replacement hardware is operating normally and show system health reports all components as healthy. Standard docker alert-service clear commands fail to remove the stale alarms.
bugs.conditions: Fan tray hardware replaced via RMA Replacement fans operating correctly (>15K RPM, health status: ok)
bugs.impact: Persistent false-positive critical alarms create operational confusion and monitoring noise.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and run: docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>" If above does not clear it. 1. docker restart alert-service 2.docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>"

bugs.title: F5OS tpm-integrity-status is Unavailable on certain versions released since October 2025
bugs.symptoms: When you run show components component state tpm-integrity-status, the TPM integrity status reports "Unavailable" # show components component state tpm-integrity-status TPM INTEGRITY NAME STATUS ----------------------- platform Unavailable
bugs.conditions: -- Running the tpm-integrity-status command from F5OS-A or F5OS-C on rSeries or VELOS: - VELOS systems running F5OS-C versions 1.8.2, 1.8.2-EHF, or 1.6.4 - rSeries systems running F5OS-A versions 1.8.3, 1.8.3-EHF, or 1.5.4 - EHFs built after October 15, 2025, including EHFs posted to MyF5 downloads in October such as: - F5OS-A-1.8.3-23493.R5R10.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.CONTROLLER.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.PARTITION.EHF-1 -- The calendar date is on or after April 4, 2026
bugs.impact: The tpm-integrity-status output reads Unavailable after April 4th, 2026.
bugs.workaround: If it is before April 4, 2026, you can run 'show components component state tpm-integrity-status' to get the TPM status.

bugs.title: Unexpected cluster installation can occur after a controller reinstall request that is followed by a controller failover
bugs.symptoms: An unexpected full cluster installation may be triggered after a controller reinstall request that is followed by a controller failover.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when the /var/omd/CONTROLLERX_REINSTALL is issued on the active controller that is followed by a controller failover.
bugs.impact: The entire cluster is reinstalled.

bugs.title: F5OS VELOS: Stale blade configuration causes tenant reboot when removing empty slots
bugs.symptoms: Removing empty slots from partition causes unexpected tenant reboot. Physically absent blade remains in OpenShift cluster, blocking F5OS upgrade completion until the slot is moved to the 'none' partition, triggering forced kubevirt reinstall and tenant redeployment.
bugs.conditions: -- Blade is physically removed but not cleaned from OpenShift cluster -- F5OS upgrade performed with stale blade configuration present -- Empty slots subsequently removed from the partition.
bugs.impact: Unexpected tenant reboot and service disruption when removing empty slots. F5OS upgrade is stuck in an inconsistent state until the stale configuration issue is resolved.
bugs.workaround: Move the affected slot to the 'none' partition.

bugs.title: Possible that cluster status output in controller CLI may not represent actual status
bugs.symptoms: There is a rare possibility that the cluster status output in the controller CLI may not display the actual cluster status in the chassis.
bugs.conditions: There is a timing case where stale values for the cluster status are written to the confd database on startup and are not refreshed when actual values are available.
bugs.impact: User will see an incorrect cluster state.
bugs.workaround: User can issue a controller failover and that will update to the correct cluster status within confd

bugs.title: Tenant image upload silently fails
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios extra disk space is required for a tenant image. If there is enough space to upload the image, but not enough extra space, the operation will silently fail.
bugs.conditions: Enough disk space available to upload a tenant image, but not enough to copy it.
bugs.impact: Silent failure when uploading a tenant image.
bugs.workaround: Clear disk space by removing old tenant images, or resize the images volume.

bugs.title: F5 VELOS VQF firmware v8.10.4.13
bugs.symptoms: F5 VELOS VQF firmware v8.10.4.13
bugs.conditions: F5 VELOS system
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.workaround: Fixes issues with L2/FDB entries and dropping of multicast traffic. See ID2183789 and ID2141089 for more information.

bugs.title: Stale USB drive entry remains in show components after USB removal on VELOS
bugs.symptoms: After a USB drive is removed, show components may still display the removed USB disk entry (for example sda DataTraveler) even though lsusb, lsblk, and platform-hal GET:drives no longer show it.
bugs.conditions: On VELOS systems, a USB drive was previously attached to a controller and then removed; stale drive data may remain shown in show components.
bugs.impact: Show components can report stale storage information, which may mislead operators about currently attached USB devices.

bugs.title: PlatformStatsBridge crash on VELOS due to malformed SNMP requests
bugs.symptoms: Multiple PlatformStatsBridge core dumps observed on VELOS controller and partition.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the system receives malformed or out-of-range SNMP queries, such as those generated by misconfigured monitoring scripts (e.g., Zabbix integration).
bugs.impact: PlatformStatsBridge process crashes, generating core files. No impact to production traffic or overall VELOS system health reported.
bugs.workaround: Ensure SNMP monitoring tools send only valid and supported OIDs. Review and correct any custom SNMP scripts or templates to avoid malformed queries. No further action required if scripts are compliant; issue does not affect production service.

bugs.title: Ports 7100 and 7200 Exposed, Allowing Remote Console Access via Management Network
bugs.symptoms: Ports 7100 and 7200, used for internal console access between controllers, are remotely accessible over the management network. This can lead to potential unauthorized access to the controllers.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized access to the controller's console using exposed ports.
bugs.fix: Ports 7100 and 7200 are included in the controller allowlist, which allows adding allowed-IP rules for these ports.

bugs.title: VELOS tenant pods unexpectedly restart after the active system controller is physically removed or powered down.
bugs.symptoms: Removing the active system controller from a VELOS chassis causes all BIG-IP tenant pods on the blades to restart. The KubeVirt virtualization layer reinstalls unintentionally, triggering the restart of all running tenant instances. The chassis recovers after the process completes, but tenant availability is disrupted during the process.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are true: * The VELOS chassis is running in a redundant system controller configuration. * The active system controller is physically removed or powered down (e.g., for maintenance or certification testing). * Either or both of these conditions result in KubeVirt being reinstalled, which causes all tenant pods to restart: * Upon failover, the newly promoted active controller detects a stale /var/omd/KUBEVIRT_REINSTALL flag left over from the previous active controller, triggering a forced KubeVirt reinstall. * Additionally, a race condition may occur where the KubeVirt verification script runs before the Kubernetes API server has fully come online after failover — causing the script to fail and independently set an internal kubevirtInstallFailed flag, which also triggers a forced reinstall.
bugs.impact: All BIG-IP tenants on the affected VELOS chassis restart after an active system controller failover event. This results in a temporary loss of tenant availability and traffic processing until the tenants return to a healthy running state. The chassis itself recovers automatically, but the tenant restart introduces unplanned downtime that exceeds the expected duration of a standard controller failover.
bugs.workaround: No permanent software workaround exists prior to upgrading to the fixed release. To reduce exposure, apply the following interim measures: (1) Clear stale flags in /var/omd/ on the standby controller before performing any planned controller failover or removal. Ensuring that flags such as /var/omd/KUBEVIRT_REINSTALL are not present on the standby prior to a transition will prevent the forced KubeVirt reinstall from being triggered by a leftover flag. (2) Use AOM Power Off instead of physical controller extraction for controller failover testing. Physically removing the active controller is more likely to trigger the race condition described above. Using the AOM Power Off method provides a more controlled failover that reduces the likelihood of hitting this issue.

bugs.title: Packet loss on a F5OS tenant when vlan-groups are in use
bugs.symptoms: On an F5OS tenant, there may be packet loss when vlan-groups are in use. This occurs due to high churn inside the FDB table due to MAC addresses being learned between different host ports resulting in temporary DLF drops while the MAC is learned on the new port.
bugs.conditions: - BX520 blade - VLAN groups - A large amount of unique MAC addresses in the FDB table
bugs.impact: Packet loss. Failing monitor probes.
bugs.workaround: Monitor probe issues may be alleviated by creating a static FDB entry for the local admin bit flipped MAC address that TMM is egressing packets from.
bugs.fix: Enable service-DAG when learning host generated MAC addresses to eliminate port-motion events between host ports.

bugs.title: The MIB description for diskTotalIops is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The MIB description for diskTotalIops is incorrect; it mistakenly states its total read/write IOPS
bugs.conditions: Description of the diskTotalIops OID is incorrect
bugs.impact: User has the incorrect description for diskTotalIops OID
bugs.workaround: Updated the description of diskTotalIops MIB in 2.1.0 and A-1.8.5, A-1.5.5, v1.8.3 LTS releases.
bugs.fix: Updated the description of diskTotalIops MIB in 2.1.0 and A-1.8.5, A-1.5.5, v1.8.3 LTS releases.

bugs.title: Unexpected Controller Switchover Observed While Copying Image to USB Drive Using dd Command
bugs.symptoms: On the active controller, copying the image to the USB controller triggers the controller switchover to standby.
bugs.conditions: -- Install the latest 2.0 iso on the chassis. -- On active controller, perform iso copy on USB using the dd command. example: dd if=<file.iso> of=/dev/sda bs=1M -- Active controller will switch to standby mode.
bugs.impact: The system will be unresponsive for some time (~200 sec). ConfD will be switched over to the standby controller.
bugs.workaround: Use oflag=direct flag with dd command: example: dd if=<file.iso> oflag=direct of=/dev/sda bs=1M

bugs.title: CLI does not give a warning when creating a tenant with a non-existent image
bugs.symptoms: By design the F5OS CLI allows one to create a tenant with an image that is not present on the system. However, there is no warning given in this scenario.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a new tenant in the CLI. -- Specifying an image that is not present on the system.
bugs.impact: The image will not be deployable until the specified image is uploaded to the system. This can cause confusion.
bugs.fix: A warning was added to the CLI (interactive user interface only ) to warn the user that the tenant image is not available for immediate deployment when a tenant is deployed. Important Note: F5OS systems are designed to be declarative APIs, and as such an absent tenant image is not considered to be an error. When the image is uploaded and available, the tenant will proceed to be deployed. The tab-complete mechanism also provides means to minimize using images that are not available for use when configuring a tenant.

bugs.title: Problematic "Pending" tenants need to be called out on the Tenant Deployments screen
bugs.symptoms: Tenants that are in the "Pending" state due to an error need to be called out better on the "Tenant" Deployments" screen in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Deploying an undeployable tenant.
bugs.impact: Confusion as to why a tenant seems to be stuck in the "Pending" state.
bugs.workaround: Look on the "Tenant Details" screen of the problematic tenant. Or use one of the options detailed in K70034058.
bugs.fix: The Tenant Deployment screen now displays a warning banner when one or more tenants remain in a pending state, guiding users to review tenant instance statuses on the Tenant Details screen for further investigation and resolution.

bugs.title: Deletion of configuration database backup on active controller using GUI/F5SH/API are never synchronized on standby controller
bugs.symptoms: Deleting a controller or partition backup file using the GUI, F5SH, or API does not result in the deletion of files in the standby controller's file system. - For partition backups: /var/F5/partition<N>/configs/ - For controller backups: /var/confd/configs/
bugs.conditions: A backup file is deleted through the GUI, F5SH, or API on F5OS VELOS platform.
bugs.impact: - Accumulation of stale backup files on standby controller. - When a standby controller is made active, the stale files are synchronized to the new standby controller.
bugs.workaround: Manually run SSH commands on the standby controller and directly delete the stale backup file. For controller backups: ssh controller-<standby_id> 'rm /var/confd/configs/<backup_name>' For partition backups: ssh controller-<standby_id> 'rm /var/F5/partition<N>/configs/<backup_name>'
bugs.fix: Fixed the defect. Backup files now get deleted on standby as well.

bugs.title: The module-communication-error not clearing post-recovery
bugs.symptoms: A shared commError flag in the VPC and VFC health monitoring tasks caused a race condition when tracking communication errors across controllers.
bugs.conditions: A shared commError flag caused a race condition where a communication error in one PSU controller could be incorrectly cleared by another PSU controller, leaving the original controller's error uncleared even after recovery.
bugs.impact: This led to scenarios where a module communication error status was not cleared even after recovery.
bugs.workaround: Restart diag-agent using the below command docker restart diag-agent
bugs.fix: Fixed Communication Error not clearing for recovered modules

bugs.title: TX_Enable Not Set for Lanes 2-4 After Hot-Swapping 400G Optic on BX520 Front Panel Port in 4x100G Bifurcated Mode
bugs.symptoms: Upon optic re-insertion in 4x100G mode on BX520 blades, there is an issue in MAC enable for lanes 2 to 4. For example, if port 3/2 is in 4x100G mode and the optic is hot-swapped, then the MAC will be enabled only for the first link 3/2.1 and not for 3/2.2-2.4.
bugs.conditions: On a BX520 blade, the front panel port is in bifurcated mode (4x100G), and the optic is hot-swapped (removed and re-inserted).
bugs.impact: The issue in MAC enable for lanes 2 to 4 will cause an issue when sending out the egress packets on lanes 2 to 4 of the port.
bugs.workaround: Admin bounce of ALL interfaces will help facilitate a clean link-up. Administratively disable the 4x100G interfaces before removing the optic. Then remove and re-insert the optic. Then re-enable the interfaces.
bugs.fix: Added a change in optic_removal part of the code such that linkscan is disabled upon optic being removed, and there are no spurious UP events for lanes 2 to 4, and make mac_enable get processed prematurely and incorrectly for them.

bugs.title: Updated the firmware log messages to reflect the actual status
bugs.symptoms: On every F5 rSeries appliances and VELOS chassis/blade systems running F5OS versions 2.0 or lower, incorrect log messages are reporting firmware update running/completed during reboot or restart. These messages appear even when the system firmware is already up-to-date and is only being loaded.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the system boots, restarts, or reboots and loads existing firmware components during initialization.
bugs.impact: Misleading log messages such as "firmware update complete" or "firmware update is running" may make users think that the firmware is updated during every reboot. This causes confusion and unnecessary escalations even when there is no functional impact to the system.
bugs.fix: Reworded the log messages on F5 rSeries appliances and VELOS chassis/blade systems running F5OS versions 2.0 or lower to the following: - "firmware load is running" instead of "firmware update is running" - "firmware load is complete" instead of "firmware update complete".
