bugs.title: Orchestration Manager crash when partition configured with mgmt-vlans
bugs.symptoms: The Orchestration Manager (OMD) process crashes and restarts when a partition is configured with mgmt-vlans.
bugs.conditions: - Partition configured with mgmt-vlans, e.g. "mgmt-vlans untagged". - The mgmt-vlans added to an existing partition.
bugs.impact: - The Orchestration Manager process crashes and restarts. - Cluster data is unavailable during the restart.
bugs.workaround: Create partition without "mgmt-vlans", or remove from existing partition: conf no partitions partition <partition> config mgmt-vlans commit

bugs.title: Assigning slots to the 'none' VELOS partition causes controller-manager pods to be disrupted and turn 0/1 Ready
bugs.symptoms: The two controller-manager pods are observed to be disrupted and not in a 1/1 Ready state after assigning blades to the 'none' partition. For example, in the output of 'oc get pods --all-namespaces', the pods are observed to be in 'CrashLoopBackOff' state, similar to the following example: [root@controller-2(VEL410):Active ~]# oc get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep controller-manager kube-service-catalog controller-manager-kb7th 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 27s 100.76.0.29 controller-1.chassis.local kube-service-catalog controller-manager-4zp6r 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 37s 100.77.0.30 controller-2.chassis.local The controller-manager pods may also be observed in the 'Error' or 'Running' state with the status as 0/1 Ready containers. The output of the 'oc logs -n kube-service-catalog <pod name>' command displays an error similar to the following: controller_manager.go:237] error running controllers: failed to get api versions from server: failed to get supported resources from server: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: subresources.kubevirt.io/v1alpha3: the server is currently unable to handle the request
bugs.conditions: Slots that were previously assigned to an enabled VELOS partition are re-assigned to the 'none' partition.
bugs.impact: - Controller-manager pods crash repeatedly and fail to turn the status to 1/1 Ready. - Orchestration Manager removes the pods that are not ready or are newly scheduled pods that have not turned ready yet. - New blades cannot be added to the OpenShift cluster while the controller-manager pods are unhealthy.
bugs.workaround: Assign the slots to an enabled partition. The CLI prompt may display a "Cluster update in-progress" message for a brief period while playbooks run to add blades into the cluster.

bugs.title: SNMP stat requests may stop working when the active controller crashes
bugs.symptoms: In case an active controller goes down (e.g., due to a hardware error), the requests to the SNMP stats may stop working until the faulty controller is replaced.
bugs.conditions: Sudden failure of the active controller.
bugs.impact: Queries on the SNMP stats fail.

bugs.title: F5OS log message ID inconsistencies
bugs.symptoms: Some F5OS logs have message IDs that do not match those documented in the F5OS Log Message Reference.
bugs.conditions: Affects all F5OS services whose service_code is in the range 1-15 (single hex digit).
bugs.impact: No functional impact to traffic or system operation. The message ID mismatch prevents users from cross-referencing log messages against the published Log Message Reference.

bugs.title: fpgamgr may crash if there are QoS queues configured in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: When QoS queues are configured in F5OS, there is a rare crash in the fpgamgr service.
bugs.conditions: QoS queues configured via F5OS. Excessive link flapping may increase the probability of this crash.
bugs.impact: Tenant traffic disruptions while the fpgamgr service restarts.
bugs.fix: The fpgamgr service no longer crashes if QoS queues are configured.

bugs.title: Some Openshift processes may experience high CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: High CPU utilization is observed in certain Openshift processes.
bugs.conditions: This condition can occur during periods of high demand on multiple system resources.
bugs.impact: You may mostly likely will not notice anything unless the top command is run in the command shell. It is possible that this condition may affect other system resources.

bugs.title: Extended parallel packet captures on partition and tenants show timestamp skew
bugs.symptoms: When running parallel packet captures on F5OS partitions and tenants for an extended period (hours), a timestamp skew will gradually become apparent. Timestamps across captures will not match for the same packets.
bugs.conditions: -- Parallel packet captures. -- Capturing for an extended period of time (hours).
bugs.impact: Difficulty lining up captured packets due to time differences.

bugs.title: Tenant stuck after node reboot
bugs.symptoms: Tenants occasionally appear to get stuck after a node is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: - Tenant is running successfully - A node is rebooted - Ocassionally tenant comes up but is not operational.
bugs.impact: Tenant is not operational after a node reboot.
bugs.workaround: - Trigger another reboot.
bugs.fix: A change in how node requests are handled caused a race condition in the code that reconfigures the guest-to-host interface making it possible to remove the just created configuration.

bugs.title: Memory leak in user_manager when remote LDAP authentication binds fail
bugs.symptoms: When remote LDAP authentication is configured and LDAP bind attempts fail, user_manager leaks memory handles on each failed attempt. Symptoms include: - Host platform memory steadily depletes over time. - Repeated error messages in system logs (authentication-mgr / var/log/messages): Trying SASL bind with bindDN <DN> SASL bind error: -1 'Can't contact LDAP server' - Eventually, host memory becomes fully exhausted, triggering the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer. - Host management interfaces (SSH, WebUI, and serial console) become inaccessible, and running tenant instances become unresponsive or freeze.
bugs.conditions: - Remote LDAP authentication is configured (system aaa authentication config authentication-method includes LDAP_ALL). - The configured LDAP server is unreachable, rejects bind credentials, or encounters a protocol/port misconfiguration (e.g., global "ssl on" configured against plaintext port 389). - Background polling (AAA_Poller) repeatedly attempts to bind to the LDAP server to synchronize role mappings.
bugs.impact: Available host platform memory is exhausted over time, leading to kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) conditions, total loss of host management access, tenant disruption, and requiring a hard power cycle/reboot of the appliance.
bugs.workaround: To halt the memory leak, eliminate the failed bind attempts using either of the following methods: 1. Correct the LDAP configuration or network reachability so binds succeed: - Ensure the server is reachable and credentials are valid. - Resolve any protocol conflicts (e.g., if using SSL, use port 636 with "ssl on"; if using port 389, configure "ssl start_tls" or "ssl off"). - Remove any duplicate or conflicting server-groups: config no system aaa server-groups server-group <duplicate_group> commit 2. Temporarily switch authentication back to local accounts until LDAP service is restored: config system aaa authentication config authentication-method [ LOCAL ] commit
bugs.fix: User_manager now properly releases LDAP connection handles and TLS contexts on all error paths in doBind, preventing memory leaks when LDAP bind attempts fail.

bugs.title: Dockerd crashes and confd remains unavailable on the affected VELOS system controller
bugs.symptoms: The dockerd-current process crashes and restarts.
bugs.conditions: Conditions that cause the crash are currently unknown. This is a rare issue.
bugs.impact: - dockerd restarts, but confd and other containers remain unavailable. - The affected controller is unreachable via its management IP, but may be reachable via the ccpeer link from the active peer controller. The controller's IP address on the ccpeer link can be determined with the following command: echo "peer controller: $(ifconfig ccpeer | grep -Po '(?<=inet )([^.]+＼.){3}')$(( 53 - $(grep Slot /etc/PLATFORM | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')))" - A shell on the affected controller displays "Waiting for ConfD" in the prompt. - The active controller reports the peer controller as unavailable or MIA in the output of 'show system redundancy-details'. - The affected controller may become unreachable in the openshift cluster, with intermittent periods of connectivity.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected system controller. This may need to be done via the AOM menu.

bugs.title: BX110 ports configured for 40G can fail to link with OPT-0036 optics
bugs.symptoms: BX110 front panel interface configured for 40G with OPT-0036 optic fails to achieve link.
bugs.conditions: - BX110 - Front panel port configured for 40G - OPT-0036 optic
bugs.impact: Front panel interface remains DOWN, preventing traffic from flowing.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected blade.

bugs.title: The superuser-bash users cannot perform ls and cat operations files from log/host/ paths
bugs.symptoms: Super users operating under the default SELinux staff_u:staff_r:staff_t context are unable to perform ls, cat, or similar file access operations on certain log and host paths due to SELinux policy restrictions
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when a user attempts to access restricted log or host files while executing under the standard staff_u:staff_r:staff_t SELinux context. The restriction is present regardless of whether the user has a superuser role.
bugs.impact: Super users cannot list directories or view files within protected log and host locations, resulting in permission denied errors.
bugs.fix: Updated the SELinux policy to allow users running under the staff_u:staff_r:staff_t context to access approved log and host paths.

bugs.title: Disabled fpga monitoring to reduce memory spikes
bugs.symptoms: The memory of the diag-agent service rises occasionally due to event bursts.
bugs.conditions: When the system is busy due to high tenant traffic, the disk I/O operations are slower. The elevated load caused the fpga-monitoring service to generate a large volume of events and disk (sqllite-db) operations, which further slowed-down the disk I/O operations.
bugs.impact: The memory of the diag-agent service gradually increases due to a backlog of events in the memory queue during slow processing.
bugs.fix: FPGA monitoring is now disabled by default. In addition, SQLite database writes are skipped when no value changes are detected

bugs.title: Overall health status of the Controller turns Unhealthy when the FEC uncorrected error rate is critical
bugs.symptoms: When the FEC Uncorrected Error Rate exceeds 0.01%(the threshold is crossed), the 'switch:port:fec-uncorrected-error-rate' attribute for the affected port is updated to severity="Critical" and health="Unhealthy".
bugs.conditions: The FEC Uncorrected Error Rate exceeds the 0.01% threshold.
bugs.impact: The controller is marked as unhealthy, and a HA failover is triggered.

bugs.title: Incorrect available resources reported for newly added BX520 blade
bugs.symptoms: After a BX520 blade is added to an F5OS chassis and then assigned to a partition, the available system resources shown for the blade (specifically Available Tenant CPU, Available Tenant Memory, and Available Tenant Disk) will be shown as much lower than expected. The available resources for the blade can be seen in the "Cluster Details" section of the partition's GUI, or by running "show cluster nodes node <blade name> state node-info" command in the partition CLI.
bugs.conditions: -- Newly added blade in an F5OS chassis. -- Blade is added to an existing partition.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue; the actual amount of available resources is correct.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, but restarting the system will clear the issue.

bugs.title: Cron entries after the first one in file do not run
bugs.symptoms: A scheduled cron job that previously worked stops running after upgrading to a version containing the fix for ID1185573 and ID1994869. The job is still listed by "crontab -l" and works when run by hand, but never executes on schedule, with nothing logged.
bugs.conditions: -- A user-defined crontab (e.g., root's crontab) or an /etc/cron.d file containing more than one schedulable entry. -- The entry that fails to run is any entry after the first in that file.
bugs.impact: User-defined scheduled jobs silently fail to run after upgrade unless they're the first entry in the crontab file. Failure is silent: the job is present in "crontab -l", runs correctly when invoked manually, and produces no errors or SELinux denials. System-managed (F5-owned) crontabs are NOT affected.
bugs.workaround: Place the required job as the FIRST entry in the crontab (or in its own single-entry /etc/cron.d file). This is a positional workaround only and is fragile - adding further entries, or any reordering, will cause later entries to silently stop running again.

bugs.title: DMA-Agent crashes while trying to disable a Service Endpoint (SEP) that is already disabled
bugs.symptoms: The DMA-Agent process crashes with an assertion failure ("Assertion Failed: FALSE"), causing ATSE data movers to stop unexpectedly. Affected tenants may become unresponsive or experience a service interruption. The crash occurs after an SEP (Service Endpoint) has been successfully enabled and a subsequent disable operation is issued against a SEP that is already in a disabled state.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS across all supported platforms. The condition is triggered when the DMA-Agent receives a request to disable an SEP that has already been disabled. For example, during tenant lifecycle operations or automated service recovery sequences where redundant disable commands may be issued against the same SEP.
bugs.impact: When this issue is triggered, the DMA-Agent crashes and all associated ATSE data movers are stopped, resulting in a loss of tenant data-plane traffic processing. This is a critical-severity issue that can cause an unplanned tenant outage requiring manual intervention or a service restart to restore normal operation.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available. If the crash occurs, restart the DMA-Agent and affected tenants to restore service. Avoid initiating rapid or repeated tenant disable operations in close succession to reduce the likelihood of encountering this issue.
bugs.fix: The DMA-Agent was updated to check the current state of an SEP before attempting a disable operation. If the SEP is already in a disabled state, the agent now skips the disable request and logs an informational message instead of triggering an assertion failure. This prevents the unnecessary crash and ensures ATSE data movers continue operating normally.

bugs.title: Cron job and systemd unit failures occur due to SELinux confd_cli denials
bugs.symptoms: Scheduled cron jobs that access the ConfD control port fail silently. This also happens to systemd units that access the ConfD control port.
bugs.conditions: A scheduled job (cron / system_cronjob_t domain) or systemd unit that connects to the ConfD control port (TCP/4565). For example, anything that invokes one of the following: - /usr/bin/f5sh - confd_cli - f5_confd_cli.
bugs.impact: Any cron-driven or systemd unit workflow that invokes the ConfD via 'f5sh/confd_cli/f5_confd_cli' stops working silently except for connection failures in the job's own output.
bugs.workaround: Use the "ssh root@localhost f5sh" command instead of f5sh. Note: This requires the usage of another level of quotes. Instead of using the following command: f5sh "config; system database config-backup name otters.xml proceed yes" Use the following command: ssh -o 'BatchMode yes' -o 'LogLevel error' root@localhost f5sh "'config; system database config-backup name otters.xml proceed yes'"

bugs.title: F5OS does not send LAG information to tenant when LAG is configured with virtual wire
bugs.symptoms: No LAG objects available in tenant.
bugs.conditions: LAG configured with virtual wire, and virtual wire is configured on a tenant.
bugs.impact: No LAG objects available in tenant.

bugs.title: BX520 blades spuriouisly reboot with a "pin reset" message in the pel log
bugs.symptoms: BX520 blades can reboot under certain traffic loads. The signature for this bug being the cause of the reboot is a "pin reset" message in the pel log: 08/04/2026 15:08:28 | 21981 | AOM | 255 | Na | 6 | AOM boot marker (v1.00.231.0.1) 08/04/2026 15:08:28 | 21982 | AOM | 255 | Na | 6 | pin reset 08/04/2026 15:08:28 | 21983 | AOM | 255 | Na | 6 | power-on reset
bugs.conditions: Any VELOS chassis using BX520 blades and under traffic load.
bugs.impact: Blade(s) reboot causing a traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: The following workaround disables Turbo Boost functionality both temporarily and persistently across system startups. The procedure must be repeated on all blades. If a blade is PXE-booted or replaced via RMA, the configuration will not persist. In such cases, you will need to reapply these steps to disable Turbo Boost. This change lowers the CPU clock speed under load, reducing throughput and increasing latency, which leads to a drop in performance Steps to Disable Turbo Boost 1. Disable Turbo Boost immediately. echo 1 > /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo 2. To disable Turbo Boost on blade startup, create a tmpfiles.d configuration file with the following command (requires root privileges): echo "w /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo - - - - 1" > /etc/tmpfiles.d/disable-turbo-boost.conf Verification Steps to Confirm Turbo Boost is disabled v1. Confirm the Max CPU frequency reflects a non-Turbo state. cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_max_freq Expected output: 2200000 v2. Validate Turbo Mode Status. cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo Expected output: 1, indicating that Turbo Boost is disabled
bugs.fix: Turbo Mode is now disabled by default, which lowers the CPU clock speed under load. This may decrease throughput and increase latency.

bugs.title: Partition may get deleted after out of memory event
bugs.symptoms: After an out-of-memory event there is a small chance that a system partition may get deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system. -- Out-of-memory event with specific timing.
bugs.impact: Partitions are wiped.

bugs.title: platform-stats container crashes SIGSEGV while collecting disk-usage stats using du
bugs.symptoms: While collecting disk-usage stats by using du for /var/export/chassis/import, it traverses state mounts causing the container to crash.
bugs.conditions: If the /var/export/chassis/import has any state ISO mounts due to image import failues or any other issues, then they can get traversed by du and cause this issue.
bugs.impact: The container crashes, leaving a core file for the user. Also, due to the container crash, users might miss collecting all the stats that the container would have captured during that time.
bugs.fix: Added the --one-file-system flag to du invocation to avoid traversing state mounts.

bugs.title: On BX520 blade, live install to a version that does not support 2x100 requires reverting to default
bugs.symptoms: If the user has a system with BX520 blades, and if they configure the portgroups on the blade to 100G (2x100 support), the live install to a version without 2x100 support fails. The known symptom is that fpgamgr on the blade will keep restarting.
bugs.conditions: On a system that has BX520 blades with the 2x100 portgroup mode configured, live istallation of a version without 2x100 support fails.
bugs.impact: Data plane will be down for the ports on the BX520 blade with 2x100 portgroup modes.
bugs.workaround: Update the portgroup modes on the BX520 blade from 2x100 to a previously supported configuration. For example, 100G and 400G are the default configurations. After the blade reboots,reclusters, and the system is stable, proceed with the live install to the desired version.

bugs.title: Allowed Slots restored to Tenant Deployments table in GUI
bugs.symptoms: In F5OS 1.8, the Allowed Slots information was moved from the Tenant Deployments table to the preview pane. This update restores Allowed Slots to the main table for easier visibility.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing Tenant Management > Tenant Deployments on affected VELOS GUI versions where Allowed Slots appears only in the preview pane.
bugs.impact: Administrators may need extra steps to view tenant slot assignments, reducing at-a-glance visibility.
bugs.workaround: Expand the tenant row to open the preview pane, where Allowed Slots and other tenant details are displayed.
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: Tenant image or F5OS ISO upload fails with "Copy failed" error in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When uploading a tenant image or F5OS ISO via the GUI file utility, the upload fails with a "Copy Failed" error message. Logs for utils-agent show: msg="file upload error" error="Failed to move file to destination path" msg="File change path failed, so deleting the uploaded file."
bugs.conditions: User attempts to upload tenant image or F5OS ISO using the GUI file utility feature
bugs.impact: Admin cannot upload tenant images or F5OS ISO files via the GUI. Uploaded file is automatically deleted by the system after the failed move operation.
bugs.workaround: You may select one of the following options below: 1. Use GUI Import instead of Upload — In the F5OS GUI, use the Import function (import via URL from an accessible repository) rather than Upload. 2. Use SCP to push the file directly to the F5OS system.
bugs.fix: Tenant or F5OS ISO images successfully upload.

bugs.title: Rebooting a VELOS blade with deployed tenants using a mgmt-vlan may cause the tenants not to return to Running state
bugs.symptoms: When a blade running tenants configured with a mgmt-vlan is rebooted, sometimes the team0.xxx links on the blade do not get re-created after the reboot. Tenants fail to return to Running state on the slot in question, remaining in status "Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute]": ('show tenants') INSTANCE TENANT NODE POD NAME ID SLOT PHASE CREATION TIME READY TIME STATUS MGMT MAC ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 tenant01-1 1 1 Running 2026-08-03T10:10:01Z 2026-08-03T10:10:44Z Started tenant instance e6:82:d4:4a:c4:70 2 tenant01-2 2 2 Pending 2026-08-03T10:18:45Z 2026-08-03T10:18:45Z Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute] 00:00:00:00:00:00 The tenant's virt-launcher pod is stuck in ContainerCreating state: ('oc get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep virt-launcher') partition-3 virt-launcher-tenant01-1-pzb7l 1/1 Running 0 22h <none> blade-1.chassis.local partition-3 virt-launcher-tenant01-2-cmcxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 19h 100.79.0.140 blade-2.chassis.local Blade's /var/log/messages contains many entries similar to the following: Multus: [partition-3/virt-launcher-tenant01-2-cmcxx]: error adding container to network ＼"mgmt-conf-tenant01＼": delegateAdd: error invoking conflistAdd - ＼"mgmt-conf-tenant01＼": conflistAdd: error in getting result from AddNetworkList: failed to lookup master ＼"team0.54＼": Link not found" The link in question does not appear in the blade's interface list: ('ip --br link | grep team0') team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.3@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.19@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.4@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.53@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.56@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.58@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> team0.59@team0 UP 14:a9:d0:c4:20:72 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>
bugs.conditions: -- mgmt-vlan configured on multiple tenants. -- Reboot a blade while the tenants are in deployed state.
bugs.impact: -- Multus is unable to bind the NetworkAttachmentDefinition for the tenant's management interface, preventing the tenant from starting up and reaching Running state. -- Blade logs are flooded with Multus errors.
bugs.workaround: To recover, move the affected tenants to Configured running-state, then back to Deployed. To avoid this issue, un-configure mgmt-vlan from the tenants in question (if possible): conf no tenants tenant <tenant> config mgmt-vlan commit Or move the tenants to Configured running-state, prior to a planned blade reboot.

bugs.title: Unusually high interface statistics observed
bugs.symptoms: F5OS interface stats randomly show abnormally high statistics.
bugs.impact: Incorrect interface statistics.

bugs.title: SNMP hrStorageTable GET-NEXT returns a genErr
bugs.symptoms: SNMP polling returns timeout error hrStorageTable GET-NEXT
bugs.conditions: SNMP GET-NEXT walks against HOST-RESOURCES-MIB hrStorageTable
bugs.impact: Timeout or genErr is seen when snmp polling is done on HOST-RESOURCES-MIB::hrStorageTable
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to the 1.8.3 Candidate or 2.1 versions that have a fix for these timeouts.
bugs.fix: Fix for the timeouts/genErr that occurred while running snmp polling on HOST-RESOURCES-MIB::hrStorageTable is available in the 1.8.3 candidate and 2.1 versions.

bugs.title: Virt-launcher pod may restart due to a libvirtd crash during concurrent VM start/stop operations
bugs.symptoms: The libvirtd process inside a virt-launcher pod can crash with a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) in qemuDomainObjBeginJobInternal. Core file can be observed.
bugs.conditions: It happens during reboot/upgrade.
bugs.impact: No cluster-wide impact, no data corruption. Other VMs and pods are unaffected. The failure window is only seen during the boot up process.
bugs.workaround: No configuration-level workaround is available. if triggered, Kubernetes/KubeVirt will automatically restart the affected virt-launcher pod and VM.

bugs.title: FPGA datapath issue allows packets to be sent from host to network out of order
bugs.symptoms: Packets from the host to network are received out of order on BX520 blade.
bugs.conditions: This typically happens in higher congestion or burst traffic conditions. The min/max packet size mix shows this issue most often, but packets out of order do happen with other random packet size mixes.
bugs.impact: Specific impact to UDP packet flows. UDP packets out of order can cause quality of service issues in audio and video streams.
bugs.workaround: Workaround requires a software update that contains an FPGA bitfile update to fix the issue.
bugs.fix: The issue is in the Transmit Routing Engine (TRE) in the FPGA transmit datapath from host to network. Part of the TRE architecture splits the transmit datapath into 2 100G packet paths, each directed at a 100G MAC interface. The issue is in how the packet paths were split. The datapath architecture uses a tuple hash to ensure that all packets from a specific packet flow are directed down the same packet path. In this case, the hash was not applied correctly which allowed packets from a specific flow to run down both 100G datapaths, which creates a race condition. In lower congestion applications, the packets hold their order. In higher congestion or bursty applications with varying packet sizes, the packets can be received out of order.

bugs.title: Port mismatch between images imported on both common controllers
bugs.symptoms: The service registry port assignment for the imported image is different in both common controllers.
bugs.conditions: The port assigned to a services registry for an imported image is different on both common controllers.
bugs.impact: Impacts bringing up of cluster service pods.
bugs.workaround: Trigger a switch over of CC mode, this would sync the port assignments of imported images among common controllers.

bugs.title: Possible that a cluster reinstall will hang in a chassis with one controller
bugs.symptoms: In a chassis that only has one controller, it is possible that a cluster reinstall will hang and not succeed.
bugs.conditions: There is a leftover file called CLUSTER_INSTALLED that should not be present after the cluster reinstall is issued causing the install to not finish.
bugs.impact: The cluster will remain in a bad state.
bugs.workaround: Remove the file and restart OMD 1. rm /var/omd/CLUSTER_INSTALLED 2. systemctl restart orchestration_manager_container.service

bugs.title: EDR license entitlement may briefly display "Missing" in logs following a controller reboot
bugs.symptoms: After a controller reboots, the EDR Enablement License entitlement status logged by the system may briefly report "Missing," even though a valid EDR add-on license is installed and active. The log self-corrects to the proper entitlement state (Active or Expired) within sometime, with no further recurrence.
bugs.conditions: This is an intermittent, timing-related issue that can occur only on controller reboot when: 1.An EDR add-on license is installed on the system. 2.A supported third-party EDR sensor (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon) is installed and running.
bugs.impact: This is a logging/display issue only — there is no functional or security impact. The EDR sensor continues running undisturbed throughout, and no license, entitlement, or sensor data is actually lost or altered. The only effect is a transient, inaccurate "Missing" entry in the logs immediately after reboot, which could momentarily mislead an administrator reviewing logs right after a reboot into thinking the EDR license isn't applied.
bugs.workaround: No action is required. The correct entitlement status (Active/Expired) is automatically logged in subsequent logs after reboot. If immediate confirmation is needed, check the current entitlement using the system's licensing display (show system licensing) rather than relying on the log entry generated during the reboot window.
bugs.fix: The entitlement status check has been updated to wait until the system has finished reading and processing the installed license at startup before logging the EDR entitlement state, ensuring only the accurate status is logged - eliminating the transient incorrect "Missing" entry on reboot.

bugs.title: Hot swapping QSFP fails to bring interface lane(s) up
bugs.symptoms: After removing and re-inserting a 400G QSFP module operating in 4x100G breakout mode, there is a chance the interface link(s) will fail to come UP.
bugs.conditions: -- Disabling the interface -- Removing the optic -- Re-inserting the optic -- Enabling the interface
bugs.impact: Interface lane(s) bringup fails impacting the datapath traffic, lag operations etc.
bugs.workaround: Enable the interface prior to re-inserting the optic.
bugs.fix: Fixed an intermittent issue causing interface link(s) to fail to come up.

bugs.title: Base Image status is not being shown as in-use
bugs.symptoms: When the base image services are imported from a different ISO than the one that is currently running, the base image services in the "show images " / "show system images" invocation is not being shown as in-use.
bugs.conditions: The base image services is imported from a different ISO than the currently running patch ISO.
bugs.impact: When a user tries to delete the base image services, the 'the image is in use by other patch ISO' error message appears.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Standby controller may not log the EDR entitlement "Active" status after a chassis power cycle
bugs.symptoms: After a full chassis power cycle, the standby controller may not produce an edr entitlement log entry at all — leaving no EDR entitlement status recorded for the standby controller.
bugs.conditions: Occurs intermittently following a full chassis-level power cycle on a system with: 1.A valid EDR add-on license installed. 2.CrowdStrike Falcon sensor installed and running on both controllers.
bugs.impact: Visibility/logging only — the EDR add-on license entitlement itself is unaffected and remains correctly active on both controllers; the sensor continues running normally. The only effect is that the standby controller's log does not show a confirming "EDR Enablement License Active" entry
bugs.workaround: Confirm the entitlement status directly via the system's licensing display (show system licensing) on the standby controller, which reflects the correct state independent of this logging gap. If the log entry is specifically needed, restart the Falcon sensor service on the affected standby (systemctl restart falcon-sensor.service) controller to trigger the correct entitlement log to be generated.

bugs.title: Docker-stats telemetry collection exceeds the configured interval
bugs.symptoms: The docker-stats telemetry collection takes more time(30s-1m) than configured(5s/10s).
bugs.impact: The off-box telemetry exporters configured with container metrics and the in-box prometheus will receive data at a slower rate than configured. The end user impact is missing the granular visibility and brief spikes in container stats.

bugs.title: Internal registry port allocation collision on image import causes upgrade issues
bugs.symptoms: It is possible for the internal registry ports assigned to imported F5OS software images to get out of sync between the 2 chassis controllers. This leads to upgrade issues when trying to upgrade to an F5OS image that has a registry port inconsistency between the 2 controllers.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur if the image partition on the active controller is above 40% usage. The issue can also occur if an image is imported only on the standby chassis controller, and then a different image is imported on the active chassis controller.
bugs.impact: Since the registry ports differ between the controllers, when the system fails over to the chassis controller after being installed, it can fail to pull some of the needed software containers, causing the system to not startup correctly.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to correct the port mismatch before upgrading to a new software version. A knowledge base article is being created with the procedure for doing this.
